# Uderia Changelog

## Nov 2026 — The public core shows nothing of the author's infrastructure; one public demo endpoint

**Why:** the last check before the core went public found the author's setup in it: the published `docker-compose.yml` mounted the production host's path over `/app` (on any other machine an empty folder, so a container without code), set the production URL and privileged mode; the changelog mapped every MCP endpoint, its database identity and which ports were forwarded, and named the warehouse's public port; the Quick Start cloned the private development repository; `docs/proposals/` argued against a named product; and 70 old performance-run outputs named the production server.

- **One public demo endpoint, on purpose:** the bootstrap MCP server is **Uderia demo — read-only (fitness_db)**, MCP endpoint 8888 (`fitness_manager`, read-only, sample data), so a new installation can be tried without a database of its own; the README's Quick Start says what it is and what it is not.
- **The compose for anyone:** `# prod-only-begin` … `# prod-only-end` blocks (the host mount, the production URL, privileged mode) are dropped by the export (`build_public_core.public_compose`), and `#public:` lines put local defaults in their place. Production's file is unchanged in meaning.
- **Every link to the repository points at `uderia-core`:** the Quick Start, the install guide, the template READMEs, the header's GitHub button, its star count and the Info box.
- **Out of the core** (`working-notes`): `docs/proposals/**` (its 19 public links became code references) and `test/performance/results/**`. Internal host names, paths, LAN addresses and non-demo ports in public documents are reworded.
- **Gate:** `test_public_core_manifest.py` fails the export when a public file names a `uderia.com` port other than the demo's, the production path or host, a LAN address of the author's network, or the private repository, and when the exported compose carries a production value.

## Nov 2026 — The Files panel follows the agent in view

**What:** the Files panel's agent filter started on *All agents* and stayed there when the conversation switched agent (a new default, an @TAG pick), so the panel kept showing another agent's files beside the conversation. It now follows the one `uderia:effective-profile` signal `main.js` emits from the resource-panel seam, the knowledge-graph panel's pattern: a closed panel ignores it; opening reads the agent in view; a switch while open refilters the list; a filter the user picks in the select holds until the panel closes; a file opened by id is shown whatever agent produced it. A list empty for that agent says so and offers *Show all agents*; the first-run view stays for a user with no files at all. Gate: `test/test_files_ux.mjs` (126).

## Nov 2026 (v1.28) — Release

**91 commits since v1.27 (2 – 14 Nov 2026).** The release of the two distributions. Headlines:

- **Two distributions from one source** — the public core (`uderia-core`) and the enterprise package (`uderia-enterprise`), built from this repository by one manifest (`oss/public_core.json`, every tracked file a decision with its reason), the package installed beside the core through the `uderia.plugins` entry point; `scripts/verify_open_core.py` proves the core alone, the full stack and a restricted key behave as the monorepo does. The core opened up on 12 Nov: sixteen of nineteen components, every storage, vector and graph backend, the Teradata depth, the account connectors. The package keeps the three OBDA planes, identity federation (OIDC, SAML, Google and GitHub sign-in), external key managers, white-label branding, the prompt editor and the acts of signing.
- **The core is Fair Source** — FSL-1.1-ALv2: any use but a competing commercial offering, each release Apache 2.0 two years after it ships; announced as Fair Source, never as open source. Strategy, assessments and an unsent upstream letter left the export; the export repositories' histories are one commit each.
- **No domain pack ships** — ANDP (its methodology is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) with its corpus, policing and VAT are in neither distribution, with the benchmarks and the unfinished tutorials; the `domain-packs` entitlement is retired.
- **Licence entitlements** — a key names the package groups (five) and components it entitles; a withheld part behaves exactly as the core does without it, applied by one module (`core/entitlements.py`); the Info box shows the licence in force.
- **Plain-text system prompts** — `schema/default_prompts/*.txt` is the one source, release-synced without overwriting a person's edit; the encryption is retired and an existing database converted once.
- **First start in the background** — the server serves at once while the embedding model loads; the Uderia Expert is bundled pre-embedded in the core and seeded once.
- **Legal drafts for counsel** — the CLAs, the enterprise licence outline, the Teradata partner draft (D13: the partner's commercial use of the core) and `legal/COUNSEL-BRIEF.md`. Both distribution repositories stay private until counsel has answered.
- **The Files panel follows the agent in view** — a new default or an @TAG pick refilters the list; a filter the user picks holds until the panel closes.
- **Fixes** — the ContextBuilder passed no plan carrier (every strategic plan built through it raised `KeyError` since 2 Nov); the two embedding-model warm-ups no longer race; consumption limits enforced from one resolver on every path; every platform-connector tool execution audited; secrets and data kept out of the Docker image.

**Deploy:** `pyproject` 1.28.0 · compose `uderia-v1-28` + build-arg default `v1.28` · annotated tag `v1.28`. The first start of v1.28 is a schema-ledger upgrade (a `VACUUM INTO` backup first). Prompts: plain text since 9 Nov — the first start converts any encrypted rows (`agent/prompt_migration.py`); no prompt deploy step. No new Python dependencies. A licence key naming `domain-packs` has the name ignored with one warning; production's key names no groups.

## Nov 2026 — The VAT pack leaves both distributions; the `domain-packs` entitlement retired

**Decision (14 Nov 2026):** the VAT pack (the import scripts for the Virtual Account Team's corpus) ships with neither distribution, the last domain pack after ANDP and policing. With it went the reason for the `domain-packs` group, which by then held only the author's benchmark harness and the unfinished tutorials, both shipped to licensees by that accident of grouping.

- **Manifest:** `agent_packs/vat/**`, `benchmarks/**` and `tutorials/**` move to `working-notes` (never shipped).
- **Entitlements: five groups** — `enterprise-components · enterprise-identity · enterprise-scale · prompt-editing · trust-signing`. `domain-packs` is gone from `core/entitlements.GROUPS`, `build_enterprise_package.SHIPPED_GROUPS`, the licence generator and the verifier. A key that still names it has the name ignored with one logged warning (`entitlements()`); keys without the field, the repository's and production's, are unaffected.
- **Texts:** the README table and licence section, the capability page, the enterprise licence outline, the partner draft's Schedule E ("all five") and PROMPT_ARCHITECTURE no longer name a domain pack. Gates: `test_license_entitlements.py`, `test_public_core_manifest.py`, `verify_open_core.py`.

## Nov 2026 — The ANDP and policing packs leave both distributions

**Decision (14 Nov 2026):** the ANDP agent pack (with its corpus skill and design playbook) and the policing pack ship with neither distribution. The ANDP pack is adapted from Teradata's AI-Native Data Products methodology, licensed **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0** (non-commercial, share-alike), and carried no attribution; the policing pack renders DDL from that standard's reference build. Licence check: Loom's Teradata patterns (`skills/builtin/teradata-patterns/`) are Apache 2.0 and stay public with their NOTICE.

- **Manifest:** `agent_packs/andp/**`, `agent_packs/policing-data-products/**` and `test/Design_Data_Product_ANDP.md` move to `third-party-content` (never shipped). The ANDP constructor (`kg_constructors/andp_semantic*`) reads a deployed product at runtime, carries no ANDP content and stays public.
- **Tests:** the seven suites that build or read either pack move to `tests-of-monorepo`; `test_agent_pack_component_config.py` skips a pack the distribution does not carry; `test_public_core_manifest.py` pins both packs as never shipped.
- **Texts:** the README table, the capability page and the enterprise package's description name the VAT pack alone; `legal/COUNSEL-BRIEF.md` §4.2 records the decision. The monorepo keeps both packs: a deployment that installed them is unaffected.

## Nov 2026 — The public core under the Functional Source License (FSL-1.1-ALv2)

**Decision (14 Nov 2026):** the public core is licensed under the Functional Source License, Version 1.1, ALv2 Future License, replacing the Apache License 2.0 before anything was published under it (all three repositories still private). Open to read, run, change and redistribute; not to be commercialised by others. Record: `docs/roadmap/OPEN_CORE_PLAN.md` §1a.

- **Terms:** any purpose except a *Competing Use* (making the software available to others in a commercial product or service that substitutes for it or offers substantially similar functionality); internal use, non-commercial education and research, and professional services for a licensee are expressly permitted. Each version becomes Apache 2.0 on the second anniversary of its release.
- **Texts:** `legal/LICENSE-FSL-1.1-ALv2.md` (verbatim, notice filled in) becomes the export's `LICENSE`; the Apache 2.0 text travels beside it as `LICENSE-APACHE-2.0`; the export's NOTICE states both. The repository `LICENSE`, the README (badge, distributions table, licence section), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, the capability page, the value layer and the introduction tutorial say *source-available* where they said *open source*; "open standards" stays.
- **Legal drafts:** the CLAs and the enterprise licence outline name the FSL; the Teradata partner draft gains decision **D13** and §4.9 — a fee-based customer deployment or Managed Service of the core is a Competing Use the FSL forbids, so the agreement grants it for the term and the run-off.
- **Announced as Fair Source**, never as *open source* or *open core* (the README's licence section says so).
- **Manifest:** `public_licence` is `FSL-1.1-ALv2`; the export refuses to build without the licence text. `docs/Strategy/**`, `docs/Assessment/**` (market assessment, partner framing, plans) and `docs/upstream/**` (an unsent letter to upstream maintainers) had slipped into the public core and move to `working-notes`; `uderia-core`'s history is squashed to one export so no earlier Apache-licensed snapshot is published with it. Gates: `test_public_core_manifest.py`, `test_value_layer.py`.

## Nov 2026 — The Google and GitHub sign-in joins the identity entitlement

The seven OAuth login routes move from `auth_routes.py` to `api/oauth_routes.py` (group `enterprise-identity`, registered optionally by `main.py`), and `auth/oauth_*.py` — handlers, configuration, middleware, rate limiter, audit logger — follow. The public core keeps local accounts, JWT and access tokens; its login and register pages hide the provider divider and buttons when no provider answers (before, the login page printed "No OAuth providers configured"). The verifier checks the route under both keys; the entitlements gate holds the modules to the group.

## Nov 2026 — First start: the model in the background, the Uderia Expert bundled and pre-embedded

- **`core/first_start.py`** — one background chain started by `before_serving`: the embedding model and the knowledge retriever load in a thread (the server serves at once; before this the start blocked for the whole load, 44 s on a busy host), then the bundled packs are seeded once for the bootstrap admin. `GET /api/status` reports `knowledge: {state: loading | ready | failed, model, download, seconds}`; the log names the download, the seconds, the pack, its counts.
- **The bundled pack** — the public core ships `agent_packs/uderia_expert/bundled/uderia_expert.agentpack`, built at export time (`build_public_core.py --bundled-packs`, 85 s, 26 MB, 6,793 chunks) from the documentation the export carries, with its vectors computed on the publishing machine; a deployment loads them in about four seconds and embeds nothing. The monorepo never tracks it (the folder's own `.gitignore`, which the export does not carry). A pack already installed (any owner) or recorded in the system setting `bundled_packs_seeded` is never seeded again; no admin defers to the next start.
- **Rehearsed** on the exported core with a fresh database and no licence: serving after 20 s, model ready 2 s later, the Uderia Expert installed in 4.2 s, @UDERIA over the API, a second start that leaves it alone, zero errors. The verifier builds with the pack, holds its documents to the exported corpus, reads the first-start lines and the seeded agent, and checks the second start does not seed again.
- **Texts:** the README's deployment notes carry a *First start* paragraph beside the requirements; the install guide a *First start* section. Gate: `test_first_start.py`.

## Nov 2026 — The core opened up: sixteen components, every backend, the Teradata depth, the account connectors, the ANDP pack

**Decision (12 Nov 2026):** the public core carries everything a single team needs to adopt the framework; the enterprise package keeps what governs an estate.

- **Public now:** Scheduler, Flow, Dashboard, Canvas, Platform and Explain Plan with their companion skills, routes, tables and panels; the Postgres session backend; the S3, Azure Blob and Google Cloud Storage file-store backends; the Neo4j graph-store backend; the Teradata vector-store backend (server-side chunking, BM25), catalog provider, deployment backend, tuning evidence, SQL pattern library and skills; the Google, Microsoft 365 and Slack account connectors with their MCP servers; the ANDP pack and the ANDP constructor. The README's distributions table, the capability pages and the value proposition say so.
- **Enterprise still:** the three OBDA planes (OBDA-READ, OBDA-MODEL, OBDA-ACT), identity federation (OIDC, SAML 2.0), the external key managers, white-label branding by host, the system-prompt editor, the VAT and policing packs, and the acts of signing. Six entitlement groups: `teradata-depth` and `saas-connectors` cease to exist; `enterprise-components` is the three planes; `enterprise-scale` is key managers and branding. The generator, the owner's manual, the Info box and the partner draft's Schedule E follow.
- **Neither distribution:** `deploy/` and `mcp_custom_objects/` — the author's own MCP endpoints, identities and warehouse operations — move to `working-notes`.
- **Mechanics:** 57 manifest rules removed (the trailing include takes the files); the eleven template markers of the opened panels and scripts are gone (plain template again; six remain: sso, prompts, obda_policy and the three planes' panels); the SDKs of the opened backends (neo4j, azure-storage-blob, azure-identity, google-cloud-storage) are the core's requirements; the gates (`test_public_core_manifest`, `test_license_entitlements`) and the verifier's restricted run (now OBDA-READ only) hold the new line.
- **"Commercial" is gone** from every licence statement (README, CONTRIBUTING, the capability and value pages, the licence outline, the partner draft, the manifest): the Uderia Enterprise Licence governs intellectual property and distribution; whether the package is monetised is a separate, open decision.

## Nov 2026 — The acts of signing are the enterprise package's (`trust-signing`)

**Why:** the Trust Circle keeps its teasing quality in the public core — every state, every station, the owed act — while the one act a company needs before it operates an agent, signing it, is the package's. The per-turn evidence signature (`core/provenance.py`) stays public: it is what "trust you can check" means and nobody performs it.

- `api/trust_signing_routes.py` (new, group `trust-signing`): the sixteen acts — sign-off of an agent, ontology, data product, action, ontology extension, skill, extension, assurance module, knowledge and planner repository, flow, dashboard, canvas and agent pack, attestation of a deployment, revocation of a signature — with their authorisers. `trust_routes.py` keeps every read (the circle, the stations, histories, verify, artifact states, keys) and stays public; the composition and the store stay public (the core verifies). `main.py` registers the acts with the optional-import idiom: absent, they answer 404 and the log says so.
- The entitlement: `trust-signing` joins `core/entitlements.GROUPS`, the package's shipped groups, the generator, the owner's manual, the Info box and the partner draft's Schedule E (eight groups).
- The page: `window.UDERIA_LICENCE` carries the licence summary; the one fetch seam in `auth.js` answers an act of signing without the entitlement with the explanation and a synthetic 404 before the request leaves the page, so every call site behaves the same; the Trust Circle keeps the owed act visible and marks it `· ENTERPRISE`.
- README distributions table: the Trust row's enterprise column names the acts; the Knowledge and Storage rows name the backends as backends (the Neo4j graph-store backend, the Teradata vector-store backend, the ChromaDB and Qdrant vector-store backends, the Postgres session backend), not the stores.

## Nov 2026 — The licence tooling is in the monorepo, in neither distribution

`maintenance/licensing/` holds `generate_keys.py`, `generate_license.py` (now with `--key` / `$TDA_LICENSE_SIGNING_KEY`, so the signing key stays in the vault and never in the tree) and the owner's manual; manifest group `working-notes`, so neither export carries it, and `Dockerfile.dockerignore` keeps the folder out of every image. The separate `trusted-data-agent-license` repository only points here now. A deployment needs nothing from this folder: the validator, the entitlements and the public key are in the core. Gates: `test_license_entitlements.py` (the generator's lists match the runtime's; the folder is in neither distribution), `test_dockerignore.py`.

## Nov 2026 — Licence entitlements: a key names what the deployment may run

**Why:** the licence said one thing, its tier, so the whole enterprise package was on or off, and the repository's own key had no weight. Before the first Partner key is issued, the key and the agreement's schedule should say the same thing, and the software should honour it.

- **The key** may carry `entitlements` (the distribution manifest's groups: `enterprise-components`, `enterprise-identity`, `enterprise-scale`, `teradata-depth`, `saas-connectors`, `prompt-editing`, `domain-packs`) and `components` (a sub-list of the nine). A key without the field is the whole package: every key issued before this change, prod's included, means exactly what it meant.
- **ONE rule, one module** (`core/entitlements.py`): a group the key withholds behaves exactly as the public core behaves without it. The enterprise package is built one root per group (`overlay/<group>`, `assets/<group>`, the partials under their group) and, within the components group, one per component (each manifest rule of the group names its component, `"component": "flow"`), and `register()` installs only the entitled roots; in the development repository the server's import guard refuses a withheld module, so the core's `try/except ImportError` seams fall through as in the public core; the component manager does not install a withheld component; the page is rendered without the withheld `{# enterprise-begin:x #}` blocks; the skills, connector and template loaders do not list a withheld directory. The prompt editor is the `prompt-editing` entitlement (route and UI).
- **The licence governs the running server.** `main.py` arms the gates only when run as the server; the package arms when it activates; `set_for_tests` arms a test. A test or script that imports the code sees the whole repository, so the battery never depends on the machine's key. `/api/v1/auth/me` reports `license` (tier, entitlements, components).
- **Generator** (licence repository): `--entitlements group,group|all`, `--components id,id`; a renewal carries the old key's fields. Owner's manual §3a.
- **Gates:** `test_license_entitlements.py` (the tables held to the shipped groups, the manifest and the template's markers; signed fixtures under a throwaway pair; semantics, paths, the template, the import guard, every seam, the package layout); `scripts/verify_open_core.py` adds a run of the merged stack under a restricted Partner key (two components, the scale group) and checks each withheld group is absent, over the probe and over REST.
- **Found by the browser rehearsal, fixed here — the page never booted without all thirteen builtin renderers.** `componentRenderers.js` imported every builtin component's renderer statically (`import … from '/api/v1/components/<id>/renderer'`), and `eventHandlers.js` the canvas one; a static import that answers 404 fails the whole module graph, so a deployment without a component — the public core without the nine enterprise components, a deployment whose licence withholds one — rendered an empty shell stuck at "Connecting". The verifier had only probed `/login` and REST. Now the server renders the installed component ids into the page (`window.UDERIA_COMPONENTS`), the registry imports only those renderers (dynamic, top-level await keeps the registration contract), the lazy opens of a dashboard, flow or canvas go through `loadRendererModule` (no request for an absent component), and the verifier reads the page's list and the served registry. Rehearsed in headless Chromium on three deployments — the public core with no licence, the monorepo under a restricted key, the monorepo under a whole-package key — each with zero console errors and the composer opening.
- **Seen on the development machine:** its tracked key is the retired App Developer tier, so the local server now runs as the public core (SSO 404, editor 404, ten components, the page without the enterprise blocks) until an Enterprise key is issued for the repository.

## Nov 2026 — Minimum system requirements stated

The README's Quick Start carries a requirements table (processor, memory, disk, software, network, browser: the minimum beside the maintainer's reference deployment), and the install guide's new *System requirements* subsection has the full version: what the figures are made of (a 2.7 GB Python environment, the 90 MB CPU embedding model, the databases and backups that grow), the one-time Hugging Face download, and what adds to the baseline (a local model server, the optional external backends, OCR). The Docker guide points at it from its Quick Start and explains the 6 GB `mem_limit`. The figures are measured: the production container's usage after 19 hours, its compose limit and the comment that justifies it, the environment's size on disk.

## Nov 2026 — The Industry Data Model constructor ships with neither distribution (licence review)

**Why:** the constructor reads the Databricks industry data models from `databricks-industry-solutions/lakehouse-industry-data-models` and deploys them as Teradata or PostgreSQL schemas. That repository's `LICENSE.md` is not an open-source licence: the materials may be used "solely for the purposes of using the Licensed Materials within or connecting to the Databricks Services", and Databricks may terminate the licence on notice. Until counsel has answered, the constructor stays in the development repository and leaves with neither export (decision of 10 Nov 2026). Production runs the development repository and is unchanged.

- `oss/public_core.json`: group `licence-review` (22 files) — the walker, source and strategy (`kg_constructors/industry_model_*.py`, `declarative_model.py`), the `kg-industry-model` template, `kgIndustryModelModal.js`, the rename script, the three Industry Model plan documents, the walker-only fixture and the ten tests that import the constructor. `build_enterprise_package.NEVER` lists the group, so the package drops it too. `model_naming.py`, `dbdeploy/` and the PDM fixture stay public: the authored layer and the declared-model constructor deploy through them.
- The core tolerates the absence: `kg_constructors/__init__.py` imports the walker and the strategy optionally (the mode is simply not registered), `dbdeploy/physical_model.py` reads metric views counts-only without the parser, the two `/v1/knowledge-graph/industry-models*` routes answer 404 "not part of this distribution", and `SourceError` moved to `kg_constructors/base.py` (re-exported by the industry source) so the five generic knowledge-graph routes catch it in every distribution.
- Four public suites read the constructor's files for one check each and are now distribution-aware (`test_kg_authored_layer`, `test_kg_source_validation`, `test_semantic_datasource`, `test_pdm_design_rules` §7).
- Documents: the eleven links to the three plan documents became code references (`docs/README.md`, `COMPONENTS.md`, `KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `ACT_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `ONTOLOGY_ARCHITECTURE.md`); the README's distributions table names the exception under the table; `OPEN_CORE_PLAN.md` has the group's row.
- Gates: `test_public_core_manifest.py` (the group is never shipped, each file in neither distribution, the shared helpers public, `SourceError` in base), `scripts/verify_open_core.py` (the merged stack registers no `industry_model` mode and the package carries none of the files).

## Nov 2026 — Component renderers are display assets: exempt from the per-IP API limit

**Why:** right after the deploy of 9 Nov 2026 a demo user's page stayed stale after login: nineteen `/api/v1/components/<id>/renderer` requests answered 429. The security sweep's *API calls per minute per IP* (60, unauthenticated `/api/` only) counted them — a renderer is loaded as an ES-module import, which carries no credential — and behind production's proxy every visitor arrives as one address, so all users shared the bucket.

- `auth/rate_limiter.py`: `API_LIMIT_EXEMPT_PATTERNS` — a component renderer is an asset, never an API call; other component routes stay counted. Gate: `test_consumption_limits.py` (55).
- Deployment note: a reverse proxy that does not forward the client address (`X-Forwarded-For`) makes every per-IP limit a shared one — the login limit included.

## Nov 2026 — A document reads the same in every distribution: the manifest limits the documentation, a public document never links a private file

**Why:** 202 links in 57 public documents pointed at files the public core does not carry — the roadmap and assessment notes, the enterprise components, the positioning pages, the author's skills — so they died in the export. Rewriting them per distribution was rejected (the user: a document must not differ between distributions); publishing everything was rejected too (the documentation of the core is limited, and the manifest controls it).

- **The rule.** `oss/public_core.json` decides which documents the public core carries (today: everything under `docs/` except `roadmap/`, `assessments/`, `optimization/` and the positioning pages). A public document may link only what the public core carries; a private file — a plan, an assessment, enterprise code, a test that moved — is named as a code reference. 172 links in 45 documents were converted at the source (the changelog, the trust manual, the trust-membrane and ontology architectures carry most).
- **Two gates, no rewriting.** `test_public_core_manifest.py` resolves every relative link of every public document against the public set and names each violation; `build_public_core.write_tree` refuses an export with a dead link (`unresolved_links`). The export copies documents as they are.
- **The merged battery.** `verify_open_core.py` inlines the package's template partials into the merged tree before the battery, as Jinja does at runtime, so the suites that read `templates/index.html` see the whole page.

## Nov 2026 — Nine components move to the enterprise package; every README states the split side by side

**Why:** the user's decision (9 Nov 2026): the public core keeps the ten components that make and ground an agent; the nine that operationalise agents across an estate — Scheduler, Flow, Dashboard, Canvas, Platform, Explain Plan, OBDA-READ, OBDA-MODEL and OBDA-ACT — ship in the enterprise package. And the difference between the two distributions must be plain to anyone opening either repository.

- **The cut.** A component moves as its tool, panel, routes, store, schema, skill and front-end (manifest group `enterprise-components`, 144 files). Its substrate stays public where the core reads it: the OBDA scope parser (`agent/obda.py`), the action types and act log, the deploy backends, the scheduler engine (it runs the consumption resets), the Canvas SQL connectors (the Database Navigator's direct connection uses them). Every public import of a moved module is an optional import (`main.py` registers the four component blueprints when importable; `rest_routes`, `platform_operations`, `platform_ontology/projection`, `tuning_evidence` degrade to "not installed").
- **Two loader seams.** `ComponentManager._builtin_dirs` reads `components/builtin` from the repository and from every asset root a plug-in registered; `core/overlay.add_asset_root` puts an asset root carrying `components/` on `sys.path`, so `components.builtin.<id>` of an enterprise component imports under the core's name (a PEP 420 namespace package). `core/platform_roles` finds the Platform component through the overlay and answers with no roles when it is absent; `core/obda_planes.plane_available` is False where the component is not installed.
- **The stripped template blocks come back.** `build_public_core.strip_enterprise` now replaces a `{# enterprise-begin:x #}` block with `{% include "enterprise/x.html" ignore missing %}`; the enterprise package ships every block as `templates/enterprise/<x>.html` (twenty today: the nine panels, the OBDA policy block, six script tags, the SSO and prompt-editor tabs), joined to the template search path by `main.py`. Before this the package restored the enterprise routes but not their interface.
- **The README states the split.** `README.md` carries a core-versus-enterprise table between `distributions-table` markers (agents, trust, components, knowledge, storage, identity, data sources, connectors, prompts, faces, marketplace, branding, licence); the enterprise package's README is built from the same block. The capability pages, the component architecture, the licence text, the plan and the site's licence table name the nine.
- **Gates:** `test_public_core_manifest.py` 70 (the ten public, the nine excluded with their skills, the Canvas connectors kept, the partial mechanics); `verify_open_core.py` counts ten components in the core export, nine in the package, nineteen in the merged stack, and the partials.

## Nov 2026 — The prompts are plain text; the licence activates the enterprise package and nothing else

**Why:** with the public core shipping every prompt in plain text, encrypting the same fifteen texts in the enterprise package protected nothing and cost real incidents (`[ENCRYPTED CONTENT]`, the rekey on renewal, the deploy script's format pitfalls). The user's decision (9 Nov 2026): the enterprise prompt set never diverges, so the prompts move into the monorepo and the encryption goes.

- **One source.** `schema/default_prompts/<NAME>.txt` — fifteen tracked files, shipped in both distributions (moved from the licence repository; `default_prompts.json` and `default_prompts.dat` deleted). `agent/prompt_defaults.py` runs at every start: a missing or `[MIGRATE]` prompt is seeded, a base prompt **no person edited** follows the release (the replaced text kept in `prompt_versions` as *Replaced by the release default*, the version moved past it), a prompt a person edited is kept. This replaces the licence repository's `update_prompt.py`.
- **The one-time conversion.** `agent/prompt_migration.py` (replacing `prompt_rekey.py`): every encrypted row (`is_encrypted`: a base64-wrapped Fernet token) is converted in ONE transaction with the version trigger suspended, trying the licence recorded by the former re-key, the current licence file and every `.previous`; a row no key opens is left, counted and the log names the recovery; `prompt_key_license` is dropped when nothing encrypted remains. Rehearsed on a copy of the local database: 30 rows converted, 5 unedited prompts followed the release.
- **The loader and the editor.** `prompt_loader.py` reads plain text, honours user → profile → base with pinned versions, and reads the licence tier once (`core/license_file.load_validated`); it never requires a licence. The editor (`system_prompts_routes.py`) stores plain text and refuses with 403 unless `core/enterprise.is_licensed()`.
- **The licence.** `core/license_file.validate` is the ONE check (RSA-PSS signature, expiry); `LICENSED_TIERS = ("Enterprise", "Partner")`; the four earlier tiers are retired. No licence → `Community` → the public core; an invalid or expired file is logged (`Licence ignored:`) and ignored — a start is never refused over it. The enterprise package's `register()` validates it and stays dormant without it. `verify_open_core.py` issues a throwaway key pair and licence instead of copying the deployment's.
- **Documentation.** `PROMPT_ENCRYPTION.md` → `PROMPT_ARCHITECTURE.md` (rewritten; every link repointed); the security architecture's §5, the capability pages, the schema and user guides, the keys README, CLAUDE.md and the `system-prompts` skill say the plain model; the site's prompt-encryption section is removed. The licence repository keeps only the keys and `generate_license.py` (tiers Enterprise, Partner); its README and owner's manual are rewritten.
- **Retiring what no licence opens.** `maintenance/retire_prompt_history.py` (`--dry-run` first, server down) replaces HISTORY rows no licence the deployment can see opens with a plain marker — never a base prompt, never an override — so the start log stops reporting them. Production (9 Nov 2026): 26 rows converted at the first start, 30 history rows of March/April 2026 (keyed by a licence replaced on 30 Oct and kept nowhere) retired at the second.
- **Gates:** `test_prompt_migration.py` (37: conversion, partial conversion, candidates from the licence files, the retire step, the release sync's cases, the licence check's refusals) replaces `test_license_rekey.py`; manifest gate 55; docs integrity; value layer.

## Nov 2026 — Open core, Phase 3 prepared: the split named everywhere, the public requirements, the per-distribution catalog, the CLA

**Why:** the two exports existed and nothing said so: the README, the value layer and the site still described AGPLv3 and four licence tiers, the public core's `requirements.txt` demanded the enterprise SDKs, and the operations catalog in the public export described routes the core does not serve. Phase 3's preparation closes those on the `open-core` branch; the repositories stay private until counsel has reviewed `legal/`.

- **The split, named in one voice.** README (badge, `## License`, author section), `docs/value/VALUE_PROPOSITION.md` (the "Open and extensible" principle), `docs/capabilities/KEY_FEATURES.md`, the policing walkthrough, the repository template manifests and the site's licence section all say the same thing: the public core (`uderia-core`) under the Apache License 2.0, the enterprise package (`uderia-enterprise`) under the Uderia Enterprise Licence, described by what it adds. The monorepo's `LICENSE` names the two distributions and their licence files. `test_value_layer.py` now requires the principle to name both.
- **The public requirements.** A line of `requirements.txt` tagged `# enterprise:` (neo4j, the Azure and Google Cloud storage and key-manager SDKs, python-jose, lxml, signxml) is dropped from the public core's file at export and declared as the enterprise package's dependency in its `pyproject.toml` (`build_public_core.public_requirements` / `enterprise_requirements`). The gate checks that no public module imports a tagged SDK.
- **The operations catalog per distribution.** The export runs `maintenance/platform_operations.py backlog --write` and `docs --write` against its own routes (bootstrap state removed again), so `test_platform_operations.py` is public and passes inside the export (83 assertions). The merged stack regenerates its catalog after installing the package — `verify_open_core.py` does so before its battery, and the package's README asks the same of every install.
- **Contributing.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` (the export rhythm, the CLA, what a change needs) and `.github/workflows/cla.yml` (contributor-assistant: signing is one comment on the pull request, signatures kept on the public repository's `cla-signatures` branch, the owner allow-listed).
- **The site** (`trusted-data-agent-web`, branch `framework-framing`): "View on GitHub" and the footer link to `rgeissen/uderia-core`; the licence section is the two distributions; `test_framing.py` holds it (68 checks).
- **Gates:** `test_public_core_manifest.py` 55 · `test_value_layer.py` 762 · `test_docs_integrity.py` 312 · the site's `test_framing.py` 68.

## Nov 2026 — Open core, Phase 2: the enterprise package

**Why:** Phase 1 made the public core stand alone; Phase 2 makes the other half installable, so a licensee runs the full stack as `pip install uderia-enterprise` beside the core, and the monorepo and "core + package" run the same code (`OPEN_CORE_PLAN.md`).

Secrets, vendor content, working notes and this repository's own gates (`tests-of-monorepo`) ship with neither distribution.
- **Two seams, one module.** `core/overlay.py`: a finder at the end of `sys.meta_path` resolves a `trusted_data_agent.*` module the core lacks from a registered overlay — so every optional import of Phase 1, and the enterprise modules' absolute imports of one another, resolve to the same module as in the monorepo without a namespace-package refactor; and asset roots, repository-shaped directories the loaders consult beside the project root. `trusted_data_agent/__init__.py` loads the `uderia.plugins` entry points before any core module (`UDERIA_NO_PLUGINS=1` starts the bare core); the package's `register()` is two calls.

- **Acceptance, `scripts/verify_open_core.py`.** Builds both, installs the package beside the core, gives the tree this repository's licence, and checks the full stack is back: every enterprise module imports under its core name; the key managers, brands, connectors, deploy backends, constructor modes, the Teradata skill, the ANDP template and ten connector manifests are registered; the server starts licensed with encrypted prompts; the SSO and prompt-editor routes answer; the Evidentia brand resolves by host and its logo is served from the package. With `--battery` the trust battery runs on the merged layout (the shipped files at their repository paths): every suite the shipped files cover passes; red is confined to the five suites that need the author's populated instance, and this repository's own gates read as not in this distribution.

**Phase 3 (publication) remains:** the public repository under the Owner's organisation with a CLA bot, the README and value layer naming the split, the site's licence section, a per-distribution operations catalog, a neutral fixture skill for the progressive-skills suites, a fixture bootstrap for the fixture-bound suites, and a public requirements file without the enterprise SDKs.

## Nov 2026 — Open core, Phase 1: the public core stands on its own

**Why:** the open-core decision of 9 Nov 2026 (`OPEN_CORE_PLAN.md`): a public core under the Apache License 2.0 and an enterprise package under a commercial licence, the line between trust and operations, copyright with the Owner. Phase 1 makes the public export install, start and answer with nothing of the enterprise package present.

- **Every seam is an optional import.** The 16 public→enterprise imports are `try: … except ImportError:` or registry lookups: the SSO and SAML routes moved to their own blueprint (`api/sso_routes.py`, registered by `main.py` when present), the prompt editor likewise; PKCE is generic (`auth/pkce.py`); branding is split into the public contract and default (`core/branding.py`, with a resolver seam) and the host-resolved registry (`core/branding_hosts.py`); the external key managers leave `filestore/kms.py` for `filestore/kms_providers.py` and register on import; the SaaS connectors register only when present and the scheduler and knowledge sync look them up; the ANDP constructor is optional, the warehouse connection opener (`kg_constructors/connection.py`) and four walker helpers (`walker_util.py`) are shared public code; Neo4j, the Teradata deploy backend and catalog provider, Postgres sessions and the cloud file stores register only when present. The import check now resolves relative imports and treats a guarded import as cut; the baseline is 0 and may not rise.
- **The public core runs without a licence.** `PromptLoader` enters Community mode when no licence file exists and `schema/default_prompts.json` does: the prompts are stored and read plain, nothing is decrypted, the tier reads *Community*. `scripts/export_default_prompts.py` writes that file from the licence repository's sources (decision: the current prompts, plain); the gate holds its prompt names equal to the encrypted set's.
- **The enterprise panels leave the exported interface whole.** `{# enterprise-begin:x #} … {# enterprise-end:x #}` marks the SSO and prompt-editor tab buttons, their panels and the SSO script in `templates/index.html`; the export strips the blocks; the gate checks they are paired and gone.
- **One plug-in mechanism.** `core/plugins.py` loads every entry point in the group `uderia.plugins` before the routes and lets a plug-in register blueprints; the enterprise package (Phase 2) joins through it.
- **Acceptance.** `scripts/build_public_core.py --out` exports 2,508 files; every module of the public tree imports with the enterprise files absent; the exported server starts without a licence, stores 15 plain prompts, answers 404 on the SSO and prompt-editor routes, and a REST-driven turn on a local Ollama model completes.
- **The battery runs in the export too.** A test follows the module it imports or the enterprise source file it reads by name (`tests-of-excluded`, derived); suites that assert the monorepo's own shape (`tests-of-repo-shape`: the documentation and value gates, the dockerignore gate, the operations catalog, the domain packs, the Teradata skills) and suites that need the author's populated instance (`tests-of-dev-fixtures`) are classified in the manifest with a reason each. Four suites became distribution-aware (`# distribution-aware`: they check what the tree carries and skip the rest). The export writes `test/.public-core`; with that marker the battery reports a listed suite that is absent as *not in this distribution* instead of red. Acceptance: the export, first-started once, runs the battery with 360 suites passing and 41 skipped.
- **Found on the way, fixed:** `knowledge_sync` imported a `GoogleConnector` class that does not exist (Drive sync always failed; it now resolves the connector through the registry); the Ollama configuration test called a `generate()` the client never had (it now lists models and runs one chat turn); `langchain-ollama` was missing from the requirements although the LangChain lane needs it for local models; a registered RAG template whose directory is absent logged an error instead of a note; `main.py` wiped and recreated `logs/` at import time, so the parallel battery raced one suite's `rmtree` against another's `makedirs` (the recurring red on a `logs` directory) — the directory is now created once and the server truncates its own log files at start.

**Gates:** `test_public_core_manifest.py` (37), `test_branding.py`, `test_file_store.py`, `test_license_rekey.py`, `test_saml_hardening.py` and `test_oidc_hardening.py` (repointed at the extracted blueprint), the declared-model walker suites, the version-pin gate (three stale template pins aligned), the outcome-loop suites (a pre-existing failure: the context accessors now tolerate an executor built without `__init__`), the trust battery on the monorepo (a few suites die in the parallel run on a `logs` directory race and pass serially; pre-existing) and inside the export.

## Nov 2026 — Uderia presented as a framework for trusted data agents, with no comparison

**Why:** to remove any read of Uderia as a product competing with the author's employer. Uderia is now presented as **a framework for trusted data agents**; **the Uderia platform** is its runtime implementation (the server, interface and REST API), never Uderia as a whole. No code changed: the interface, the brand defaults, emails, role files and playbooks are exactly as on main.

- **Value layer.** The core says what the framework is (the agent model, the trust model, the platform as its runtime implementation) and what is built on it, each extension point with its contract. `POSITIONING_PLATFORM.md` became `POSITIONING_FRAMEWORK.md` and makes no comparison of any kind; the Teradata page says Uderia adds to Vantage and replaces nothing. The value index fixes the vocabulary (framework · platform · deployment · Uderia) and two new rules: no comparison wherever Uderia is presented, and Uderia as a whole is never "a platform" or "a product".
- **External trust collateral.** The proof packs drop the vendor-assessment framing (ratings, "GREEN for only one vendor (Teradata). Uderia matches the sole leader.", "competitors", "leapfrog", "best-in-class") and open with what each proves and what you can check. The served trust pages drop "most platforms", "competitors can't copy", "beyond parity" and "moat". **The policing demo page is withdrawn** from `/static/trust/` with its index section and companion links; the pack's own story page keeps its Evidentia naming but loses the named vendor and every product comparison.
- **Wording across presented pages.** The runbook, the manuals, the guides, the capability pages, the docs index, the release notes and the architecture docs rendered into the trust pages say Uderia, the framework, the platform (runtime) or the deployment as each sentence means. Pillar 1 is **Deployment Security**. Architecture docs that compared Uderia with named products or "the market" (Canvas, MCP server, next-step recommender, ontology, agent ops) state what Uderia does instead.
- **From ideation to operationalization, both halves.** IFOC is how you work; the second half is that the interface is one client of a REST-driven engine, so what a team shapes interactively runs as code without being rebuilt: an agent's setup is created and exported through the API (agent packs), a question runs unchanged from REST, a scheduler, a pipeline or an MCP client. The README opening, the value core (a ninth outcome, the *Actionable* principle, "What the framework is"), both positioning pages, Key Features (*Agent setup as code*) and the user guide's Operationalization section say so; no generator was added (a conversation becomes code by sending the same prompt with the same agent).
- **The value layer states the path and makes trust a principle.** The value core opens with its own *From ideation to operationalization* section (two halves: how you work, how it leaves the interface). Its six principles keep their count, with *Transparent* becoming **Transparent and trusted**: what can be seen can be checked, so trust is earned, shown and carried, never asserted (answer gates, per-turn scoring, signed parts, evidence, fail-closed authority, the Trust Circle, trust that travels and is checked again), each claim linked to where it is substantiated. Key Features' *Transparent and Trusted* section opens with that trust model; the framework page carries the path, and its *Transparent and trusted* property.
- **The README rewritten as the single description page.** One sequence a reader can follow: what Uderia is and what it lets a team do; *why it exists* (the five hard parts an organisation answers for: answers within the evidence, actions within the mandate, a record others can check, a cost with an owner, a path to production); *how it works* (an agent is a configuration; one engine; a diagram of who asks, the engine, what stays yours and the signed record; the four classes with their bootstrap agents); *from ideation to operationalization* with the REST call that runs a refined question from code; *trust you can check* at four moments, with a one-line offline verification of a signed answer; the six principles in a line each; *built to be built on* (19 builtin components and the extension contracts); *what Uderia is not* (a model, a data store, a replacement for your governance); then Quick Start and documentation routed by what the reader wants to do. Every claim links to where it is substantiated; the diagram renders (checked with Mermaid 10).
- **Efficiency named.** The README tagline gains a third phrase in the same shape — *Cloud-Level Reasoning. Zero-Trust Privacy. Token-Level Efficiency.* — and the promise becomes "a framework for building **efficient** data agents", in the README and the value core, each backed where it is made by the planner's mechanisms (plan once, known steps without a model call, proven plans replayed, earlier results carried forward, per-turn tokens and cost from the provider) with links to the Fusion Optimizer and proof pack P4. The app's welcome screen keeps its two-line tagline (brand defaults in code, unchanged).
- **Seven balanced principles; Open and extensible added.** The seventh principle, **Open and extensible** (open source, open standards at every boundary — MCP both ways, OAuth/OIDC/SAML, OpenTelemetry-shaped spans, Ed25519, W3C formats — sixteen documented extension points, and the one closed layer stated plainly: below the Enterprise licence tier the system prompts are encrypted). All seven now share one shape — a bold statement, 45–75 words, a *Where to check* line with its links — and the README's one-liners are balanced the same way. The extension table in the value core lists all sixteen points (components incl. your own, skills, extensions, repository templates, knowledge sources, knowledge-graph constructors, context-window modules, execution engines, model providers, vector and graph stores, data sources with custom objects, connectors, assurance modules, agent packs, branding, integration), mirrored by the README's grouped table; Key Features gains its *Open and Extensible* section; the framework page's *Neutral* property becomes *Open and neutral*. The Financial governance principle claims what exists (consumption per user, cost by provider and model). Restored the value core's closing pointer to the writing rules, lost in the previous merge of principles. Gate: test_value_layer.py 727 checks — seven principles, each balanced and checkable; sixteen extension points counted consistently; the closed layer always stated.
- **The ambition stated: the autonomous enterprise.** The README and the value core carry, in the same words, *Where it is heading: the autonomous enterprise* — routine questions and decisions delegated to agents, people's attention where judgement is needed; autonomy earned, not switched on (each agent given as much as its evidence supports: gates from observing to enforcing, changes from parked for review to approved, authority failing closed); some acts staying with people by design (signing, credentials, approving a change); and today's path linked across the whole range, from assisted to self-operating (coordinators, unattended scheduled runs that stop to ask, signed actions, and agents that operate Uderia itself through the Platform component within the roles they are granted). Gate: present in both, the same words, earned-not-switched-on, people's acts, the path linked.
- **Left as is, by decision:** the README's licence section; the Evidentia brand descriptor and naming; internal planning documents (roadmap, strategy, assessments), which still carry the comparison language the presented pages no longer do.

**Gate:** `test_value_layer.py` 488 → **620**: no comparison across the value and capability layers, the proof packs, the README and every published trust page (read as rendered text); the front door, the value pages and the trust landing page call Uderia a framework and name the platform as its runtime implementation; no presented page calls Uderia as a whole a platform or a product. Mutation-tested. The trust bundle is re-rendered and current.

## Nov 2026 — The four defects the documentation sweep recorded, fixed

**Why:** the sweep below compared every page with the code and recorded four places where the code, not the docs, was wrong. Each is fixed at its root, with a gate that fails against the old behaviour.

- **Secrets in the image.** The Dockerfile copies the whole build context and the repository carried no ignore file, so a build from a working checkout baked `.env` (`SECRET_KEY`, `TDA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), the JWT secret, the provenance signing key and every database into the image layers. `.dockerignore` is gitignored (a host may keep its own), so the rules ship as **`Dockerfile.dockerignore`**, which BuildKit reads in preference. `docs/` stays in the image (the knowledge sync reads `file://` sources from the project root); `benchmarks/` is left out. Gate: `test_dockerignore.py` (54: every secret and data path excluded, no tracked file the image needs excluded).
- **Limits that never followed the user.** The per-turn check (`ConsumptionManager.check_rate_limits` / `check_token_quota`, run on every turn, REST included) compared against limits copied onto the `user_consumption` row when it was created; a reassigned or edited profile, the Global Override and the admin exemption never reached it, while the UI path's `ConsumptionEnforcer` read the live profile. **ONE resolver** now, `auth/consumption_limits.py:effective_limits` (admin exempt → Global Override → assigned profile → default profile → unlimited), read by both paths; the cached columns are kept in step for the admin views and are never what a check compares against. A user with no profile at all is now unlimited on both paths (the per-turn check used 100/1,000). `test_consumption_healing` set its limit on the cached column; it now sets it through a profile.
- **Two limits enforced nowhere.** *Configuration changes per hour*: `auth/config_change_limit.py:limit_config_changes` on the ten agent, LLM-configuration and MCP-server create/update/delete/import routes — 429 `rate_limit_exceeded` over the limit, each successful change audited as `config_change`, which is the count (activation is not a change; admins exempt). The recorder it relies on wrote `AuditLog` rows without their NOT NULL `status`, so even a caller would have counted nothing; it now writes through `log_audit_event`. *API calls per minute per IP*: a `before_request` hook (`rate_limiter.enforce_ip_api_limit`) over `/api/` requests without a valid credential (a Bearer token or `token=` parameter is validated, an access token read-only so its use is not counted twice); signed-in traffic is governed per user, the notification stream is exempt, the master switch rules. Gate: `test_consumption_limits.py` (54; the reassignment and Global Override cases fail against the old check).
- **An audit promise nothing kept.** The shell connector's enable dialog said "All executions are audit-logged". `invoke_connector_tool`, the one dispatch every engine reaches a connector through, now writes an audit row per execution for every platform connector (`connector_tool_invocation`: user, connector, tool, arguments with credential-like keys redacted and long values truncated, outcome, duration; failures and timeouts too; an audit failure never breaks the tool). The dialog says exactly that. Gate: `test_connector_audit.py` (15).

**Docs:** DOCKER, CONSUMPTION_PROFILES, SECURITY_AND_TRUST, SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE §3.4/§8.3/§9.4 and CONNECTOR_ARCHITECTURE now describe the behaviour as it is. Files: `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.dockerignore`, `auth/{consumption_limits,config_change_limit}.py` (new), `auth/{consumption_enforcer,consumption_manager,rate_limiter}.py`, `main.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `core/platform_connector_registry.py`, `mcp_servers/builtin/uderia-shell/{manifest.json,server.py}`, `test/{test_dockerignore,test_consumption_limits,test_connector_audit,test_consumption_healing}.py`, `test/trust_battery.sh`.

Then every user-facing page was checked claim by claim against the code.

**Gates:** new `test_docs_integrity.py` (every link and anchor under docs/, README and CLAUDE.md resolves; every fence closes; both indexes list every architecture doc; the schema list is complete; stated counts match the code) and `test_value_layer.py` (the value layer's writing rules, and no positioning register in the capability layer); `test_uderia_expert_corpus.py` reads the overview layer. ## Nov 2026 — Findings re-read not recalled, and the per-turn tool ledger

**Why:** a comparison of Uderia's harness against a competing agent harness found two in-loop mechanics Uderia lacked by name: a *Findings* tier (verified observations such as a row count or a column distribution, re-read by the model rather than recalled — the primary hallucination-prevention mechanism on long-running work) and the loop rules *no repeated work* / *circuit breaker per tool*. Everything else on that list Uderia already had (guardrails in the loop, approve-once, run-as-user, cache-aware prefix, context folding, stubs, durable waits, judges, memory). The companion-skill rewrite into progressive form was deliberately NOT done: the owner wants an agent to be able to choose progressive or whole skills.

**Findings** — `agent/findings.py` + the 13th context-window module `components/builtin/context_window/modules/findings/`. A finding is what a tool RETURNED, never what the model said: tool · the statement or object it addressed (the executed SQL when a rewrite ran) · row count · columns (≤12) · the values of a single-row result (a count, an aggregate; ≤8 columns) or the first row of a multi-row one. Extracted DETERMINISTICALLY (zero LLM tokens), bounded (≤12 per turn), at the ONE persistence seam: `session_manager.update_last_turn_data` stamps `turn["findings"]` from an Optimize `execution_trace` (the real `{action, result}` shape — note `tool_output_summary` is a phantom key no producer writes); the ReAct lane stamps its own from the rows `_capture_data_result` kept (`data_results`, with the TRUE row count of a truncated capture); an Ideate turn without tools carries `[]`; older turns are extracted on read. The module (priority 68 · 3% · max 8%; `tool_enabled`, `llm_only`, `rag_focused`) renders `[Verified results from earlier turns in this session]` + the re-read rule, newest turn first, raw numbers (`4812`, never `4,812`), excluding the current turn; condensation keeps fewer turns but the newest turn is **pinned** under any budget; abstains on turn one and with nothing to say; `purge` is refused (findings are the record's own). Delivery: the executor caches the contribution (`_cw_findings_text`, `_get_findings_context()`) and every engine appends it after the KG enrichment — Ideate, Focus, ReAct (`conversation_engine`), the strategic planner, the Optimize plan gate. Trust: the executor hands the gate the text it showed (`trace_extra["findings_context"]`); the live gate folds its numbers into the persisted `context_numbers`, and `RunRecord.vouched_numbers` reads `findings_context` — a figure the platform put in front of the model is one the turn's inputs vouch for, in flight and post hoc. UI: `findings` is named and coloured in the context panel and the admin handler. **Gate:** `test_findings.py` (51: extractor, block, module, persistence over an isolated store, the two vouch readers, the delivery seams).

**The per-turn tool ledger** — `agent/turn_tool_ledger.py`, contextvar-scoped per turn (opened/closed in `execution_service` beside the loop guard), applied at the ReAct chokepoint `tool_enforcement._guarded` AFTER the SQL gate (a denied or blocked call is refused in the gate's own words, never "reused" or "disabled"), `TDA_*` exempt. *Reuse:* an identical (tool, arguments) call that already SUCCEEDED this turn hands back the first result, led by a note, without reaching the tool (signature = `assessors/tool_repetition.signature`, the loop guard's and the Scorecard's one definition); a write (by statement, else by tool name) invalidates every memoised read before it runs — count · insert · count sees the insert; a failed call is never reused; `TDA_TOOL_RESULT_REUSE=0` switches it off. *Breaker:* a tool whose EXECUTION fails N times in a row (raised and no deterministic retry recovered it, timed out, or a server error payload — a platform refusal never counts) is disabled for the rest of the turn with a recovery-shaped block (`tool_disabled_for_turn`: names the tool, says to answer with what it has); a success resets the streak; N = `APP_CONFIG.TOOL_BREAKER_FAILURES` / `TDA_TOOL_BREAKER_FAILURES`, default **4** (the dialect retries absorb the common one-shot SQL refusals), `0` = off. *Batched calls:* LangGraph's tool node already runs a reply's tool calls concurrently (`asyncio.gather`); pinned by a timing test inside a compiled graph. **Gate:** `test_tool_ledger.py` (51, incl. the real guarded coroutine: a reused call never reaches the tool, a failing tool is cut off after four, a refusal never counts).

**Two defects found on the way, fixed the same day.** (1) **Agent Memory never reached a model.** The `user_memory` module assembled, measured and showed its `[Remembered about this user]` block in the snapshot, but no engine or builder read `contributions["user_memory"]`. Now the executor caches it (`_cw_memory_text`, `_get_memory_context()`) and ONE reader, `executor._session_context_blocks()` (memory first, then findings), is what every engine appends after its KG enrichment — Ideate, Focus, ReAct, the strategic planner, the Optimize plan gate; the Coordinate engine hands the block to the coordinator after its own assembly (`coordinator.memory_context`) and `GenieCoordinator.execute` puts it on the prompt once, before the KG enrichment (its experts recall through their own engines). (2) **Four readers of the execution trace read a phantom key.** The trace entry is `{action, result}` (the executor's `turn_action_history`), but the `workflow_history` and `plan_hydration` context modules and the session store's turn ingestion read `phase["tool_output_summary"]`, which no producer writes — every phase read `unknown (0 rows)` and the module's hydration never fired (the planner's own pass had been fixed in place earlier, with a note). ONE reader now: `core/trace_shape.py` (`phase_output · phase_action · phase_rows`, with the legacy nested/top-level fallback kept), used by the planner, both modules and the ingestion; the hydration readers skip `TDA_*` entries (the agent's own logging carries no data). **Gate:** `test_cw_delivery_defects.py` (30, in the battery: the reader over real and legacy shapes, the two modules on a real trace, the ingestion, the memory delivery on every engine and the coordinator). Regression-clean across the eval suite (deterministic 65 · runner 15 · reliability 80 · judges 92 · cli_rest 33 · online 126), memory 86, fusion_structural 122, grounding 184.

**Regression-clean:** react_tool_bound 33 · loop_guard 22 · mcp_raised_tool_error 24 · grounding 184 · document_context 33 · strategic_history_source 14 · turn_siblings 67 · honesty_gate 249 · eval_deterministic 65 · focus_attachments 60 · leaked_sql_recovery 42 · turn_served_model 15 · fusion_structural 122 · input_requests 223 · assurance_points 509 · turn_failure 38. **Server restart** (backend). ## Nov 2026 — A cached embedding model loads without asking the hub

**Report (prod boot, 2026-11-03):** the log filled with `HTTP Error 503 thrown while requesting HEAD https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2/…` and `Retrying in 8s [Retry 5/5]` — huggingface.co was down for hours — and the container took 136 s to serve. Every client-side embedder is a SentenceTransformer behind ChromaDB's wrapper, which asks the hub whether each model file is still current on EVERY process start, even for a model fully on disk; with the hub unreachable the client retries five times per file with exponential backoff before falling back to the cache.

**What:** ONE rule in `core/embedding_cache.py`: a model whose snapshot is in the local cache (`config.json` + `modules.json` present as real files — a partial download never loads offline) is constructed with `local_files_only=True` (no network at all); an uncached model downloads as before. Decided per model from the cache's own state at load time — never a process-wide switch (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE` would also refuse the FIRST download of a model a user configures later; the `--offline` launch flag still exists for air-gapped hosts and, when set, rules). Every construction site goes through `sentence_transformer_embedding_function` (rag_retriever ×2, collection_utils, repository_constructor, embedding_providers); the gate pins that no site bypasses it.

**Measured:** the local boot serves without a single hub request while huggingface.co still answers 503. **Gate:** new `test_embedding_offline.py` (18, in the battery). **Server restart** (pending on prod — not restarted mid data load, per the user).

## Nov 2026 — Planner Health: the planner repository's twin of Corpus Health

**Report (prod, 2026-11-03):** re-signing @PXPRODO for the demo account failed with *planner "Default Collection - Teradata MCP - policing_estate_agent" is not signable: champion cases contain unsafe SQL / injection (stacked-statement)* — and nothing in the UI could say WHICH of the 11 learned cases, nor remove it. The gate merged every case's scan into one label list, and the only curation primitive was a `DELETE …/rows/<case>` route no screen called (the operator replayed the scanner by hand against the rows endpoint to find the case: a learned champion whose SQL was two statements, answering a per-robbery question with two unrelated totals — wrong on its own terms, and replayed verbatim on every hit).

**What:** a champion case is replayed verbatim on a retrieval hit, so the planner gate is where a poisoned or wrong case is stopped — and now it names the case and offers the act. (1) **Per-case findings at the root** — `validators.planner_case_findings` is the ONE per-case reading (case id, question, labels, the argument and an excerpt of the text that tripped the scanner, acknowledged-or-not); `planner_validator` is built on it: the verdict names the cases ("— 1 case: “How many exhibits…” — remove each case or acknowledge its finding with a reason under Planner Health") and carries `detail.findings`. (2) **Acknowledge, like a document's** — `acknowledge_planner_finding` stamps the owner's judgement ON the case (`trust_ack`: labels · reason · by · at; `retriever.stamp_case` writes the vector store AND the on-disk mirror the gate reads), so it enters every hash formula: the signature reads changed until re-signed and the re-signed signature carries the judgement; the labels are the boundary (a later, different finding re-opens the case); an acknowledged case is signable at band `partial`, never clean. (3) **The finding reaches the blocker** — the planner ingredient computes `planner_finding_summary` from the cases already in hand (a regex pass, no I/O) and `IngredientRef.finding` → `AgentTrust.to_dict().blocking[].finding` (outside the composition hash; absent when nothing to say — byte-identical otherwise), so the Trust Circle's SIGNED evidence reads *planner "…": 1 case not signable — "How many exhibits…" (stacked-statement) · remove the case or acknowledge its finding under Planner Health*, and the blocker route says Planner Health for a planner, Corpus Health for a corpus. (4) **The panel** — `handlers/plannerHealth.js` in the repository inspect view (planner repositories only, same place and grammar as Corpus Health): chips (`N cases scanned` · `N cases block sign-off` / `no open findings` · acknowledged · noted), the gate's own verdict quoted, each flagged case with its excerpt and three acts — **Show** (select the row), **Acknowledge** (themed prompt, reason required), **Remove** (themed confirm; the existing delete). No Quarantine: a champion case has no kept-but-excluded state worth having. (5) **Live everywhere** — both acts are recorded trust events (`planner_case_removed` · `planner_finding_ack`, SIGNED-station, labelled in the inbox) and broadcast; the panel follows a write made elsewhere through `uderia:trust-event` scoped to the inspected collection, the rows table re-reads, the Trust Circle re-fetches. (6) **Routes** — `GET /v1/rag/collections/<id>/scan-manifest` (the gate's own reading over the on-disk cases; owner-only) and `POST …/rows/<case_id>/acknowledge-finding` (409 with nothing open), ONE ownership rule (`_owned_planner`) shared with the delete.

**Found on the way — fixed at the root:** a learned case is stored in the vector store as `case_<id>` but a template-populated seed under its bare `<id>` (`rag_template_generator`), and `delete_case` assumed the prefix — it could not remove a seeded case at all. One resolver (`RAGRetriever._stored_case_id`) now serves delete and stamp; the mirror file is always `case_<id>.json` (what the gate reads).

**Measured:** the admin's real learned planner (263 cases) scans clean — no false positives on a live repository. **Rehearsed** headless (Playwright, `modern` + `light`): panel → Trust Circle evidence → Acknowledge (gate partial, blocker's finding gone) → Remove (store − 1, rows re-read, manifest 2 · 0 open · 1 noted, both acts in the inbox); zero console errors.

**Gates:** new `test_planner_health.py` (78) + `test_planner_health.mjs` (48), both in the battery; `test_trust_membrane` 244 unchanged; pins cascaded (`ui.js` 1.284 → root). **Server restart.** Files: `core/trust/{validators,attestation,composition}.py`, `agent/rag_retriever.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `static/js/handlers/{plannerHealth,agentPerformanceHandler}.js`, `static/js/ui.js`, `templates/index.html`, `docs/RestAPI/restAPI.md`.

## Nov 2026 — One vocabulary for components: Auto, active, and the one creation exception

**What:** the three words (available · enabled · active) now mean the same on components as on skills, and "Auto" is one mark. (1) **Auto on components** — an agent that stores no `componentConfig[id].enabled` follows the manifest's class default and the Capabilities row reads **Auto**; a hand on the switch (toggle, intensity) owns it and the entry is written; *Reset to default* hands it back; a save never strips a stored switch (a no-op save keeps a signed agent's hash). The editor fetches the components scoped to the agent's class, so an existing agent's Auto row shows the pure manifest default (`manifest_default`, new on `GET /v1/components?profile_type=`) and a new agent's the creation default — written only where it differs from the class default. (3) **The creation exception stays, named** — `on_for_new_agents: false` (the Database Navigator alone) is the one signature-preserving way to move a default for new agents without writing a switch onto signed agents; the card now says so (*New agents: start without it — existing agents keep it*). The component card's "Always enabled" for system components is gone (Needs Input can be switched off per agent); every card shows the one creation-default toggle, *On for my new agents*.

## Nov 2026 (v1.27) — Release

**153 commits since v1.26 (25 Oct – 2 Nov 2026).** Headlines:

- **Needs input (PROP-011)** — a turn that cannot go on without a person stops and asks instead of guessing: ONE interrupted state (`input_required` · `auth_required`, never terminal — every poller asks `core/turn_states.is_settled`), ONE record with a single-use signed resume binding, ONE ledger whose guarantees hold at the tool chokepoints, the plan loop and the gate seams; the platform's resolvers raise `choose` where two of the user's things share a name; the model's act on three carriers (`TDA_AskUser`, the planner's `plan_type: input_required`, `ASK_USER:` / the `uderia-ask` block) — taught by prompt text that exists only while the component is in use (`{needs_input_carrier}`); chains relay a child's question up and the answer down; a scheduled run waits, tells its channel, resumes, expires `unanswered`; a flow pauses at the node that asked; an unconnected connector is `auth_required`; MCP elicitation both ways; remembered answers per session or agent; the `needs_input` system component (the card under the answer, the composer rule, the split panel, the Inbox, *Waiting for you*); the assurance point at REVIEWED owning `guessed_past_ambiguity`; `authorityConfig.inputPolicy` in the agent editor. Measured live on every face (fire drill + probe 31/31, browser pass 17/17); on a weak model the decision to ask is the prompt's hypothesis — the platform held every time.
- **Agents can use Uderia itself** — every REST route describes itself (`@operation`: effect · scope · tier, one policy, a gate with a shrinking backlog); `TDA_Platform` finds and calls operations as the user with a one-request token; use cases in the `platform-playbooks` progressive skill; **Platform roles** declared by the component and signed by what they grant — Guide, Agent Builder (every class), Knowledge Curator, Automation Builder, Quality Analyst, Insight Builder, Publisher, Admin Monitor, Problem Solver — chosen in the editor with the write mode (off · review · allow; `governs` writes and every DELETE parked for a person; approval runs as the owner); **agents can ask other agents** where an administrator allows it; knowledge graphs for agents with ownership closed on fifteen routes; the platform counts for the model; an unreachable data source is named as such.
- **The two live campaigns** — the trust campaign on every engine class (five agents, invariants I1–I10, a coverage gate, a baseline) and the Optimize campaign (levers as agents, a database oracle, the lane's machinery as a coverage registry, a weak model as the stress test) — and what they fixed: a fire-drill switch for provider failures, an honest failed turn with a red JUDGED, coordinator figures observed in flight, two rewrite passes (`placeholder_sql`, `database_before_sql`), each Optimize agent learning into its own planner repository, binding scope and signed-seed replay, the 8888 upgrade's blind spots, planner retries that stop resending the catalog, the strategic planner seeing earlier turns again, ONE history builder for every engine, ONE prompt-cache plan for every provider, judge spend per judge model, a price for every model in use, a hard cost cap.
- **Hardening** — four routes that answered without a token closed; `POST /v1/configure` requires a user; the "all users" session list no longer unscopes the process; the repository's licence and a deployment's own are separate files and a renewed licence keeps the prompts (`prompt_rekey`); an unreadable database is announced and backed up daily; a NULL failed-login counter no longer breaks a login; finished task records expire; CORS configurable; the server stops promptly with tabs open.
- **UI** — iPad: the shell follows the visible area on every change, the keyboard closing brings the page back, 16px fields, the conversation never cut; the status strip and header read quietly (Ready · Working · Reconnecting · Offline; *Waiting for you*); the governed tool surface widened (meaning ranker, full descriptions, the finder as the surface's search); component signals (one page bus, one change event, a results ledger; own-or-elsewhere editing); the conversation header's own New-session; the Guide's trailing trust state; JUDGED's members on reloaded turns; a red turn renders on the scorecard.

**Deploy:** `pyproject` 1.27.0 · compose `uderia-v1-27` + build-arg default `v1.27` · annotated tag `v1.27`. ## Nov 2026 — Needs input: the prompt carriers are variables — nothing of the act where it cannot be taken

**What:** the four carrier texts that teach the model's act (the `uderia-ask` block for Ideate and Focus, the planner's Directive 2a `plan_type: input_required`, the self-correction's `ASK_USER:` format) were static prompt text, so every agent paid for them whether or not the `needs_input` component was in use, and the component toggle governed only the faces. Now each prompt carries `{needs_input_carrier}`; the text lives in `input_requests.CARRIERS` and is substituted per turn by the rendering engine (`carrier_section`), empty whenever the model may not ask — component off for the agent, policy `never`, no ledger. `policy_for` reads the component chain (`component_enabled`): off ⇒ `interactive never · raisers observe`, `TDA_AskUser` not offered, an ambiguity recorded, never raised — the toggle governs prompt, tool and posture as one rule. The planner lists the carrier among its stable keys (the cache prefix keeps it). The *when-to-ask* rule in the two conversation prompts stays general wording — it holds without the component, where asking is asking in prose.
