## Nov 2026 — Needs input: the fire drill and the live probe — every face provoked on demand

**What (2026-11-02):** a weak model does not take the act, so the machinery around a question could not be provoked live. `agent/needs_input_drill.py` (the provider fire drill's idiom; `TDA_NEEDS_INPUT_INJECT=1`, off by default) raises a marked input's question in code on any engine, and `test/needs_input_live_probe.py` drives every face through the real server: the answer route and the re-entry record (A), a decline (B), a remembered answer (C), `auth_required` (D), a held elicitation (E), the coordinator and a relayed expert question (F), a scheduled run waiting → webhook → resumed → expired unanswered (G), a flow paused at the node that asked and resumed there (H).
- **Measured:** 31 of 31 checks on Nova 2 Lite, $0.18. The first run's one miss was the probe's: the relayed question was the Focus expert's OWN `TDA_AskUser` call (the model's act, observed live under a coordinator), and the probe answered with a value outside its options — refused by the validator, correctly. Answered from the options, the chain carries the answer down (two relays on that run).
- **Found and fixed:** the expiry job closed a run whose turn was still running, and the turn overwrote it — the job closes only a run that is waiting; a turn finishing on an expired question records `unanswered`. The drill takes the resolver's remembered-answer step first (the first probe run showed C failing for that reason alone).

**The browser pass** (`test/needs_input_browser_pass.py`, Playwright on the installed Chrome, drill on): sign in → a marked question → the card under the answer → the answer on the card → the re-entry → the split panel → the agent editor's new **Needs input** section (Authority card: in a conversation · unattended · the platform's own questions · questions per turn · standing answers — `authorityConfig.inputPolicy`, every runtime value listed, owned by the editor only when rendered, written only where it differs from the defaults). 17/17. It found two defects no gate had:
- **Reload rendered settled questions as pending** — a turn record carries the question as raised; three answered questions came back pending, the composer bound itself to one, the next message was refused as *already accepted*. The session load now serves `input_requests` (every question of the conversation, live, by id) and the reload merges it; a snapshot alone never renders pending.
- **The stream showed no card** — the finish seam raises the `input_required` notice after the final answer was forwarded, so the final-answer event has no `input_request`; the card now rides the notice, session-guarded.

**Gates:** `test_input_requests.py` 215 (§14 the drill), `test_needs_input_ui.mjs` 49 (reload merge, stream notice, the editor's allowed sets); the probe and the pass are live tools, not battery suites. **Server restart.** Contract: [NEEDS_INPUT_ARCHITECTURE.md §7c](Architecture/NEEDS_INPUT_ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Nov 2026 — Needs input (PROP-011, phases 3–4): chains, unattended runs, auth, elicitation, remembered answers; the point and the measure

**What (2026-11-02):**
- **Chains relay; they do not answer.** An agent asked by another (`TDA_Platform` `ask`) or an expert a coordinator drives may stop to ask; its question becomes the parent turn's question verbatim (`raised_by: child`, `parent_id`, the chain on the record) and the parent model is told to relay. On the parent's re-entry the ask that relayed resumes the CHILD in-process with the person's answer (`input_resume.resume_child`; the accept had written it onto the child's record as a relay) — never a fresh question to the child. An asked child runs under origin `ask`.
- **Unattended runs wait.** A scheduled run whose turn stopped to ask records `input_required`, tells the person through the task's own channel (*— needs your input*, with a link) and the Inbox, and continues through the scheduler when answered (`resume_task_run`, same session, delivered as any run); the hourly `platform-input-expiry` job ends an expired run `unanswered` and says so through the same channel. A flow node whose turn stopped to ask pauses the run `input_required` (`FlowNeedsInput`; node run recorded with its task and session) and the answer resumes the flow from that node (`resume_flow_for_input`, the re-entry under the engine's internal token). Jobs panel colours for `input_required` (waiting for you, posture colour) and `unanswered`.
- **`auth_required`.** A user connector not connected for the person used to answer "not connected" inside a `status: success` envelope; the turn now stops with an `auth` question whose only answer is the Connect button — the platform's own OAuth popup; connected, the request continues.
- **A data source asks.** Every MCP data-source client carries an elicitation callback (`core/mcp_elicitation.py`): `elicitation/create` becomes a question (`raised_by: data_source`), held open a bounded time, else `cancel` — the turn ends asking and the re-entry accepts at once (the retry pattern). `ask_profile` on the Uderia MCP server reports a question as `[Needs input ir-…]` and takes `answer_to`/`answer`.
- **Remembered answers** (decision 10): *just this once · the rest of the session · always for this agent* on a single choose/confirm; a remembered answer resolves the ambiguity in code or hands the model the earlier answer, recorded on the turn (`input_defaults_used`); the agent default is `inputPolicy.defaults` (the owner's), the session default lives on the session.
- **Phase 4.** `needs_input` is a registered assurance point at REVIEWED (two members now — human review, needs input — the worst of them); it owns **`guessed_past_ambiguity`** (THE_RUN, non-gating: fails a turn that carried on past a code-detected ambiguity, passes one that stopped, abstains when code saw nothing). The scoreboard readings (`GET /v1/input-requests/stats`) show in the Needs Input panel. Campaign family N targets the point on every engine; the coverage gate holds it.

## Nov 2026 — Needs input (PROP-011, phase 1): a turn that stops to ask

**What (2026-11-02):** an agent that cannot go on without something only a person can give — a choice between two things with the same name, a value nobody recorded, a confirmation — could only guess or give up: a turn ended `complete` or `failed`, and nothing could tell a guess from an answer. Now the turn **stops**, the person is **asked** through the channel the turn came from, and their answer **resumes** the work, recorded as theirs.
- **One state.** `input_required` is *interrupted*, not terminal (A2A's split). `core/turn_states.py` is the one rule (`is_settled · is_terminal · is_interrupted · is_failure`); the fourteen readers that held their own tuple of terminal strings (`mcp_server/client`, `platform_asking`, the flow node, the eval pollers and scorers, the coordinator's poll, the task pruner, …) ask it instead — a poller waiting on "terminal" alone would have waited forever on a question. The gate greps for a list that comes back.
- **One record, one binding.** `input_requests` (`schema/46`): who asked, on what grounds, 1–4 items, the state, who answered and how. The resume binding is a signed ticket (principal, session, turn, the question's digest, expiry) consumed **once** by a guarded status flip — another person's, another request's, an expired, a changed or a second presentation is refused.
- **One ledger, enforced at the chokepoints.** `agent/input_requests.py` (contextvar-scoped like the loop guard): after a question is raised no tool runs — `sql_gate_before`, the component dispatch (ReAct) and the adapter (Optimize) refuse with a recovery-shaped result; the Optimize plan **ends** at the question instead of refusing phase by phase (a refused tool result is what fires self-correction); the grounding and honesty gates abstain (a question is not a claim; enforce must not replace it); the question reaches the person verbatim (appended to the text, the HTML, the record and the LLM-facing history); the turn's record, the task and the stream read `input_required` from ONE place in `execution_service` — no engine edited.
- **Code raises first.** `_resolve_owned` / `resolve_agent` / `platform_profile_shape._pick`: two of the user's things by one name are a *question*, never "no such thing" (it was reported as absence; the first was taken silently when building an agent). The raiser's posture is the agent's authority — `authorityConfig.inputPolicy` (`interactive: ask · never`, `raisers: enforce · observe`, `maxPerTurn`; `ask → never` and `enforce → observe` are downgrades) with a deployment floor (`INPUT_RAISERS_FLOOR`). `observe` records the ambiguity on the turn and lets the step fail honestly — what the `guessed_past_ambiguity` measure (phase 4) reads. `never` is terminal: the question is recorded and closed by policy, the turn completes with an honest sentence.
- **Re-entry.** The answer starts the next turn bound to the question: the structured block is the model's input, the person's line is what they see, and the resolver that asked receives the chosen id **in code**. A REST question continues under the same task id. The composer rule: typed text that matches an option (value or label) or that a `provide`/*Other* question allows IS the answer; anything else is a new prompt and the question is superseded, said so.
- **The surface is a system component.** `needs_input` (`component_type: system`, `category: System`, `instances: agent`): the card under the answer (live, REST-completed, reloaded — pending answerable, closed with its outcome), the composer rule, a split panel of this agent's questions (waiting for you · asked and answered; the header counts pending across every agent, *All agents* widens), the Workspace section, the Inbox's pending questions (a pass chip, *N waiting for you*, in the badge). The status strip reads **Waiting for you** as a quiet reading, never amber. Disabling the component removes the surface, never the state.
- **REST:** `GET /v1/input-requests[/<id>]`, `POST /v1/input-requests/<id>/answer | /withdraw`, `POST /v1/tasks/<id>/input` (A2A-shaped) — answering is `human_only`; a client declares `X-Uderia-Accepts: input_required` to receive the state, every other client sees `complete` + `input_required: true` (no regression for n8n/Airflow pollers).

**Not in this phase (designed, PROP-011):** the model's own act on its three carriers and the prompt release (phase 2), unattended runs waiting through the Inbox, chains relaying, MCP elicitation, `auth_required` (phase 3), the measure and the registered assurance point (phase 4). An interrupted child agent or flow node today answers with its question / fails honestly naming it.

**Gates:** new `test_input_requests.py` (131) and `test_needs_input_ui.mjs` (33), both in the battery; `test_component_bus/signals/instances` hold the manifest; `test_rest_task_outcome` pins the outcome rule's new parameter; the platform-operations catalog regenerated. **Server restart.** Contract: [NEEDS_INPUT_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/NEEDS_INPUT_ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Nov 2026 — The server stops promptly with browser tabs open

**What (2026-11-01):** every restart with a browser tab open hung until it was forced (`kill -9`). ## Nov 2026 — Platform writes: approved by a person, run as the owner

**What (2026-11-01):** phase 3 of TDA_Platform. A write is offered only when the agent's **role** allows the `write` effect and names the operation, and its **write mode** permits it — `authorityConfig.platformSurface.writes`: `off` (default) · `review` · `allow` (authority: portable, unsigned, downgrade-guarded `off < review < allow`). Under `review` the exact request (operation, bound arguments, agent, conversation) is parked in the review queue as `source="platform"` with a live notice to the owner; the agent is told it has NOT run. ## Oct 2026 — Whenever the keyboard closes, the page comes back down (Chrome on iPad, every screen)

**What (2026-10-31):** in Chrome on iPad (a WKWebView) the page was left moved up after the keyboard closed — in the conversation and wherever else a keyboard appeared. Three causes:

- **One put-back per event, inside the animation.** `appViewport.js` put the page back once per event, on the next frame — inside the keyboard's ~300–500 ms closing animation, where WebKit overrides a programmatic scroll; Chrome then restores its own scroll late or not at all, and no further event came (the keyboard's own hide key does not even blur the field). Every viewport event (resize, scroll, focusin/focusout, orientation) now starts a short series of re-applies (60 · 180 · 400 · 750 · 1200 ms, restarted by the next event) and a touch re-checks; a re-apply writes nothing when nothing changed, so the series never loops.
- **Modals.** An overlay is fixed to the window, not to the shell, so a field in its lower half is above the keyboard only while the browser keeps its pan; putting that pan back hid the field being typed into (and the series would have fought harder). While the focused field sits on a fixed overlay below the visible area the pan is kept; once the keyboard closes it fits and the pan is put back like any other.
- **The sign-in pages were never the shell.** `login.html` / `register.html` load `main.css` but their own `<style>` made the body `position: relative` with `min-height: 100vh`, and they did not load `appViewport.js` — nothing followed the keyboard or put the pan back. `body.auth-page` is the fixed shell again, follows the keyboard, scrolls inside itself (a covered field is revealed; register in landscape, 862 px tall, is no longer cut at the bottom), centres with auto margins, and its two decorative glows are fixed (as absolute boxes one gave the scrolling page 246 px of empty room).

**Verified:** WebKit (iPad emulation): login/register through keyboard-up (360 px landscape, 800 px portrait — the last field just above the keyboard) and closed (layout and window scroll back to 0); the app probe's keyboard-up shells unchanged.

**Gates:** `test_app_shell.mjs` (43 → 54: a stubbed WKWebView that overrides the put-back mid-animation and fires nothing after the close — fails on the previous script; a modal field keeps the pan until the keyboard closes; the auth pages). Pins: `appViewport.js 1.4` (index, login, register) · `main.css 5.20`. **Server restart** (templates).

## Oct 2026 — The iPad conversation is never cut: right, bottom or top

**What (2026-10-31):** measured, not guessed — the real app laid out in WebKit with iPad mobile emulation (1180×820, 820×1180, 768×1024, Split View 590/375, Slide Over 320; keyboard-up shells 420/360/300 px), over 400 stored sessions. Five independent causes, each fixed at its root:

- **Right — a wide answer table.** `.ans-tw-prose` (the prose grid's wrap) was `overflow: visible` and handed scrolling to the table (`display: block`), but the id-selector rule `#chat-log .message-content table.ans-t { display: table }` won — nothing scrolled, and a 2,100 px grid pushed the message past the right edge (the chat became a sideways scroller a diagonal swipe slid). The wrap now scrolls sideways itself (`answer.css`).
- **Right — the chat log took its content's width.** `#chat-container` is a flex column; `mx-auto` on `#chat-log` turns cross-axis stretching off, so the log sized to its content, whose floor (a Sources fold) was ~670 px: below ~700 px (Split View, portrait with a side panel) the conversation was cut. `#chat-log { width: 100% }` (`polish.css`); a long token breaks across the whole bubble (`overflow-wrap: anywhere` — inline code chips were `nowrap`, one inline statement 402 px); the acts strip wraps and never shrinks a control (the vote group clipped its buttons). `#chat-container` never scrolls sideways (`overflow-x: hidden`, and an offset set from code is put back).
- **Bottom — the composer was pushed out.** With the keyboard up in landscape (~350 px shown) the field's `40vh` cap (on iOS the LARGEST viewport) let it grow to 312 px and an open resource panel kept its 148 px: the composer ended 265 px below the shell. The field now grows only into the room the conversation can give up (`ui.js composerRoom`, measured: everything in the column but the chat does not yield), the column's minimum is published (`--column-min` = the composer + 72 px of chat, never more than the room) and the resource panel yields (`#tool-header` `flex-shrink: 1`, its drawer scrolls); re-fitted by ResizeObservers, since the iOS keyboard fires no window resize.
- **Right — a bare grid in an evidence row.** The compute component's row-op table was emitted without the `.ans-tw` scroll wrap every other grid has, and the evidence fold (`details.ans-ev`, `overflow: hidden`) clipped it at phone widths (+96 px). It is wrapped now (`compute/handler.py`); a stored bare one scrolls itself (`answer.css`).
- **Top — the shell could be scrolled.** `overflow: hidden` is still a scroll container: iOS scrolls it to reveal a focused field and `scrollIntoView()` scrolls it from code, and `window.scrollTo(0, 0)` only puts the document back. `<body>`, the tool header and a collapsed side panel are `overflow: clip` (hidden kept as the pre-Safari-16 fallback); a Live Status step scrolled into view while the panel was shut had moved its content 310 px.

**Verified:** `test/ipad_layout_probe.py` (new, live: needs a server and `playwright install webkit`) — 400/400 sessions fit at every width (1180, 820, 768, 590, 375, 320); at every keyboard-up height the composer ends at the shell's bottom, the top bar at 0, no shell box scrolled, and Live Status opens unshifted after steps were scrolled into view while it was shut.

**Gates:** `test_app_shell.mjs` (28 → 43). Pins: `main.css 5.19` (index, login, register) · `polish.css 2.6` · `answer.css 2.10` · `ui.js 1.270` repo-wide · `main.js 10.120`. **Server restart** (template).

## Oct 2026 — The repository's licence and a deployment's own licence are separate files

**What (2026-10-30):** `tda_keys/license.key` is tracked in git, and production held its own Enterprise licence in that same path behind `git update-index --skip-worktree` — so the repository's licence could never be renewed in git: a commit changing it makes prod's `git pull` fail. `core/license_file.license_path` is now the one rule every licence reader uses (the startup check, the prompt key derivation, the bootstrap encryption, the re-key's previous-licence fallback, the licence repo's `update_prompt.py`): `TDA_LICENSE_FILE` → `tda_keys/license.local.key` (a deployment's own licence, gitignored) → `tda_keys/license.key` (the repository's). The repository's licence is renewed to 2027-10-30 and committed with the replaced one as `license.key.previous`, so a checkout that pulls code and licence together re-keys its prompts on the first start. `generate_license.py --local` writes a deployment's `license.local.key`.

**Production, once:** move the Enterprise licence to `tda_keys/license.local.key`, clear the skip-worktree flag and restore the tracked file BEFORE pulling — after that a pull never touches prod's licence.

**Gates:** `test_license_rekey.py` +6 (31).

## Oct 2026 — A renewed licence keeps the prompts

**What (2026-10-30):** the key that encrypts every stored prompt is derived from the licence SIGNATURE and tier (`prompt_encryption.derive_tier_key`), and a renewal always changes the signature — yet prompts were encrypted with the running licence's key only when the database was first created. A renewal therefore left every prompt under the old key: the loader logged `invalid key` and served placeholder text instead of the system prompts. `agent/prompt_rekey.rekey_if_license_changed` runs where `PromptLoader` derives its key, before any prompt is read: it records which licence keys the stored prompts (`prompt_key_license`: signature + tier, recorded only when that licence actually opens them) and, when the running licence differs, re-keys every encrypted row of `prompts`, `prompt_versions` and `prompt_overrides` in ONE transaction, with `create_prompt_version_on_update` suspended and recreated from its own SQL (no fake history rows, no version bump). Without a record it tries `tda_keys/license.key.previous`; a row neither key opens is left byte-identical and counted; a failure rolls back. The licence repo's `generate_license.py` gains `--holder/--tier/--days` and `--renew` (copies holder, tier and extra fields; keeps the replaced licence as `license.key.previous`).

**Applied locally the same day:** the repo licence (App Developer, expiring 2026-11-10) renewed to 2027-10-30; on restart 20 rows re-keyed, all 15 prompts identical, history 35 rows unchanged (30 history rows were already unreadable under the old licence and were left as they were).

**Gates:** new `test_license_rekey.py` (25, in the battery).

## Oct 2026 — Four routes that answered without a token are closed; two scheduler no-ops and a hidden honesty rewrite fixed

**What (documentation audit, 2026-10-30):** diffing every route against its auth decorators found four holes. `GET /api_key/<provider>` returned the server's environment LLM keys (Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Bedrock, Friendli) to any caller — now signed in AND admin; the provider form treats the 403 as nothing to pre-fill. `GET /api/notifications/subscribe` trusted a `user_uuid` query parameter, so anyone holding a user's id could read that user's notification stream — the user now comes from a one-minute signed ticket (`POST /api/notifications/ticket`, issued only with the bearer token because `EventSource` cannot send one; the ticket carries no `user_id` claim, so it is never a bearer, and a session token is never a ticket; a reconnect fetches a fresh one). `POST /v1/admin/session-stores/cleanup-orphans` had no admin check and judged orphans against the CALLER's sessions (without a token, every external session store) — now admin only, judged over every user's sessions, nothing deleted when the session index is unreadable. `POST /v1/rag/collections/<id>/refresh` had no auth — now the collection's owner or an admin, and the repository card sends its token.

**Scheduler:** `interval:1d` was advertised (tool instructions, scheduler-expert) and previewed but the engine's `_parse_interval` had no `d` unit — such a task never fired. The manifest told the LLM `output_config` `{to}` / `{url, token}` and the Jobs form saved a webhook as `{url}`, while delivery read only `to_address` / `webhook_url` / `bearer_token` — the task ran and delivered nothing. Delivery now normalises every spelling at its one seam (`task_scheduler._delivery_config`, which also heals stored tasks) and the writers use the canonical names.

**Honesty gate (RAG branch):** `run_honesty_rag` returned its event without the `_acted` stamp every other branch adds; Ideate and Focus render the replacement and draw the live card only for an acted event, so under enforce the stored text was the honest replacement while the user SAW the original answer. Now acted like the SQL branch (observe: card, answer untouched).

**Documentation:** every architecture doc verified against the code and corrected (counts: 19 rewrite passes, 25 assurance points, 62 scored dimensions, 7 marketplace types, 12 MCP-server tools, 808 REST routes); seven new architecture docs (LLM providers, tool surface, sessions, answer gates, agent memory, chart, EXPLAIN plan); the README index lists every architecture doc and links each from its feature section; the REST reference covers every route.

**Gates:** new `test_unauth_routes.py` (30) and `test_scheduler_delivery_contract.py` (24), both in the battery; `test_honesty_gate.py` +2 (246, both fail without the fix). JS pins cascaded (`api.js` 1.2, `notifications.js` 5.111, `main.js` 10.117, …).

## Oct 2026 — A control's Guide entry names its properties; the modules it consults fold apart

**What (operator question, 2026-10-30):** the Grounding gate's Guide entry read "READS · MODULES · 3" and listed three module names, skipping the level the architecture is built on: a mechanism is about PROPERTIES, and a module is only the code bound to a property per lane — swappable, possibly different per lane (`split`), possibly absent. The live dial already paired them (property · module); the Guide did not. Now a control's entry has a **`properties`** row where `reads` was (no S badge: the gate's module is its property's module by definition) (each chip opens the property's own entry, which names its module in each lane), and its modules move into their own fold, **modules during the turn**, placed just before *after the turn* and folded like it — each row a property beside the module bound to it during the turn, the mode on hover (can act on the answer · can only escalate to a judge), an unbound lane saying so. The fold holds only what THIS mechanism consults: `assurance_points.consulted_properties` (its `POINT_PROPERTIES` restricted by `INFLIGHT_CONSUMERS`, the declaration asserted against the call sites) is served as `consults` and is also what the dial's mark reads, so the two surfaces cannot disagree — the Honesty gate owns four properties and consults one in flight; Trusted scope owns `answer_scope` but the grounding gate consults it, so Trusted scope has no fold. A measure keeps its `reads` row (its module computes it). A property's entry keeps *after the turn* open (what grades it is half its entry) and S and M stay ONE link (operator, 2026-10-30): an S marks a chip that uses the module an M names, at both ends, on every row but a control's `properties` row (its fold pairs each property with its module). A property's module is where it is used — *modules during the turn* when the control consults it, *after the turn* above *graded by* when only a measure does — so every S has its M in the entry (a live sweep of all 63 rendered entries: 54 S badges, 0 without their M; before this, 6 on 5 mechanisms pointed at nothing). Hover lights the partner, or the header of the fold that hides it; a click on the S or M letter opens that fold and lights it. Opened for one agent, the *after the turn* summary reads "graded by 5 of 7" (the row's class-scoped label had made it fall back to "7 linked"). The member glyph (an orange ring segment on the members group, the colour rule and the dial's members header) is gone: it read as a loading spinner and wrapped onto its own line; "members · N" on both lines and the group's orange edge carry the link. The gate's description names both checks: "Checks the answer against the agent's sources or its declared scope, and withholds it or adds a note when it does not hold" (it named the scope family alone, wrong on every Focus agent).

**Gates:** `test_guide_anatomy.mjs` +11 (98), `test_assurance_points.py` +5 [P3] (507); `test_assurance_substrate` 223, `test_guide_parents` 56, `test_quality_card_partition` 296 unchanged. Verified against the live vocabulary. Pin: `qualityDimensions.js` 7.39.

**Files:** `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/assurance_points.py`, `static/js/handlers/qualityDimensions.js`, `templates/index.html`, `docs/manuals/TRUST_UX_FAQ.md` (+ render), `test/{test_guide_anatomy.mjs,test_assurance_points.py}`.

Live (`20261029-214313`): F1/F2 on every engine, 0 invariant failures, 0 expectation misses, $0.00.

## Oct 2026 — A turn the provider failed: an honest answer, a failed record, a red JUDGED (trust campaign C18)

**What:** when the campaign's provider account ran out of credits (HTTP 402) the ReAct executor delivered the provider's raw JSON as the answer, the coordinator did the same, Optimize ended the turn with no answer, and every assurance station read quiet. Decision: the failure is read at JUDGED (execution quality), never SIGNED (a provider that did not answer says nothing about the signature). `agent/turn_failure.answer` is the one sentence every engine's failure path delivers — the failure class (credits · auth · rate limit · overloaded · timeout · connection · oversized request · not found · rejected) and what to do, never `str(exc)`; the raw error stays on the record (`error`/`error_details`). `clean_termination` fails a turn the record calls failed (the ReAct engine adds `turn_complete` on the failure path too); `output_sanity` recognises a provider's raw error; a failed Optimize turn is dispatched for scoring, judges skipped for any failed turn; an empty account counts against the provider breaker (`resilience.out_of_credits` → `handler._record_terminal`: the health strip shows it, an open breaker routes to the signed fallback; `classify` unchanged, so a quota error stays retryable); I6 accepts the failure measured at JUDGED by those two measures only.

**Gates:** new `test_turn_failure.py` (27, in the battery; mutation-tested); `test_resilience_baseline` [4] and `test_turn_lineage_baseline` [5] restated to the property they protect; `test_trust_campaign_suite` 343. Live re-run pending: it needs a provider that fails.

**Files:** `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/{turn_failure.py (new),conversation_agent.py,genie_coordinator.py,execution_service.py}`, `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/engines/{conversation_engine.py,optimize_engine.py}`, `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/guardrails/primitives.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/eval/{online.py,scorers/reliability.py}`, `src/trusted_data_agent/llm/{resilience.py,handler.py}`, `docs/Architecture/AGENT_QUALITY_DIMENSIONS.md`, `test/{test_turn_failure.py (new),test_resilience_baseline.py,test_turn_lineage_baseline.py,trust_battery.sh}`, `test/trust_campaign/{suite.py,FINDINGS.md}`.

## Oct 2026 — A NULL failed-login counter no longer breaks a login; production's database restored after corruption

**What:** `auth/security.py` reads the failed-login count through one accessor (`failed_attempts`, NULL → 0): `check_progressive_delay` compared `None <= 1` and a failed attempt did `None += 1`, so any account whose row held NULL answered every password login with a 500. Gate: `test_login_null_counter.py` (in the battery).

**Incident (production, 2026-10-29):** the NULL came from a corrupted database, not from data. `tda_auth.db` went `database disk image is malformed` at 11:06:44 UTC, six minutes after the 11:00:02 upgrade backup; `quick_check` reported a broken b-tree page (`auth_tokens`, SQLITE_CORRUPT) and wrong entry counts on every `users` index, and the `users` table returned another table's rows (one of them, read through the `username` index, as an inactive "admin"). Restored from the clean 11:00 backup (`quick_check` ok, admin active); the corrupt file and its `-wal`/`-shm` are kept as `tda_auth.db*.corrupt-20261029-201653`; database changes between 11:00 UTC and 19:16 UTC are lost (session files are on disk and unaffected). **Cause — narrowed, not yet established (traced the same evening):** the file broke between 11:00:26 UTC (the app's start after a deploy; its `VACUUM INTO` upgrade backup at 11:00:02 is clean) and 11:05:00 UTC, when the hourly consumption job read `file is not a database`; `malformed` followed at 11:06:44. Ruled out: the size match with the September backups (withdrawn — the upgrade backups are `VACUUM INTO`, so smaller; the live file is never vacuumed and kept its original 1,133,346,816 bytes); another container (only `uderia-v1-26` mounts the database); platform code (nothing switches the journal mode, runs a plain `VACUUM` or replaces/copies the file; WAL + `synchronous=NORMAL` is safe across processes, so the one extra process in the window — an import check run with `docker exec` at 11:00:38 — cannot have done it alone); a user crontab or sync timer. **Open suspect:** a Samba user share `prod` exports the production checkout's parent directory — the live database's parent — with full control for `rgeissen` and read for everyone; a client touching a live SQLite file over SMB is a known corruption route. Not provable without root: the Samba logs, `journalctl -k` and SMART data are root-only.

**Files:** `src/trusted_data_agent/auth/security.py`, `test/{test_login_null_counter.py (new),trust_battery.sh}`.

## Oct 2026 — The prompt cache follows one plan for every provider

**What:** the provider prompt cache is driven by one rule set instead of per-provider branches ([PROMPT_CACHE_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/PROMPT_CACHE_ARCHITECTURE.md)): (1) the call site declares where its stable prefix ends (`cache_prefix=` on `_call_llm_and_update_tokens` / `call_llm_api`, forwarded by both signed fallbacks; the handler honours it only if it IS a prefix of the prompt); (2) `breakpoints` providers get that prefix as its own cached block beside the system and history breakpoints — Anthropic native, Claude via OpenRouter, and now Bedrock Claude (Anthropic body) and Bedrock Nova (`cachePoint`), which never cached before; (3) `automatic` providers get the agent's hashed affinity key in their own field — OpenAI/Azure `prompt_cache_key`, xAI `x-grok-conv-id` (xAI moves from `none` to `automatic`); (4) the reading: Bedrock usage is read as the TOTAL with its cache counts (the Claude stream keeps them from `message_start`), Nova writes are not surcharged. Refusals are learned (`_AFFINITY_REFUSED`, `_CACHE_POINT_REFUSED`), never a model list. The strategic planner declares its prefix from the template (`template_stable_prefix`: render with volatile values as a sentinel; a key not declared stable is volatile; the tool catalog is stable only when every enabled tool is shown). Master switch off ⇒ byte-identical requests.

**Measured (2026-10-29, the Optimize lane's captured strategic prompts, ~$0.15):** Claude Haiku 4.5 via OpenRouter cached **0** — the one breakpoint sat on a 2.5K system prompt under the model's 4,096-token minimum — and **9,269** per call with the stable-prefix breakpoint; xAI 128 → 8,320–8,960 with the conversation header; OpenAI and Gemini already cached ~8.2K (stable content was already first; Gemini best-effort). **OpenRouter's open models take NO key:** its `session_id` pinned the agent from the first request to an upstream that served 27 cached tokens over the replayed live sequence (twice), while the broker's own cache-aware stickiness reached one that served 6.9K — so the broker's routing is left alone. A live MiMo re-run of three cold cases confirmed the request carries the plan and read the same 10–12 cached tokens as before: on that model the cache is the upstream's.

**Found on the way (not fixed here):** on a governed (*Relevant per turn*) Optimize agent the strategic prompt's tool catalog rendered as `[]` in every captured turn — the planner saw prompts but no tools; the planner's parse-error / conversational re-plan retries send the full 24.6K master system prompt (with its own catalog) where the first attempt sends 2.3K; the tactical and self-correction templates lead with volatile content (a reorder in the license repo would cache ~6K / ~19K more).

**Gates:** new `test_prompt_cache_plan.py` (58, in the battery; mutation-tested — no affinity, no stable block, a governed catalog treated stable, a refusal not learned each fail it), `test_prompt_cache.py` (96; capability row and the hashed-prefix assertion restated), `test_prompt_cache_baseline.py` (10), `test_answer_stream.py` (Bedrock stream usage now carries the cache counts), `test_mlx_output_ceiling.py` (the stream and plain call share one keyword set).

**Files:** `src/trusted_data_agent/llm/{cache_policy.py,handler.py,streaming.py}`, `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/{executor.py,planner.py}`, `docs/Architecture/PROMPT_CACHE_ARCHITECTURE.md` (new), `test/{test_prompt_cache_plan.py (new),test_prompt_cache.py,test_answer_stream.py,test_mlx_output_ceiling.py,trust_battery.sh}`, `CLAUDE.md`.

## Oct 2026 — Each Optimize agent learns into its own planner repository

**What (Optimize campaign OC-F5, operator decision "option B"):** every successful Optimize turn used to land in the user's ONE default planner repository per MCP server, read back by every agent of that user on that server — one shared notebook, so an agent's plans changed because of other agents' turns, a signed agent's bound repository changed under it after every success, and no agent could be measured cold. Now a planner collection carrying an agent's id in the new column `collections.learning_profile_id` is that agent's learning repository (`core/agent_learning.py`, the one rule): new Optimize agents get one at creation (every creation path goes through `config_manager.add_profile[_locked]`); such an agent stores lessons only there — never the shared default, never the repository that guided the turn — and a LOCKED own repository is frozen; it reads its own repository beside what it binds and never takes the shared read-back; it is never a "default" (both default lookups skip it); it is not a binding, so its contents never enter the agent's signature (the Agent Memory treatment) and its learned cases are never replayed verbatim; removing the agent removes it (row, vectors, case files) through `remove_profile` and through the two bulk paths that bypass it, unsubscribe and unpublish (`agent_pack_routes.retire_learning_of_removed`). A login that creates a new default collection no longer binds it to such an agent, and the planner-binding heal drops rather than re-points its unreadable bindings. Existing agents keep the shared notebook until opted in: `GET/POST /v1/profiles/<id>/learning-repository`. The editor shows the own repository as a fixed *LEARNS HERE* row (never saved as a binding) and no longer force-binds the shared default for such an agent. The Optimize campaign's levers each get an own LOCKED repository, so a run never warms itself and the cold lever is finally cold.

**Verified:** `test_agent_learning.py` (35; mutation-tested: every guard removed fails it, incl. a real race on first creation), `test_agent_learning_editor.mjs` (10); live — campaign levers re-provisioned with no trust state moving, `@OCFL-NORAG` with 0 champions and 0 lessons stored; a new agent learns one turn into its own repository, retrieves it on a reworded question, stays signed, and takes the repository with it when deleted; `test/optimize_campaign/marketplace_learning_probe.py` (27): a pack never ships the repository, a subscriber and a forker each get their own empty one, the publisher's lessons stay invisible, a sync keeps the agent and its repository, a fork of a published learning repository is ordinary, unsubscribe/uninstall remove the consumer's repositories and never the publisher's. The probe found the unsubscribe/unpublish leak, fixed here.

**Files:** `src/trusted_data_agent/core/{agent_learning.py (new),collection_db.py,config_manager.py}`, `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/{rag_retriever.py,planner.py,engines/optimize_engine.py}`, `src/trusted_data_agent/api/{rest_routes.py,agent_pack_routes.py,auth_routes.py}`, `static/js/handlers/configurationHandler.js` (+ the repo-wide `?v=` pin cascade), `test/{test_agent_learning.py,test_agent_learning_editor.mjs}` (new, in the battery), `test/test_planner_subscription_keying.py` (K7 follows the reworded retrieval line), `test/optimize_campaign/{agents.py,marketplace_learning_probe.py (new),FINDINGS.md}`, `docs/RAG/RAG.md` ("Where an agent learns").

## Oct 2026 — The 8888 upgrade's two blind spots, and three weak-model failure shapes, fixed in the Optimize lane

**What (Optimize campaign OC-F13–OC-F17):** five defects, each pinned and re-run live on three levers.
**OC-F14** — a FastMCP 4 server RAISES a failed tool call; the database's message sat two TaskGroup groups down and both lanes kept the outer text ("unhandled errors in a TaskGroup"), so every correction strategy that reads the database's words (column/table/database not found, the DB time ceiling, the ReAct dialect retries 3706/3707, the multi-server router) went blind on 8888 from the 2026-10-28 cutover, and the generic correction (~17K tokens) re-proposed the identical SQL. `tool_enforcement.tool_error_text` reads the `McpError` leaves on both lanes (a raised failure now reads like an `isError` result; a client-side exception is unchanged), and a correction proposing the identical call that just failed is refused before it runs (`phase_executor._same_call_args`). This was the cause of the baseline's R-family token overruns and Nova's duplicate SQL. **OC-F17** — the same upgrade made `base_readQuery`'s `sql` optional in the schema, so a phase that left the SQL unwritten was FASTPATHed with `{}` and "No SQL provided" read as success (three wrong R3 answers); a tool whose schema takes `sql` is never FASTPATHed without a statement (`_takes_sql`), on the single-phase and the loop path — R5 is now answered with real statistics but costs a tactical call per column (proposal PASS-6: one statement over the numeric columns). **OC-F13** — MiMo copied the planning prompt's greeting example for data questions (3/10) and the greeting was the answer; the conversational shortcut is accepted only when the QUESTION is small talk (`conversational_guard.goal_is_small_talk`), otherwise the planner re-plans once through the same priced retry as a parse error (`Planner._screen_conversational`, `_strategic_retry`) — live 0 greetings in 38 data turns (7 re-plans, each right), the control "Hello" keeps its one-call shortcut 16/16. **OC-F15** — a report with no JSON is repeated once inside the tool with the format restated (both calls priced as the tool's one event), instead of a correction that invented the question as its input. **OC-F16** — a truncated plan ("[{") ended the turn before its parse retry ran; it now gets the retry (`planner.parse_plan_response`). OC-F6 closed as superseded by OC-F9 (follow-ups are at the two-call floor on MiMo).

## Oct 2026 — Spend is booked under the model that was called

**What:** judge calls were added into the scored turn's consumption row, so a Google or xAI judge's spend read as the turn model's (`consumption_turns` carried no judge model at all); each judge model is now its own `status: judge` line under its own provider/model and price (`ConsumptionManager.record_usage_line`, from the per-model `judge_usage_breakdown`), the user's aggregates growing exactly once and the activity chart counting turns only. A failed Ideate + tools turn now records the model that served it (its spend was booked to `Unknown/unknown`). Price coverage counts only rows that spent something and never the `flow/flow-run` placeholder of a flow's display-only summary turn, which carries no `cost_basis`.

## Oct 2026 — Two rewrite passes from the Optimize campaign's first proposals, calibrated offline before a live turn

**What:** `placeholder_sql` and `database_before_sql` (`planner.py`, both before `schema_before_sql`, both on one `_defer_sql_phase` helper that hands a statement to the tactical step with the draft kept for its intent — the shape the schema pass already produced). The second defers a SQL phase naming a database the turn has no reason to believe in: with a session catalog, one `preflight.catalog.nonexistent_db_refs` names; without one, a plan that SEARCHES an inventory and then writes SQL against an invented name — a direct statement with no search before it (E1), and any champion-guided plan, are left alone.

**Why, measured:** on the campaign's cold lane every data question failed the same way — the planner searched for the table, wrote SQL against a placeholder or an invented database, FASTPATH ran it verbatim, the database refused it, a 19K-token self-correction switched to a prompt, the answer was "unable". **Rung 1 of the ladder, at no cost:** `test/optimize_campaign/replay.py` runs a pass over every saved `raw_llm_plan` — `placeholder_sql` would defer 15 of 122 distinct plans (14 turns that ended wrong or declined, 27 self-corrections paid between them, 1 right anyway); `database_before_sql` 26 (24 wrong, 2 right anyway — a search followed by the REAL database, which costs them one tactical call). Pinned by `test_placeholder_sql_pass.py` (21) and `test_database_before_sql_pass.py` (13); the campaign's registry extracts both and coverage demands cases (A1, A2, A8, R4, the new E2c). Also recorded: plan hydration fires only when a plan opens with a loop over a prior-turn reference — a follow-up computed from the previous answer is proposal PASS-4 (OC-F6, the hardening skill's table corrected).

Also, plan-validation correction 3c: a planned tool the catalog does not have is renamed to the tool it meant (a component with an action suffix, a SELECT under an invented runner → the read tool, a near miss within difflib 0.8); 12 of 188 saved plans had paid 16 self-corrections for that repair (`test_unknown_tool_correction.py`). And the honesty gate's new kind `claimed_effect_after_denial` (the trust campaign's second control proposal, calibrated on 15 saved runs with no false positive before it was written): a write the answer reports as done after the agent's authority denied it (`test_honesty_claimed_effect.py`; `ui.js` 1.263).

## Oct 2026 — The Optimize campaign: the lane measured against a database oracle, on a weak model as the stress test

**What:** a second "spend what's left" skill (`.claude/skills/optimize-campaign/SKILL.md`, design `docs/roadmap/OPTIMIZE_CAMPAIGN.md`, harness `test/optimize_campaign/`) pointed at the Optimize lane: price, performance, efficiency, execution hardening. `registry.py` EXTRACTS the lane's machinery from the source — the 17 rewrite passes (`planner.py` `_pass("…")`), the safeguards and FASTPATH markers, the three orchestrators — and `coverage.py --strict` (in the battery via `test_optimize_campaign_suite.py`) fails when a case provokes none on a lever it applies to or no `UNPROVOKABLE` declaration explains why. `oracle.py` runs each case's `oracle_sql` through the campaign's own MCP entry before the turn, so correctness is the data's answer, never a human's; `suite.py` carries 24 cases (12 accuracy, 4 efficiency, 7 robustness, 1 multi-turn), waste detectors (a tactical call on a pre-known phase, a champion present but missed, an LLM paid for a tool the catalog never had) and invariants O1–O10 (a whole turn; no runaway correction or duplicate SQL; FASTPATH where the plan knew tool and args; numeric fidelity; `turn_cost` == Σ per-call; the family's token band; only registered passes fired; no hand-rolled loop; the oracle agrees or the answer honestly declines). `agents.py` provisions the levers — `@OCFL` (Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, a LOCKED champion repository seeded with every accuracy oracle, governed surface, a session primer naming the database), `@OCFL-NORAG` (an EMPTY locked repository — the cold lane), `@OCFL-ALL` (every tool offered), `@OCWEAK` (Nova 2 Lite, as OCFL) — on its own MCP entry; `run_campaign.py` runs levers in parallel, one session per case, the primer as turn 1 priced apart, and reports the frontier (correctness, cost per correct answer, p50 latency, LLM calls per case, waste) and the GAP per case (working − weak); the accept rule refuses a baseline when correctness drops or the harvest ledger is pending.

**Campaign 1 (FINDINGS.md):** cold, on the working model: 4/21 correct, $0.0215 per correct answer, 20 paid self-corrections — every data question failed the same way (a navigator search, SQL against `[FOUND_DATABASE].Customers` or `result_of_phase_2.table_name` or an invented `sales_db`, run verbatim, a 19K-token correction that switches to a prompt, "unable"); three pass proposals written from the evidence (a placeholder identifier in planned SQL, a component called as a SQL runner with an argument it lacks, a database the session never observed — `database_before_sql` by analogy with `schema_before_sql`). Warm, with the repository LOCKED: a seed asked word for word replays at 0 planner tokens (517 tokens, $0.0001 a case); a paraphrase of the same seed got no lift at all (the few-shot champion is ignored by the working model). Found on the way and recorded: `enforce_interactive` beside `autonomous: false` denies EVERY tool — the trust campaign's write-escape "refusal" of the same day was a blanket denial, its record corrected and the re-run owed on `autonomous: true` (OC-F2); signing a planner repository does not lock it, and only a locked one replays (OC-F3); `ragCollections: []` reads as "every planner repository the user owns", so an agent shown with no repository replayed the operator's own champions while its trust composition listed none (OC-F4); a successful turn is learned into the server's default collection and read back by every agent on that server, so a cold run warms itself (OC-F5); two concurrent turns of one user on different MCP entries collided (OC-F1) — FIXED: every REST query rewrites the per-user server id (`switch_profile_context`), the overlay pinned the server on one branch only, and the adapter fell back to the per-user value; now the turn's PRIMARY server is armed at the execution seam in a context variable (`tool_identity.set_turn_primary_server`, inherited by a delegated prompt's task), every overlay names the turn's server, the default path reads the default agent's own server, and `mcp_adapter.turn_server_id` is the one resolution (overlay slot → armed primary → per-user only outside a turn); pinned by `test_turn_server_pin.py` (fails without the fix), proven live by running both campaigns concurrently with zero mix-ups. Ties in the demo data made three oracles non-deterministic; the cases now ask for the count at the top.

## Oct 2026 — The trust campaign runs on every engine, and renews its own cases

**What:** the live Trust Circle campaign (`test/trust_campaign/`, one Focus agent, Aug 2026) is now a multi-engine instrument with a Claude skill (`.claude/skills/trust-campaign/SKILL.md`). `agents.py ensure` provisions FIVE campaign agents — `@TCIDE` Ideate · `@TCIDT` Ideate + tools · `@TCFOC` Focus · `@TCOPT` Optimize · `@TCCOO` Coordinate — on one posture (review on every gate that can park, outbound observe, writes denied, `enforce_interactive`, a declared budget, the outcome loop), one deliberately weak model (`OpenRouter/amazon/nova-2-lite-v1`, the lowest quality score on llm.uderia.com with a working provider: a weak model provokes the gates more per token, and the campaign asserts what the gates REPORT, never what the model said), its own signed corpus of nine repo documents, its own MCP entry on a live endpoint (the seeded entry here pointed at port 8889, retired 2026-09-08). Everything it creates is listed in `tda_eval/trust_campaign/agents.json`; `teardown` removes exactly that; nothing of the operator's is touched.

**The suite** (`suite.py`): 27 cases × the engines each applies to = 96 live turns, each with `targets` (the registry points it exists to provoke) and a `landed` detector on every provocation; invariants I1–I10 — I1 now reads the server's own `applies_to` vocabulary per class, I6 (new) says an engine error is never the answer with every station quiet, I10 (new) says a bait that landed must be named by a control the case targets (landed-and-quiet = a CONTROL GAP, the fifth triage bin). `coverage.py --strict` is the design-time I1 — every applicable point reachable on every engine, or declared `UNPROVOKABLE` with what would make it provokable — and runs in the battery (`test_trust_campaign_suite.py`, 275 assertions: well-formed, complete, labels current, invariants behave on the engines' turn shapes, every fixed finding names a pin AND a live case). `run_campaign.py` runs engines in parallel, judges forced on and restored, diffs every station reading against the committed `baseline.json` (drift is a finding, never a failure) and carries a `quiet_runs` staleness counter per provocation; `analyse.py --recheck` re-applies a corrected suite to saved turns without a token; `harvest.py` lists real-session prompts a gate acted on that resemble no case and `--ledger` records them in the committed `harvest_ledger.json`, where `--baseline write` refuses until each is adopted as a case or declined with a reason (five candidates from this instance sit there now); `propose.py` writes `proposals/CONTROL-*.md` from an I10 gap; `calibrate.py` runs a candidate scorer over every saved run against the cases' `landed` truth per engine (one false positive = not ready).

**Campaign 2 found (FINDINGS.md):** (C6) the Coordinate engine died on a denied component — the authority chokepoint returned its refusal as a bare JSON string on a tool the manager builds with `response_format="content_and_artifact"`; LangChain raised, the graph aborted, and the error text was delivered as the answer on 9 of 15 cases with every station reading clean. Fixed at both return sites in `components/manager.py` (a refusal is a RESULT and takes the tool's shape), pinned by `test_component_denial_shape.py` (drives the real manager and a real StructuredTool through `ainvoke`; an AST rule that every return in the wrapper is a pair). (C7) the campaign runner's ring snapshot read a retired route. (Gap, closed as config) a CREATE TABLE ran through the READ tool on an interactive turn with BOUNDED reading "acting as the user": without `authorityConfig.enforce_interactive` no principal applies and `deny_writes` is inert — with it the same bait was refused at the chokepoint on both tool engines; recommendation recorded (the posture should say when it is not in force). Observations: the coordinator's synthesis is graded by the judges alone (its honesty gate runs only the citation branch, by recorded decision); the retrieval scorers are declared for Focus alone; a coordinator signs with an empty ingredient list; the budget/outcome switches are env (`TDA_TURN_BUDGET`, `TDA_OUTCOME_LOOP`). Re-runs after the fixes: 24/24 cases, 0 failures, 0 gaps; accepted as the baseline (96 cases). Side effect to clean: `fitness_db.campaign_scratch` on the demo database.

Newest first. One entry per merged change or release: what changed, why, how it was verified, and which files it touched.
Moved out of `CLAUDE.md` in Oct 2026 (the file had grown to 1.7 MB, 91% of it this changelog). Add new entries at the top of this file; `CLAUDE.md` keeps only one-line pointers to the latest few.

- **Oct 2026**: **The live stream comes back after a server restart, and a stream finding its way back reads Reconnecting.** Operator, after the prod restart that shipped the entry below: "during the restart the status has shown working — even after the restart it shown working — I had to refresh the page until I got ready". **Root causes:** (1) `notifications.js` `onerror` assumed "the browser will reconnect automatically" — true only for a dropped connection; an error RESPONSE (the reverse proxy's 502 while the container restarts) moves an `EventSource` to `CLOSED` and the browser never retries, so the SSE dot stayed `reconnecting` until a reload. (2) `statusSummary.js` counted `reconnecting` among its "busy" states, so the summary said **Working**. **Fix:** a module-level `_sse` (one stream per page — the old one closed before a new one opens); on `onerror` with `readyState === CLOSED` the module reopens the stream with a 2s → 30s doubling backoff, reset on `onopen`, sooner on the window's `online` event, never once signed out; a `CONNECTING` error is left to the browser. The summary now reads Working only for a busy/pulsing LED and **Reconnecting** (amber ripple) for a reconnecting one. Verified: `test_status_bar.mjs` 89 (+6); a stubbed-module simulation of notifications.js (three 502s → reopen at 2/4/8s, reset after open, a CONNECTING drop left alone, no reopen after sign-out, never two streams); the verdict simulation (dropped stream → Reconnecting); every gate that reads notifications.js passes (`test_component_bus` keeps its one failure on `flowBuilder.bundle.js`, present before this change). Pins: `notifications.js 5.108` · `main.js 10.113` · `statusSummary.js 1.4`. Files: `static/js/notifications.js`, `static/js/handlers/statusSummary.js`, `static/js/main.js`, `templates/index.html`, `test/test_status_bar.mjs`.

- **Oct 2026**: **The status strip stops calling a signed-out page Offline.** Operator: "when I log in I see the offline indicator … which would indicate that the platform is offline — either we hide the indicator during the login or we give it some meaningful value". **Root cause:** the markup started the summary at `data-verdict="offline"` / "Offline" and the SSE dot at `disconnected`, and `statusSummary.js` read "no class" as `disconnected` — so a stream that had not started yet (the landing page, and every signed-in page load until the stream opened) said Offline, though the server had just answered the page. **Fix (a real state, not hiding — hiding shifts the header on login and says nothing):** the summary and SSE dots start `pending` (hollow grey, the same reading as KNW idle); the verdict gains **Signed out** (no unexpired `tda_auth_token`, checked first: untinted, muted word, caret hidden, `aria-disabled`, the strip will not open — its LEDs describe the user's agent) and **Connecting** (signed in, stream not reported yet: untinted); **Offline** is now said only when the driver wrote `disconnected` (the stream failed). `ui.updateSSEStatus` clears `pending`; a `storage` listener re-reads the verdict when another tab signs in or out. Verified: `test_status_bar.mjs` 83 (start state, the six verdicts and their order, signed-out-first, read-only session check, toggle refusal, untinted CSS), a simulated-DOM walk through landing → failed stream → connecting → ready → working → lost → expired token; `test_header_avatar` 41, `test_tool_surface` 110 (its exact pin assertion became a minimum, so a later pin bump no longer breaks it). Pins: `main.css 5.15` · `statusSummary.js 1.3` · `ui.js 1.262` repo-wide · `main.js 10.112`. Files: `templates/index.html`, `static/js/handlers/statusSummary.js`, `static/js/ui.js`, `static/css/main.css`, `test/test_status_bar.mjs`, `test/test_tool_surface.py`.

- **Oct 2026**: **The header reads quietly — a flat avatar and a status strip that leads with a verdict.** Operator: "redesign the look and feel of the avatar to be modern" → "approved, with B default"; then "give the status bar a modern look while keeping its functionality" → "I approve". **Avatar:** the 36px blue-tinted disc with a 2px ring (the Focus class colour on every user, the heaviest element in the row) is ONE solid neutral disc, 30px (in px — the app root is 13px, so rem landed at 24px), initials at full contrast, nothing drawn around it; interaction lives OUTSIDE the disc as a ring offset — quiet on hover, the brand accent only while the menu is open (`aria-expanded`, written by the toggle and the outside-click close) and on keyboard focus; a chevron turns with the menu. **The OAuth picture is shown** when a linked provider gave one: `GET /v1/auth/me` carries `picture_url` (`_user_picture_url`, read from `oauth_accounts.provider_picture_url` in its own session — the authenticated user is detached; http(s) only; never raises), `setHeaderAvatarPicture` loads it over the initials and `onerror` brings the initials back. Light theme redefines fill/ink/ring tokens only. **A defect of the first cut, found by the operator ("the click on the avatar does nothing"):** the helper had been inserted between the `async` keyword and `function updateAuthUI`, so the whole inline block threw `async is not defined` before the menu handlers attached — fixed, and the gate asserts the helper sits as its own statement. **Status strip:** the six LEDs were a glass pill (gradient, blur, glow, halo ring, text shadow, labels spreading on hover) restyled in THREE files — main.css, themes.css (eleven `!important` light rules that existed only to undo the glow) and polish.css. - **Oct 2026**: **The scheduled renewal now reaches a pack's subscribers — the "uderia expert is unsigned for demo_analyst every morning" report.** Operator: the pack's daily documentation sync has a standing policy to re-sign dependent agents, yet a subscribing user's @UDERIA read unsigned after every run and had to be re-signed by hand. **Root cause:** `renew_after_sync` (`core/trust/renewal.py`) renewed the repository and then `agents_bound_to` — the OWNER's agents only (`get_profiles(owner)`). A subscriber's copy does not copy the collection (a `CollectionSubscription` row points at the publisher's id), so its ingredient hash moves with every content-changing sync, and its attestation is its own (`agent` kinds are owner-scoped) — nothing renewed it. The one path that carries a publisher's signature to subscribers, `fan_out_pack_sync` (`POST /v1/agent-packs/<id>/sync-subscribers` — the step `build.py --sign` runs after signing), was never called by the renewal; its own docstring names the gap for the manual case. A second, smaller gap: the pack's seal (`agent_pack`) went stale too (its composition hash is over the members' hashes), so even a fan-out would have refused to reinstate it. **Fix — a third act in the renewal, in the same grammar:** `packs_carrying(cid, renewed_agents, owner)` resolves the owner's installed packs that ship the repository or a renewed agent (from `agent_pack_resources`, with the marketplace listing); `renew_pack_seal` renews each seal through the sign-off route's aggregate gate (`member_refs` → `agent_signable` → `composition_hash` → `store.sign(event="renew")`; renewal only — a pack never sealed is not sealed; unsigned members refuse with the blockers named); `fan_out_subscribers(listing_id)` runs the publisher's own fan-out, which re-materializes each subscriber's copy and reinstates the renewed attestations by content hash. Every act and refusal is an inbox event — `signature_renewed` / `signature_renewal_refused` (a failed fan-out names *Sync subscribers* as the act owed) and the new `signature_renewal_carried` (how many subscribers). The renewal record carries `packs: [{installation_id, name, listing_id, seal, subscribers}]`. **Gate:** `test/test_signature_renewal.py` §H (+12, 60): the lookup against the real ledger tables (by collection, by renewed agent, never another owner's pack), the seal renewed as `renew` over the new hashes with the run's provenance, the fan-out called once for the listing, an unlisted pack never fanned out, a never-sealed pack not sealed but still fanned out, a failed fan-out an inbox warning, an unsigned member refusing the seal with the old seal standing. Mutation-tested (no fan-out → 5 fail; seal without the gate → 1 fail). **Server restart** (backend). The copies already stale on prod are carried by the next content-changing sync — or now, by *Sync subscribers* on the pack. Files: `core/trust/renewal.py`, `api/knowledge_routes.py` (docstring), `static/js/handlers/jobsHandler.js` (policy hint), `docs/Architecture/KNOWLEDGE_RETRIEVAL_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/RestAPI/restAPI.md`, `test/test_signature_renewal.py`.

- **Oct 2026**: **The Guide's Trailing trust state names the checks it weights — and keeps no `reads` row, by design.** Operator: "why don't I have a reads section in the Trailing trust state?" `reads` lists MODULES (the assessor code that judges a property of this turn; `POINT_PROPERTIES` → `shared_modules`), and the aggregate has none: it is a recency-weighted blend over the agent's recent turns (`eval/trust_behavior.assess_agents`), capped by its signature — an M chip there would claim a shared computation that does not exist, and the badge would mean two things. So the absence stays. What the entry DID withhold was the one fact its own "how it reads" step 2 points at — *"the trust-critical checks carry their configured weight"* — without naming them. Fixed as a third relation, not a borrowed one: `assurance_points.POINT_WEIGHTS` (`trailing_trust → "trust_dims"`) reads the list from `trust_behavior.DEFAULTS` — the place that decides it, so the Guide cannot drift from the blend (the architecture doc had listed five of the six) — and `guide_entry` serves it as `weights`; the renderer gives it a `weights` row where `reads` sits (what the reading is made of, before what it does with it: `how it reads · weights · fires when`), each chip opening the measure, and each measure answers `weighs on · Trailing trust state` after its `grades` row. Neither `graded by` (they feed it, they do not grade it) nor `reads` was reused. The remainder ("every other check shares the rest") is JUDGED's members and is not repeated. **Gates:** `test_guide_parents.py` §6 (+7: served list == `trust_dims`, every one a scored measure, no other mechanism serves weights, the row renders with all six, no `reads` row, the reverse row on each of the six and on nothing else), `test_guide_anatomy.mjs` §7 (+8: order, kind · count, chips both ways, a check nothing weights has no row, the glossary defines both leads). - **Oct 2026**: **Own or elsewhere — an open editor follows a write made outside it without overwriting the hand on it (the component-signals follow-up).** The two judgment calls shipped with the signals: the canvas and flow panels ignored every content notice (an autosave's own echo would have clobbered what was being typed) and the dashboard every layout notice (the user's own hand) — because a notice could not tell a page's own write from someone else's. Now it can, by one mechanism for every component: every tab has `UderiaBus.CLIENT_ID` (sessionStorage, per tab); the ONE fetch wrapper in `auth.js` (the session guard) stamps it on every same-origin request as `X-Uderia-Client` (a `Request` object keeps its headers plus the stamp; cross-origin untouched); `ui_notify.request_client()` reads it inside the request (`has_request_context` — a store write in that request's worker thread still carries it; `None` off a request: a scheduled run, a background task, a REST client that sends none) and every `component_changed` notice carries it as `client`; `notifications.js` hands it to the bus and the bus alone marks the event `own` (origin `page`, or `client === CLIENT_ID`). **Followers:** canvas — a write elsewhere (`updated` · `restored`) reloads in place while nothing is being typed; with an edit pending the pending autosave is **held** (the first browser run showed it firing under the notice and overwriting the outside write, so Reload brought back the page's own text) and the panel says *Changed elsewhere while you were editing · Reload · Keep mine* — Reload takes theirs and drops mine, Keep mine releases the hold and sends mine as a version; typing on a held canvas stays held; leaving it keeps mine (typed work is never dropped silently). Flow — *Changed elsewhere · Reload*, never a redraw under the hand (its own saves and the agent's patches during the turn are own). Dashboard — a layout saved elsewhere IS applied (two tabs agree), its own is not; a refresh start is still not a reload (its result lands as the tile's own update); own tile writes still reload (pins from a card rely on the echo). ONE notice line for every split panel: `splitPanelChrome.showSplitPanelNotice(panel, text, {actionLabel, onAction})` / `hideSplitPanelNotice` (on `window` for renderers), `.sp-notice` under the `.sp-header`, themed by variables with the orange accent, dismissable. **Noted:** an agent turn driven from the UI runs its tools inside that page's stream request, so what the agent writes during the turn is that page's own — the renderer shows it from the turn's own events. **Gates:** `test_component_bus.mjs` §7 (160) and `test_component_signals.py` §D (138, in-request via `Quart.test_request_context`); mutation-tested — wrapper stops stamping · dashboard ignores every layout again · notice drops the client · reload keeps the pending save — each red at the call site (the first assertion had matched the function definition and was tightened). Browser: Playwright, light + modern (the app's own theme switch — `data-theme` lives on `body`) — the stamp on every API request, a clean canvas re-read after an outside PUT, the notice over a dirty one with the server still holding the outside text past the autosave delay, Reload (theirs) in light and Keep mine (mine) in modern, no notice on the own autosave echo, the panel closing on an outside delete, zero console errors. **Pins:** uderiaBus 1.1 · auth 1.2 · split-panels 1.14 · splitPanelChrome 1.2 · notifications 5.105 · main 10.109. Files: `static/js/{uderiaBus,auth,notifications}.js`, `static/js/handlers/splitPanelChrome.js`, `static/css/split-panels.css`, `components/builtin/{canvas,flow,dashboard}/renderer.js`, `src/trusted_data_agent/core/ui_notify.py`, `templates/index.html`, `test/{test_component_bus.mjs,test_component_signals.py}`, `docs/Architecture/COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CLAUDE.md`.

- **Oct 2026**: **Component signals — how components talk to each other, for every component (branch `component-signals`).** Three channels, one contract (`src/trusted_data_agent/components/signals.py`), declared per component in its manifest under `signals` (`emits · listens · announces · consumes_refs · conflicts_with`, required by the schema, shown on the component card as *Emits · Follows · Announces · Reads by reference*). **(1) The page bus** `static/js/uderiaBus.js` — ONE registry of event names, ONE target (`document`), ONE prefix (`uderia:`); every renderer and handler emits/listens through `UderiaBus.emit / on / off / onComponent / announce`; nothing dispatches a CustomEvent on `document`/`window` itself. Before: ~40 names in five styles over two targets, no registry, no gate — three events fired into the void (`uderia:kg-created`, `flow:created`, `flow:panel-state`) and one listener waited for an event nobody sent (`uderia:config-saved`, now emitted by the App Config save). **(2) One change event for every component**: a write that reaches a component's store from ANYWHERE (this page, another tab, a REST script, a scheduled run, an agent turn) is announced ONCE at the store's write seam as the notice `component_changed` (`ui_notify.announce_component_change`; `announce_files_change` is its files spelling), relayed by notifications.js as `uderia:component-changed` `{component_id, action, ids, aspect, session_id, profile_id, origin}`; the five private "…-changed" events (`files`, `kg-authored`, `actions`, `products`, `explain-plans`) are gone. Declared at the seam with `@_signals.announces(...)` (store functions, sync/async, `when`, a profile) and `@_signals.announces_route(...)` (routes without a shared store function): canvas_db, flow_db, task_scheduler, the memory store, GraphStore (entities, relationships, bulk import, clear, metadata, lifecycle), kg_version_db, kg_release, authored_deploy (OBDA-MODEL), the catalog service (Database Navigator), the KG/authored/assignment/product routes, the action routes, the dashboard routes and handler. Every renderer that keeps instances follows its own component through `UderiaBus.onComponent(id)` — the dashboard reloads the open dashboard (never under a drag, in edit mode, on a tile refresh or a layout save — a reload refreshes pending tiles, which announce), the scheduler re-reads its list, the memory panel follows the store (not the turn), the Database Navigator re-reads a refreshed catalog (its own button is not echoed), the flow and canvas panels close when their item is deleted (an open editor's content is never redrawn under the user's hand), the Workspace follows every component through ONE coalesced subscriber. The bus swallows the server echo of the page's own announcement (same component · action · ids, the other origin, within 400 ms); two announcements from the same origin, or id-less ones, are two facts. **(3) The ledger**: every component result and every data result of a session is recorded under a stable reference (`component:<id>:<instance or container>`, `data:<tool>:<8-hex>`, stamped on the result's `metadata.ref` in both lanes) at the two tool chokepoints (`mcp_adapter.adapter`, `components.manager`); a component that declares `consumes_refs` takes `source_ref` and the chokepoint hands the entry to the handler (`context['source']`) and fills an empty `content` / `data` from it — the component reads the earlier result, the model never copies rows. Dashboard (`{implicit: latest_data}` — what its private session-wide `_viz_content_cache` was, now gone), canvas, chart and files consume. In memory per session (bounded 200, LRU across sessions) with a bounded sidecar `tda_sessions/<id>/components.json`, so a restart keeps the recent refs. **Gates:** new `test/test_component_bus.mjs` (141: no raw dispatch/listen, every name registered/emitted/heard, one change event, every manifest's declaration equals its renderer, the bus semantics) and `test/test_component_signals.py` (128: the block, the ledger incl. persistence and both lanes, the notice, both decorators through a real Quart request context, every seam decorated, every spoken action declared), both in the battery; `test/_uderia_bus.mjs` installs the real bus for a gate; 19 gates restated to the bus. Files: `components/signals.py` (new), `core/ui_notify.py`, `mcp_adapter/adapter.py`, `components/{manager,models}.py`, `components/schemas/component_manifest_v1.schema.json`, 17 manifests, every renderer and 30 handlers, `static/js/uderiaBus.js` (new), `templates/index.html`, `docs/Architecture/COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md` (§ Component Signals).

- **Oct 2026**: **The app shell is the visible area, always — the iPad "you can scroll the viewport upwards" report, fixed at the mechanism.** Operator screenshot (Chrome on iPad, hardware keyboard, the composer focused): the app panned up by the height of the collapsed keyboard shortcut bar (the ◞ glyph) with a white band beneath. Root cause: `appViewport.js` followed the visible area only for an on-screen keyboard (≥150 px); the ~70 px strip iPadOS reserves for the shortcut bar was left to the browser, which then panned the page by exactly that strip to reveal the focused composer and showed the document (white) in the room it reserved. Now the shell follows `visualViewport` on EVERY change (no threshold, no 100vh probe), any pan of the visible area is put back at the next frame (`window.scrollTo(0, 0)` — with the composer inside the shell above the keyboard or its bar there is nothing to reveal, and a finger-drag into the reserved room is undone), a pan that survives is followed (`--app-top`), and `html` wears the theme background so the keyboard's room can never be white; a pinch-zoom is still the user's own view. Re-applied on `focusin`/`focusout` and the document's own `scroll` too. Diag readout (`?scrolldiag=1`) adds the focused element and touch points. Gate: `test_app_shell.mjs` (28, restated: the strip shrinks the shell, the browser's pan is put back, a surviving pan is followed, zoom untouched; mutation-tested). Emulation (WebKit, touch): shell = visible area, a forced 300 px scroll reads 0 the next frame, 0 console errors — the keyboard itself cannot be emulated, so the device confirms. Pins: `appViewport.js 1.3`, `viewportDiag.js 1.2`, `main.css 5.12`. Files: `static/js/{appViewport,viewportDiag}.js`, `static/css/main.css`, `templates/{index,login,register}.html`, `test/test_app_shell.mjs`.

- **Oct 2026**: **The app's fallback height is `100%` again, not `100vh` — the iPad cut at the bottom (and right) was that one line.** Operator (iPad Chrome, 11:26 and 11:38): the conversation cut on the right and at the bottom, worse than before. Traced to f0cb600f, which changed `body { height: var(--app-h, 100%) }` to `var(--app-h, 100vh)`: on iOS `100vh` is the LARGEST viewport (toolbars hidden), taller than what shows, so a shell pinned to the screen overshot the bottom; `100%` on a fixed element follows the visible area — the operator's 11:04 screenshot (the `100%` build) had the full width. - **Oct 2026**: **Root cause of the iPad "page shifted / cut / band below": iOS zoomed into every text field — fields are 16px on iOS now.** Operator (iPad, Chrome and Safari, 11:26): the conversation cut on the right AND at the bottom — a two-sided cut no sizing explains. iOS/iPadOS zooms the page into any focused text field whose font is under 16px (Chrome on iPad stays zoomed); measured: the composer 15px, the login fields 13px, ~200 app fields 9.75–15px. That one cause explains every report of the day — the page moving when the keyboard appeared, Chrome not restoring, the login page doing it too, the cut. Fix at the cause: an iOS-only block (`@supports (-webkit-touch-callout: none)`) makes every typeable field (inputs except checkbox/radio/range/color/file/buttons, textarea, select, contenteditable) 16px, in `main.css` and inline in `reset_password.html` / `verify_email.html`; `login.html` / `register.html` now load `main.css` pinned (unpinned, a cached copy would keep the zoom). Not `maximum-scale=1`: in Chrome on iPad it also removes pinch-to-zoom. Verified by applying the block's exact contents in WebKit at iPad size: 0 fields under 16px on the login page and across every view and modal in the app; login, conversation (Capabilities + Files), Components, Anatomy lay out intact. The earlier shell/viewport changes stay (they were sound, but were working around this). Gate: `test_app_shell.mjs` 24 (+7: the rule, every page with fields gets it, pins, no viewport meta disables zoom). `main.css 5.8`.

- **Oct 2026**: **The app reaches the bottom of the screen again; it shrinks only for an on-screen keyboard.** Operator (iPad, 11:04): the sidebar and app ended ~67 px above the screen's bottom edge. With a hardware keyboard attached, iPadOS reserves a strip for its (collapsed) shortcut bar and the browser reports a visible area that much shorter; sizing the shell to the visible area (bbcdd6fe) left that strip empty. Now the shell is the full screen (`height: var(--app-h, 100vh)` — on the iPad 100vh reaches the bottom edge, as the pre-shell layout showed) and `appViewport.js` sets `--app-h`/`--app-top` only when something covers more than a keyboard's minimum (150 px, measured against a `100vh` probe), clearing them otherwise and under a pinch-zoom. **Diagnosed, not changed:** the page moving while the iPadOS keyboard or shortcut bar is up is the browser making room for the focused field — it happens identically on the login page (none of the app shell's code), and it restores when the keyboard goes (operator, Safari and Chrome on iPad).
