- **Oct 2026 (v1.26)**: **Release** — 161 commits since v1.25 (7 Oct 2026). Headlines: **Files and file stores** (PROP-010 — everything a session produces and every chat attachment lives in an admin-configured, encrypted store with one audited exit: save any export, dashboard snapshots, flow file nodes, *Add to knowledge*, `TDA_Files` opt-in per agent; Azure Blob and Google Cloud Storage backends; file keys under an external key manager — AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS, Vault Transit; CSV/TSV/XLSX attachments; a Files tab in Components → Files; a deleted attachment is never read again and its text goes with the purge; an attached document is evidence for Focus, the gates and the Agent Performance scores; the `document_context` module wired to the turn's attachments); **evidence per result** (PROP-009 — attestation history, a sealed bill of materials per turn, the answer's Evidence view and the estate-wide Evidence tab, portable evidence bundles, a hash-chained ledger, opt-in key custody and external anchoring); **the OBDA planes as components** (OBDA-READ, OBDA-MODEL, OBDA-ACT — no master switch, one Off · Observe · Enforce policy per plane, the Actions Designer, four eyes, Act II captured on production); **federal hardening** (SAML/OIDC hardening, key policy, idle sessions with a server-side marker, an append-only audit log that now stores each event's detail); **trust legibility** (Trust Circle: a chosen posture reads *watching*, one station registry, a verdict line; the Assurance Guide as one anatomy with parents, members and a glossary; the answer capsule says each fact once); **cost and model honesty** (one usage per streamed call — Celeris had been metered 3×, an override turn names the model that served it, a leaked SELECT is run and a record with no query behind it is named); plus load-time work (login, Anatomy, Trust, Evidence), the grounding-gate false-positive roots, a synced repository keeping its signature, and a console sweep of every screen. **Image rebuild needed:** `requirements.txt` adds `azure-storage-blob`, `azure-identity`, `google-cloud-storage`, `azure-keyvault-keys`, `google-cloud-kms>=2.21,<3`, `grpc-google-iam-v1<0.14.4` (all optional at runtime). - **Oct 2026**: **The Agent Performance scores read the attachments a turn read — and abstain once one was deleted.** Operator follow-up to the previous entry's open item. Traced: the after-the-turn scorers build a `RunRecord` from the persisted turn, which carried attachment text only through S9's `attachment_sources` stamp (off by default) — so `numeric_fidelity` scored a figure quoted from the attached contract as ungrounded whenever the repositories returned unrelated chunks (unit gate: 0.0 with the attachment out, 1.0 with it in), and on a Focus turn answered from the attachment alone `grounded_overlap` and `numeric_fidelity` abstained ("no data to ground numbers against", stored spans of the previous release). Two lanes also disagreed on the support set: the in-flight gate counted S9 attachment chunks, while the post-hoc `groundedness` judge and the assurance assessors read retrieved chunks only. **Design (asked: store the text, or a reference?):** a reference — persisting the text in the history would keep a deleted file's content alive after the purge that the previous entries made real. **Fix:** the turn records WHICH attachments it read — `attachment_evidence.files` (ids + names, never text; `session_files.begin_turn`/`end_turn` armed in the execution service beside S9's registry, stamped at persistence); the two scoring sites (`evaluate_turn_online`, `POST /v1/evals/score-turn`) fill in the text through the guarded manifest (`session_files.with_attachment_evidence` → `texts` + `lost`) before building the record; `RunRecord.support_chunk_texts()` is THE support set (retrieved chunks + S9 readings, else the attachment text) read by the grounding adapter, the groundedness judge (evidence labelled as including the user's attached documents), the assurance run context and `grounded_overlap`; `grounding_text()` adds the attachment text when S9 is off. An attachment deleted since is **lost**: `RunRecord.attachment_evidence_lost_reason()` is ONE wording, `numeric_fidelity`, `grounded_overlap` and the groundedness judge abstain with it, and `AssessmentContext.evidence_lost` makes every assessor requiring `chunks` abstain — enforced once in `Assessor.run`, beside `platform_authored`. The in-flight gate now passes the text under the same `attachment_evidence` key (S9's station is no longer touched by the synthetic stamp). `entry_has_text` is the one rule for "an attachment carries text" (an image's placeholder never counts), shared with `attached_material`. Scorers read the full extracted text — a superset of the excerpt the model was shown. `context_utilization` unchanged (it asks whether retrieved knowledge was used). **Verified:** `test_focus_attachments.py` 60 (§G: the stamp carries no text, persisted on the turn, hydration live/lost/placeholder, support set, numeric fidelity 0→1, judge inputs + label, corpus assessor convicts without / clears with, grounded_overlap on an attachment-only turn, every reader abstains on deletion; the support rule and the contract abstain mutation-tested), `test_assurance_marketplace.py` 32, battery green; live: stored online spans for a zero-match Focus turn read `grounded_overlap` 1.0 (4/4) and `numeric_fidelity` 1.0 (3/3) where the previous release abstained, *Score this turn* agrees. Files: `filestore/session_files.py`, `agent/execution_service.py`, `core/session_manager.py`, `eval/types.py`, `eval/online.py`, `eval/scorers/{judges,reliability,deterministic}.py`, `agent/assurance/{contract,run_context}.py`, `agent/grounding/{adapter,runtime}.py`, `agent/executor.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `docs/Architecture/{FILES,AGENT_OPS_EVAL,KNOWLEDGE_RETRIEVAL}_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `test/test_focus_attachments.py`.

- **Oct 2026**: **An attached document is evidence: Focus answers from it when its repositories hold nothing, and no gate calls its figures unsupported.** Operator: fix the Focus early return seen in the previous round (a Focus agent answered "No relevant knowledge found" when its repositories had nothing on the question, before reading the attached document). Rehearsing it live exposed the wider defect: on a Focus agent whose repositories DID return chunks, the correct answer quoted from the attached contract ("7.25 percent … capped at 40 percent") was **withheld** by the grounding gate in review mode — the attached text was never evidence unless the optional S9 attachment-sources switch (`TDA_ATTACHMENT_SOURCES`, off by default) was on; the knowledge-sufficiency honesty check would equally have replaced an attachment answer in enforce mode. **Fix, one helper:** `PlanExecutor.attached_material()` → `(texts, unreadable)`: the document text the turn sends (`documents_for_turn`), S9's readings, and whether an image the model saw natively carries something no check can read (an image's manifest placeholder is never counted as text; a file deleted from Files never counts). Focus: the no-results answer only when nothing usable was attached; otherwise synthesis with a knowledge block saying no repository held anything (and not to present the attachment as the repositories), the retrieval event and persisted turn carry `answered_from_attachments` and name the searched repositories, Live Status adds *Answered from* (`ui.js`, `eventHandlers.js`, `livingAnswer.js`). Grounding: `run_grounding(attached_texts=…)` adds the text as an `attachment_sources` stamp (the deterministic family and the judge both read it via `RunRecord`) — only on a turn the gate grades anyway, so attachments alone never make a turn groundable; passed from the executor's one seam and from Coordinate (the text it gave the coordinator). Honesty: `scan_rag_sufficiency(support_texts=…, unreadable_material=…)` counts only the specifics the attachment does not carry (by the corpus family's trigger rule); an unreadable image ⇒ no finding; defaults byte-identical. **Also:** a REST turn's attachment chip read "NaN MB" and an image read "Text" (the documented REST shape is `{file_id, filename}`) — `add_message_to_histories` now takes size and image flag from the upload record, and the chip shows no size rather than NaN for turns stored before. **Verified:** new `test_focus_attachments.py` (37, in the battery; the support rule, the early-return condition, the grounding join and the stored-facts enrichment each mutation-tested), `test_file_store.py` 250 (the reader-count check restated to ≥4 — the helper reads the guarded manifest), honesty 235, document context 33, attachment freeze 195, outcome loop 79, battery green; live on a local server: PDOCS (repositories hold nothing) answered from the attachment with the retrieval step saying so; UDERIA (repositories return 10 chunks, review mode) — withheld before, now *Grounding Gate → pass corpus-supported* with the correct figures; Ideate and Optimize attachment turns correct (one Optimize run hit an empty model response at the final report, two reruns correct); light + modern render, 0 console errors. **Follow-up (same day):** the after-the-turn scores — see the entry above. Files: `agent/executor.py`, `agent/engines/{focus,coordinate}_engine.py`, `agent/grounding/runtime.py`, `agent/honesty/{gate,runtime}.py`, `core/session_manager.py`, `static/js/{ui,eventHandlers}.js`, `static/js/handlers/{livingAnswer,chatDocumentUpload}.js` (+ importer pins), `docs/Architecture/KNOWLEDGE_RETRIEVAL_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `test/{test_focus_attachments (new),test_file_store}.py`, `test/trust_battery.sh`.

- **Oct 2026**: **The document part of the context window is wired to the turn's attachments, with today's limits as the floor.** Operator follow-up ("tackle topic 2": the document indexing step never received attachments). Traced wider: the `document_context` module read `session_data["attachments"]` (nobody wrote it) and a plaintext `manifest.json` (gone since attachments became sealed files) — it ALWAYS reported "no attachments"; Live Status showed 0 document tokens while up to 50K chars were in the prompt; the Balanced type's `no_documents_attached` rule moved the document budget away even with a document attached; the executor read the allocation (`_cw_document_max_chars`) BEFORE the assembly that wrote it, so Optimize/ReAct always used the fixed limit; the search path for documents never ran (and its indexing was fire-and-forget, racing the first turn); and the module's purge deleted the session's uploads folder — sealed manifest included — through `POST /v1/context-window/modules/document_context/purge`. Operator decision (asked): wire it, keep today as the floor. **Fix:** `executor.document_char_limit(tokens_allocated)` is THE limit (allocation, never below `DOCUMENT_CONTEXT_MAX_CHARS`) at every site (executor, Coordinate — no hand conversion left); the executor and Coordinate put the turn's attachments into the assembly context; the module loads them through the one loader (`load_document_context` → `readable_manifest`), is measured, and its text IS what the turn sends (executor replaces its pre-assembly text — native multimodal blocks kept, S9 readings re-appended; Ideate/Focus take `executor.documents_for_turn()`); `condense`/`condense_rag` never go below the floor; with `rag_offload` configured the index is filled before assembly (awaited, 30 s bound), the assembly passes it as `ctx.session_store`, and a document cut at its excerpt is completed with passages searched for the question from beyond the cut — only this turn's readable attachments, never a duplicate; purge now drops only the search index (`SessionVectorStore.forget_module`). **Verified:** new `test_document_context.py` (33, in the battery; floor and filter mutation-tested), attachment freeze 195, S9 baseline 9, image sources 65, KG context module 42, file store 250, battery green; live on a local server: the module sees the attachment (1 document, cut recorded) and the rule no longer fires; on the default type a clause beyond the 20K excerpt is still lost (as before); with a rehearsal type using document search the same question answered "7.25 percent … capped at 40 percent" from the searched passage (index built in ~0.35 s for 60K chars), the document budget growing to 67,584 chars from surplus; Optimize answered correctly with 3,450 document tokens now counted. **Seen, not changed:** Focus answers "no relevant knowledge found" when its repositories return nothing, before it ever reads an attached document (pre-existing early return). Files: `agent/executor.py`, `agent/engines/{ideate,focus,coordinate}_engine.py`, `components/builtin/context_window/{base,handler,session_vector_store}.py`, `components/builtin/context_window/modules/document_context/handler.py`, `docs/Architecture/CONTEXT_WINDOW_ARCHITECTURE.md` §5.4, `test/test_document_context.py`, `test/trust_battery.sh`.

- **Oct 2026**: **A deleted attachment is never read by a turn again, its text goes with the purge, and its chip says so.** Operator question: *what happens to the turns that have a file attached that got deleted?* Traced: the turns themselves are untouched (question, answer, trace, evidence; the answer stays in the history later turns read) and a turn only reads the attachments of its own submit — but two gaps. **(1)** The text read from a file at upload lives in each conversation's sealed manifest (the upload's own, and any it was attached to from Files); deleting the file did not touch it and neither did the purge, so after "deleted — unreadable even from a backup" the text survived, and `load_document_context` / the multimodal fallback / the attachment-sources reader served it to any turn that named the id (a REST client can). **(2)** The chip of a deleted attachment looked live and its preview failed. **Fix:** `session_files.readable_manifest` (the manifest without entries whose file is deleted or gone) is THE manifest every turn reader takes (`executor` ×3, `image_sources`; a structural check pins it); the purge — expiry, retention 0, a deleted conversation, a removed user — calls `session_files.forget_files` once per user (`service._purge_all`), removing the entry and its text from every manifest that references it; Recently deleted keeps the text so a restore is complete. The chip reads `GET /v1/files/attachments?session_id=` (`live` · `deleted` + `purge_after` · `gone`, from the conversation's own manifest — so files attached from Files are covered, which the old kept-list read missed) and says *Deleted* with *Restore* while it can (struck-through name, a tooltip naming the date and that the answer stays), *Deleted* alone once purged; an unreadable manifest says nothing rather than a false "Deleted"; chips follow deletes/restores/purges made anywhere. **Verified:** `test_file_store.py` 250 (§V: read by turns while live, refused in both conversations once deleted incl. the multimodal fallback, restorable, forgotten in both on expiry purge and at once with retention 0; both mechanisms mutation-tested), `test_files_ux.mjs` 115, `test_attachment_storage_freeze.py` 195 unchanged; live in headless Chrome (light + modern): a REST delete turns the chip to *Deleted · Restore* within 2 s, *Restore* on the chip brings back *Keep* and clears `deleted_at`, 0 console errors. Files: `filestore/{session_files,service}.py`, `api/files_routes.py`, `agent/executor.py`, `llm/image_sources.py`, `static/js/handlers/filesKeep.js`, `templates/index.html`, tests above.

- **Oct 2026**: **Components → Files has a Files tab, and a file change made through the REST API reaches every open page.** Operator (screenshot of the Files component detail): every other component's detail carries a tab to manage what it holds (Canvases, Dashboards, Flows, Knowledge Graphs, Jobs) — Files had none. **The tab:** new `static/js/handlers/filesTabHandler.js` (the Canvases-tab shape: list ↔ detail), registered after Profiles in `componentHandler.js` — search, the panel's kind filters with counts, storage used; per file rename, keep, download (the one governed route, audited), delete with undo, restore from *Recently deleted*; the facts and *Used in*; *Open in Files panel* for preview and attach. **Root cause found rehearsing it:** a rename made through the REST API never reached the open tab — nor the Files panel in another tab. The routes run rename/delete/restore/keep in `asyncio.to_thread`, and `trust_events.broadcast_notice` skipped silently off the event loop ("loop-guard"), so every worker-thread notice of every caller was dropped. It now hands the put to the serving loop (`APP_STATE["serving_loop"]`, recorded at startup; `call_soon_threadsafe` — an `asyncio.Queue` is not thread-safe); with no serving loop (a script, a test) it still skips. **Also:** the detail named a conversation by the title it had at upload ("New Chat") while *Used in* named it as it is now — `service.provenance` now returns the current `session_title`, read by the tab and the panel; uploaded images show the image glyph. **Verified:** `test_file_store.py` 238 (§U worker-thread notice reaches the queue / on-loop unchanged / no serving loop skips — mutation-tested; current conversation name), `test_files_ux.mjs` 111 (+7 tab assertions, mutation-tested), battery green; live in headless Chrome (light + modern, 1680 and 1366): select, rename round trip, a REST rename appearing in the open tab within 1 s, filters, search, open-in-panel, download through the governed route (audit row written), 0 console errors. Files: `static/js/handlers/{filesTabHandler (new),componentHandler}.js` (+ importer pins), `core/trust_events.py`, `main.py`, `filestore/service.py`, `components/builtin/files/renderer.js`, `templates/index.html`, tests above.

- **Oct 2026**: **The audit log stores an event's structured detail, and "my audit log" answers again.** Found while building Files: `AuditLog` had no column for `log_audit_event(..., metadata=…)`. `metadata` is SQLAlchemy's own schema attribute on every model, so `AuditLog(metadata=…)` set a throwaway instance attribute and nothing reached the row — every event's structured detail (a download's bytes, format, file, session; a security event's severity; an admin act's target) was lost on every install, kept only by the optional SIEM export. The reader then did `log.metadata` — the schema `MetaData` object — and handed it to the JSON encoder, so `GET /v1/auth/me/audit-logs` (and the admin user detail's recent events) answered **500**, verified before the fix. **Fix:** a real column `audit_logs.metadata_json` (model attribute of the same name; `metadata` stays SQLAlchemy's), written by `log_audit_event` (`default=str`, so a non-JSON value cannot fail the audited act), read back as parsed JSON; `auth/database._run_audit_table_migrations` adds it to an existing database at startup (an `ALTER … ADD COLUMN` is not an UPDATE, so the append-only triggers are untouched; older rows read `null`); the append-only trigger's one allowed update (account deletion nulling `user_id`) now also requires `metadata_json` unchanged, where the column exists. **Gate:** `test_audit_integrity.py` 33 (+6: the column is append-only, account deletion still allowed, the model has the column and no `metadata` column, the migration adds it idempotently to a legacy table, `log_audit_event` → reader round-trips the metadata, an event without metadata reads `None`); mutation (the old `metadata=` kwarg) fails it. Battery green. **Live (local):** the migration ran on the real database, the endpoint answers 200, a new download event reads `{bytes, format, file_id, session_id, store, …}`. **Server restart** (backend; one schema column, ledger-backed). Files: `auth/{models,audit,database}.py`, `core/audit_integrity.py`, `test/test_audit_integrity.py`.

- **Oct 2026**: **A record fabricated after every data query failed now reads `danger` at the honesty gate, and the ReAct lane's reserved-word retry quotes every word Teradata names in turn and hands the model the LATEST refusal — prod session 09bc567f turn 2 (@IDRETL, gemini-3.1-flash-lite).** The agent compiled the governed `ecommerce.ecommerce_cart` metric (valid, fully quoted SQL) but never executed it; it wrote its own four-table join using TWO Teradata reserved words as identifiers — the table `retail_core.account` and the alias `CM` — and Teradata refused it (3707). **The retry did fire** (log: *Teradata names the reserved word 'account' — retrying once with the identifier quoted*), the quoted statement was then refused on `CM`, that second refusal RAISED inside the retry (`langchain_mcp_adapters` raises `ToolException` on a refused statement), the handler logged *retry skipped* and returned the ORIGINAL result — so the model saw the `account` error seven times over and never learned about `CM`; it resubmitted variants (AS, INNER JOIN, TOP 20) seven times, the loop guard's *do not repeat the identical call* note notwithstanding, then gave up on the join and presented a five-row "system-wide" cart table (142,890 · 98,450 · 72,110 · 65,320 · 12,450) attributed to a metric that never ran. **The one trust finding was correct** — the grounding gate flagged exactly those five figures as unmatched (`numeric_fidelity 0.17`, annotate) — but it was the weaker reading: the honesty gate read `pass`. Replayed offline on the persisted turn: `fabricated_after_failure` abstained because its quantity detector reads prose ("1,250 customers"), not a markdown table, AND its failure-disclosure exemption matched *"I am unable to execute a direct join"* — a disclosure about the segment breakdown that excused the invented system-wide figures; `unsourced_record` abstained because a query had been ATTEMPTED. Attempted is not retrieved. **Fix 1 — honesty (`honesty/gate.py:assess_unsourced_record`):** abstains only when a data query SUCCEEDED (the grounding gate owns tool-backed answers); a turn whose every raw-SQL query failed is read like a turn that ran none — the record's values are still checked against everything the model was given, so a record copied from the context stays supported. The no-query wording and every other branch are byte-identical. **Fix 2 — the chain (`tool_enforcement._alias_retry_core`):** one round per reserved word Teradata names (≤ `ALIAS_CHAIN_MAX` = 3, cumulative quoting), through the ONE retry body (`_retry_core(keep_failed=True)` — the body hands back a failed retry and turns a raised refusal into its model-facing result; every other retry keeps its one-shot contract byte for byte). Outcomes: the rewritten statement runs → its rows + a note naming the words; refused the same way → the ORIGINAL (unchanged contract); refused for something ELSE → the LATEST refusal, led by a note saying what was quoted and that the earlier refusal no longer applies. The Optimize lane already chains across its correction attempts; the ReAct lane was the one returning a stale error. **Verified:** `test_honesty_gate.py` 223 → 235 (the real turn as the fixture: fires, names the five figures, count 7; one succeeded query → abstain; copied record → abstain; prose → abstain; annotate/enforce/dial wording) — fails 8 on the old gate. `test_sql_dialect_react.py` 118 → 120 (+chain section: account → CM → rows with BOTH quoted; CM repeated → the CM refusal handed over, args untouched; same refusal → original, one retry; a 3802 after the retry reaches the model; a returned-not-raised refusal chains; the bound) — fails on the old enforcement. - **Oct 2026**: **The conversation input no longer lags while a large knowledge graph is open in the split panel — two DOM observers were feeding each other at full speed.** Operator report: typing in the composer became extremely slow with a big KG in the split window. Measured in headless Chrome on the local server with `energy_utilities_core` (500 sampled nodes, 338 edges — ~5,000 SVG elements): with the panel open the main thread was ~190% busy while IDLE (283 long tasks in 3 s) and input→paint latency per keystroke was **112 ms** (22 ms without the panel); switching off the SVG filters and CSS animations changed nothing, so the graph's painting was not the cause. **Root cause — a two-observer loop:** `splitPanelResizer.js` observes every panel's `style`/`class` attributes and rebuilt its drag handles on EVERY record (remove + re-insert under `#chat-canvas-split`); `subHeaderAutohide.js` observes that row's childList (subtree) and re-wired every panel on every change, calling `classList.add('sp-has-subheader')` on a panel that already wore it — which still re-sets the attribute, which the resizer saw, which rebuilt the handles, which the scanner saw… One turn per animation frame, each one restyling the whole row (the 5,000-element graph), for as long as any panel with a sub-toolbar was open. Probe: 32 class re-sets (old value == new value) on `#kg-split-panel` and `#explain-plan-split-panel` in 2 s, every one from `_updateHandles ← _onAttributeChange`. **Fix at both roots:** the resizer's attribute observer now compares the visible panels' SEQUENCE (ids + flex `order`, the only thing a handle depends on) and returns when it is unchanged — a hover class, a focus ring, a toolbar height or a same-value class write rebuilds nothing; a newly opened/closed panel or a reorder still does. Regression-clean: split_panel_structural 14 · split_panel_reorder 67 · split_panel_menu_unclip 7 · panel_open_control 109. No server restart needed beyond the template pin bump (`splitPanelResizer.js 1.9`, `subHeaderAutohide.js 1.1`). - **Oct 2026**: **A tab on a revoked session now ends the session once, says why, and keeps the server's idle clock in step — the "Runs always says No scored runs yet" report.** The operator saw every Agent Roster card's RUNS section read *No scored runs yet.* Prod log: at 16:40:57 the demo session's token was revoked for 30 minutes idle (`auth_tokens.last_used_at`, hardened mode); the tab stayed open on it, and each click logged *attempt to use revoked token* three times (runs · timeline · trust-history) while the page painted each widget's own empty state — the runs ledger's `catch` turned a 401 into *No scored runs yet.* It "worked again" because the user signed in again at 16:44:20. **Three defects, one root — two clocks and no shared reaction.** (1) The browser idle lock (`idleLock.js`) measures INPUT and the server measures authenticated REQUESTS; a user who reads, scrolls or types for half an hour without a request keeps the browser clock alive while the server's runs out, so the lock never fired. (2) Most handlers call `fetch` directly with the stored token, bypassing `AuthClient.authenticatedFetch`'s 401 handling, so a dead session reached each widget separately. (3) The ledger's error branch read as a fact about the agent. **Fixes:** `auth.middleware.session_invalid_marker(auth_header, path, status)` is the ONE rule — a 401 on an `/api/` path on a request that presented a web session token (a Bearer JWT, never a `tda_` access token) means the session was refused — stamped as `X-Session-State: invalid` at ONE `after_request` seam in `main.py`, so every emitter (the decorators, the hand-rolled admin/marketplace checks) is covered. `auth.js` installs ONE fetch guard on every page: on that marker (never a bare 401, which an endpoint may use for something else) and only while a token is stored, it clears the session once and sends the user to `/login?reason=session`; the login page explains it; it never redirects from the login/register pages. `idleLock.js` touches `/api/v1/auth/me` at most every 5 minutes (≥1 min, ≤ a third of the limit) while the user is active, so the server's clock follows the browser's and the lock, not the server, ends an idle session. The runs ledger's failure reads *Runs could not be loaded — <reason>*; *No scored runs yet* is left to the renderer that sees the rows. **Verified:** a real browser against the local server with the API route stubbed — a marked 401 ends the session and lands on the login page, a bare 401 leaves the session untouched; on prod, an invalid Bearer JWT gets the header. **Gate:** `test_session_idle.py` +16 (the marker's five rules, the one seam, the guard's four properties, the login note, the heartbeat and its throttle, the ledger's honesty). Pins: `agentPerformanceHandler.js 15.182`, `idleLock.js 1.1`, `auth.js 1.1` (now pinned on all three pages). **Server restart.** Files: `auth/middleware.py`, `main.py`, `static/js/auth.js`, `static/js/idleLock.js`, `static/js/handlers/agentPerformanceHandler.js`, `templates/{index,login,register}.html`, `test/test_session_idle.py`.

- **Oct 2026**: **A provider error no longer imports every SDK an `except` clause names, and the trust battery is green again.** Found while chasing a "flaky" `test_envelope_silence` ("…in about the silence bound, not the provider's hang", red on clean `main` under the battery's parallel load). Instrumented in fresh processes, the 0.2 s silence cut fired on time, but the retry started ~1.0 s later, every time and only on a process's first error. **Root cause:** the attempt loop's `except (_anthropic.InternalServerError, _anthropic.RateLimitError, _openai.APIError)` reads lazy SDK stand-ins (`llm/lazy_sdk.py`). Matching ANY raised exception against that tuple imported anthropic AND openai on the request path, including on a Google-only deployment that never touches them. `configuration_service`'s rollback clause did the same with four SDKs next to `Exception`. **Fix at the root:** `lazy_sdk.loaded_attrs("module:Attr", …)` resolves the classes only for modules already imported (stand-in loaded or in `sys.modules`). An instance of a class from a never-imported module cannot exist, so no match changes, and `except ()` matches nothing. Both multi-SDK clauses use it; single-SDK clauses guard a call that already loaded their SDK and are unchanged. Measured: first-error cut→retry 1.2 s → 0.207 s. (b) `_strip_structure` blanks a table's header row (a `|` line above a separator row) and bolded row labels; cells and plain first cells stay claims. (c) `grounding_text()` uses `retrieved_chunk_texts()`. (d) The Assurance Guide's grounding entry states that structure is never checked. **Result on the prod turn:** 1 unsupported claim (the misquote, still triggering), corpus numeric fidelity 1.0, scorer 7/7. - **Oct 2026**: **A synced repository can keep its signature: the owner's standing policy after a sync that changed content.** The @UDERIA knowledge base is kept current by the daily CDC sync, and every sync that touched a file left three human acts owed: re-acknowledge the injection findings the ingest firewall re-raised on the changed documents (the scan record follows the content, so a prior acknowledgement vanished), re-sign the repository, re-sign every agent that binds it. Two per-repository columns (`collections.sync_auto_ack_findings`, `sync_auto_resign`; self-applying), set from the Task Scheduler → Platform Jobs tab (*After a sync that changes content*), applied by ONE module `core/trust/renewal.py` after the sync's document loop: (1) **carry-forward, always** — a prior acknowledgement is carried onto the re-scanned record when the finding labels did not widen (the judgement covered these labels; a widened set is a new question), the record saying it was carried; (2) **auto-acknowledge** — open findings on the documents this run changed, with a reason naming the run and the policy, one inbox event each (`corpus_finding_auto_ack`, deliberately NOT a receipt); (3) **renew** — the repository through the same act the sign-off route now uses (`sign_knowledge_repository`; the route delegates to it), then every agent of the owner that consumes it by the badge's own ingredient rule. A renewal is a renewal: never a first signature; the owner's authority checked as the route checks it (approver tier; refused under separation of duties); the validator's and the bottom-up gate's refusals stand; every act and refusal is an inbox event with its reason (`signature_renewed` / `signature_renewal_refused`). Recorded as the new establishing event `renew` (`store.sign(event=)`, a closed grammar) with `verdict.renewal` naming the run, the repository, the files and the policy — history reads *renewed by the scheduled sync*, never *signed by the owner*. The sync result carries `renewal` and `updated_doc_ids`; the scheduler log line prints it; Sync Now renders it. Gate: `test/test_signature_renewal.py` (48; in the trust battery). - **Oct 2026**: **A re-ingested document keeps only its current chunks; the corpus stops contradicting itself.** Follow-up to the grounding-gate validation (session 727292c3): the @UDERIA corpus answered with both "the `OBDA_ENABLED` master" and "there is no master switch". The daily CDC sync had re-ingested every changed doc that morning, but its cleanup removed only chunks with an OLDER `ingest_epoch` (`ingest_epoch < new`) — and the pack's original import stamps no epoch at all, so those chunks never matched and outlived every update (15 of them still served on prod: the manual, the FAQ, the OBDA/ACT/authority/substrate docs, the REST reference). Root cause fixed at one seam: `knowledge_sync.superseded_chunk_ids` (pure) names every chunk of a document that is not from the current epoch — older and epoch-less alike — and `_remove_superseded_chunks` is the ONE removal path, used after a re-ingest AND as a repair sweep on unchanged documents that have been re-ingested before (a registry `ingest_epoch`; one metadata-only read per document; client-side chunking only — a server-side store carries no epoch and a sweep there would delete a document whole; a never-re-ingested document keeps its epoch-less chunks, which are its current ones). The sync result carries `swept`. **Incident during the work:** the first sweep on production (14 Oct, 09:32 UTC) emptied 72 of the 108 documents — a pack import writes the registry's `ingest_epoch` but stamps NO epoch on its chunks, so for a never-re-ingested document the epoch-less chunks were its current ones and the rule read them as superseded. Guarded within the hour (commit `5ed85981`): the sweep removes nothing unless at least one chunk stamped with the registry epoch is in the store (`require_current`); the post-re-ingest cleanup keeps the plain rule; the collection was restored by a full re-index from the current files. Also: the last live sentence naming a master switch for the write planes (ACT_ARCHITECTURE §authority table, the `action` component row) now names the component chain. - **Oct 2026**: **An action's signature covers the model facts it depends on; signing stands on the extension its target lives in.** Raised in Act II: *shouldn't a change to the graph invalidate an action?* Before, an action's signature covered its contract and its A1–A6 proof only: after signing, the model under it could change (an attribute's allowed values, a new attribute on the target, a different deployed table), and the action kept reading trusted and kept being performed against a proof of a model that no longer existed. Signing checked the base ontology only, never the extension that holds an extension target (Act II's Lead). **Changed:** (1) the validation report records `model_facts`, the facts A1/A2 read from the graph (the target's resolution, its columns, the writable attributes' closed domains), computed by ONE pure function `action_types.model_facts` for validation (through the store) and the trust reading (through the graph rows), from the published model only (a draft moves nothing); (2) `trust/actions.live_hash` puts today's facts into the stored report, so a change to one of them reads *changed* with `drift` in words (`the allowed values of Status changed` · `new attribute witness_name`), and a change elsewhere in the graph, or a base re-sign, moves nothing (the action binds the facts it depends on, not the model's signature: no churn, no cycle); (3) signing a stale proof is refused `stale_report`, perform's refusal says what moved, and a report from before the facts were recorded reads *changed · awaits a fresh validation* (validate once more); (4) signing stands on the base AND the target's extension (`_model_ingredient`), and the refusal names which; (5) the Designer: Next is **Validate again** with what moved; when signing waits for the model, Next is **Open Govern** (the KG panel answers `uderia:open-govern`), the Designer re-reads itself when Govern signs, and Escape closes only the dialog on top; a refused sign shows the gate's words, not `unsigned_ingredient`. The other direction is deliberate: a changed action never moves the graph's signature. **Verified:** `test/test_action_trust.py` §8 (69 pass), `test/test_action_surfaces.mjs` (57); rehearsed locally in the browser on the RH kit (light + dark). A description edit on the target left `record_rhlead` trusted; closed allowed values on `Status` read *changed · the allowed values of Status changed*; preview refused with the same words; Validate again → Open Govern (the extension had been edited) → publish `witness_name` and sign the extension in Govern → the Designer read *new attribute witness_name* → Validate again → Re-sign → signed and intact. **On production:** `record_lead` and `close_lead` read *awaits a fresh validation* after the deploy: validate each once more, then sign. Files: `core/action_types.py`, `core/trust/{actions,validators}.py`, `core/action_perform.py`, `static/js/handlers/{actionDesigner,knowledgeGraphPanelHandler}.js`, `components/builtin/action/renderer.js`, docs (ACT_ARCHITECTURE, manual §2.13), tests.

- **Oct 2026**: **An act claimed but never taken is recovered, or disclosed — never marked Verified.** Production, asking @PXPROD to record lead L-0002: the answer read "I have prepared the request to record the new lead … awaiting your confirmation … use the Confirm control in the action panel", but the turn called no tool (`tools_used: []`): nothing was prepared, no Confirm existed, and the answer still carried **Verified**. The model had echoed the previous turn's wording (L-0001) instead of calling `TDA_Action`. Whether a turn produced an action record is a fact the code holds, so the model no longer decides it. **Fixed, three layers:** (1) **recovery**: when an answer claims an act (`honesty/primitives.claims_act`: prepared · awaits confirmation · parked · recorded/closed …) while this turn's action record (`action_perform.turn_actions()`) is empty and `TDA_Action` is available, the conversation agent retries once with a platform note telling it to call `perform` now; the retry's tokens are added to the turn (`act_recovered`); (2) **honesty backstop**: `honesty/gate.assess_unbacked_act` (needs an open turn record, `action_perform.turn_active()`, so it never accuses outside a turn) runs first in `run_honesty`: in *observe* mode it records an event, *annotate* appends "Note: Nothing was prepared or written in this turn …", and *enforce* replaces the answer, so an answer claiming an act it never took can no longer pass as Verified; (3) **instructions**: `TDA_Action` (medium + heavy) now says every change needs its own `perform` in THIS turn, that an earlier turn's act is not this one's, and that the Confirm control is in the answer (not "the action panel"). **Verified:** `test/test_honesty_gate.py` (204 pass: the claim primitive, the act-free and act-backed turns, out-of-turn silence, annotate/enforce wording); live locally with a forced claim. The server logged the claim once, the retry performed `record_rhlead` for L-1007, and the answer showed the action card with Confirm (light + dark checked). Files: `agent/honesty/{primitives,gate,runtime}.py`, `agent/conversation_agent.py`, `core/action_perform.py`, `components/builtin/action/instructions.json`, `test/test_honesty_gate.py`.

- **Oct 2026**: **Access in the warehouse is stated and checked before every act — Model ACT and Instance ACT.** Raised in Act II: every access right was met by failing (a landing refused CREATE DATABASE, the ledger refused CREATE TABLE, an action's probes refused SELECT under no role) and the person learnt the GRANTs one failure at a time. **Added:** `dbdeploy/access.py` states what each act needs — WHO (a login or a role) must hold WHAT on WHICH object, and why: a landing (`CREATE DATABASE` on the parent of a new sibling · `CREATE TABLE` for a new table · `DROP TABLE` for a column ALTERed into an existing table · `REFERENCES` for a reference), the action ledger (`CREATE TABLE` for the MODEL login), performing (the write login holds the role; the role holds exactly the operation's rights + `INSERT` on the ledger) — and `judge` marks each held or missing against the dictionary (`TeradataDeploymentBackend.read_access`: `DBC.AllRightsV` / `AllRoleRightsV` / `RoleMembersV`; a database-level grant covers its tables; an unreadable dictionary holds nothing), with the exact `GRANT` for what is missing. **Surfaces:** Govern's Preview shows *Access · the landing login …* and keeps **Land** disabled; a Land without it is refused `409 access_missing` before anything is created or altered; the Actions Designer shows *Access in the warehouse* in the Define form (re-read as the connection, columns or role change; a stale answer is never shown as the current one) and in each action's details, with **Copy the grants** (`POST /v1/actions/access`). The requirements and the GRANT templates are in `ACT_ARCHITECTURE.md` §1a and the operator guide §2.13, gated against the code. Also: every parent-reference note (no key · not deployed · no attribute names the key) is said when a table is created, not on a later column landing. **Verified locally in the browser (light and dark):** a new role holding nothing → the Define form named all three requirements and their GRANTs; after running exactly those, it read *grants everything*; a landing previewed through the writer → *DROP TABLE … missing*, Land disabled, a REST Land refused with nothing changed; through the operator → held, landed with a sealed receipt. `test/test_act_access.py` (20, in the battery), `test_business_terms` §D. - **Oct 2026**: **Actions, rehearsed end to end before the person meets them: two logins never confused, a ledger refusal named, A6 names its GRANTs, no dead end, an Inbox route, and a Designer a person can read.** Act II on production: defining `record_lead` ended in "validation could not run — 500". The cause, and everything else the remaining road would have met, was found by rehearsing it locally on a parallel setup on the shared Teradata (an operator login that owns its space, a writer login holding two empty roles — the production shape), in the browser, scene by scene: define insert + update, validate, grant, sign, grant to an agent, Try it, an agent turn that records (confirm) and one that closes (review → Inbox → approve). **Found and fixed:** (1) **identity** — every Teradata deployment backend ran its statements through teradataml's process-GLOBAL `create_context`, so with two logins in one process a statement ran as whichever had connected last (the ledger's CREATE "through the operator" ran as the writer; validation's probes could read another login's rights). Each backend now holds its own `teradatasql` session (PAT-only configurations keep the global context); the action perform path already used its own connection. (2) **the 500** — validation created the action ledger through the action's WRITE login, which may not `CREATE TABLE`; the ledger is a model change and is now created through the connection the model was landed through (`default_connection(purpose="model")`), and a refusal is a named result (`ledger.missing`, the warehouse's own sentence via the ONE `friendly_db_error`, which also trims the landing's Go stack). (3) **A6** names the exact `GRANT …;` statements, also when the role holds nothing yet, and says the rights in words (SELECT, UPDATE — not `RU`). (4) **dead end** — a blocked action said "fix the contract and validate again" with no button; its owed act is now **Validate again** with the blocker in its Next box. (5) **the write connection** — the Designer defaulted to "the first connection listed" (the model operator) and the Define form lost a connection chosen while the default was still loading; a late response is now dropped, and the default is the connection the graph's agents write through (`writes_through`), then the action's `validated_with` / `defined_with`, never a guess. (6) **review** — a parked write's card now offers **Review it in the Assurance Inbox** (`agentPerformance.openInbox()`, waiting for the view's load), and the agent is told a parked write is decided in the Inbox, never by Confirm. (7) **the Designer** — the owed act in a Next box (as in Govern); sections with titles; Granted to takes the platform's capability-to-agents pattern (class pills + a search + grouped by class) with the agents grounded on the graph first; Try it speaks the operation (an insert's fields say required · optional · `default: open`, the key once; an update asks which row and writes only what is filled in). **Verified:** the rehearsal in headless Chrome (light and dark), the rows in the warehouse (`L-1001` recorded, `L-1002` closed with its reason, the ledger naming the agent); `test_action_validation` §C (a statement runs as its backend's login — mutation-checked) and the GRANT wording; `test_action_define` (the purpose split; the race guard; the write-connection default); `test_action_surfaces` (Validate again); `test_extract_trust_inventory` (re-baselined, ledgered). - **Oct 2026**: **A configuration that could not be read is never answered with the template; an unreadable-file error discards the pool.** Production incident, 13 Oct 11:14–11:23 UTC: every ORM read of `tda_auth.db` failed with `file is not a database` (logins, token checks, configuration) until a restart; the file itself was intact (`quick_check` ok). Docker's event log shows a diagnostic process opening the live WAL database inside the container 63 s before the first failure — the mechanism is not reproduced; the rule now is to never open the live database from a second process. The incident exposed a data-loss path: `load_config` fell through EVERY exception to the new-user bootstrap — cached the template as the user's configuration and tried to save it over theirs; only the failing writes prevented the loss (no save succeeded in the window; verified from the log), and the cached template would have been persisted by the next ordinary save had the database recovered first. **Fix:** a failed read or an unparseable stored configuration raises `ConfigUnavailableError` (nothing cached, bootstrapped or saved); only a successful read with no record bootstraps; a migration failing after a good read returns the configuration read. And a SQLAlchemy `handle_error` hook treats unreadable-file errors as a disconnect, invalidating the connection and the pool so the next request reconnects (guaranteed fresh connections — not proven to have cleared this incident). **Gate** `test_config_read_failure` (12, both fixes mutation-checked). **Files:** `src/trusted_data_agent/core/config_manager.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/auth/database.py`, `docs/Architecture/SQLITE_CONCURRENCY.md`.

- **Oct 2026**: **A proposal row shows the state NOW, not the state it was answered in; the Designer's tooltips are the platform's.** Act II on production: asked "Leads also need a closure reason", @PXPROD proposed the attribute without drafting it (`drafted: false`) and offered the draft; the person clicked **Draft it**, which drafted it and re-drew the row in place — but that re-drawn row is not part of the stored turn, so on reload the turn showed "Not drafted." with the Draft button again, for an attribute that existed (a click would have been refused "already exists"). A first reading of the screenshots took the in-place row for the agent's own draft and added a `next` field to the proposal result (what is owed, decided in code — kept: it makes the agent's follow-up unambiguous); the session file showed the real sequence. **Fix:** every proposal row names the node a draft creates (`data-kg-node`); on every render, live and reloaded, the page reads the authored layer once per graph and a row whose node exists says "Drafted on the authored layer — <stage>" and offers nothing; it re-reads whenever the authored layer changes (a row stored before the stamp derives its node from its act, by the handler's own rule). Also: the proposal result carries `next` — what is owed, decided in code (`_act_next_step`): ALREADY DRAFTED → say so, the next acts (land, publish) are the person's in Govern, never offer again; NOT drafted → offer it — and both instruction levels say to follow it ("offer to draft only when it says NOT drafted, never after a draft"). The growth is recorded in the inventory ledger and re-baselined. **Verified** on a local server: a row proposed without a draft, then drafted, re-displayed — "Not drafted." + button before, "Drafted on the authored layer — not yet published." without it after, light and dark, no page errors. **Gates** `test_kg_act_ux` §2c (82), `test_kg_normalisation` (93), `test_action_define` (55), `extract_trust_inventory` OK. **Files:** `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/{handler.py,instructions.json}`, `static/js/ui.js`, `static/js/handlers/actionDesigner.js` (+ pins), `test/extract_trust_inventory.mjs`, `test/trust_inventory.baseline.json`.

- **Oct 2026**: **Defining an action is a person's act in the Actions Designer — prepared, one click.** Found walking Act II by hand: the Designer validates, signs, grants and previews, but nothing in the UI could DEFINE an action — on 7 Oct a script posted both contracts, and the first validation refused `record_lead` because its hand-typed contract declared `lead_id` an integer over a text column. **Fix:** a "Define an action" form. The person decides the concept, the operation, the writable columns, the bound, the role and the posture; the platform derives the deployed table (views excluded and refused by name), the key (the warehouse's unique index, else the model's), each column's contract type (the live dictionary through `contract_type_of`, the exact inverse of A2's rule — a derived contract cannot fail A2), the closed value domains, and the warehouse's roles for the table ranked per operation (exact rights from the one `TARGET_RIGHTS` table A6 reads, then a name that says the operation — on the shared system it prefills `Policing_Lead_ROLE_RECORD` for insert and `…_CLOSE` for update). **Frictionless:** the form opens prepared (the concept defined last, else an extension's first; its table read; the operation it has no action for yet; the suggested role), and with a warehouse chosen one click defines and validates, opening the A1–A6 checklist on the new row; validation defaults to the live connection. A text field leaving focus no longer rebuilds the form under the pointer — found in the browser run, where it swallowed the Define click. **Verified** in headless Chrome against a local server on the shared Teradata (Fitness `Customers`: prepared, one click → A1–A5 hold, A6 names the missing role; reopened on the next operation; no page errors) and the role read live against the Lead table. **Gate** `test_action_define` (33, mutation-checked). **Files:** `src/trusted_data_agent/core/action_types.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/dbdeploy/{action_validation,action_model}.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/api/action_routes.py`, `static/js/handlers/actionDesigner.js` (+ pins), `docs/Architecture/ACT_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

- **Oct 2026**: **A base update replaces what a walk produces — never an extension's realisation or a signed contract.** Raised in Act II on production ("if someone publishes a new version of the base model, does the Lead survive?"). An experiment on a copy of the shape: the Lead and its attributes survived a base update, but the schema, table and columns its landing wrote were DELETED — the concept survived, the model no longer knew where it lives (the `implements` edge dropped with no finding, since it started at the table). The keep rule read `layer` only and a landing writes physical-layer nodes. Mapping every reader of "what is the base" found the same split in four more places: signed **action types** (with their ledgers) and **data products** — logical-layer, authored by a person, never walked — were deleted by the same update; `split_layers` (the marketplace base listing and the agent-pack export) carried a landed table as **base**, an unpublished extension's included; the **released view** kept a pinned table of an unpublished extension and missed a published one landed after the pin; the base hash already used the right predicate (`is_extension_layer`), so the readers disagreed about what the base is. **Fix:** one keep rule, `kgstore.types.is_kept_on_replace` (authored + observed layers, an extension's realisation, the stacked contracts), applied by both backends (SQLite per row in Python, the generic path every other store uses); a walked node sharing a realisation's name takes its marks (`REALISATION_MARKS`) so it stays the extension's; a dropped container is stamped on the concept the realisation realises; a realisation whose concept is gone is listed (`realisations_orphaned`); `split_layers` splits by `is_extension_layer` (a realisation never travels as base; the extension's conformance composes with its own realisation, `realisations_of`); the released view drops realisations from the pinned base and adds the published ones with the edges that locate them (fingerprinted, so a later landing rebuilds it). **Gate** `test_extension_survives_base_update` (21: a published landed extension with an ALTERed base column, an action type + ledger and a data product through base updates on SQLite and the generic path, a warehouse-reading walk, dropped containers and orphans, the marketplace split, the released view — every fix mutation-checked); the existing replace/release/trust/pack/subscription suites green unchanged. **Files:** `src/trusted_data_agent/kgstore/{types,base,sqlite_backend}.py`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/graph_store.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/core/trust/extensions.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/core/kg_release.py`, `docs/Architecture/ACT_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

The end of the road, once reached, owes nothing: it now reads done (the intermediate states keep "now"). The suite's assertion said "marks published done" while testing for "now"; corrected. **Files:** `static/js/handlers/knowledgeGraphPanelHandler.js` (+ pins), `test/test_kg_act_ux.mjs`.

- **Oct 2026**: **A call made after the turn is booked once and shown on every engine; the Govern audit trail says when, who and what.** Found on production in Act II: the model-gap proposal suggestion (a paid call on the agent's model) showed in the Live Status as a bare card titled `proposal_suggestion`, twice (the form was opened twice — two paid calls), its tokens counted on the turn but nowhere in the reload's figures and nothing live. Mapping every path that assigns such a call to a turn, per engine class, found the same class elsewhere: the agent-memory extraction re-priced the WHOLE turn at the session model and sent its live step into a stream that had already closed; a **Coordinate** turn never replayed the steps appended to it (Smart Next Steps, memory, the judge); **Optimize** replaced a producer's step title with the raw type, and a bare stored event aborted its whole replay; **Ideate/Focus** turns shown as a summary card dropped them. **Fix:** one booking, `core/post_turn_usage.book_post_turn_call` — session totals, the turn's priced increment, consumption, the step persisted in the replay shape, and live on the notification channel (a per-call `token_update` and the step, session-guarded) — used by the proposal suggestion and the memory extraction; every engine's reload replays `turn.system_events` (Coordinate after its own events, the three summary-card fallbacks too), a stored title is kept, a bare legacy event is lifted into the payload shape on load; one details renderer (what it did, model, tokens, cost) in all three step renderers; the four title maps and the last-statement reader know both types; a reopened form reuses its suggestion. **Govern:** two publishes of the same extension (7 Oct replay, 12 Oct) read as one duplicated row because a row showed no time, no person and no subject; rows now store `actor` and `subject` (additive columns — the append-only triggers are untouched) and read `12 Oct 2026, 14:01 · you · published 1 entity · 9 attributes · conformant`; the section above a published Lead is **Added to the model**, the top pill **Model lifecycle**. **Gates** `test_post_turn_usage` (19, the booking executed against a stubbed store, mutation-checked), `test_kg_draft_views` §G (34; migration on an old table keeps it append-only; the wording executed), `test_model_gap_act` (28; reuse), `test_business_terms`. **Files:** `src/trusted_data_agent/core/post_turn_usage.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/proposal_suggest.py`, `components/builtin/memory/runtime.py`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/graph_store.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/core/ontology_governance.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/api/rest_routes.py`, `static/js/{ui,eventHandlers,notifications}.js`, `static/js/handlers/knowledgeGraphPanelHandler.js` (+ pins), `docs/Architecture/{COST_TRACKING,ACT}_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

- **Oct 2026**: **Landing an extension from the Govern dialog creates its database where the login may, at a size it has — and says so.** Found walking Act II by hand on production, before clicking Land: the Govern dialog sends no provisioning, so the backend's defaults applied — `CREATE DATABASE UDERIA_EXT_Policing_Core FROM dbc AS PERM = 10 GB` — as the model-operator login, which may create databases only under itself and has 1 GB. The 7 Oct replay passed parent and size by hand, so only the UI path was broken (and untested). **Fix:** `TeradataDeploymentBackend.provisioning()` decides both, deterministically, with the reason: parent = given > configured `database_parent` > the connection's default database > **the login's own space**; size = given > configured > **half of what the parent has free** (`DBC.DiskSpaceV`, capped at 10 GB); `ensure_database` creates exactly that. The deploy preview now carries `provisioning`; Govern says *"creates UDERIA_EXT_Policing_Core under uderia_ext_admin (the landing login's own space), 500 MB (half of the 1,000 MB uderia_ext_admin has free)"* and shows both as editable fields when a database is to be created — a change asks for a fresh preview, and Land sends what the preview showed. The declarative-model deploy passes its own parent and is unchanged. **Verified** as a dry run against the shared Teradata with the operator login (no DDL): the default and an override both read as above. Gate `test_landing_provisioning` (16). **Files:** `src/trusted_data_agent/dbdeploy/teradata_backend.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/kg_constructors/authored_deploy.py`, `static/js/handlers/knowledgeGraphPanelHandler.js` (+ pins), `test/test_landing_provisioning.py`, `docs/Architecture/ACT_ARCHITECTURE.md` §2.3.

- **Oct 2026**: **The trust battery runs in ~2 minutes instead of 13½; importing the platform takes ~1.3 s instead of ~3.3 s; drafts stay out of the model's views.** **(1) Parallel battery** — measured: 286 suites (214 Python, 72 JS), sequential 13 min 30 s, of which ~11 min was each Python suite importing the platform (~3 s) in its own process; JS ~15 s in total. `test/trust_battery.sh` now runs the suites through `xargs -P` (cores, ≤ 8; `--jobs=N`; `--serial` for the old behaviour) and prints the report in the listed order through the SAME judge the serial path uses (`_judge` → `classify_suite` → `_report`); a worker that leaves no exit code, or a suite that never ran, fails the battery. Suites that measure wall-clock time (`test_stream_activity_timeout`, `test_envelope_silence`, `test_eval_online`) run alone after the pool. `test_trust_battery_contract` drives the real worker and collector (42). **(2) Lazy provider SDKs** — `python -X importtime` showed ~60 % of the import was SDKs no import needs: google-genai, openai, anthropic, boto3 (imported at the top of `llm/handler.py`, `llm/client_factory.py`, `core/configuration_service.py`) and Google Cloud text-to-speech (`core/utils.py`, 0.87 s alone). New `llm/lazy_sdk.py`: a stand-in that imports its module on first attribute read — constructors, `except` clauses and `isinstance` read the real classes, so the semantics are the eager import's; voice keeps "not installed ⇒ None" via `find_spec`. Executor import 3.3 s → ~1.3 s; the server and every script benefit too. Gate `test_lazy_imports` (13; re-adding one eager import fails it by name); `test_llm_resilience`'s frozen retry clause reads the same classes through the stand-ins. **(3) A timing suite with honest margins** — `test_envelope_silence` checked a 0.15 s silence bound against 0.05 s ticks and failed under machine load; its bounds are now 0.5 s with silences a full second past them — the same cases; 16/16 green with eight copies running at once. **(4) Drafts stay out of the model's views** — after drafting a Lead on production the model's card read 286 entities (275 + the draft's 11 nodes) and the graph view drew the draft, while every agent — by the §2b rule — could not see it. The card's figures, the graph view (`graph-spec`, its totals) and a node's expansion (`node-neighborhood`) now leave unpublished authored nodes out, counted apart as `draft_entities`; the Drafts section lists them. `GraphStore.DRAFT_SQL` is the rule in SQL, gated to classify exactly as `_unpublished_authored` (`test_kg_draft_views`, 10). Verified live: draft created → card 275 (6 drafts apart), no Lead node in the view, CaseObject's expansion without it, the Drafts section listing it. **Battery:** green, ~2 min. **Files:** `test/trust_battery.sh`, `test/test_trust_battery_contract.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/llm/lazy_sdk.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/llm/{handler,client_factory}.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/core/{configuration_service,utils}.py`, `test/test_lazy_imports.py`, `test/test_llm_resilience.py`, `test/test_envelope_silence.py`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/graph_store.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/api/rest_routes.py`, `test/test_kg_draft_views.py`, `docs/Architecture/ACT_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

- **Oct 2026**: **A proposal in plain words lands — the form suggests what the concept records, and code supplies everything physical.** Two findings from Act II on production, both about the person extending the model: the form opened empty (the investigator had to invent every attribute), and what they typed had to be warehouse identifiers — "Assigned investigator" would have been skipped at landing as "not a plain identifier", and the link to CaseObject was created only if one attribute was spelled exactly like its physical key. **(1) Business terms in, the model's terms out** — new pure `agent/kg_constructors/business_terms.py`, run by `propose_entity` for every face (conversation, form, REST): each attribute becomes an identifier in the model's own naming style, the words kept as its `label`; the concept gets an identifier of its own as its key unless one was named; belonging to an entity adds the reference named exactly like that entity's declared key and typed like its deployed column (read from the graph); the platform's additions carry `added_by_platform` and the proposal row says "It records … The platform adds …" in words; idempotent across the Draft it pass; the authored listing returns `label`, `data_type`, `added_by_platform`. **(2) The suggestion** — opening the form asks `POST /v1/knowledge-graph/propose/suggest` (`agent/proposal_suggest.py`): one small call on the answering agent's own model for what such a concept records and which of the model's entities it belongs to; code drops anything that is an identifier, the reference, or an entity outside the model, bounds it, and books the call's tokens and cost to the note's turn (session totals, the turn's priced increment, consumption, a Live Status step); the form fills only what the person has not written and says whose suggestion it is; 403 while ACT is off. **(3) Named for what it is** — the form's button reads **Check the proposal** and the verdict *"the model's rules read it as …"* (here and in the KG theatre): the advisor is deterministic rules, not a person or a model, and the old wording suggested otherwise. **(4) A reference to a view is never declared** — both deployment backends now report each object's kind, and the delta planner declares a foreign key only to a TABLE parent: a parent realised as a view (every `Policing_Core` entity) keeps the reference in the model and lands the column, with the reason stated, instead of an `ALTER TABLE … REFERENCES v_CaseObject` that would fail. **Verified:** `test_business_terms.py` 45 (naming styles, the added key/reference and its type, idempotence, the view rule in the planner, the suggestion's filter, the wiring and booking), `test_model_gap_act.mjs` 26, `test_pdm_delta` 66, `test_act2_rehearsal` 110; end to end on a local server in headless Chrome — the gap question, the form filled from @PXPROD's model (*Summary · Status · Priority · Assigned investigator · Created date · Due date · Notes*, belongs to CaseObject), the advisor's verdict in words, Draft it → nine attributes with labels, `lead_id` the platform's key, `object_id VARCHAR(255)` the platform's reference; the local draft removed afterwards. **Files:** `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/kg_constructors/business_terms.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/proposal_suggest.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/api/rest_routes.py`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/handler.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/dbdeploy/{delta,teradata_backend,postgresql_backend}.py`, `static/js/ui.js` (+ pin cascade), `static/css/answer.css`, `templates/index.html`, `docs/Architecture/ACT_ARCHITECTURE.md` §2.2a, `test/test_business_terms.py`, `test/test_model_gap_act.mjs`, `test/test_component_enablement.py`, `test/test_kg_normalisation.py` (a drafted entity now carries the platform's reference to its parent), `test/trust_battery.sh`.

- **Oct 2026**: **Federal hardening: SAML, OIDC/OAuth, keys, idle sessions and append-only audit (branch `feature/federal-hardening`).** Closing the code gaps a standards review for an FBI briefing found. **SAML 2.0:** attributes are read only from the element the XML signature covers (the old code verified, discarded the result and read the original tree: signature wrapping); Audience must name this SP; a bearer SubjectConfirmation must name our ACS and answer an AuthnRequest we issued (the ACS route never consumed the RelayState, so nothing tied a response to a request); assertion IDs single use; DOCTYPE/entity declarations refused (XXE); IdP-initiated SSO off unless `TDA_SAML_ALLOW_IDP_INITIATED`. **OIDC:** back-channel logout tokens were decoded without a signature check; now verified per OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout 1.0 (JWKS, iss/aud of an enabled provider, logout event, iat, jti replay, no nonce) and they end the user's platform sessions (revoking the `sso_sessions` row alone never logged anyone out); id_token validation fails closed without `python-jose` (the unverified fallback is deleted); PKCE S256 on every OIDC authorization and on Google/GitHub/Microsoft/Okta social login (`TDA_OAUTH_PKCE=0` kill switch); the OAuth state check no longer logs the session. **Keys:** ONE `core/key_policy.py` replaces three copies of the default master key (read with identical semantics, no ciphertext changes meaning); `TDA_PROVENANCE_KEY_PASSPHRASE` encrypts the Ed25519 evidence key at rest (a plain file is migrated in place, same public key); **hardened mode** (`TDA_SECURITY_PROFILE=hardened` or `TDA_ENV=production`) refuses to start with the default/short master key or an unencrypted on-host signing key, and refuses session tokens with no server record; default mode only warns (no change for running deployments). **Sessions:** browser idle lock on real user input, shared across tabs, one-minute warning (`static/js/idleLock.js`); server-side idle expiry on token use (`auth_tokens.last_used_at`, self-applying); `TDA_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES` (default off, 30 in hardened mode). **Audit:** `core/audit_integrity.py` installs triggers making `audit_logs`, `sso_sync_events`, `kg_lifecycle_audit`, `pack_lifecycle_audit` append-only within `TDA_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS` (floor 365); the only allowed update is the database nulling `audit_logs.user_id` on account deletion; `User.audit_logs` no longer cascades deletes (deleting an account erased its audit trail); syslog / JSON-lines SIEM export (`TDA_AUDIT_SYSLOG`, `TDA_AUDIT_JSONL`). Gates: `test_saml_hardening` 26, `test_oidc_hardening` 32, `test_key_policy` 29, `test_session_idle` 21, `test_audit_integrity` 26, `test_idle_lock.mjs` 10, all in the battery; mutations fail by name. In-process smoke on a fresh database: login, authenticated call, logout then 401, idle limit injected, audit rows written and a delete refused. Still open: built-in MFA, FIPS 140-3 validated crypto, in-app TLS. **Turning it on (follow-up):** `docker-compose.yml` never forwarded `TDA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`; a deployment had its key only because `main.py` calls `load_dotenv()` on the working directory's `.env` (production's 34 stored secrets all decrypt with its own 43-character `.env` key, none with the default — verified read-only), so the key silently depended on where the server was started. And `maintenance/rotate_encryption_key.py` re-encrypted `user_credentials` only, so a rotation would have made connector credentials, OAuth tokens, SSO/SAML secrets and global TTS credentials unreadable (production holds 1 connector credential and 4 OAuth tokens). Now compose forwards all eight settings (empty = unset; `key_policy.master_key()` treats an empty key as unset, so `${TDA_ENCRYPTION_KEY:-}` can never become a literal empty key), and the script re-encrypts all three key families in one transaction, writes the key to `.env` (0600) without printing it; its default old key follows the server (environment, then `.env`, then the default). Gate `test_rotate_encryption_key` (28, encrypts with the platform's own modules and decrypts under the new key; dropping a source or changing a salt fails by name), `test_key_policy` 29 → 30. Operator procedure: [SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md §13.1](Architecture/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md). Doc: [SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md §13](Architecture/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md). Server restart (backend + templates).

- **Oct 2026**: **PROP-009 Evidence per result — built, all seven increments (branch `feature/evidence-per-result`).** Answers *"for this answer, what produced it, and was each part signed and unchanged at that moment?"* (PROP-009 (`docs/proposals/PROP-009-evidence-per-result.md`), [EVIDENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/EVIDENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md)). **(1)** Attestations are kept as history (a re-sign appends, never overwrites), agent and deployment attestations are scoped by owner (fixes the shared bootstrap-id defect: two accounts' `profile-default-chat` no longer share one row), and every signing key is registered so a retired key still verifies. **(2)** A bill of materials — every signed part the answer used, with its content hash and the attestation it matched — is sealed into each turn's chain (`trust.bom` step), on all five engines and genie; `verify_content` re-derives it. **(3)** A content-free evidence record per answer (outlives the session) and the answer's **Evidence** view: when answered · now, per part. **(4)** "Used by N answers" in the trust popover and an estate-wide **Evidence** tab in Trust (SIGNED/PROVEN route there). **(5)** Portable bundles: `POST /v1/evidence/export` carries the exact bytes each signature binds (captured from the badge's own resolvers, up to `TDA_EVIDENCE_CONTENT_LIMIT_BYTES`), the sealed chains and the keys; `scripts/verify_evidence.py` (needs only `cryptography`) and the offline page `static/trust/verify-evidence.html` (WebCrypto) reach the same verdict. **(6)** A hash-chained ledger of every attestation event and answer record, written in the same transaction; verification names breaks, edits, removals and records written around it, and proves an exported checkpoint is still reached. **(7)** Opt-in key custody (`TDA_EVIDENCE_SIGNER=command`: an HSM/KMS/Vault the server can ask but not read; every returned signature is verified before use) behind one signer seam (`core/signing.py`), and opt-in external anchoring of signed checkpoints (`TDA_EVIDENCE_ANCHOR=file|webhook|rfc3161`; the RFC 3161 request is byte-identical to `openssl ts -query`). Defaults are byte-identical. **Found on the way:** the anchor's skip rule compared only the sequence number, so a ledger truncated and re-extended (a reused number, a different hash) would never have been re-published — now sequence and hash; and an answer's chain is verified with the key it names, so older answers keep verifying after a custody switch (2,182 persisted chains re-verified). Gates (all in the battery, each mutation-tested): attestation history 55, BOM 50, view 57, estate 47, bundle 68, ledger 55, custody 50, UI 78. Live-verified: anchoring at startup and on demand, an audit export of 78 attestations passing 80/80 in the standalone verifier against the deployment fingerprint. **Closeout:** the opt-in paths were run against real services (SoftHSM 2 over PKCS#11 as the command signer, a real webhook receiver, freetsa.org for RFC 3161 — its receipt passes `openssl ts -verify` and fails on a one-byte change), and the verifier page plus the in-app *Verify in this browser* were driven in real Chrome on a real turn. That run found a gap: an exported answer's question and answer text were shown but never checked, so an edited answer read *9 of 9 verify*. Both verifiers now re-hash them against the chain's `query_intake`/`turn_complete` steps (first 4,096 code points, which is what is sealed; the export carries the answer field the chain sealed, and an older record's unsealed answer reads *not checked*, never verified); bundle gate 68 → **77**, three mutations fail by name (incl. JS slicing by UTF-16 unit). The summary no longer says *signer NOT confirmed* when the key matched and another check failed. Operator docs: manual §2.14 + §3.5b + control-map and process rows, FAQ §10 (12 entries), README section, two welcome-screen entries. **The fifth trust story** — [the-anatomy-of-an-answers-evidence.html](../static/trust/the-anatomy-of-an-answers-evidence.html), built from a real hosted-instance answer (`@PXPROD` on the demo account, *179,193 robberies*, 8 parts all signed) with a try-it panel that verifies the exported file in the reader's browser and refuses three tampers by name (answer number, model, a forged signature); its inline verifier is kept equal to `evidenceVerify.js` by `scripts/build_evidence_verifier_page.py` (`STORIES`), and gate §I pins the sample and every tamper. Building it found two platform defects, both fixed: extensions, action types and data products hashed with a private `_canon_hash`, so their exports read *changed since signed* (now through `content_hash`, byte-identical, gate §H); and an extension was named by its raw `ext-<uuid>` in every answer's evidence (now *extension by <user>*, `extensions.extension_label`, gate §J). `EVIDENCE_ARCHITECTURE` is now rendered on the trust site. Bundle gate 77 → **97**.
