- **Oct 2026**: **ACT four eyes — a designated approver decides an agent's parked writes, never its owner; the supervisor gets their own agent (branch `feature/act-business-operating-model`, PROP-008 §5.4a).** Before, a parked write could be approved only by the account owning the agent, so the Act II investigator/supervisor split was played by one person. Now `authorityConfig.actions.approvers` (usernames; `GET/POST /v1/actions/approvers`, refusing an unknown account `approver_unknown` and the owner `approver_is_owner`) moves the decision: the park resolves the names (`action_perform.resolve_approvers`; the owner is never their own approver) and stores ids on the review item (`approvers_json`, self-applying); a designation naming no active account **refuses the park** — never parked where nobody may decide, never a silent fallback to the owner. ONE rule `review_queue.may_decide` (approvers ⇒ only they; else the owner): the approve route answers `403 not_your_decision` before anything runs, `decide` enforces it underneath and records `decided_by`. Visibility: `list_items(awaiting_me=True)` only on the decision surfaces (reviews listing, the new `TDA_Action pending_approvals` verb); Trust History, the agent story and the audit pack read the caller's own agents' items alone (a shared tag never attributes another person's write); `pending_count` counts what THIS person owes. The write still runs as the owner's agent on the owner's connection; ledger and act log name the approver (`approved_by`; act log gains `approvers`), Trust History says whom it awaited and who decided (`decided_by`; a pre-column decision names nobody, never a guess), face word `On approval`. Inbox: an owner's write awaiting someone else shows `awaiting <approver>` with no buttons and no danger dot, never counted toward the owner's badge; another owner's write names them and never folds into the caller's same-tag agent. Answer: `pending_approvals` rows with Approve / Reject the person clicks (`renderer.decideApproval` posts the review route and flips the row) — no agent ever approves. **Two defects the live run found, fixed at the root:** (1) replaying a parked row's invocation hash through `/perform` parked the same write twice — `claim_action_confirmation` now also refuses an invocation the turn's AGENT already acted on (`409`); (2) a client disconnecting mid-approval cancelled the handler between the write and its disposition, leaving a PERFORMED write on a PENDING item — the write and the disposition now run as one unit under `asyncio.shield`. **Setup (local):** account `demo_supervisor` (user tier, password 0600 in `~/.tda/act2_supervisor_login.json`, never printed), its agent `@PXSUP` (Ideate, action component only, default + REST-activated), designated approver of demo's `@PXPROD`. **Live, end to end (Oct 7):** investigator closes lead 4 → parked for the supervisor; owner approve 403; hash replay 409; supervisor asks `@PXSUP` "what closures await my approval?" → approves → 1 row, receipt; Trust History: *Parked write (close_lead) approved by Detective Sergeant (supervisor)*; browser-verified (owner row without buttons, supervisor Approve flips to `Done · 1 row · receipt`, zero page errors). **Recorded open:** approvers are per agent (no per-action approver or quorum); no profile-editor field yet; an update that changes nothing still parks (`no value changes`). Gates: new `test_action_four_eyes` (**47**, in the battery; 8 mutations fail by name), `test_action_rest` 74 → **75** (replay refusal, mutation fails by name), `test_action_surfaces` (a pinned refusal literal restated as its property). Docs: ACT_ARCHITECTURE §3.5 + §6 + §7, PROP-008 §5.4a + §14.5, AGENT_AUTHORITY §2b, restAPI (reviews fields, 403, approvers endpoint); trust site re-rendered. **Reset made accurate (operator: "make sure that the reset script is accurate"), audited against every table keyed on the rehearsal's sessions or graph:** `act2_reset.py` now archives the supervisor's sessions as that account (`supervisor_sessions`, recorded by the driver), reads the legacy `session` key too, removes the graph's usage telemetry for the removed nodes AND action types (`kg_entity_usage`), names a LANDED tuning proposal with its DDL and keeps its record (a structure on a `Policing_Core` table is never undone as a side effect), and states what it keeps on purpose (consumption ledger, lifecycle audit, the supervisor setup; session delete is the platform's archive). **Platform defect found by the audit:** deleting a scheduled task never removed its run history — the schema's `ON DELETE CASCADE` never ran because the scheduler's connection does not switch foreign keys on; `task_scheduler.delete_task` now deletes the runs in the same transaction (`test_scheduler_actions` +1, mutation fails by name). New `act2_supervisor.py` sets the supervisor up idempotently. - **Oct 2026**: **The Act II rehearsal — the whole ACT road driven as an investigator on the policing core model, and the eighteen defects it found (gate §A–§R), each fixed at the root (branch `feature/act-business-operating-model`, PROP-008 §14).** Every scene of the Act II story was driven locally as `demo_walkthrough` through @PXPROD against Teradata 20.00.22.31 (+ PostgreSQL 17.11): a question the model cannot answer → a proposed `Lead` → land in `UDERIA_EXT_Policing_Core` → publish → sign → record / close / undo leads through signed actions (conversation, flow, schedule, dashboard tile, MCP), parked closes decided in the Assurance Inbox, workload tuning, a second warehouse, an offline-verified receipt and the audit pack. **Fixed:** a question about a concept the model does not record now LEADS with that fact (`_model_gap`) instead of answering from a near neighbour; - **Oct 2026**: **The model's markdown renders. It never leaks as syntax, and platform notes always read as the platform's.** Operator, on a Focus turn (`@UDERIA`, session 6a476a76 turn 3) whose answer ended in a literal `***` and `*Source: … (Collection: …)*`, then: *"address the whole problem class"* and *"annotations must be clearly visible as annotations."* **Root causes:** (1) the answer renderer (`formatter._render_standard_markdown`) only treated `---` as a rule and only did `**bold**` and `` `code` `` inline. A battery of about 25 common markdown forms found most leaking as literal text: `***`/`___`/`* * *` (the last as a list item `* *`), `*italic*`/`_italic_`, `~~strike~~`, `[links](…)`, `1.` ordered lists, `> ` quotations, `+` bullets, task lists, escapes, closing `##`. `<https://…>` vanished as an unknown tag, and raw HTML from the model or a corpus document reached `innerHTML` unescaped. (2) The model copied the citation line it was shown (`Source: … (Collection: …)`, `executor._format_knowledge_for_prompt`), but the grounding support set held chunk *content* only. So the answer's own citation was flagged "unsupported" (`README.md`, `Uderia Documentation`, …), and the two lanes each had their own chunk extractor. (3) Every note producer concatenated `html + note`, so the Scope note landed below nine collapsed sources; the guardrail annotation still drew its own inline-styled orange div. **Fixes, all at the root:** ONE inline renderer `formatter.md_inline` and extended block rules (rules decided before lists, `<ol start>`, list-type changes close cleanly, task checkboxes, recursive quotations, setext `===`). Code spans and escapes are held aside before anything else; links only for http/https/mailto, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, quote-safe attributes; images linked by alt text, never fetched. Prose is HTML-escaped (an existing entity is kept); attribute-free `<br>`/`<b>`/… are allowed. Identifiers are never mangled (`snake_case`, `__init__`, `a*b*c`, `*args`). The streamed-line client mirror (`ui.js` `_provInline`/`_provTailHtml`, plus ordered/quote joining at the head/tail seam) renders identically; it had pinned the opposite `<b>` rule from the server. ONE chunk-support definition `eval.types.chunk_support_text` / `RunRecord.retrieved_chunk_texts` = content + the citation line, read by the in-flight gate and the post-hoc `run_context`. The Focus and Ideate engines now record each chunk's `collection_name` (found live: the gate's chunk-only event dropped the repository). ONE note placement `answer_surface.place_note`, directly under the prose and above the first evidence element, used by grounding, honesty, compute lineage, budget, confidential and guardrail notes; the guardrail note is now the shared `Guardrail` note kind. A model-written quotation (`blockquote.ans-md-quote`: body size, 1px neutral hairline, no icon/kind word) can never look like a note. Also: a Scope note no longer reads "tools?." once the code ticks are stripped. **Proof:** new gate `test/test_markdown_render.py` (**182**, in the battery; executes the shipped JS for parity, replays turn 3's real shape); **11 mutations fail by name**. Assertions restated as properties: `test_answer_stream_dom` (the tail's `<b>` rule) and `test_guardrails` (the retired orange div). Battery GREEN; `ui.js` pin cascaded through 25 importers to `main.js 10.21`, `answer.css 2.1`. Live on `@UDERIA` (headless Chrome, `modern` and `light` themes): rule + italic source line, no `***`, the citation not flagged, the remaining genuine Scope finding above the Sources row. Already-stored answers keep the HTML they were saved with (re-ask to see the new rendering). Server restart (backend + template). **Follow-up (same day, "did we lose the trust annotations?"):** a side-by-side run of every annotation producer on the previous release and the new code (grounding annotate/block, honesty ×3, guardrail annotate/redact, figure lineage, budget, confidential) found no lost notes, but two real issues, both fixed. (a) The unsupported-claim highlighter searched for the claim as written in markdown, so a claim containing `*italics*` lost its highlight once italics rendered. It now searches for the claim rendered by the same inline renderer, allowing formatting tags inside the match only when they open and close within it; this also means a claim with an apostrophe is highlighted (the old escape never matched it). (b) **The Conversation lane (Ideate+tools, and every expert of that class) never showed gate notes:** it rendered the HTML from the GATED text, so a gate's sentence was drawn as model prose (`> This answer may reference…`), which would now have looked like a model quotation. - **Oct 2026**: **Flow topology templates, increments 3 + 4 — iterative, debate, teacher–student and pair programming on ONE loop structure (branch `feature/flow-topology-templates`).** Operator: *"proceed — but think deep on how to fill in the remaining topologies."* The four dialogic shapes differ only in who sits in the loop, what each reads and who decides, so the engine gained three general things, not four special cases — new pure `core/flow_rounds.py`: **round history** (inside a loop every node reads `round`, `max_rounds`, `previous_<alias>` — always defined, empty in round 1, so `str.format` never leaves a prompt unsubstituted — and a bounded `history` transcript; after the loop `history`, `outcome`, `rounds_completed`, `converged`, `exit_reason`), **a convergence exit** (`scope.exit_when = {node, condition}`; absent ⇒ the fixed-iteration loop byte for byte; a missing or unevaluable verdict never stops the loop and is reported), and **one verdict shape** `{passed, score, verdict, feedback}` (an abstention is `passed=None` and never stops it). Two node types: **`judge`** (an agent reviewing in free text ending `VERDICT:`/`SCORE:` lines, through the ordinary LLM-node path incl. the slot refusal, or the eval **judge panel** via `build_panel` + consensus, its cost billed to the run) and **`artefact`** (binds the round's code to ONE canvas per run, a version per round). `_run_scope` runs nodes of one dependency level concurrently under `parallelExecution` (the debaters of a round), pins each participant's session across rounds, emits `flow_scope_round_complete`/`flow_scope_complete`. Generators: iterative (worker → judge, panel by default), debate (debaters → moderator → synthesiser after the loop), teacher–student (the teacher teaches and decides), pair programming (driver → canvas → navigator, who decides) — the back edge is `type: "cycle"`, `flow_layout.frame_scopes` sizes the loop frame. Canvas: a loop frame with the exit condition and a live round badge, judge nodes with a verdict chip, the canvas node with *Open canvas · vN*, and a dedicated **loop-back edge** (a smoothstep between stacked nodes collapsed onto the straight line); the picker preview draws the loop. **Live round against real agents found three defects, each fixed at the root:** (1) **a flow could not see code an agent put into a canvas** — the conversation agent's auto-canvas strips a fenced block from `final_answer_text`, so the driver wrote code every round and the flow saw prose; the turn's final payload now carries `canvas_contents` (data, every canvas incl. a real `TDA_Canvas` call) and every flow LLM node folds it back into its output (`_fold_canvas_contents`) — a general fix for any flow node whose agent uses canvases; (2) prose about code was saved as the code → `code_from_reply` keeps the last real version and tells the next round no code arrived; (3) **a navigator told "no code was received" still passed** → `convergence_gap`: a round whose artefact got no code cannot end the loop, decided in code. Live after the fixes: iterative 3 rounds, ended honestly at the limit with the panel's feedback carried forward; pair programming, debate and teacher–student converged with real content. Gates: new `test_flow_dialogic` (**126**, in the battery; nine mutations fail by name), `test_flow_topologies` 194, picker 89, version pins 103; battery GREEN. Pins cascaded for `workspacePanelHandler` (opens the run's canvas) to `main.js 10.13`. **Follow-up (same branch):** every addable node type now comes from ONE declaration `ADDABLE_NODES` (the left palette, ⌘K, the edge "+" menu, the number keys incl. **6 Judge / 7 Canvas**, the help overlay and the new-node defaults — five hand-kept lists had drifted, so judge and canvas reached none of them; a dropped node now gets the same defaults as a clicked one, a judge defaulting to the eval panel); the **round limit is editable on the loop frame** (− / + stepper, disabled while running, `update_scope` clamps to 1–20 via `flow_db.clamp_scope_rounds`, version label *"Set loop to up to N rounds"*); **a finished latest run is restored on reopen** (`_runOutcomeOverlay`: statuses, verdicts, canvas + version, how each loop ended — the same fields the live stream sets). The toolbar's **default-profile control opens the shared agent picker** (search + IFOC class pills — the Inspector's filter idiom; FlowSelect only as the fallback). Gates: picker 89 → **109**, dialogic 126 → **129**; five mutations fail by name; battery GREEN; verified in headless Chrome (palette, restored outcome, stepper round-trip, class pills). **Then the remaining items:** loops are made, edited and removed on the canvas through ONE rule set, new `core/flow_loops.py` (`make_loop` / `update_loop` / `remove_loop` / `adopt_scope`; the canvas, the REST patch ops and the TDA_Flow tool all route through it; a refusal is a `LoopError` → 400 with a code and the fix in words) — *Make loop* on a multi-selection, *Repeat as a loop* on a step, ⌘K, and a loop editor from the frame's *Edit* (name, rounds, stop rule: none / judge passes / judge passes with a score ≥ t / custom condition evaluated before storing, history window, remove); *Earlier runs* in the status bar paints any of the last 15 finished runs through one painter that clears the previous run first; each loop's `history_window` is editable and the debate template defaults it to 2 (a step after the loop still reads all of it); recently used agents are offered as "recent" suggestion chips on open slots (`flow_topologies/recent.py`; never fills, accepted classes only, max three per slot). Both levels now name every available topology, the loop ops and the judge/artefact node types (kept under the P2 minimal-exposure cap), the manifest offers `delete_scope` and no longer claims a loop's members are editable in place; new gate section 18 (dialogic **175**) ties the tool text to `catalog()` so it cannot fall behind the registry again (the old text fails 6 by name). - **Oct 2026**: **Flow topology templates (PROP-007, increments 1 + 2) — a flow is born from a shape, its gaps are slots, and the picker pre-fills them from a coordinator's experts (branch `feature/flow-topology-templates`).** Operator: a template approach in the Flow component with a graphical topology picker; a template is a COPY, never re-applied; the picker pre-fills from a coordinator's experts where it makes sense; as frictionless as possible. **Increment 1 (the model, `core/flow_topologies/`):** the registry as DATA (`registry.py` — ten rows incl. the nine Loom topologies + blank, each with parameters/ranges, slot roles, `requires`; a shape whose primitives are not shipped is DECLARED and shown greyed with its `unavailable_reason`, never hidden; swarm is a hand-off to the coordinator editor, not a flow), four shipped generators (pipeline · parallel · fork-join · conditional) producing ordinary `task_llm` nodes carrying `data.slot = {role, required, accepts, hint}` — a slot is a FIELD, never a node type, so every existing code path sees a normal node once filled; `slots.py` is the one safety rule the executor, REST and tool handler all call: an open REQUIRED slot is refused BEFORE the profile cascade can fall back to a default (`FlowSlotUnfilledError` → REST 409 `flow_slots_unfilled`, recovery-shaped); `definition.template = {id, version, params}` stamps the generation (copy, never link). **Increment 2 (the picker + the surfacing):** ONE server-side `preview()` (shared by picker/REST/tool, `GET /v1/flows/templates/<key>`) applies the pre-fill rules — SYMMETRIC roles fill in the coordinator's declared `slaveProfiles` order with the adapting parameter clamped to the expert count (a parameter the user TOUCHED is never overridden), ASYMMETRIC roles get suggestion chips only, a JUDGE slot defaults to `judge_panel`, a non-genie source is a suggestion on every slot; **fills travel keyed by ROLE as ordered lists with holes** (`{stage: [null, "profile-b", null]}`) because node ids are minted per generation. The picker (`openTopologyPicker` in `components/builtin/flow/renderer.js`, plain DOM, theme tokens, monochrome glyphs keyed identically to the registry) reaches from three entry points — the profile Flows tab New button, the Workspace Flows section `+`, and the canvas switcher's *New flow…*; the canvas marks an open slot (dashed accent node, `slot · role` badge, role+hint subtitle), the Inspector relabels Profile ID as *Agent for this slot* filtered to `accepts`, **Run Flow is disabled while any required slot is open** (an `N slots to fill` pill opens the health panel), and ONE `_slotIsOpen` reading mirrors `slots.py` so a slot never inherits the flow default. Flow rows carry `open_slot_count` chips. **Gates:** `test_flow_topologies` **170** + new `test_flow_topology_picker.mjs` **60** (executes the shipped picker under the DOM stub against the REAL `preview()` via a Python subprocess; in the battery); **nine mutations fail by name** — one first ESCAPED (asymmetric filled by order was an equivalent mutant on fork-join with 3 experts/3 workers) and the conditional fixture closed it; one was caught only by a crash and the assertions were made to name it. **Found by the gate, not review:** the Create button had NO click listener (Enter only); the DOM stub lied in three places (`remove()` left `isConnected` true, `el.id` did not reflect to the attribute so `getElementById` missed it, no `removeEventListener`) — fixed in `test/dom_stub.mjs`. Pins cascaded (`flowsHandler 1.1`, `workspacePanelHandler 1.3` → `main 10.6`; pins gate 101). Battery: every red reproduces identically at HEAD (missing optional packages in this container, no bootstrapped DB). **Operator-testing round (same branch):** pre-fill became an explicit **Start from a team** selector — a coordinator is listed as a ROSTER (*@POLICE — @NIBRS, @CASEDF, @PDOCS*) beside *Choose agents individually*, with the boundary stated (*"runs these agents in this flow's fixed order — @POLICE's own routing is not used"*); a flow never intercepts the coordinator, which decides per question at run time while a flow runs a graph fixed when built (they meet only at the roster, and a slot may HOLD a coordinator). Every agent choice — picker slots, the team selector, the canvas Inspector's agent field — opens the platform's ONE agent picker (`AgentAnatomy.openAgentPicker`: search + IFOC class pills + keyboard), restricted to what a slot accepts; it gained an optional `specialRow.icon` so *Leave this slot open* shows the open-slot mark. Parallel got its own glyph (lanes, no join) and the gate asserts no two glyphs are equal; slot titles are the node labels. The topology suites' fake aiohttp now starts from the real module (google-auth imported mid-test had crashed the refusal sections). - **Oct 2026**: **The EXPLAIN plan panel holds a large plan — segments, a graph laid out for the width it is shown in, findings folded by kind.** A real 37-step plan showed only fragments: nine source tables in one row made the graph ~2,300 px wide, so the steps sat off screen and only edges were visible; four identical product-join sentences and a dozen "redistributes" lines pushed the graph below the fold. **Segments:** the panel (and a dashboard tile) is split into Overview (stat tiles, the comparison, findings, *where the time goes*) · Graph · Steps (every step, sortable by order/time/rows, filter to steps with a finding) · Statement; ARIA tablist, arrow keys, last segment remembered; a re-explained plan with a comparison opens on Overview. **Screen-aware graph:** `layoutPlan(spec, {maxWidth, tables})` narrows nodes, wraps long rows (a parallel group's rows inside one labelled frame), widens nodes into spare width, and folds the source tables into the steps that read them when they would not fit one row (switchable: *Tables in a row / in steps*); a ResizeObserver re-lays it out on panel resize / fullscreen; zoom re-lays out for `width / zoom` (zooming out shows more of the plan), *Whole plan* = `fitAllZoom`. **Reading:** selecting a step lights its edges and the steps at their other end, the step's facts dock under the graph (beside it in a wide container), ←/→/↑/↓ walk steps in execution order, Escape clears; a node carries a bar for its share of the estimated time; the key is a toggle (shown when there is room). **Findings:** `groupFindings` folds every kind found more than once into one line — the finding once, its explanation once, a chip per step in execution order, worst first. The answer's preview card is laid out for an answer's width. A real 195-line Teradata plan (`EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM DBC.UserRoleRightsV`: 9 tables, 4 parallel groups) joins the fixtures. Gate `test_explain_plan_renderer` 72 → **125**; verified in headless Chrome, both themes, narrow panel and fullscreen. - **Oct 2026**: **"Pin to dashboard" is one act in one place — the footer of every pinnable answer row; the floating hover button is gone; the EXPLAIN preview draws its steps again.** The act existed in four forms: a floating hover button injected over chart / knowledge-graph / flow / plan cards by a page-wide observer (it covered the card's own controls — the open-in-panel control among them — and could not be found without hovering), a footer button on data tables, a Next Steps chip that asked the agent to pin (a turn and tokens for a click), and the agent's own `add_tile`. - **Oct 2026**: **A start that changes the database schema backs it up first, and refuses when it cannot (Loom adoption topic 3, the schema ledger).** Uderia re-applies `schema/*.sql` and its self-applying ALTERs on every start with no record of what was applied. New `core/schema_ledger.py` wraps that bootstrap (`auth/database.init_database`) without replacing it: **(1)** a fingerprint of everything that can change an existing database — the schema files, the DDL lines of the Python sources (CREATE / ALTER / DROP / ADD COLUMN / RENAME, whitespace-normalized; an unrelated edit does not move it), the ORM's DDL and the release version (`vMAJOR.MINOR`, so a commit after the tag is not an upgrade); **(2)** when it differs from the last recorded start on a database that holds tables, a `VACUUM INTO` copy is taken BEFORE the bootstrap (free space checked, the copy integrity-checked, the newest 3 upgrade backups kept, maintenance backups never touched) — `prepare()` runs before the bootstrap's `try`, so under `TDA_SCHEMA_BACKUP=required` (default, compose-forwarded) a failed backup refuses the start before anything changes; `best_effort` proceeds with a warning, `off` skips it; **(3)** every start is a `schema_ledger` row (version, fingerprints, backup, the actual schema hash before and after); a start that changed the schema while its fingerprint did not is flagged `changed_without_backup` — the fingerprint's blind spot is measured; **(4)** a drift report — every schema file applied to an empty in-memory database statement by statement and compared with the real one — at admin `GET /api/v1/admin/schema/ledger`; it reports, never repairs. **Found:** ten schema files (10, 11, 22, 25, 26, 29, 32, 36, 42, 44) are never applied by the bootstrap; on this instance the drift names `installed_assurance_modules` (declared, never created), `schema_version` and `kg_profile_assignments.created_at` (the inline CREATE diverges from the file). Live: the first start under the ledger took a 993 MB backup in about 4 s; the fingerprint is stable across processes. Not adopted: a dry run (the bootstrap's change set cannot be computed without running it; the backup is the undo). Gate `test_schema_ledger` (**45**, in the battery); five mutations fail by name. **Production:** the first start after this deploy takes one backup of `tda_auth.db` next to it. - **Oct 2026**: **A provider that stops sending is cut INSIDE the resilience envelope, per attempt, on every lane — retried, served by the signed fallback, recorded.** The open work the Loom adoption plan listed for the already-adopted stream timeout. Until now the silence limit (`llm/streaming.py`) wrapped the whole `call_llm_api` from the executor: the envelope's retry/fallback loop runs inside that call, so a stalled stream was cut OUTSIDE it — never retried, never served by the signed fallback, never recorded — and the LangChain lanes (Ideate+tools, Focus, Coordinate) had no limit at all (the S4 config comment had named the gap for Anthropic/Google SDK clients only). Now, under `RESILIENCE_ENVELOPE`: ONE implementation, `streaming.activity_limit` (a context manager; `await_with_activity_timeout` and a new per-chunk `iterate_with_activity_timeout` are built on it); the handler's attempt body runs inside it (`_attempt_limit` — re-indented mechanically, `git diff -w` = one line), so every direct `call_llm_api` caller (the adapter's report calls, session naming, judges, the recommender, components) is covered; the LangChain wrapper runs every provider call under it (attempts, continuations, the signed fallback; streams per chunk). `resilience.classify` reads the cut: `stalled`/`no_response` → a retryable `timeout` (≤ `TIMEOUT_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, or the signed fallback at once — an `llm_recovery` step), `ceiling` → terminal `stream_ceiling` (a retry would write the same long answer); a LangChain stream that already yielded is never re-run. - **Oct 2026**: **Loom adoption integration (a) completed — reserved words in every name position, `COUNT(DISTINCT *)`, and a warning for a decimal division Teradata truncates.** Each form measured on Teradata 20.00 before any code. **(1) Reserved words** — Teradata names the word as "the '<word>' keyword" wherever a name is expected, not only after `AS`: a table alias (`SELECT input.x … input` → 3706 "between the 'SELECT' keyword and the 'input' keyword"), a qualified column (`t.Count` → 3707 "between '.' and the 'Count' keyword"), a bare column (`SELECT Threshold` → 3706). The reader (`sql_dialect.reserved_alias_from_error`) takes those three anchors (after `AS`, after `SELECT`, after `.`) and no others — the battery caught a first, broader version claiming production's 3707 "between '(' and the 'TD_SYSFNLIB' keyword" (a function expected, not a reserved word), which must reach the LLM correction; the existing rewrite quotes the word only where sqlglot reads it as an identifier, so a misplaced real keyword (`FROM WHERE`) is declined. Both consumers inherit it (Optimize `TeradataReservedAliasStrategy`, the ReAct/Navigator retry). **(2) `COUNT(DISTINCT *)`** (3706) → `COUNT(*)` over `SELECT DISTINCT *` in `teradata_syntax_rewrite`, for one plain source only (alias and WHERE kept; a join, a comma join, another select item, GROUP BY/HAVING/QUALIFY/ORDER BY, a derived table, a set operation → declined, because there the count is a choice). **(3) `1.0/n` — a warning, never a rewrite** (the fix changes the result): `7/100.0` returns 0.1 (true 0.07), `1.0/3` 0.3, `7.25/2` 3.62 — silently. New `agent/preflight/decimals.py` finds, on the parse tree, a division whose operands carry a decimal literal of ≤ 2 places with no FLOAT and no explicit decimal cast with more places; a percentage multiplier (`x*100.0/total`) and a division wrapped in `ROUND`/`TRUNC`/a decimal `CAST` to no more places are left alone. After the statement RAN, the one SQL gate (`sql_gate_after`, every lane) attaches a note naming the expression and both remedies (a FLOAT operand, a literal with more places); a failed statement gets none; Teradata only. `PREFLIGHT_DECIMAL_MODE` (env `TDA_PREFLIGHT_DECIMAL_MODE`, compose-forwarded, default `observe` — logged and tallied; `enforce` attaches the note). **Fixed on the way:** the Preflight SQL reading on the dial named every non-database finding "an unknown database or column" — a value or decimal finding now names itself, and under `enforce` it says the finding was noted, not blocked; a decimal-only note no longer stamps an empty `preflight_unverified` list. ONE rewrite, two consumers: the Optimize chain's new `TeradataSyntaxStrategy` (first dialect strategy, a System Self-Correction step) and the ReAct / Navigator retry (`_syntax_retry_core`, first in `dialect_retries`, recorded as a `teradata_syntax` rewrite). Like the TOP and reserved-alias fixes it runs only AFTER Teradata refused the statement, so an MCP backend that accepts the original (the adapter cannot know the dialect) is never touched. - **Oct 2026**: **The Teradata SQL rules we teach a model were checked against a live Teradata — two were wrong, and our own LIMIT→TOP rewrite could produce a refused statement.** Came out of assessing Loom's 84 Teradata patterns for import as a progressive skill library: every SELECT in them was run through `EXPLAIN` on Teradata 20.00.22.31 (read-only). **Loom's patterns could not be imported as they are** (they were then corrected statement by statement and executed — see the `teradata-patterns` entry): of the 54 patterns whose functions exist on this system, 40 hold at least one statement the database rejects (102 of 267 EXPLAINs were refused; 38 of those were artifacts of the mechanical placeholder substitution, which leaves about 64 real defects — roughly a quarter of the statements); confirmed defects include `SELECT *, expr` (Error 3706 — it must be `t.*`), `LIMIT`, reserved-word aliases (`AS amp`, `AS value`), `COUNT(DISTINCT *)`, DBC columns that do not exist (`DBC.StatsV.SampleSize`, `DBC.QryLogV.MaxSpoolUsage`) and the claim that `EXCEPT` is not valid (it is). 20 further patterns call functions this system does not have (`AI_*`, `TD_HNSW`, `TD_VectorNormalize`, `TD_LinReg` …). **The same check on our own content found:** (1) `teradata-sql-expert` rule 3 and the three bootstrap session primers in `tda_config.json` taught `LIMIT n OFFSET m → SELECT TOP n … QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() … > m` — TOP and QUALIFY in one SELECT is **Error 6916**; now a QUALIFY window with no TOP (`BETWEEN m+1 AND m+n`), and for a row limit on a QUALIFY query, TOP outside a derived table. (2) rule 6 taught `CAST(date_col AS VARCHAR(10)) = '2025-01-01'` — the text follows the session's date format (`'25/01/01'` under IntegerDate), so the comparison **matches nothing and raises no error** (measured: 0 rows where the DATE literal finds 5); now `date_col = DATE '2025-01-01'`. (3) rule 11 implied `LISTAGG` works without DISTINCT — it is not a function here; now `XMLAGG`. (4) `sql_dialect.teradata_top_rewrite` (one rewrite, Optimize strategy + ReAct retry) turned `… QUALIFY … LIMIT n` into `SELECT TOP n … QUALIFY …`, trading Error 3706 for 6916; it now declines when the OUTER query block carries a QUALIFY (a QUALIFY inside a derived table is another block and is still rewritten; folding the limit into the QUALIFY is not equivalent, so there is no mechanical rewrite). **Consequence:** the skill's content hash moves (v1.1.0), so a signed agent that carries `teradata-sql-expert` reads `changed` until re-signed. The bootstrap primers ship disabled; copies already stored in user profiles are not rewritten (locally 19 profiles carry them, none enabled). Gates: new `test_teradata_sql_rules` (**31** CI-pure; **42** with `TDA_LIVE_TERADATA=1`, which runs the refuted and the taught forms against catalog views), `test_sql_dialect_react` 66 → **69**; 7 mutations fail by name. - **Oct 2026**: **The LLM call timeout is a limit on the provider's silence, not on the length of the call.** Found by reading Loom (teradata-labs' Go agent framework), which times streamed calls per read. `executor._call_llm_and_update_tokens` wrapped every call in `asyncio.wait_for(120 s)`, including calls that carry the answer stream (Ideate, Focus synthesis): a streamed answer still being written at 120 s was cut with *"did not respond within 120 seconds"* while its tokens were arriving — a long report, or any slow local model. Now `llm/streaming.py:await_with_activity_timeout`: every provider stream helper marks each chunk it receives (`note_activity` — every chunk, not only text: a reasoning, tool-input or usage chunk is the provider working), and the limit counts from the last mark. A call that streams nothing is cut exactly where it was (120 s after it started); a stream that falls silent is cut 120 s after its last chunk and says *"stopped sending its answer"*; a stream that never stops meets `LLM_STREAM_MAX_SECONDS` (600, 0 = none). The call still runs in the caller's task (`asyncio.timeout`, as `wait_for` does on Python 3.12), so `handler.LAST_CALL_USAGE` is read afterwards as before; the Bedrock read runs on a worker thread, where context variables are not visible, so the mark is handed over explicitly. **Not covered:** the Anthropic helper marks text deltas only (the SDK's `text_stream`; no thinking is configured on that lane today); the LangChain lanes and the adapter's direct report call never had the whole-call limit. Gate `test_stream_activity_timeout` (**32**, in the battery — the helper, the five provider helpers over fake wires, the real executor method); **12 mutations fail by name** (one first crashed the suite and its check was hardened). Server restart (backend). Files: `llm/streaming.py`, `agent/executor.py`, `core/config.py`, `test/{test_stream_activity_timeout.py,trust_battery.sh}`, `docs/Architecture/FUSION_OPTIMIZER_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

The whole header is the handle, as a browser tab is clickable and draggable: a press that does not travel 6 px stays the control's click, one that travels is a drag and its click is swallowed (text fields exempt) — the first version excluded header controls and a 360 px panel header is almost entirely controls. `splitPanelResizer.js`: `visiblePanels()` is the one "which panels show, left to right" rule (flex `order`, then DOM position) and is exported for the reorder module; each resize handle takes the `order` of the panel to its right; the conversation stays the flex filler on **either** side of a handle (it was assumed leftmost). Hidden panels keep their slot; the ends of the row are the ends of the whole sequence. Per viewer in `localStorage` (`uderia_split_order_v1`), reconciled at load. Gate `test_split_panel_reorder.mjs` (**67**, in the battery — both shipped modules executed over a simulated flex row); 15 mutations fail by name (one escaped the first pass — the lone-panel check asserted after the drag ended — and was closed). Verified in headless Chrome in both themes with real mouse drags (the new script injected, since the running server's template predates the tag): flow to the front, the conversation to the far right, a resize with the conversation on the right, a drag by the title button firing no click, keyboard move, reset. Known limit: keyboard tab order follows the DOM, not the visual sequence. Server restart (new script tag in `index.html`); pins `splitPanelResizer 1.8`, `splitPanelReorder 1.0`. Files: `static/js/handlers/{splitPanelReorder,splitPanelResizer}.js`, `templates/index.html`, `test/{test_split_panel_reorder.mjs,trust_battery.sh}`, `docs/Architecture/COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

- **Sep 2026**: **Multi-source stages 3a + 3b — the planner knows every server's tables, and a statement over two servers is split by code, never substituted (`MULTI_SOURCE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` stages 3a–3b, branch `feature/multi-source-implementation`).** After 3.0 the Optimize lane answered every single-server question and no cross-server one (0/33). Traced: the planner had each server's DATABASES and still invented tables or put real ones in the wrong database; told the tables (3a), it named them right — in ONE statement, which routing refuses, and self-correction (one action) swapped in a one-server query: the phase counted as done and the report stated a confident wrong number. **3a:** each server's catalog (tables; columns when ≤ 16 tables) is read with its database list through the server's own tools resolved by role (`source_routing.ensure_catalogs`; cached with the list, bounded, failure-tolerant), rendered in the ONE Data sources note both lanes read with the rule *one statement reads the tables of ONE server*, and seeded into the session's column store. **3b, decided by code (`agent/cross_source.py`, 0 LLM):** one fetch per server — the columns the statement uses of that server's table, its own WHERE conjuncts pushed down when every join is INNER, that server's own tool — and the ORIGINAL statement as the combine step (`TDA_Compute` op sql over `p<N>`), so join, aggregation and ordering run unchanged with every combine protection; a statement reading an earlier phase's rows as a table (`… IN (SELECT id FROM s1)`) is the same case. Two seams, one splitter: the planner pass `cross_source_shape` (17 passes now; references follow through `renumber_plan_refs`, fetches in one parallel group) and the phase executor at a refusal carrying `code: spans_servers` + `split`. What it declines (unplaceable table, two tables of one server, a nested SELECT other than `col IN (SELECT one column FROM one table)`, CTE, UNION, `SELECT *`, unattributable column, forward reference) is withdrawn to the tactical step with the split named, or ends the phase with the refusal — **a one-server substitute is never the phase's answer.** **Four defects the traces found, fixed at the root:** a `sum` phase ran beside the combine it totalled (`_phase_compute_deps` now covers earlier compute phases); the tactical LLM invents `sales__base_readQuery` for the unaliased first server (`_resolve_unknown_tool`, never a guess between servers); a zero-row fetch was never a statement, so `p1` resolved to nothing and a correction invented a total (an empty result that declares its columns is registered; an empty column borrows its peer's type in the combine); a correction writing SQL over `p<N>` tables goes to the combine, not the database. **Bench (13 × 3):** Optimize cross-server 0/33 → **26–29/33** over three runs (29 · 27 · 26), controls 6/6, $0.0015 per question (1.15× the stage-0 baseline; 3.5× at 3.0), LLM calls 2.2 (baseline 3.6); Ideate+tools **38/39 → 39/39** at 2.4× lower cost. Every remaining Optimize miss is honest — the model's column choice on a graph-less agent, or a figure the plan never fetched. **Recorded:** the 3a commit's numbers were measured with the combine switches unset after a restart (2/33, $0.0011); with them on, 5/33, $0.0013 — the plan's §3a and §7 carry the correction. The stage-3 exit criterion is half met (beats the baseline; does not yet beat Ideate+tools on cross-server) — investigated and recorded before 3c–3k. Gate `test/test_cross_source_plan.py` (**116**, in the battery); **25 mutations fail by name** (two escaped first passes and were closed). Files: `agent/{cross_source,source_routing,planner,phase_executor,executor,result_sets,compute_sql,execution_service}.py`, `mcp_adapter/adapter.py`, `test/test_cross_source_plan.py`, `docs/Architecture/{MULTI_SOURCE,FUSION_OPTIMIZER}_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `.claude/skills/fusion-hardening/SKILL.md`.

- **Sep 2026**: **Multi-source stage 3.0 — schema before SQL, and a describe call is facts, never the answer: the Optimize lane answers questions on an agent with no knowledge graph (`MULTI_SOURCE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` stage 3.0, §9 decision "options 1 + 2", branch `feature/multi-source-implementation`).** Stage 0 had measured Optimize at 0/39 on the two-server fixture, both single-server controls included. Traced on a real turn: the plan wrote `SUM(sale_total)` against a table whose columns are `TotalAmount`, `SaleDate`…; the database refused it; the correction LLM answered "describe the table"; the describe SUCCEEDED and the retry loop took that success as the phase's answer. **One fact source, `agent/schema_facts.py`** (the tables a statement reads, the agent's own describe/list tool, the session store first, every read recorded into the preflight column store), and four deterministic rules: **(1)** `ColumnNotFoundStrategy` / `TableNotFoundStrategy` read the real columns / tables from the database when no graph has them — a mechanical fix when one close match exists (incl. qualifying an unqualified table this turn listed in one database), else facts to the LLM with the directive to rewrite the SAME statement; nothing read ⇒ nothing added. **(2)** in the retry loop, a correction that stands a discovery call in for a failed SQL call: its result becomes facts and the original statement is retried (the stand-in's attempt granted back once). **(3)** the `schema_before_sql` plan pass (after `date_range_wiring`, before `text_date_cast`; 16 passes now) inserts a describe before a raw-SQL phase that reads a table the turn has no columns for and leaves the statement to the tactical step (draft kept as intent); never for a table the graph, the session or a retrieved champion's SQL already vouches for, never without a describe tool, at most four per plan; the inserted describe waits for earlier discovery and settles its table on the turn's own listing; a withdrawn statement never takes FASTPATH. **(4)** in the tactical loop of such a phase, a discovery action is recorded as facts and the loop continues. **Found and fixed on the way:** a reference dotted to a reference (`result_of_phase_2.result_of_phase_4`) left the database half as literal text — now `database.table` when both sides are scalars; the table strategy put the placeholder "the specified database" in its prompt and a model copied it into a real tool argument. **Bench (day one — the bench now clears the fixture's learned cases before every question; a first run let one question's success guide the next and was kept as a record):** Optimize 0/39 → **6/39** — controls **0/6 → 6/6**, cross-server still 0/33 (the plan shape, 3a–3k) — at 3.5× the cost per question (describes, tactical SQL, corrections, most spent on the cross-server questions that still fail); Ideate+tools unchanged at 38/39. Gate `test_schema_facts` (**82**, in the battery — the real retry loop driven end to end); **31 mutations fail by name** (two escaped first passes and were closed); `test_tool_identity`'s build gate caught a second spelling of the tool-name rule (now `base_name`). Stage 1's ReAct infra rows rerun: 38/39, equal to the baseline. Files: `agent/{schema_facts,phase_executor,planner,executor}.py`, `test/{test_schema_facts.py,trust_battery.sh}`, `test/performance/multi_source_bench.py`, `docs/Architecture/FUSION_OPTIMIZER_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

- **Sep 2026**: **Multi-source agents, stages 0–1 of `MULTI_SOURCE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`: a measurement, one routing decision for both lanes, and a down HTTP MCP server finally classified as down (branch `feature/multi-source-implementation`).** **Stage 0 — measure first:** a fixture that splits `fitness_db` across two MCP servers (two view databases, one read-only login each, `test/performance/fixtures/multi_source/`), 13 questions with exact ground truth, and `test/performance/multi_source_bench.py` (per lane: pass rate, cost, latency, calls reaching the holding server without a re-route, share of two-server questions answered through a combine). Baseline on `main`, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, 3 runs: **Ideate+tools 38/39, Optimize 0/39** — Optimize fails even the single-server controls because its planner writes each query's SQL before any schema is known (guessed `sale_total`, `service_tickets`), and after a failure reads the real columns then goes to the final report; recorded as the open decision (plan §9) that stage 3 must answer first. **Stage 1 — the shared layer:** where a multi-server agent's call runs is decided ONCE (`source_routing.plan_before` / `plan_after` → `CallDecision`, one re-route record `reroute_info` naming its plan phase, one routed stamp `routed_source`); both lanes (the adapter's `_invoke_routed`, the ReAct wrapper) only run the call. What differs is declared in `SourceLane` (the `SqlLane` precedent): `plan_bound` — Optimize honours a server its plan chose. The turn keeps ONE record of unreachable servers (turn-start probe, ReAct tool loading, a mid-call transport failure), announced once per turn in BOTH lanes (closes R3: Optimize now names a down server before planning) and one note (`turn_sources_note`) reaches every prompt path (the Optimize fallback prompt path had none). The first server is read through `agent_mcp_servers.primary_of` (ratchet gate `test_primary_server_reads`). **Found and fixed on the way:** `transient_transport_error` classified a refused HTTP connection as NOT a transport failure (httpx raises its ConnectError FROM httpcore's, whose type was not listed) — so for every HTTP MCP server the "could not be reached" handling, the re-route and the one resend never applied, on both lanes; a list cached before a server went down hid it for 30 minutes (now dropped on a mid-call failure); with one of two servers down the note dropped the reachable server's list and the planner invented a database. Stage-1 bench: routing without a re-route 0.977 → 0.994 (Ideate), 1.0 → 0.985 (Optimize; it now re-routes where it used to fail); pass rates within variance; 15 questions unanswered because the admin account hit its hourly request limit (the bench now reports those apart and can rerun them). - **Sep 2026**: **An agent's MCP tool/prompt selection has ONE home — the profile; the eye icon persists it, the editor never saves "all" over a failed listing, and a switched-off prompt never runs.** Reported: "the mcp prompts still show as activated in the profile configuration even though I assume they are deactivated." Three defects, one family: **(1)** the resource panel's eye icon (`/prompt/toggle_status`, `/tool/toggle_status`) changed only the process-wide `APP_STATE['disabled_*']` list — unauthenticated, never written to the profile, reverting on the next profile switch or restart, and changing the agent for every user meanwhile; both are now `@require_auth`, take the panel's `profile_id`, and persist through ONE module `core/profile_selection.py` (`toggle_selection` list arithmetic · `toggle_updates` primary vs `additionalMcpServers` entry · `universe_resolver` from the classification snapshot, the master's when inheriting · `plan_toggle` refusals: `TDA_*` 400, unowned/not-offered 404, "all" with an unknown list 409), refreshing the runtime lists only when that profile is the loaded one; the editor's cached profiles reload on `uderia:profile-selection-changed`. **(2)** the editor saved `0 selected === 0 available` as `["*"]`, so a save while the prompt listing had failed (swallowed as "does not support prompts") switched every prompt back on — now `resolveSavedSelection(loadState, …)` carries the stored selection forward unless the list actually loaded and is non-empty, and `/v1/mcp/resources` reports a failed listing as `prompts_error` (only MCP -32601 means "no prompts", `prompts_listing_unsupported`). **(3)** nothing refused to RUN a switched-off prompt — `disabled_prompt_refusal` (fail-open) is checked by the planner before loading the prompt, by a delegated prompt phase (skipped with a Plan Optimization note) and by `POST /v1/prompts/<name>/execute[-raw]` (`403 prompt_disabled`). Prompts are signed capability, so a panel toggle on a signed agent reads 🟠 until re-signed. Gate `test_profile_selection` (**61**, in the battery; mutations fail by name); regression-clean: agent_mcp_servers 73 · resource_panel_servers 21 · multi_mcp_baseline 114 · profile_editor_surface 67 · data_sources_ui 128 · version pins 92 · inventory 780/0. Files: `core/profile_selection.py`, `api/{routes,rest_routes}.py`, `agent/{planner,executor}.py`, `static/js/{api,eventHandlers}.js`, `static/js/handlers/{configurationHandler,capabilitiesManagement}.js` + pin cascade, `test/test_profile_selection.py`, `docs/RestAPI/restAPI.md`.

- **Oct 2026**: **v1.24 deploy follow-up — production comes back by itself after a slow start or a Docker daemon restart.** Two failures during the v1.24 deploy: the first start exceeded Hypercorn's 60 s startup limit (the embedding model took 44 s on a disk still busy unpacking the 7.3 GB image), and a Docker daemon restart in the middle of the deploy killed every container on the host — the `unless-stopped` ones (all Teradata MCP endpoints) and Uderia's `restart: "no"` stayed down, so the profile editor showed "unhandled errors in a TaskGroup" for every MCP-backed agent. Now: `config.startup_timeout` = 300 s (`TDA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`), `restart: always` for Uderia and every `deploy/mcp/*` endpoint (the `always` containers were the ones that survived). - **Sep 2026**: **PROP-006 B9 (part) — one of a multi-server agent's servers down is named, never silent (branch `feature/multi-source-hardening`).** Tested with a real unreachable server: the turn already survived (fail-soft loading), but activation said "all tests passed" (it only checked the server was configured) and nothing told the user or the model — so a question about that server's data could be answered as if the data did not exist. Now: activation reports each additional server (`test_results.additional_mcp_servers`, warning when unreachable, never a failure); the ReAct lane emits a Live Status *MCP Server Unavailable* step (persisted, titled on reload) and a note on the user side of the turn (only when a server failed — the cached system prompt untouched); a call whose server stops answering mid-turn reads "could not be reached — do not retry, answer from the others and say so" in both lanes, and a read goes once to a server KNOWN to hold the data (never guessed). Live: asked for the down ANDP server's catalog, the agent answered that the source is currently unavailable. Gate `test_mcp_source_routing` 103 → **124**. Open: per-server breaker, honesty-gate disclosure. Files: `agent/source_routing.py`, `agent/engines/conversation_engine.py`, `agent/conversation_agent.py`, `mcp_adapter/adapter.py`, `agent/tool_enforcement.py`, `core/configuration_service.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `static/js/eventHandlers.js` + pin cascade, `docs/Architecture/MULTI_SOURCE_ARCHITECTURE.md` §9.6b.

- **Sep 2026**: **PROP-006 B10 — a multi-server agent's call goes to the server that holds its data (branch `feature/multi-source-hardening`).** The phase-2 live finding: with a fitness and a NIBRS server whose `base_readQuery` descriptions are identical, the model sent a `fitness_db` count to the NIBRS server, the login was refused (3523) and it answered "no permission". Measured first: each login's own database-list tool returns exactly the databases it may read, so that list IS the server's descriptor. New `agent/source_routing.py` (one core, both lanes): holdings per (user, server) from a role-resolved list-tool probe (8 s, cached 30 min, failures re-probed after 2 min) refined by each call's outcome and the turn's own list results; **before** a call, a statement naming a database the called server lacks goes to the ONE other server that holds it (several → refused naming them, nothing sent); **after** a 3523/3524/3802 on a read (never 3807 — a missing table, which once poisoned the holdings), once to the holder or the only other server (the first error stands if that fails too); never a write, a denied name (Agent Authority on the name that would run, fail-closed), a tool outside the server's selection, a `TDA_`/connector tool, a second hop, or a single-server agent. The route is decided BEFORE the SQL gate so preflight/loop guard/authority judge the tool that really runs, in its own scope (`preflight.dialect.server_scope`). Named on the Server row (`mcp_source.reason = routed`, `called`, `from_server`, `databases`; ReAct via a turn re-route ledger read at tool end) and in a `[Routing]` note the model reads first. Switch `TDA_MCP_SOURCE_ROUTING` (default on; multi-server agents only). **The model is told which server holds what:** the seam warms each server's list once per turn (routing turns only) and both lanes carry a short *[Data sources]* block — which tools reach which server and the databases each login reads (system catalogs out, capped) — at the top of the Optimize tool definitions and on the ReAct user side; "which databases can you read?" was answered from the first server alone, now both agents list both. **M11:** a dashboard tile's MCP refresh runs under the tile profile's own servers (`source_routing.profile_call_scope` — its first server as the call's server, aliases, names, routing), not the user's currently active server; a tile stamped from a wrong-server call is re-routed on refresh (live: 100 rows). **O8:** a learned plan naming a server the agent no longer has (`crm__base_readQuery`) is re-keyed by the plan validator (Correction 3b) to the one catalog tool of that base name, named as a Plan Optimization step. **One statement never spans two servers:** a SELECT over databases held by different servers is refused before it runs (`split`, naming where each lives), and the planner's SQL-consolidation pass keeps such phases apart (`spans_servers`, observed live merging a fitness and a NIBRS count into one failing SELECT). **Override agents get their additional servers:** an @TAG / REST `profile_id` override built its catalog from the first server only; `optimize_engine.merge_override_additional_servers` now merges the rest before the overlay (live: 48 NIBRS tools, a NIBRS count answered on that server). The *[Data sources]* note leaves out a login's own user space (the model once queried `nibrs_source_agent.victim`). Gate `test_mcp_source_routing` (103 → 181 with B9, the descriptor, O8, M11, split, consolidation and override, in the battery; 13 mutations fail by name — one first escaped as an equivalent mutant and was replaced by the scope mutation that matters); live-verified on both lanes with a forced wrong call (ran only on the fitness server, answered 100). Files: `agent/source_routing.py`, `mcp_adapter/adapter.py`, `agent/tool_enforcement.py`, `agent/conversation_agent.py`, `agent/execution_service.py`, `agent/preflight/dialect.py`, `core/agent_mcp_servers.py`, `core/config.py`, `static/js/ui.js` + pin cascade, `test/test_mcp_source_routing.py`, `docs/Architecture/MULTI_SOURCE_ARCHITECTURE.md` §9.6.

- **Sep 2026**: **PROP-006 phase 2 — an agent can call several MCP servers: classified per server, one catalog under unique names, every call routed to its own server, configured in the editor (branch `feature/multi-source-agents`).** Brief: `MULTI_SOURCE_AGENTS_BUILD_BRIEF.md` §7. Built freeze-first: `test_multi_mcp_baseline` (golden written from pre-phase-2 code) holds a single-server agent byte-identical in tokens, calls, snapshot, signature and routing, with two NAMED exceptions (M10: gaining a server flags reclassification; M9: the delete guard now also covers Ideate+tools agents). **Names (decision 2):** the primary's tools keep their names, an additional server's read `<alias>__<name>` (`core/tool_identity.py`; an AST gate forces every tool-name rule through `base_name`). **Storage (decision 10):** `additionalMcpServers: [{id, alias, tools, prompts}]`, instance-local, validated at the door (`400 invalid_additional_mcp_servers`, `[]` removes the key); ONE resolver `core/agent_mcp_servers.servers_of`. **Runtime:** one per-server classification path shared with the primary (snapshots in deployment-local `additionalMcpClassification`), the turn's alias → server map armed at the execution seam (per turn, never process-global), `resolve_mcp_target` the one name → (client, server, server-side name) resolver for tools and all four prompt fetches, pooled per-server clients, ReAct tools loaded per server; preflight facts per server (O5/O6), planners keyed to an additional server load for the agent (M6); trust names each server in the deployment half (`additional_mcp`, absent for a single server; attesting over an unclassified one is refused naming it). **Editor (decision 11):** Data sources → Tools adds / removes servers with a short name suggested from the server's distinctive words; Resources picks each server's tools and prompts by their own names; a single-server agent sees at most an "Add another MCP server" control (only when another server exists) — no fetch, no Resources change, no key. - **Sep 2026**: **Multi-source agents, phase 1 (PROP-006, branch `feature/multi-source-agents`) — an agent may combine results from several sources in one read-only SELECT that code runs, and every source is configured in one place.** Built from the regression assessment (`MULTI_SOURCE_REGRESSION_ASSESSMENT_2026-09.md`) with the operator's binding rules: a single-source agent gets no added burden, one code path serves both, transparency and every trust capability hold for multi-source exactly as for single-source, code decides wherever it safely can. **The combine** (`TDA_Compute` `op: "sql"`, `agent/compute_sql.py`, switch `TDA_COMPUTE_SQL` under `TDA_COMPUTE_LINEAGE`, off ⇒ byte-identical behind `[[gate:compute_sql]]`, frozen by a baseline suite committed green first): tables `s1…sN` (or `p<N>` in a plan — parallel phases finish in any order), a sandboxed in-process DuckDB, the one SQL checkpoint under the logical name `compute_sql`, completeness refused or disclosed, join keys measured on the rows under a fixed normalization ladder (the winner applied and named), empty join / fan-out / truncation reported, a sealed receipt, personal data masked on the card. **Every result names its source** (`ts`, `source_id`, `phase`, and for a combine `inputs` + `origin_sources`), recorded at the one registry seam. **Isolation rules** at two levels: the administrator's by ENDPOINT (hold for every user reaching a system — `core/source_endpoints.py`, never a credential), the agent's own by source id (`combineIsolation`, only adds, validated at the door, instance-local, in the deployment trust half only when non-empty), plus the ontology's cross-domain rule; a chained combine is judged on its original sources. **Transparency:** on a turn that read more than one source (the one `multi_source` condition), the Number Lineage step names each source and each combine's inputs (live and reload, one title rule for both engines), and the lineage dialog shows the second hop from a combined figure to each source and its read time. **Configuration — one *Data sources* section** in the profile editor: the MCP select moved in (same element), the Navigator's default source and query databases (rows, Test, Make default, a searchable picker that says why a connection cannot be added), and — only with two or more sources — Combining results with the administrator's rules locked and the agent's own as sentences; the administrator's editor under Administration → Trust → Enforcement; `GET /v1/data-sources`. Theme variables only (the browser caught the global card rule restyling the first version, and the editor's hard-coded dark label colour washing labels out in light mode — both fixed and gated). **Two things the live turns taught, both code:** a combine that names results under the wrong statement numbers is re-pointed when exactly one re-assignment binds (`compute_sql.repair_table_assignment`; isolation and completeness re-checked on the inputs actually used, the re-pointing named), and a column whose every value is a plain number written as text (the Teradata MCP server serialises numbers as JSON text) loads as a number while codes like `"007"` stay text (`_numeric_text_type`, named in the result). **Phase 2 decided (not built):** unique tool and prompt names across an agent's servers — the primary server keeps real names, additional servers are `<alias>__<name>`, every rule reads the base name through one parser; additional servers stored as `additionalMcpServers` (instance-local); servers added in Data sources, tools picked per server in Resources. **Named exception:** the `compute-expert` skill is not edited — its raw-hash would move every agent that carries it; the guidance is in the gated tool text and the refusals. Gates: `test_compute_sql_baseline` 49, `test_compute_sql` 182, `test_combine_ux.mjs` 32, `test_data_sources_ui.mjs` 79 (all in the battery), `test_dbnav_query_ui` §5 and `test_duckdb_driver` §2 restated; mutations fail by name; verified in headless Chrome in both themes. **Phase 2 (several MCP servers) is designed, not built.** Doc: [MULTI_SOURCE_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/MULTI_SOURCE_ARCHITECTURE.md). Files: `agent/{compute_sql,result_sets,compute,compute_lineage,obda,tool_enforcement,phase_executor,executor}.py`, `agent/honesty/primitives.py`, `components/builtin/compute/*`, `core/{source_endpoints,agent_authority,config}.py`, `core/trust/deployment.py`, `api/{rest_routes,routes,admin_routes}.py`, `static/js/handlers/{dataSources,combineRulesAdmin,figureLineage,configurationHandler}.js`, `static/js/{ui,eventHandlers}.js`, `templates/index.html`, `test/{test_compute_sql_baseline,test_compute_sql}.py`, `test/{test_combine_ux,test_data_sources_ui}.mjs`.

- **Sep 2026**: **DataAgentBench closed for now; its platform capabilities merged; multi-source agents proposed (PROP-006).** The phase-3 baseline (Uderia Ideate + Database Navigator on `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, dev subset, 1 run) answered **4 / 24** (Pass@1 0.167, $0.21 total, every question under a minute) against a leaderboard top of 0.87–0.95. Almost every miss had one cause: the answer needs rows from **two databases combined**, and an agent can query several sources but cannot combine their results — the model joined in its head from truncated rows and fabricated (bookreview q1 "the 1920s", truth "the 2020s"). Closing that properly is an architecture decision (several data sources of any kind per agent, including several MCP servers, plus a governed combine step), so it is taken on its own merits in PROP-006 (`docs/proposals/PROP-006-multi-source-agents.md`), not to win a benchmark; the closure and its reasons are recorded in `DAB_BENCHMARK_SCOPE.md §Closure`. **Kept (general-purpose, merged to `main`):** agent `query` over several Database Connections with every SQL protection, one SQL gate for all three lanes, DuckDB and MongoDB connections, dialect-aware preflight per source, and from the last round (`ca923de4`): the Navigator answers an object named without its `source_id` from the one allowed source that holds it (naming the `source_id`; the agent had repeated one refused call ~20 times), a SELECT passed as `query_text` runs as `sql`, a turn cut off at its output limit after tool cards says why, and the DAB driver never scores a tool's output as the answer. **Local models (M3 Pro, MLX):** five Gemma 4 builds measured — 26B-A4B MoE fastest (44 tok/s gen, 529 prefill) but stalling end to end, 12B QAT 4-bit the only correct answer (1/3); the text-only converter, speed harness and e2e runner live in `benchmarks/dab/models/`; five open local-model defects are recorded in the scope doc. Welcome page + README gain the "Ask Across Several Databases" entry. Gates: `test_mlx_output_ceiling` 21, `test_navigator_multi_source` 27; battery GREEN.

AS JSON))`, `TABLE(TD_SYSFNLIB.TD_RANGE_DATE(…))`, `UNNEST(result_of_phase_2)`, `IN (SELECT date FROM result_of_phase_2)`). - **Sep 2026**: **The SQL checks speak each statement's own dialect and judge it only with its own source's facts; statements that write files are writes (P3 of `DAB_BENCHMARK_SCOPE.md`, branch `feature/dab-benchmark`).** Every preflight check parsed as Teradata and read facts recorded session-wide, so a Database Navigator query on PostgreSQL naming `public.business` was judged against the Teradata catalog (under `enforce`, refused as a nonexistent database), a MySQL statement yielded no column references at all (every check silent), and the empty-result note told any database to run `SELECT TOP 20`. ONE module `agent/preflight/dialect.py` holds both rules: the call's dialect + source set once by `guarded_sql_call` (`using`), every analysis parse reads `dialect.read()`, and `dialect.ns(session)` picks the facts — Teradata (every caller that sets nothing: the MCP adapter, the ReAct wrapper) shares the session's facts exactly as before, any other source keeps `<session>::<source>`; every Teradata-only rewrite stays gated to Teradata. Where no ontology describes a source, its **own dictionary** arms the checks: the Navigator's `describe` records the table's complete column list and each `query` the schema list (`guard.record_source_dictionary`, never on Teradata), so a wrong column is refused before it runs naming *the database's own dictionary* and the real columns. **Found on the way:** `SELECT … INTO OUTFILE/DUMPFILE`, `COPY`, `EXPORT DATABASE`, `ATTACH`, `LOAD DATA`, `INSTALL` were classified as reads in every dialect — each writes files on the database server and a read-only transaction does not stop them; `sql_is_write` refuses them (literals and comments stripped first, so `'copy that'` stays a read), inherited by `deny_writes`, the MCP adapter, the ReAct wrapper and the Navigator; and the Navigator returned a preflight refusal's short error only, dropping its recovery text. - **Sep 2026**: **MongoDB is a first-class Database Connection — read-only in two halves, and the first connection whose statements are not SQL.** Built as the feature class (DAB's agnews and yelp datasets are MongoDB), with every surface DuckDB got: the Canvas, the Database Navigator catalog, agent queries, the connection form and test. **(1) One declaration, now with a language:** `DRIVERS["mongodb"]` joins the driver declaration and every driver names its query language (`language`: `sql` / `mongodb`; `DOCUMENT_DRIVERS`, `driver_language()`) — the JS mirrors (connection form, profile editor, connector manifest, Canvas) stay pinned equal. **(2) One statement format, one parser, one executor:** a MongoDB statement is JSON — a collection and an aggregation pipeline, or a find-style filter/projection/sort/limit converted to one pipeline — parsed and checked by `core/mongo_query.py` (pure) and run by `core/mongo_client.py` (pooled client, server-side `$limit` + `maxTimeMS`), which the Canvas connector, the catalog provider and the agent's query all call. **(3) Read-only in two halves** (MongoDB has no client-side read-only mode): the platform's half is a stage **allowlist** (a stage MongoDB adds later is refused until reviewed) plus `$out`/`$merge`/`$function`/`$accumulator`/`$where` refused anywhere, `$lookup`/`$unionWith`/`$facet` sub-pipelines included — decided before anything is sent (`not_read_only`); the database's half is the **login's rights**, read from `connectionStatus` with `showPrivileges` and classified (`classify_privileges`: no authenticated user = access control off = anyone can write). An agent query on a login that can write — or whose rights could not be read — is refused (`writable_login`) unless the connection's owner ticked *Allow agent queries on a login that can write* (`allow_writable_login`); the connection test names the rights, **amber** when the login can write. The Canvas runs what its owner wrote, as for SQL. **(4) Catalog** (`dbcatalog/mongo_provider.py`): collections read as tables, views as views with their pipeline; MongoDB declares no schema, so fields are **sampled** (up to 200 documents, every BSON type named — `double|int32|string` — presence counted, nested fields as dot paths) and `unavailable` SAYS so (*a declared schema — fields sampled from N documents of about M*, or *read from all N documents*); `_id` primary, unique indexes marked, metadata counts on the listing, exact `count`; a connection naming a database is scoped to it; MongoDB's own `system.*` collections are not listed (found: `system.views` inflated a database's collection count). **(5) The agent's query:** `collection` + `pipeline` arguments exist only behind the query gate (an agent without the opt-in still sees a byte-identical tool — `test_navigator_query_baseline` 12/12); SQL sent to MongoDB or a pipeline sent to SQL is refused as `wrong_query_language`, naming the right arguments; results reach the registry with the canonical JSON as the statement, personal fields masked by collection, statement numbers as for SQL. **An agent-written pipeline is a free-formed data operation exactly like raw SQL** — `obda._is_document_query` feeds the exclusive-data-surface denial, the OBDA lane and the honesty gate. **UX:** the connection form shows the auth database and the consent box only for MongoDB (database optional, port 27017, host may be a `mongodb+srv://` URI); the Canvas runs `language: 'mongodb'` (JSON-highlighted, the connection picker shown, no MCP fallback); the navigator's *Sample query* / *Query in canvas* / *Open in canvas* carry a MongoDB statement as `mongodb`; the query card counts documents. The companion skill's gated query section gains *On a MongoDB source* — a builtin skill edit, so a signed agent carrying `database-navigator-expert` reads changed until re-signed. **Proof:** new `test_mongodb_driver` (**133**, in the battery — the declaration, the JS mirrors and the form logic executed under Node, the full read-only truth table, the rights truth table, the classifiers, the handler's refusals decided before anything runs, and — against a MongoDB on localhost when one answers — the provider, the Canvas executor and the agent's query end to end in a throwaway database, plus DAB's own databases read and left unchanged); **9 mutations fail by name** (the sub-pipeline recursion escaped the first pass — the operator scan masked it — and the case that isolates it was added; one was first caught only by a crash and was hardened). Live with access control on (a temporary `mongo:8.2 --auth`): read-only login → "login is read-only", query runs; readWrite login → named with *insert, update, remove on database shop*, query refused before anything is sent; root → any database; wrong password → test fails. Live REST (create, test, sources, describe, preview, count, Canvas run) and the form in headless Chrome (fields per driver, both tests, amber caution, save, no page errors). - **Sep 2026**: **DuckDB is a first-class Database Connection, every driver is declared once, and a built-in connector is what its manifest says it is.** DAB (the data-agent benchmark) ships half its datasets as DuckDB files; per the benchmark imperative (§0: a benchmark need is built as the whole feature class, never tactically) DuckDB was built as "a file database as a connection" with every surface an existing direct driver has. **(1) One driver declaration:** `core/database_connections.DRIVERS` names each driver's label, catalog reader (`teradata` · `information_schema` · `sqlite` · none), whether it is a file, whether its reader returns comments, and its package — the store's validation, the Canvas SQL connector, `resolution.DIRECT_DRIVERS` (now the same object), the generic catalog provider, the connection form, the profile editor's two source pickers, the Canvas connector form and the connector manifest all derive from it or are pinned equal by the gate (six hand-kept lists before). **(2) DuckDB executor** (`canvas/connectors/sql.py`, sync on the executor pool): structured typed rows, `max_rows`+1 truncation, `read_only=True` for agent queries (a write reads `not_read_only`, nothing changed), and a missing path is REFUSED naming it — `duckdb.connect()` would otherwise create an empty file whose tables "do not exist". **(3) DuckDB catalog** via `information_schema`, with two DuckDB corrections: `constraint_column_usage` lists a foreign key's OWN columns (the PostgreSQL join named the child as its own parent) → keys from `duckdb_constraints()`; `schemata` lists `main` once per attached catalog → the file's catalog only. **(4) Comments were a false capability:** the generic reader advertised `COMMENTS` for PostgreSQL and fetched none — and the personal-data classifier reads column comments — now read for PostgreSQL (`col_description`/`obj_description`) and DuckDB, declared per driver, soft (an unreadable comment is SAID in `unavailable`, never a failed describe). **(5) Built-in connector identity:** `install_server` wrote whatever its payload carried, so the Database Connection connector sat locally as an `mcp_stdio` Platform connector with no connection manager behind its card (the Canvas's "Manage connections…" pointer landed nowhere useful). The manifest now owns a built-in's `name/display_name/description/version/connector_type/requires_user_auth` at install, on every read, and via `reconcile_builtin_connectors()` at startup (logs what moved); admin state (enabled, credentials, permitted tools) untouched, a remote connector sharing a built-in's id keeps its own row. **Form:** file drivers hide host/port/login and name the field "Database file path". **Proof:** new `test_duckdb_driver` (83 — declaration, JS mirrors, the form logic executed under Node, executor, catalog on a fixture with keys/views/comments/two schemas, the PostgreSQL comment read, all five DAB `.duckdb` files end to end and unmodified) + `test_builtin_connector_identity` (18), both in the battery; **12 mutations fail by name** (the remote-id guard escaped the first pass — the fixture's remote connector had no built-in namesake — and the collision case was added).
