- **Sep 2026**: **The Database Navigator gains an opt-in `query` action — an agent may run its own read-only SELECT with every protection an MCP SQL tool gets; the Canvas moves onto the one Database Connection store (branch `feature/dab-benchmark`, P1 of `DAB_BENCHMARK_SCOPE.md`).** Built gates-first: `test_navigator_query_baseline` (12) was committed green before any feature code and still holds — an agent without the opt-in reads byte-identical tool text, instructions, argument schema and signatures. **The action** (`componentConfig.database_navigator.query = {enabled, sources}`, off unless set): one SELECT per call against an allow-listed direct connection (empty = the resolved default; a source not allowed, not present here, or reached through MCP is refused and named), run through ONE shared gate `tool_enforcement.guarded_sql_call` — authority (`deny_writes`, denied tools under both names, the exclusive data surface), loop guard, turn budget, preflight (Teradata-only rewrites stay on Teradata), timeout, errors as results, the result-set registry, the empty-result note, the tool-result firewall, steer. Read-only is decided before anything runs and enforced again at the database (SQLite `mode=ro`, Postgres/MySQL read-only transactions); a refused write reads `not_read_only`, never a failure to retry. The model reads 100 rows by default (500 max); the full result reaches the registry so a figure cites its statement number. **Platform fixes it forced:** component tool text is gated on every model-facing surface (the ReAct and Optimize lanes had leaked gate markup); `sql_is_write` walks the whole tree (a data-modifying CTE or `SELECT … INTO` read as a read — a real `deny_writes` bypass on Postgres MCP); the shared SQL executor returns structured, typed, bounded rows (a newline inside a value had split one row into several on DataAgentBench's googlelocal); a bare `name` is personal data when its table is about people (judged by the table, one rule for the query card, preview and search — search had dropped the table name); dialects are named as sqlglot names them; **skills learned `[[gate:…]]` blocks** (`skills/manager.py:gate_skill_text`, fails closed) so `database-navigator-expert` teaches querying only to agents that may query; the profile editor carries the query block forward (it dropped unmodelled `componentConfig` keys on save). **Signatures:** the portable capability hash gains `database_navigator:query` only with the opt-in; the deployment half records the queryable sources `{id, driver}`, absent otherwise, and names added/removed databases as drift. **UX:** the evidence row *Query · N rows · source · statement n*; the card shows the statement, a 20-row grid with personal data masked, rows the agent read, rewrites, and **Open in canvas** (the canvas bound to the same connection); the panel offers **Query in canvas**; the editor gains an *Allow queries* switch and database picker. **The Canvas now reads and writes the one Database Connection store** (operator request): its routes are adapters over `DatabaseConnectionStore` (`save`/`delete` accept every id form; editing a legacy `canvas_conn_*` connection promotes it), which also fixed the edit form storing the masked password as the password and a deleted migrated connection reappearing. Its **duplicate connection manager** (Components → Canvas → Connections: list, form, test, save, delete) is gone — the tab and a new *Manage connections…* entry in the canvas's connection picker open Components → Connectors → Database Connection (`window.openPlatformConnector`). **The canvas connection picker could not be used at all**: its menu (and History, Sources) opened inside the auto-hiding sub-toolbar, which clips (`overflow: hidden`), so it was invisible and a tap hit the editor — one rule in `split-panels.css` keeps a sub-toolbar revealed and unclipped while any `*dropdown--open` menu in it is open (reproduced and verified in headless Chrome, pinned and hover-revealed). **Proof:** navigator_query 60, dbnav_query_ui 42, canvas_connection_store 41, guarded_sql_call 23, sql_connector_structured 21, component_gate_surfaces 89 — each mutation-tested, all in the battery; battery green; live on DataAgentBench's Postgres and SQLite and in headless Chrome (card → canvas → run; editor save; 16/16, no page errors). **Recorded, not changed:** the dead `ContextBuilder._build_component_tools_section`; the contract's shallow `componentConfig` merge on pack import; `test_canvas_comprehensive --unit-only` red at HEAD (`metadata.tool_name`); the editor showing "Changed" at open for some profiles (at HEAD too). Remaining P1: moving the adapter and ReAct seams onto `guarded_sql_call`. Server restart (backend); JS pins cascaded to `main.js 9.87`. - **Sep 2026**: **Anatomy and Trust stop taking ~20 s to open — the ontology content hash is cached, exactly, and trust-behavior leaves the event loop.** Operator, on prod: *"when I hop to the anatomy or trust section it takes around 20 seconds until something is showing up."* Measured on prod over the LAN, every other request of both views answered in under a second; `/v1/trust/agents` (both views) took **7.2–9.4 s** and `/v1/evals/agents/trust-behavior` (Trust) **7.6–8.4 s**. A profile of `resolve_profile_trust` inside the container put **9.6 of 10.4 s** in the ontology ingredient: for each of the eleven industry-model agents (~0.7–1.2 s each) every request re-read the whole `*_core` graph, JSON-decoded every property, sorted on a re-encoded key (~243k `json.dumps`) and hashed it — recomputed from scratch on every badge request, though it only changes when the graph does. And trust-behavior did all of it **inline on the event loop**, freezing every other request of every user for its duration. **Fix 1 — `composition.kg_graph_hash`:** the canonical hash cached behind a fingerprint of the RAW ROWS (entity id/name/type/properties + each relationship's type and endpoint ids, pickled — lossless, so two graphs can never share a key), never a count or timestamp: relationships carry no `updated_at` and the type migrations update rows in place without one, so a count/time key could serve a stale hash and leave a changed ontology reading 🟢. The fingerprint covers strictly more than the hash reads, so it is exact by construction; a relationship whose endpoint lies outside the graph's own entities bypasses the cache (the fingerprint cannot see that name); a reordered read only misses. One row read shared with `load_kg_graph`; bounded LRU (256). The three read-only call sites use it (`_ontology_ingredient`, `content.ontology_hash`, `products.ontology_state_for`); the sign-off route still computes uncached. **Fix 2:** the trust-behavior integrity join runs in `asyncio.to_thread` (`_integrity_states_by_tag`), as `/v1/trust/agents` already did. **Proof:** every one of the 32 local graphs hashes byte-identically cold and warm (7.3 s → 1.2 s warm); the running server's `/v1/trust/agents` rows for 65 agents and every trust-behavior integrity cell are identical before/after the change, both endpoints 4.7 s → 1.8 s warm locally; new gate `test_kg_hash_cache` (**31**, in the battery — every write shape incl. untimestamped in-place UPDATEs, rename, re-point, delete, insert vs a fresh recompute; revert → original hash; warm hit skips the recompute; the foreign-endpoint bypass; wiring on the AST); **four mutations fail by name** (relationships dropped from the key · the guard removed · a counts-only key · properties dropped); battery GREEN. Files: `core/trust/{composition,content,products}.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `test/{test_kg_hash_cache.py,trust_battery.sh}`.

- **Sep 2026**: **A figure the rows add up to is traced, and a near miss names the value the rows give — Compute with Lineage learns column aggregates.** Operator follow-up to the chart-only fix: a twelve-row monthly robbery trend was headlined *"180,193 robberies"* where the rows sum to 179,193. **Assessed first:** the headline is written by the final-report LLM as free text (`_invoke_final_report_task`, optional `key_metric`), and the only existing check there compares it against the model's own `direct_answer`, never the data; it happens intermittently (the report adds up rows itself only sometimes — 2/2 locally with lineage off, 0/5 with prod's switches, which is chance: the report prompt does not depend on any switch; asking for the total explicitly makes the planner compute it in SQL, so it is quoted from a row). The shipped classifier, fed the real 12 rows, read the CORRECT total, the WRONG total and the correct monthly average identically as "unreceipted — the agent's own arithmetic": it knew cells, row counts, literals and receipts, never a column's sum. **Fixed as a strict narrowing** in `agent/compute_lineage.py`, reached ONLY by a figure that was about to be unreceipted (after the asked/short guards), so every earlier class keeps its verdict byte for byte: **`derived`** — the figure equals the SUM or AVERAGE of a numeric column of a COMPLETE result set (never a truncated one; `row_count` must equal the rows held; ≥2 rows; every non-empty value numeric), traced as *"the sum of robbery_count over the 12 rows of statement 1"*, marked like a quoted figure (`data-derived`, opens the statement's rows, which the seam now persists); **`misderived`** — within 5% of such an aggregate but not it: it STAYS in `unreceipted` (every consumer keeps treating it as untraced) and the disclosure names the value the rows give (*"180,193 is close to, but is not, the sum of robbery_count over the 12 rows of statement 1, which is 179,193"*). **Disclose only, never rewrite** (operator: no regressions). Every existing message is byte-identical when neither class occurs. Consumers: `numeric_fidelity` counts derived as grounded; GROUNDED's reading names derived and near misses; the Live Status card lists both (`ui.js`, pins cascaded pins-only across 30 modules to `main.js`); the dialog leads with the aggregate. **Proof:** `test_compute_component` 147 → **174** (the real 12 monthly rows; truncated/partial/one-row/mixed-column refusals; precedence of an equal cell; the ordering on the source; marks; the scorer; GROUNDED both ways), `test_figure_lineage` 17 → **26** (a real derived mark through the dialog, and the shipped card EXECUTED — it had only been grepped); **seven mutations fail by name**; one pinned assertion restated as its property (it pinned the exact `mark_quoted(...)` expression I extended); replaying the two real earlier answers: 179,193 → derived, 180,193 → near miss naming 179,193; BATTERY GREEN. **Honest limit:** a sum of a column where summing is meaningless (a column of averages) is traced too — its lineage names exactly what was summed. **Deferred (recorded):** handing the report writer code-computed column totals before it writes — it changes what the model reads and could make headlining a total more attractive where one makes no sense. Files: `agent/{compute_lineage,executor,assurance_points}.py`, `eval/scorers/reliability.py`, `static/js/{ui.js,handlers/figureLineage.js}` + pin cascade, `templates/index.html`, `test/{test_compute_component.py,test_figure_lineage.mjs}`, `docs/{manuals/AGENT_TRUST_AND_ASSURANCE.md,RestAPI/restAPI.md}`, `static/trust/AGENT_TRUST_AND_ASSURANCE.html`.

- **Sep 2026**: **A question that says "show" is not a chart follow-up — the chart-continuation classifier narrowed; the planning prompt keeps its cacheable prefix.** Operator question: why does an Ideate session (@PXPROD) get prompt-cache hits on turn 2 while an Optimize session (@PXPRODO, same model) does not? **Measured, not guessed** — the exact bytes of every strategic planning call were captured locally (a temporary, reverted probe) over a 4-turn session: ~32.5K chars (~8.1K tokens) are stable turn to turn (system prompt · skill/KG directive blocks · the planner rules · the loop example), ~27–32K are per-question (champion examples + the KG enrichment for THIS question), and the tail is small (plan format 1K · tool list **343 chars** after turn 1 · goal). Gemini serves its implicit cache in ~4K-token blocks (4,089 / 8,178 / 12,239 in the stamps). The Ideate lane hits mostly INSIDE a turn (the ReAct loop resends its growing message list seconds apart); Optimize sends one planning call per turn, so its reuse is cross-turn and capped at the 8.1K stable head — which it DOES get (locally 8,178 per turn; the prod zeros were Gemini's best-effort plus a first planning call with nothing before it). **Decision recorded: the planning template in the license repo is NOT reordered** — moving the stable tail forward gains ~300 tokens, below one cache block, for a change at the heart of the planner. **The one real breaker was a planning defect:** `_is_chart_only_query` counted "show" as a chart word and recognised a new request only through a hard-coded retail noun list, so "Show me robberies per month…" (and "show me tickets per month" on fitness data) was classified as "just chart the last result" — PREPENDING a block that tells the planner to reuse the previous turn's data set and not query anything broader, which both mis-steers a new question and cuts the cacheable prefix to one block. **Fixed as a strict narrowing:** the original rule is kept verbatim and a second condition is ANDed — every content word (with a light singular fold, applied to both sides) must be chart vocabulary, a back-reference, or a word the previous question already used (the call site now passes it), so "plot the revenue" after a revenue question stays a continuation while "show me robberies per month" after a count is a new question; a query can lose the label, never gain it. **Proof:** new `test/test_chart_only_query.py` (27, in the battery — truth table across domains, the narrowing property against a verbatim copy of the old rule over a phrase corpus, the call site on the AST); four mutations fail by name (one — dropping the original rule — ESCAPED the first corpus and was closed with a case the retail list rejects but whose words all repeat the previous question); live before/after: all 8 multi-turn plans identical (@OPGGT + @PXPRODO), the genuine "show me a bar chart" follow-up still a continuation (4,084 cached, unchanged), the two false positives now reuse the full head (4,084→8,170 · 4,089→8,179); Fusion bench (fresh sessions, the path cannot fire) regression-clean (same 18 LLM calls, same corrections, 0 failures); fusion suites + BATTERY GREEN. **Seen, not caused, recorded:** a 12-row monthly trend turn headlined 180,193 against a true 179,193 under an identical plan — the report writer's own arithmetic, the known aggregate-fidelity gap, and no lineage record flagged it. Files: `agent/planner.py`, `test/{test_chart_only_query.py,trust_battery.sh}`.

- **Sep 2026**: **A figure mark never lands inside an attribute value — and a chart plots the measure, not a numeric key.** Operator, on session 42eb166c turn 2 (@PXPRODO, *"robberies per month — rising or falling?"*): *"Render error: Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON"* on the dashboard card, while an Ideate profile worked. **Root cause:** Compute with Lineage marked the SQL filter literal `2023` — and found it in the dashboard's `data-spec` attribute (the tile title *"Monthly Robbery Trend 2023"*), wrapping it in `<mark …>` INSIDE the JSON. The "never inside a tag" guard was `(?![^<]*>)` — "no `>` before the next `<`" — which a single-quoted attribute value that itself carries markup (`'{"content": "<table>…"}'`) defeats; Optimize tripped it because its SQL carried the `2023` literal. **Fix at the root, ONE tokenizer:** new `agent/html_marks.py` masks every tag WITH its quoted attribute values before any marking and restores it byte for byte, so a mark can only land in text; both answer markers route through it — the compute-lineage figure marks (`compute_lineage.mark_html`) and the grounding gate's unsupported-claim marks (`grounding/adapter.mark_unsupported_claims_html`, the same guard, the same exposure). **The chart, found on the live re-run:** with the JSON fixed, the auto-viz plotted `month_number` (1..12, a straight staircase) instead of `robbery_count` — every chart/KPI path took "the first numeric column". ONE rule `_measureIndex` in the dashboard renderer: a numeric column is key-like when its name ends in a key/ordinal word (`id`, `number`, `rank`, `code`, `year`, `month`, …) or its values are a consecutive integer run; the first non-key numeric is the measure, all-key → the last one; all four sites (G2Plot spec, KPI list, both label-merge paths) ask it. **Proof:** `test_compute_component` 143 → **147**, `test_corpus_grounding` 75 → **77**, `test_dashboard_viz_typing` 51 → **61**; three mutations fail by name (tag masking dropped in each marker; the first-numeric pick restored). Live on @PXPRODO: the spec parses, the figures in the text are still marked, the line plots robbery_count over the months. **Not repaired:** the already-persisted turn 2 of 42eb166c keeps its broken spec (re-ask, or regenerate the turn). Files: `agent/html_marks.py`, `agent/compute_lineage.py`, `agent/grounding/adapter.py`, `components/builtin/dashboard/renderer.js`, `test/{test_compute_component,test_corpus_grounding}.py`, `test/test_dashboard_viz_typing.mjs`.

- **Sep 2026**: **The streamed answer lands IN PLACE — the stream is drawn in the final answer's shape, and the line the reader is on keeps its pixel row.** Operator: *"the stream of the answer is visible but then afterwards is overlayed with a new output format … that makes it hard to follow"* — keeping the final format. Measured in headless Chrome on Ideate, three causes: (1) the authoritative answer was a NEW bubble playing the `messageFadeIn` entrance (invisible → +30px → scale .96, 0.6 s) over the text being read; (2) the stream was drawn by `marked` in the browser while the final is drawn by the formatter's own line-based renderer (`_render_standard_markdown`) — different paragraphs, colour, spacing, lists, tables; (3) the settle then followed to the bottom. **Fix — one renderer, landed in place:** `answer_stream.stream_html` renders the provisional text with the SAME formatter function the lane's final uses (markdown for Ideate/Focus/Conversation, `_render_direct_answer` while the Optimize report streams its sentence; complete lines only, an unclosed fence and a pipe line that may still become a table header held back) and `answer_delta` carries it as `html`/`html_upto` (only when the render changed, never on a withdrawn message; none for genie, whose final is rendered by the stream's own renderer). The client draws that html as-is and only the line being written itself, as the paragraph it will become (a bullet joins the list above it). At `final_answer`: `captureReadingAnchor()` before the stream is dropped (the line being written while following, else the line at the reading point), `landInPlace()` after the settle — `msg-in-place` (no entrance animation) and a scroll correction that holds the anchored line on its pixel row (found again by its words; else the answer's top edge); the settle no longer follows to the bottom. Measured after: first/middle/last lines move **0 px** at the landing and 2 s later, on Ideate, Ideate+tools and Focus. **Open, operator's call:** on Optimize the streamed sentence is not in the final when the report leads with a key figure (`_render_direct_answer` suppresses it) — position holds, the words change. Gates: `test_answer_stream` 136 → **153**, `test_answer_stream_dom` 39 → **61**, `test_living_answer_dom` 161 (two positional pins restated); ten mutations fail by name (one escaped the first fixture and was tightened); battery GREEN. Files: `agent/answer_stream.py`, `agent/execution_service.py`, `static/js/{ui,eventHandlers}.js`, `static/js/handlers/livingAnswer.js`, `static/css/main.css`, `templates/index.html` + pin cascade, `docs/RestAPI/restAPI.md` §3.13.5.

- **Sep 2026**: **Two preflight checks disagreed about the same two columns — the declared KEY is half the ontology's evidence, and the column check was reading the other half.** Operator, on the Preflight SQL card of prod session `be4979bf` turn 2 (@PXPROD): *"1 call(s) referenced non-existent column(s) v_offence.ori, v_offence.incident_number"*. **A false positive** — the statement RAN and returned rows, joining `Policing_Core.v_Offence` to `v_Incident` on exactly the key the ontology declares, and the **JOIN check on the same graph correctly recognised that key**. **Root cause:** a conformant ontology records a table's identity in TWO places — non-key attributes as `contains` edges, the key as a PROPERTY (`business_key = 'ori, incident_number, offence_seq'`) — and both column-list builders read the edges alone, so `v_Offence` was known with 10 of its 12 columns. Measured on the prod graph: 15 entities declare a key, **2 have key columns absent from their attribute list** (`Offence`, `Offence_SuspectedOfUsing` — the UNION-derived views whose keys come from the CTE rather than a registered data element), so every join on their declared key flagged. Observe mode on prod, so nothing was blocked; under `enforce` it would have blocked correct, declared-key joins — the exact inverse of the guard's purpose. **Fixed at the root, in the platform rather than the product:** new `kgstore/keys.py` is the ONE reading of an entity's declared key (`key_columns` + `with_declared_keys`), consulted by BOTH list builders (`sqlite_backend.all_table_columns`, the whole-graph session store; `handler._full_table_columns`, the per-turn event) and by the handler's existing `_key_columns`, which now delegates — two parsers over one declaration is how the two checks came to disagree. The completeness floor stays on the CONTAINS evidence and the key is unioned **after**, so adding keys can never make an incomplete list pass. **A widening I caught and reverted before shipping:** the first version also read `primary_key`/`key_columns`, which is what `source_validation` reads — that gave **3,864 entities of this instance a declared key they previously had none for**, silently changing what the JOIN guard judges (the conversation bench caught it). The runtime set is now exactly the two properties the join check has always read, proven **byte-identical to the original handler parse across 40,000 real entities**; `source_validation` keeps its deliberately wider net (a constructor-time probe, where reading one property too many costs a probe, not a verdict) and no longer delegates. Also: the header clause promising "the NAMES listed on its line" is withheld when no line carries them, and the measure/dimension bounds are split (12/6 — measures are the required argument, omitting dimensions takes them all). **The bound moved too, with its reasoning recorded in the test** (30,000 → 32,000): the worst turn had only **118 characters (0.4%) of headroom** before any of this, so no setting short of rendering nothing fits under 30,000 — and the decisive check is that **the original unbounded regression at 35,001 still fails at 32,000**, so raising it kept the gate's teeth. **Proof:** kg_enrichment_relevance 142 → **159**, kg_conversation_bench 47/2 → **49/0**, fusion 79, product_contract_render 89/1 → **90/0** (its one-source assertion counted raw occurrences of a string and was tripped by the theatre's seed-CHANNEL label — a different question over the same fact; fixed at the root with ONE `_is_product` predicate, not by relaxing the gate); **five mutations fail by name** (gate removed · declared-name signal dropped · header ungated · ordering dropped · remainder uncounted). **Live-verified on the real production metric set:** 2 of 32 metrics carry names, the right one per question, and the asked-for measure now leads its line. **Battery GREEN** — including both reds that predated this session. - **Sep 2026**: **A metric is compiled by its declared NAMES, and a cache miss is only drift where the platform asked for the bytes.** Two operator questions on prod session `d9a60903` (@IDAUTO, *"how much revenue did we generate with our cars"*), three root fixes. **(1) The enrichment never named a metric's measures.** `compile_metric` selects by declared measure NAMES, which on a real product are display-style (`Total Fi Product Revenue`), not the column they aggregate — and the METRIC ENTITIES line rendered formula, deployed, base table and `compilable` but **not the names**, while this metric's `formula` is empty, so the model had nothing to copy. It asked for the COLUMN `fi_product_revenue`, the name filter emptied, and the turn burned two tool rounds before falling back to raw SQL (which answered correctly). `resolver.resolve_capabilities` now carries `metric_measures`/`metric_dimensions` (declared order, de-duplicated, tolerant of the walker's dict shape and a bare string list); the line renders them bounded at `_METRIC_NAMES_SHOWN`=16 with the remainder **counted** (`+N more`), never dropped silently, and the group header says to use those names *exactly as written — a column name is not a measure name*. A non-compilable metric renders no names line (it would be bait). **(2) The refusal was a dead end.** `query_product`'s REJECT has always named its admissible members; `compile_metric`'s said only *"a metric query requires at least one measure"* — not that the name was unknown, not what the names are. New `no_measure_message` + `closest_declared` in `metric_compiler.py` (containment first — a column name inside a display name — then difflib on folded forms at a floor that separates a naming slip from an unrelated concept, so an unrelated name is offered **no** hint rather than a false one) make it recovery-shaped: it names every declared measure, says a column name is not a measure name, resolves `'fi_product_revenue' → closest declared: 'Total Fi Product Revenue'`, and tells the model to call again. Because it lives in the shared semantic core, the BI face (`metric_api`, the governed REST) inherits it — define once, consume everywhere. **(3) The cache reading claimed drift its own hash refuted.** The SIGNED station read *"an unchanged prefix missed the cache 1 time(s) — something in the prefix moved under the agent"* on a Gemini turn whose `prefix_hash` was unchanged and whose cached share was 42%. The attested-prefix rule was reasoned for **breakpoints** (Anthropic-shaped), where the platform asks for exactly those bytes and hashes them — there a miss does mean something *outside* the hash moved. Under **best-effort** caching (Gemini `implicit`, OpenAI-shaped `automatic`) the provider caches on its own, the platform placed no breakpoint, and a same-prefix miss on back-to-back calls is the provider's choice, not drift. `_read_prompt_cache` is now capability-aware (`CACHE_CAP_BREAKPOINTS` / `CACHE_CAPS_BEST_EFFORT`, pinned equal to `llm.cache_policy`): breakpoints still `warn` — with honest wording about what the unchanged hash implies — while best-effort is informational (`pass` with the share when something was served, `na · best-effort` when nothing was) and **never a finding**; a turn that crossed providers reads `mixed providers`. The DEFINITION sites (`MECHANISM_NOTE`, `MECHANISM_DERIVATION`, `UNGRADED_REASON`, the `cache_policy` docstring) carry the same condition as the reading — one fact, every surface, one answer, gate-asserted **per dict** (the first version joined every dict holding the key, so the derivation's wording masked a definition that had drifted back). **Proof:** pdm_metrics 100 → **110**, metric_api 44 → **47**, kg_resolver 38 → **42**, fusion_hardening_aug 74 → **79**, prompt_cache 87 → **96**; **ten mutations fail by name** (the bare refusal · a false closest-match hint · the resolver dropping the names · the line dropping them · the bound dropped · warn-on-any-miss · the best-effort branch borrowing the breakpoint wording · the vocabulary drifting from `cache_policy` · either definition dict drifting back). **Two recorded traps, both mine:** a mutation whose replacement was the *rendered* string matched nothing across a two-f-string split and mutated nothing (a no-op reads exactly like an escape); and two "escapes" were a wrong grep token — this suite prints `FAIL:`, not `✗`. **Live-proven on the real prod metric node** (`dealer.dealer_retail_sale`, 26 measures / 16 dimensions): the line now reads `compilable; measures: 'Row Count', …, 'Total Fi Product Revenue', … (+10 more); dimensions: …`, and the exact prod call returns the recovery-shaped refusal naming the closest declared name. Also fixed: `test_capsule_stamp_readings` (my own gate, one commit old) printed a result line the battery could not parse — *coverage unverifiable*, the exact half-a-gate the battery contract exists to catch — now canonical. Files: `dbdeploy/metric_compiler.py`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/{resolver,handler}.py`, `agent/assurance_points.py`, `llm/cache_policy.py`, `test/{test_pdm_metrics,test_metric_api,test_kg_resolver,test_fusion_hardening_aug,test_prompt_cache}.py`, `test/test_capsule_stamp_readings.mjs`, `docs/Architecture/{TRUST_STATUS_COMMUNICATION,KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH_ARCHITECTURE}.md`.

- **Sep 2026**: **A gate stamp with NO verdict is an absence, never a conviction — the answer capsule read "withheld — confirmed drift" under a dial reading all quiet.** Operator, on prod session 0c09571e (a @PXPRODO session-primer turn): *"why do all stations show green but at the bottom we have Grounding withheld — confirmed drift in red?"* The persisted stamp was `{ran:false, action:"na", reason:"no groundable content in this answer"}` — the grounding gate ABSTAINED (a primer acknowledgement makes no groundable claim), which `assurance_points._read_grounding` reads as `na · nothing in this answer to ground`. - **Sep 2026**: **A platform release is not an agent's deployment drift — the third shape of the TDA_* leak closed structurally, and the deployment reader stops hashing platform tools.** Operator, reading @PXPROD's SIGNED station after a prod deploy + restart: *"previously signed agents need a Re-attest — why? and why do the TDA_ tools drive this?"* The drift text was the whole story: *tools appeared: TDA_Compute · tools removed: TDA_Canvas, TDA_Charting, … (8)*. Neither is an MCP tool — they are the platform's runtime-injected categories (`System Tools` = the TDA_* framework tools, `Component Tools` = the action components), which the Sep-8 fix had stripped at the persistence chokepoint (`save_profile_classification`) — and they were back in the record, dated 2026-09-15, a week after that fix. **The restart was not the cause: the deploy that came with it changed the platform's component set (S3 shipped `TDA_Compute`), and the record carried platform tools, so the deployment hash moved.** **Root cause, the third shape:** `GET /v1/profiles/<id>/resources` (the resource panel, hit on every profile switch) read the snapshot through `get_profile_classification` — a LIVE reference into the config cache — and wrote `System Tools` + `Component Tools` into it for rendering; the next plain `update_profile` (any editor save, an activation-list write, a pack sync — none of which pass the stripping saver) persisted the enrichment. Worse, the endpoint assigned only the tools it found MISSING over the existing category, so a record holding the 8 pre-S3 components was rewritten to `[TDA_Compute]` alone — exactly the "1 appeared, 8 removed" the screenshot shows. Measured on prod: **49 of 91 snapshots polluted; of 57 deployment attestations, 10 read green only because they were attested OVER a polluted record** (they flip the moment the component set changes). Proven step by step on the OLD code: the GET alone changes nothing on disk, the following PUT persists the cache. **Fixes at three layers, each gate-asserted and mutation-tested:** (1) **structural** — `get_profile_classification` hands out a `deepcopy`, so no reader can mutate the record again (two readers fixed one at a time was a per-caller guard; the third would have come); (2) the endpoint copies AND merges the component category instead of replacing it; (3) **the trust reader** `catalog_from_classification` ignores the injected categories — by the ONE declared set `config_manager.RUNTIME_INJECTED_CATEGORIES` (the saver's own constant, now module-level), never a name heuristic, so an MCP tool named `TDA_something` stays in the surface, and a record that predates the strip no longer moves the badge when the platform adds a component. **Repair:** the existing purge cleans records (container stopped — the cache trap); new `maintenance/normalize_deployment_attestations.py` rewrites an attestation ONLY when platform tool names are the sole difference between attested and live (signer + time preserved, a note appended, DB backed up; model/connector/real-tool drift is left as genuine). Live-verified locally: purge → restart → resources GET → profile PUT → the record keeps only `All Tools`; the normalizer moved @PXPROD's deployment half `changed → trusted` with offline verify intact. **Recorded, and paid for again:** a mutation harness restoring with `git checkout -- <file>` silently discarded the UNCOMMITTED fix, so the first live experiment ran on the old code — restore from a copy, never from HEAD. Gate `test_classification_snapshot_isolation` 34 → **49** (getter copy incl. nested; every injector's category literal ∈ the declared set; the endpoint copies + merges; the reader hashes a polluted record equal to a clean one, a component-set swap is no drift, a look-alike MCP name survives); three mutations fail by name. - **Sep 2026**: **A figure the turn's INPUTS account for is never "the agent's own arithmetic" — Compute with Lineage learns two classes, `literal` and `declared`.** Operator, on prod session 03d85a6c turn 2 (@PXPROD, *"How many robberies are there?"*): the receipt traced 179,193 to its row and then called the offence code **`'120'`** *"the agent's own arithmetic"*. It came from the knowledge graph's value domain AND from the agent's own `WHERE offence_code = '120'` — the classifier knew only receipts and result ROWS, so a figure the turn's inputs vouch for was convicted beside genuine invention. Two new classes in ONE order (receipted → quoted row → row count → **literal → declared** → asked → short → unreceipted): a **literal** is a standalone number in a data statement the turn ran (a comparison, an `IN` member, a `BETWEEN` end, a date literal's year, a `TOP`/`LIMIT` bound — never an identifier fragment like `V4019`, never a positional function argument like `SUBSTR(…, 8, 4)`), traced *"used as a filter in statement N"* / *"the bound of statement N"*; a **declared** figure is a code the graph's value domains declare on a CODED column, traced to `<leaf>.<column> (label)`. **The label follows the COLUMN, never the value** — the first live replay attached *Handgun* to the robbery filter because `'120'` is Robbery on `offence_code` and Handgun on `armed_with_code` and the lookup was keyed by code alone; `literal_column` now reads the compared column off the statement (`=`, `IN`, `BETWEEN`, alias-qualified), every candidate per code is kept, and a label is attached only on the literal's own column; a bare code declared on several columns says so and asserts none. The seam (`executor._run_compute_lineage`) hands the enrichment event's `value_domains` to `assess`; `numeric_fidelity` counts both classes as traceable; the GROUNDED reading, the Live Status card (*From the statement* / *Declared*) and the lineage dialog (*Used as a filter in statement 1 — <SQL>*) speak them; a literal wears the quoted mark with `data-literal`, a declared code a plain `figure-declared` span that opens nothing. Genuine arithmetic beside them is still convicted (gate-asserted); the legacy event shape and a turn without literals/codes are byte-identical. Gate `test_compute_component` 117 → **143** (extraction truth table, column resolution, the ambiguity case, the prod turn, ordering, marks, seam + scorer on the AST, live scorer), `test_figure_lineage` 17 → **21**; **eight mutations fail by name** (incl. label-by-value and first-candidate-on-ambiguity); pins cascaded (`ui 1.142`, `figureLineage 1.8`, `trust.css 11.2`); `test_pack_skill_ownership` re-pinned from a literal to its property (36). Live-verified: the prod turn replayed locally reads *used as a filter in statement 1 — a declared code of v_Offence.offence_code (Robbery)*, `decision=pass`, no FIGURES note. - **Sep 2026**: **Session cost is a property of the SESSION — one definition, every reader; it no longer moves with which answer of an experiment is adopted.** Operator, on prod session 856afac4 (a regenerate): *"the session total (tokens) doesn't change if I swap cases — but the session cost changes — I think this is a flaw."* Correct, and it was two definitions on one KPI row: the plan-reload endpoint overlaid the session TOKENS from the session-level counters (whole session, always current) but the session COST from the turn's frozen `session_cost_usd` snapshot ("cost up to and including this turn, at the time it ran"), and the session-load path read the LAST turn's snapshot — so answer 1 carried $0.0039 (only itself existed), answer 2 carried $0.0094 (both), and adoption chose which one the KPI showed; post-hoc costs (judges, extensions) billed to an earlier turn staled the newest snapshot the same way. **The audit covered every producer and reader** (six engine persist sites incl. the executor's partial save · `update_turn_token_counts`' prefix recompute · the reload endpoint · the session GET · the live `_recomputeLiveCost` base · the session UI cache · the flow-run turn, which stamps `turn_cost 0` but `session_cost_usd = flow cost` · the Awareness analytics). **ONE definition** `session_manager.session_cost_total(session_data)` = Σ `turn_cost` over EVERY turn in the record — a non-adopted sibling and a purged/toggled-out turn (`isValid:false`) count, because they spent the money and the token counters beside it never subtract either; a legacy turn is priced from its tokens at its own provider/model; a flow-run turn contributes its `turn_cost` (0), exactly as its 0 turn tokens enter the counters. Every reader derives from it: the reload endpoint overlays it UNCONDITIONALLY beside the token overlay (the "only if missing" prefix-sum that served the snapshot is gone), the session GET serves it at the top level and `sessionManagement.js` prefers it (the last turn's snapshot stays the fallback for an older backend) and seeds the live ledger's base from it, and `executor._calculate_session_cost_at_turn` — the engines' snapshot — delegates to it, so the snapshot and the live figure are the same arithmetic. The per-turn snapshots themselves are untouched (audit records) and the flow-run stamp is now inert for every reader. **Proven live** on a real regenerate through the UI (headless Chrome): stored snapshots `{1: 0.002862, 2: 0.00387}` — the exact two figures the KPI toggled between — and the KPI now reads `$0.003870` across every adoption, both readers equal to Σ. New gate `test_session_cost_total` (**16**: the truth table incl. invariance under adoption, the flow turn, legacy pricing and its fail-soft, every reader on the AST, the frontend preference); two mutations (siblings skipped · the reload serves the snapshot when one exists) fail by name; turn_cost 44 · siblings 67 · baseline 14 · fusion 122 · eval_online 126 · genie_ux 42 · flow contract 89 regression-clean; pins cascaded (`sessionManagement 3.71` → `main 9.82`, gate 90). **Recorded, not changed:** the Awareness cost analytics (`rest_routes.py` ~12409) re-prices from tokens at the session model and skips `isValid:false` turns — since S8 that excludes a non-adopted sibling's spend from the analytics; a separate surface with a separate contract, left for its own decision. - **Sep 2026**: **"Recalled proven strategies · none matched" on a turn a champion had guided — the event's existence IS the fact.** Operator, on prod session 856afac4 (@OPTIM, guided by champion `7c478fd7` from planner 26): *"shows 'none matched' even though a CCR has been used — why?"* The planner emits `rag_retrieval` ONLY when cases matched (`if retrieved_cases:`), and its payload is the FIRST case (`case_id` + `full_case_data`) — no `count`, no `cases` list — while the receipt's reducer read exactly `d.count || d.cases.length`, got 0, and printed the opposite of what the event's arrival means. - **Sep 2026**: **The grid is one type system, and the receipt's marks speak one vocabulary — grey is the absence family, never "done".** Three operator findings on the shipped body, read from screenshots. **(1)** *"can we please left align the table data?"* — then, on the screenshot, *"it currently looks very inconsistent"*: the seam was not only the alignment split but TWO type systems in one row (sans names left, mono digits right). Every column of `table.ans-t` is now left-aligned and every cell is set in the body's typeface; a numeric cell keeps its `ans-num` mark and the grid's tabular figures, so digits still stack on the left edge — one table, not two. **(2)** *"we must come up with a consistent nomenclature for the colouring of the dots — and when a step is active"*: the receipt spent green twice — as a CHECK's verdict (`la-gate.la-pass`) AND as an ACT's colour (`la-fix`: a correction, a retry, a fallback) — so *Corrected the statement* read green beside a grey *Computed the figures*, both acts. The vocabulary, recorded in the stylesheet and gated: an **act** (assembled · read · queried · computed · corrected · retried · served by the fallback) carries no verdict, so no colour — its fact (*no LLM round spent*) is carried by its words; a **check** (sources · screen · claims · figures · revision) carries a verdict and wears the trust family verbatim (solid pass · half warn · outlined danger); **running** is one signal for both populations, the breathing accent. **(3)** *"grey looks like inactive — this is why I don't like it"* and *"what does 'worked' mean — and why does it have a grey dot?"*: grey is the absence family on every trust surface (dashed *did not run* / *not turned on*), so a solid grey dot on a finished act — and the work line's 55%-grey dot on settle — said *inactive* where they meant *done*. A done act is now a **solid dot at full text strength** (`--text-primary`, light on dark / dark on light: *it happened*), and the work line uses the receipt's words with the same dot: **Working** (steps running, breathing) → **Writing** (folded at the first token — the work is done but the answer is still being written, so *Done* there would be false) → **Done** (settled, solid), or **Stopped**; "Worked" is retired. **Proof:** `test_answer_surface` 93 → **94** (one type system per row), `test_living_answer_dom` 147 → **150** (no `la-fix` rule paints a trust colour, a fix chip is never a gate, the default mark is `--text-primary` never `--text-muted`, the three state words at fold/settle/reload); live in headless Chrome, both themes: the work line's dot orange through *Assembling … Computed … Writing*, solid on *Done*; every act row solid full-strength, every check row green. Manual §2.3 records the vocabulary; public trust site regenerated. - **Sep 2026**: **Every hardened agent read 🟠 `changed` after the S5/S7 deploy — a NEW signed key flipped attestations that nothing about the agent had earned; a key registered after the attestation baseline is now omitted at its defaults.** Operator: *"validate why all agents of the demo walkthrough user are now unsigned again — is this associated with a platform restart?"* Not a restart. - **Sep 2026**: **S1.1 — The Living Answer: the streaming answer as ONE bubble with a lifecycle, every motion carrying a fact (on `main`, default ON wherever S1 streams).** A market assessment (Claude.ai/Code · ChatGPT · Gemini 3.8 · Perplexity · Cursor 3 · Copilot · Databricks Genie · Snowflake Intelligence · ThoughtSpot) found the field converged on four patterns — a calm status line before the first token, a collapsible process block that streams and then folds to one summary line, chunked reveal with a caret, Stop at the composer — and that **nobody renders verification as part of the stream**. S1 shipped the mechanics (one provisional bubble, a caret, the follow lock, Stop where Send was) and left the column EMPTY between Send and the first token — on an Optimize turn the whole planning + tool phase. **Built (`static/js/handlers/livingAnswer.js`, a plain script; the S1 bubble in `ui.js` streams INTO it and is byte-identical without it):** six acts on ONE bubble — **Born** at `task_start` (a status line in plain words + elapsed seconds + the turn's tokens; a six-phase rail — context · retrieve · reason · draft · screen · seal — whose RUNNER's position is the phase); **Working** — each curated step lands as a CHIP in consumer words (*Assembled the context · 6 modules*, *Queried fitness_db.Sales · 32 rows*, *Asked @NIBRS · answered · 3.2s*, *Considered your steer*, *Corrected the statement · no LLM round spent*, *Served by the fallback*; a running chip breathes, then SNAPS to its fact) and opens its Live Status card (depth 3); **Fold** at the first token — the chips converge into a summary line with counters that count up (*Worked 5.2s · 1 query · 4 entities*), click reopens (depth 2); **Writing** — only the new characters rise in (batches younger than the animation are re-wrapped with a negative delay so a rise completes across re-renders), a table renders once its header row closes, a fence once it closes; **Settle** — the chrome moves onto the authoritative message and the marks it carries LAND in place (a `[REDACTED:…]` span swept on, `mark.claim-unsupported` drawn, a receipted figure underlined), the gate events (`grounding_gate` · `guardrail` · `honesty` · `compute_lineage`) having filled the rail by SHAPE (solid · half · outlined · dashed = held · worth a look · found something · did not run); **Sealed** — the seal pops on `turn_score_complete` (or at the stream's end once persisted) and the summary ends with its word (*clean* / *N findings*). **ONE clock** — every motion keys off event arrival, never a timer; reduced motion keeps every fact and removes the travel; theme tokens only. **Gate on the server's word:** `task_start.stream` is stamped only under `APP_CONFIG.ANSWER_STREAMING` (`routes.py`), so the baseline is byte-identical off; per-viewer opt-out `localStorage.tda_living_answer=0`. **A pre-existing S1 defect the live drive exposed, fixed at the client:** the cancel endpoint queues its `cancelled` frame the instant it cancels and the executor yields its own while unwinding, so BOTH precede the partial `final_answer` — the client drew a CANCELLED line and dropped the bubble the partial was about to land in; the CANCELLED line + teardown are now DEFERRED to the stream's end and drawn only when no partial arrived (`test_answer_stream_dom` re-pinned to the rule). **Proof:** `test_living_answer_dom.mjs` (**69** — the shipped module executed under the DOM stub across Ideate+tools · Focus · Optimize · Conversation · Coordinate · Stop · abort · session switch · opt-out, plus the wiring on the AST of five files); **12 mutations fail by name** — one ESCAPED the first pass (`indexOf < i` accepts −1, so a dropped rail read as transplanted) and was hardened rather than accepted; the DOM stub gained `isConnected` + a reflecting `hidden`; every JS gate green (pins cascaded to a fixpoint, inventory re-baselined with the module classified as a trust surface); **live, headless Chrome against a real server, six real turns**: Ideate+tools · Optimize · Ideate+KG (@IDAIRL: 5 queries · 1 correction · 8 receipts) · Focus (10 documents) · Stop (partial kept, hairline, no CANCELLED line) · Optimize in light theme — born 0.6–1.1 s after Send, first token 1.7–8.6 s, every contract check green, zero page errors. **Recorded, not built:** the process block + rail on a RELOADED historical turn (Live Status reload already carries depth 3); a per-agent chip allow-list beyond the one curated map. - **Sep 2026**: **Two concurrent users, one process — the adapter's in-turn LLM tasks and tool routing read THIS turn's identity, never the process-global slots (found by the first prod check after the S1–S10 flip; pre-existing, not the switches).** With the admin's Optimize turn (OpenRouter, server A) running beside the demo account's Gemini turn (server B): **(1)** `get_user_mcp_server_id` validated the per-user server id against the process-global `APP_STATE['mcp_client']` — which holds whichever server the LAST user to activate a profile connected — declared A's id "stale", and **rerouted A's tool calls to B's policing endpoint** (the correct per-turn overlay client, holding only A's server, then raised "couldn't find server"); a silent cross-tenant reroute. Now validated against the **user's own configured servers** (`config_manager.get_mcp_servers(user_uuid)`); a genuinely stale id falls back to that user's own first server, never another user's. **(2)** the four in-turn LLM tasks in `mcp_adapter` (filter · core · final report · complex report) read `STATE.get('llm')` and passed no provider, so `call_llm_api` fell back to `APP_CONFIG.CURRENT_PROVIDER` = B's Google and dispatched A's OpenRouter `AsyncOpenAI` client through the Google branch (`'AsyncOpenAI' object has no attribute 'aio'` — the turn died at `TDA_FinalReport`). ONE rule `adapter.turn_llm(STATE, user_uuid)`: the `@TAG` overlay (now carrying `llm_provider`/`llm_model`/`mcp_server_id`) wins outright; else the PER-USER registry (`llm_by_user` / `current_provider_by_user` — the executor's own authority); the global slot only as the last resort. `invoke_mcp_tool` prefers the overlay's own server id. Gate `test_provider_globals_isolation` 23 → **37** (+ it and `test_rest_activation_firewall` join the battery they had sat outside of); both mutations fail by name. - **Sep 2026**: **S1–S10 merged to `main` and switched ON by default in `docker-compose.yml` (S9 excepted).** The ten `TDA_*` deployment masters were not forwarded into the container at all (Docker passes nothing it is not told to), so "on" had to be a compose edit. Recommended posture, recorded in the compose block itself: **S1 streaming · S2 prompt caching · S4 resilience · S8 regenerate/branch · S10 steer & reattach ON** (visible or cheaper on every turn, nothing to opt into); **S5 budget · S6 tool surface · S7 outcome loop ON but inert** until a profile opts in (`turnBudget` · `toolSurface.mode=governed` · `outcomeConfig.enabled` + a gate at annotate/enforce); **S3 compute lineage ON** — the one increment that adds a tool + companion skill to every data turn, so verify with a real turn per class after the first prod flip; **S9 attachment sources OFF** until the image carries `rapidocr-onnxruntime pdfplumber` (without them every image reads "not readable", which is honest but a downgrade from the model seeing it natively). A fallback LLM (S4) is a per-profile binding, not the switch. Any switch reverts to the byte-identical baseline with `=0` in the untracked `.env`. Files: `docker-compose.yml`.

- **Sep 2026**: **S10 Steer & Reattach — talk to the agent while it works; a running turn never dies with the tab (branch `feature/beyond-claude-agent`, off by default).** Two properties a running turn lacked, one substrate. **Reattach:** `core/turn_stream.py` is a process-global, cursor-numbered per-task event log written at the ONE place every UI frame passes (`routes.py /ask_stream`'s queue) — `open` at `task_start` (payload gains `reattach: true`), `append`+`stamp` (the SSE-standard `id: <seq>` resume field on every frame), `mark_done` in the task's `finally`, `events_since` with a retained floor (4000 frames; below it a DECLARED `reattach_gap`, never a silent skip), `active_for_session`, an async `tail` (asyncio.Event wake, `: ping`, `reattach_end`), a finished log kept 15 min. The turn never knows it was reattached, so every lane inherits it. **Steer:** `core/steer.py` — a bounded per-session queue (5 waiting · 600 chars) delivered at the agent's NEXT STEP on every lane: prepended to the next tool result (`tool_enforcement._lead` — keeps the content_and_artifact tuple and the MCP content-block shapes), the next tactical prompt (Optimize), the final-report prompt (`TDA_FinalReport`), or **carried** to the next turn and delivered after its question — recorded either way (`turn_data.steers`: considered-at / carried; a live `steer_consumed` notification). **The deviation, recorded:** the Messages API — and every provider the platform speaks — has no mid-conversation `system` role, so the one mechanism everywhere is a note at the next step under an explicit operator lead (*"the user changed the instructions while you were working … this wins"*); the live runs taught two things about the MODEL, not the seam — a note APPENDED after a long JSON tool result was ignored (prepend), a carried steer BEFORE the next question was ignored (after). REST: `POST /v1/sessions/<id>/steer` (202 · 409 `no_running_turn` · 400 `invalid_steer`), `GET …/steers`, `GET …/active-task`, `GET /v1/tasks/<id>/events?since=`, `GET /v1/tasks/<id>/stream?since=` — owner-scoped, `404 steer_reattach_disabled` off. **UX** (`steerReattach.js`): the composer stays LIVE while an answer streams (*Steer the agent — considered at its next step*; Enter steers, the button stops via `e.submitter`), a steer pin under the question (`role=note`, *sent* → *considered with the result of base_readQuery*, a polite live region), the *Steer Considered* / *Steer Carried to the Next Turn* step live + on reload, `processStream` reading the cursor and `_maybeReattach` tailing through the SAME renderer on a drop (bounded retries, `404` = gone, *reconnected — caught up*), `reattachRunningTurn` on a fresh tab / session switch (the turn shown running, its trace backfilled). Under `APP_CONFIG.STEER_REATTACH` (env `TDA_STEER_REATTACH`; off ⇒ byte-identical, frozen by `test_steer_reattach_baseline` 10). Gates `test_steer_reattach` 48 + `test_steer_reattach_ui.mjs` 33 (the shipped module executed under the shared DOM stub, which gained `removeAttribute`), both in the battery; **25 mutations fail by name** — two ESCAPED the first pass (a cursor moving backwards; the consumed-guard masked by idempotency) and were closed rather than accepted. Bench (`conversation_lane_bench.py --drop --steer`, the first question per class cut after six frames): off → `resumed` 0, `answered` 0.5/0.8, the steer refused; on → `resumed` 1, `answered` 1/1, react `steer_considered` 1 at `base_readQuery` with the answer in German, the pure-LLM ideate turn honestly `carried`; cost and latency flat. A bench defect found on the way: the refactored consumer returned at `final_answer` and raced the turn's persistence (every column empty) — a stream is consumed to its END, because the server closes it only after the record is written. **Honest limits:** compliance is the model's — the record says WHERE, the answer shows WHETHER; a pure LLM turn cannot be steered mid-turn on any provider (carried, said so); a carried steer rides the next turn's stored `user_query`; the log is per process (a multi-worker deployment needs a shared store — four functions). - **Sep 2026**: **S9 — Grounded Multimodal: an attachment is a source, not a prompt (branch `feature/beyond-claude-agent`).** The parity move (the model sees an image natively) already existed; the beyond is that **the platform reads the attachment itself and vouches for what it read.** Under `APP_CONFIG.ATTACHMENT_SOURCES` (env `TDA_ATTACHMENT_SOURCES`, default off = byte-identical, frozen by `test_attachment_sources_baseline` over the real loaders + the eval record). ONE pure module `llm/image_sources.py`: `extract` — an image's OCR boxes clustered into rows/columns by `table_from_boxes` (rows at 0.6× the median box height, columns by the widest row's anchors, captions dropped, the header detected as a non-numeric first row over numeric rows); a PDF's tables + text (pdfplumber), a text-less PDF rendered and OCR'd; CSV/TSV; text/docx — `source_text` for a VERIFIED source only, `document_text_for` for the model (with a provenance line), `to_record`/`from_record` for the manifest, a per-turn contextvar registry. **Three states, one rule:** *verified* = read by the platform, joins the grounding evidence (`RunRecord.grounding_text` + `attachment_chunks`, merged into the gate's turn by `run_grounding`) and its tables become S3 result sets (`result_sets.register`, a non-tool registration carrying `source` — the compute stamp persists it even with no receipt, so a quoted figure traces to the image on reload); *unverified* = the model's own transcription of an image nothing could read (per-agent opt-in `attachmentConfig.transcribeImages`, its own minimal system prompt — under the master prompt the model answered with a tool-call JSON), recorded and **never evidence**; *unread* = the model saw it natively, nothing vouched. **Proven live:** on a text-less bar chart the model transcribed `1 | 75 · 2 | 45 · 3 | 25` (invented) and stated them as facts — stamped unverified, excluded from the grounding text, the GROUNDED station warns. Extraction happens ONCE at upload (the endpoint stores the full record and replaces the image placeholder / plain text with the platform's reading for text-only providers; `.csv`/`.tsv` join the formats; capabilities name the engines); the executor seam after the document loaders registers the sources, the tables, appends an image's rows to the document context once, yields the *Attachments Read as Sources* step; genie registers through `register_from_manifest`; the persistence chokepoint stamps `attachment_sources` (evidence text in full — one text, two moments); the GROUNDED reading `na · pass · warn · na`; a session-scoped content endpoint serves the bytes. UI (`attachmentSources.js`): the badge in words on every chip (`read · OCR · 1 table · 3 rows` at upload → `used as source · …` after the turn, flipped live by the standard render path the step reaches before engine dispatch), thumbnails with alt text FROM the extraction (data: URLs — the CSP allows `data:`, deliberately not `blob:`), the capsule's **Attachments** row with a crop of the cited region, the lineage dialog opening an attachment statement on file/region/row, a keyboard-removable named remove control. `test/dom_stub.mjs` gained `insertAdjacentHTML`/`outerHTML`. Bench (`--attachments`, ideate + react): off → `numeric_fidelity` None, `figures` 0; on → sourced 1 · verified 1 · `figures_from_attachment` 6 / 2 · fidelity 1.0, cost and tokens flat. Live (IDPURE + an OCR'd table): APAC quoted from row 2 of statement 1, the total honestly disclosed as the agent's own arithmetic; headless Chrome both themes: chip, thumbnail, crop (region outlined), lineage crop + highlighted row, composer badge, keyboard removal, zero page errors. - **Sep 2026**: **S8 — Regenerate as an Experiment: a second answer, and the reason to prefer it (branch `feature/beyond-claude-agent`).** A regenerate is a **scored sibling** — a new turn under the SAME question (no second user message), run through the ordinary execution path by any engine, scored like any turn, compared by the Scorecard's verdicts; exactly one sibling is **adopted** (the newest on arrival; Adopt reverts — the record keeps every sibling). An edit-and-resend is a **branch**: the edited question heads a new branch, the turns it displaces stay in the record, the view (and the model's context) follows the active branch; branches nest. Under `APP_CONFIG.TURN_LINEAGE` (env `TDA_TURN_LINEAGE`, default off = byte-identical, frozen by `test_turn_lineage_baseline`). ONE pure module `agent/turn_lineage.py` (readers · acts · ONE validity rule), the relation armed at the execution seam and read by the two session_manager seams — an edit's head registered BEFORE its message lands, a sibling's answer numbered with its OWN turn and INSERTED beside its question in BOTH histories (the context stays `user · adopted answer · user · answer`), the record stamped at the persistence chokepoint; **ONE mechanism for "not in the model's context"** — the existing `isValid` flag every reader honours; a sibling **travels with its question** (it inherits the root's branch). UI: `turnLineage.js` — the **Experiment** card under the adopted answer (verdict strips drawn by the Agents lens's ONE mark builder, published as `window.agentPerformance.mark`; Adopt; a two-column compare; arrows/Enter), the branch switch, **Regenerate ▾** (same or any activated agent; `r`) and the inline **Edit → Resend as a branch**; every act re-reads the session (`handleLoadSession(…, force)` — the one reloader). **Found live, fixed at the root:** a sibling of a pre-branch question was displaced by the branch (cut-off on its own number) → judged on the root; the post-stream reload was a no-op (early return for the session on screen) → forced. `test/dom_stub.mjs` — a shared DOM for executing plain-script modules under Node. - **Sep 2026**: **S7 — the Outcome Loop: the gate's finding goes back to the model ONCE, and the same gate grades the revision (branch `feature/beyond-claude-agent`).** Until now a grounding finding was a verdict ON the answer — annotated or withheld — never an input the model could act on. Now, with `APP_CONFIG.OUTCOME_LOOP` (env `TDA_OUTCOME_LOOP`, default off = byte-identical, frozen by `test_outcome_loop_baseline`) and a profile's `outcomeConfig {enabled, maxRevisions ∈ {1,2}, revisableKinds}` (signed posture: `enabled` a flag, `maxRevisions` a floor under the downgrade guard; absent hashes as `{enabled:false}`), a draft the gate ANNOTATES with a **fixable deterministic finding** (an unsupported claim · a reference outside the declared scope · a figure no result holds — a judge's ruling is a verdict, never a span) is handed back to the model with the finding, its exact spans and the fix, and the revision is **re-graded by the same gate**: cleared → delivered clean with its own verdict; not cleared → the honest annotated FIRST draft, never the failed revision, *never a second silent try*; never on a block; fails open. - **Sep 2026**: **S6 — The Governed Tool Surface: only the tools that could answer, and a record of why (branch `feature/beyond-claude-agent`).** Uderia already KNOWS which tools a turn can need — the KG enrichment names the tables in play, the classification names each tool's category, Agent Authority names what is denied — so under `TOOL_SURFACE` (env `TDA_TOOL_SURFACE`, default off ⇒ byte-identical, frozen by `test_tool_surface_baseline`) a profile with `toolSurface.mode: governed` (portable, **unsigned** — what the model SEES, never what it MAY do) is shown only the tools that could answer THIS turn: ONE pure selector `agent/tool_surface.py` — the discovery/execution backbone (`DISCOVERY_TOOLS` + the SQL executor) and every `TDA_*` always; a tool whose identifier tokens (name · category · description) overlap the question's vocabulary ∪ the enrichment's entity leaves; a category the question names lifted whole; Agent Authority's denials first — **never offered, never findable**; the rest HELD with a reason per tool. `TDA_FindTools` (a headless builtin, relevant only under switch ∧ governed) searches the held set with the same scorer, widens the surface (recorded), names a denied match as a finding, returns the closest held names when nothing matches. **Optimize**: armed BEFORE context-window assembly as a per-executor STATE overlay (the @TAG ChainMap precedent — `structured_tools` filtered, `tools_context` rebuilt, `mcp_tools` whole so a found tool still executes), the `tool_definitions` module renders the ambient surface, and the planner RE-SELECTS after the KG enrichment (offered can only grow; the cached contribution re-rendered). **ReAct**: a LangGraph **dynamic model** binds offered ∪ found per call while the ToolNode holds every tool — a held tool's schema never enters the prefix until found (LangGraph 1.0's native deferred-schema form). The `tool_surface` stamp at the persistence chokepoint; the `tool_surface` mechanism at BOUNDED (owns nothing; a denied tool asked for = warn, acted); the *Tool Surface* Live Status card (chips per set, reason on hover; live + reload); the editor's Tool Surface select beside the MCP server. **Found live, fixed at the root:** the first arming site (the planner) ran AFTER the context window had already rendered the catalog, so the surface never reached the prompt (planning tokens flat) — moved before assembly + module reads the surface + a re-select step; the assembly's `isinstance(app_state, dict)` hid every ChainMap overlay from the `tool_definitions` module (a latent @TAG-override bug) → `.get`-based. - **Sep 2026**: **S5 — The Visible Budget: a turn that paces itself, and hands back what is left (branch `feature/beyond-claude-agent`).** A profile declares how much ONE turn may spend — `turnBudget` {steps · tokens · seconds}, each optional, **signed as posture** with every unit a ceiling under the downgrade guard — and under the deployment switch `TURN_BUDGET` (env `TDA_TURN_BUDGET`, default off ⇒ byte-identical, frozen by `test_turn_budget_baseline`) the model SEES what is left: at every tool boundary the result carries a `[Budget] 2 of 6 steps used · ~9k of ~40k tokens used.` note (nearly used at 75%; the finish instruction once a unit is exhausted), and a further data-tool call is then REFUSED, recovery-shaped (the tool, the unit, *answer now with what you have and say what is left*) — exhaustion is a **recorded graceful finish**, never a killed turn; the hard stops (cost cap, input-token cap) stay the last line one unit above and a turn they stop is stamped `killed`, never graceful. ONE pure core `agent/turn_budget.py` + a per-turn contextvar armed at the execution seam; the two chokepoints (`tool_enforcement._guarded` gate-before + note-after, `TDA_*` never counted or refused; the adapter's success seam counts the step); tokens recorded at every accounting seam (executor · ReAct · genie); the Optimize phase loop **skips** the data phases the budget cannot afford (a parallel group TRIMMED to what is left, synthesis kept, the skip recorded AND yielded live as a `turn_budget` step) and the report prompt carries the finish instruction; the quiet **finish line** under the answer (text + html, `role=note`) beside the S3 seam on both delivering engines; the `budget` stamp at the persistence chokepoint. **The mechanism `turn_budget` at BOUNDED OWNS `budget_adherence`** (1.0 within · 0.5 graceful · 0.0 killed · abstain) — a budget is a boundary and its adherence a measurement of that boundary, so unlike S2–S4 this mechanism owns its dimension (STATION_DIMS · qualityDimensions · AGENT_QUALITY_DIMENSIONS · stages in step; the contract's posture set gains `turnBudget`). UX: the **Turn budget bar** in the Live Status header (`budgetBar.js` — a real `progressbar` per unit, `aria-valuetext` in WORDS, colour = attention: amber ≥80%, red only exhausted, the ending in words; session-guarded, reset per turn, restored on reload from the stamp; fed by a `turn_budget` notice over the notification channel at every boundary), the `turn_budget` Live Status card (live + reload through the shared title helper), the **Continue where it stopped** chip in the dock (component-independent, offered before the enabled-components early return — its turn picks up exactly the remaining work with its own budget), the editor's Turn Budget card under Trust Configuration → BOUNDED. **Two defects the live run found, both fixed at the root:** a model firing FIVE tool calls in one round passed every one through a gate that still read "0 used" (the step was counted AFTER the run while the batch ran under `asyncio.gather`; live: *5 of 2 steps used, 0 refusals*) — the budget is now RESERVED at the gate (`claim`/`claim_seen`, one count per gated pair, the ungated adapter seam still counts once) and the batch case is a load-bearing gate assertion; and the Optimize skip fired only at group boundaries, so two data phases of one parallel group both ran under a 1-step budget — the group is trimmed to what is left. Gates `test_turn_budget` **114** (+ freeze 11) + `test_turn_budget_ui.mjs` **33**; **21 mutations fail by name** (16 backend incl. the batch overrun and the count-after revert, 5 frontend); battery GREEN (two S4/dial pins that grepped exact chain literals converted to properties). Bench (react + optimize, off → on): `budget_armed` 0 → 1, `graceful` 0 → 0.5 / 0.75, `killed` 0, `answered` 1 → 1, cost + latency flat; live: a ReAct turn under `steps: 2` asked for five counts — **2 ran, 3 refused before running**, the answer named the three tables left, the Continue turn retrieved exactly those; headless Chrome both themes (progressbar roles + words + token colours, keyboard focus + tooltip, three cards on reload, the chip first, zero errors). - **Sep 2026**: **S4 — the Resilience Envelope: retries you can audit, fallbacks you can trust (branch `feature/beyond-claude-agent`, spec `BEYOND_CLAUDE_CONVERSATION_AGENT.md` §S4).** Behind the master `APP_CONFIG.RESILIENCE_ENVELOPE` (env `TDA_RESILIENCE_ENVELOPE`, default off ⇒ the pre-S4 retry loop and the plain LangChain classes byte for byte — `test_resilience_baseline` EXECUTES that loop with a fake provider and pins its retries, backoff and re-raise). **ONE pure policy** `llm/resilience.py`: `classify(exc)` — retryable (rate limit · overloaded · server · timeout · connection) vs terminal (auth · bad request · context too long · not found · **unknown — retrying a bug is noise**) vs refusal; `backoff` honours the provider's `retry-after` up to 60 s (beyond that it is "come back later", not a wait), else base·2^(n−1) capped at 30 s; `finish_kind` (stopped · truncated · refused, every SDK's spelling); a **bounded continuation** (the partial rides as the assistant's prior turn + one "continue exactly, never restate" instruction, at most 2, joined without a separator, a restated tail trimmed); `refusal_answer` (an honest delivered answer naming the category — never a canned "technical error"). **Two actors, every lane:** the handler's attempt loop (all provider branches build their messages from `history_source` + `prompt`, so ONE substitution continues them all; a refusal raises `ProviderRefusal` which `executor._call_llm_and_update_tokens` turns into the honest answer, 0 tokens, gated and sealed like any answer) and `llm/resilient_chat.py` for the LangChain lanes — the instance is **re-classed in place** (`object.__setattr__(inst, '__class__', Sub)`, the `_ThinkingAwareChatGoogle` precedent generalised per provider class) so the provider's constructor, fields and `bind_tools` are untouched; the RAW tools are remembered on `bind_tools` and **re-bound in the fallback provider's format** on a cross-provider fallback; the fallback is called through its own `_agenerate`/`_astream` directly (no nested LangChain run — the lane's callbacks see ONE call); a stream that has already yielded is never re-run. **The signed fallback:** `llmFallbackConfigurationId` is an instance BINDING (never portable) resolved ONCE at the execution seam — `resolve_fallback` accepts only that configuration, only if the user owns it, never the primary, never anything improvised; a fallback never falls back (depth guard at both sites); its resolved identity enters the **deployment half of the trust envelope** (`fallback_llm`, absent when none is bound so no attestation written before S4 moves; `describe_drift` names a changed fallback). **The breaker** `core/provider_health.py` (process-wide, per provider): 3 consecutive RETRYABLE failures inside 120 s open it 60 s (doubling per re-trip, capped 10 min), half-open admits one probe, a success closes it; open + a fallback ⇒ the fallback serves IMMEDIATELY (the timeout is never paid); open + no fallback ⇒ attempted once, no backoff — a breaker never refuses service for lack of an alternative; a terminal error or a refusal is never a breaker failure. **Every act is a record:** `agent/resilience_envelope.py:TurnResilience` (a contextvar) records each `RecoveryStep`, broadcasts it live as an `llm_recovery` Live Status step over the per-user notification channel (the judge-step precedent), `ProvenanceChain.finalize()` seals the steps as `llm_recovery` at the ONE chokepoint (timestamp-free content; `verify_content` re-derives them from the stamp — a tampered step is a named mismatch), `update_last_turn_data` stamps `turn['resilience']` (steps · counts · primary · `served_by` · refusal; absent when nothing was recovered), `served_model()` is the one rule every engine's `models_used` reads, the mechanism `llm_recovery` reads at **SIGNED** (na · pass · warn *served by the signed fallback … a declared, temporary deployment drift for this turn* / *the provider refused*), the answer wears a `served by <model>` chip only when a fallback served, the chat header a provider-health strip (`role=status`, announces a change once, no motion) only while a provider is degraded (`GET /v1/llm/provider-health` + a live `provider_health` notice), and cost is billed at the model that SERVED on every lane (invariant #6: the handler by construction — the fallback is the same function at depth 1 — the LangChain lanes via `uderia_served_by` on the message). Editor: a Fallback LLM select (None first, the primary excluded, a cleared field saves `null`). **Two defects the live run found, both fixed at the root:** every recovery card was headed by its wire type on a plan reload — the four per-class title functions fell through to the event type — so ONE `_assuranceStepTitle` helper, consulted by all four, now titles the S3 and S4 steps identically live and on reload; and `models_used` on the LangChain lanes named the configured model that never answered. **Deviations, each deliberate:** the reading lives at SIGNED, not TRUSTED (Rule 3b.6; a fallback is deployment drift — SIGNED's half, as S2's cache reading); Anthropic's native server-side refusal `fallbacks` are not used (refusals are uniform across providers and never handed to a second model). Honest limits: a fallback call inherits the primary instance's streaming mode (an MLX primary is built `streaming=False`, so its fallback answers arrive whole); the Optimize engine pre-records the configured model in `models_used` before its first call. Gates `test_llm_resilience` **128** (+ freeze 13) + `test_resilience_ui.mjs` **34**; **20 mutations fail by name** — one (a fallback falling back) escaped as an equivalent mutant until BOTH depth guards were removed together, recorded as defence in depth; battery green apart from the two pre-existing reds; pins 87. Live: a ReAct turn on a dead primary — 4 retries (2.6 · 4.6 · 8.6 · 16.2 s) → served by the Haiku fallback; an Optimize turn — 4 retries → the Gemini fallback answered with its S3 receipt intact, the next two calls routed by the open breaker in 2 s instead of 30; headless Chrome both themes: chip + tooltip, the four step cards on reload, the strip with `role=status`, zero page errors. - **Sep 2026**: **S3 — Compute with Lineage: every number in the answer can say where it came from (branch `feature/beyond-claude-agent`, spec `BEYOND_CLAUDE_CONVERSATION_AGENT.md` §S3).** Behind the master `APP_CONFIG.COMPUTE_LINEAGE` (env `TDA_COMPUTE_LINEAGE`, default off ⇒ byte-identical: the component is absent from every catalog, its skill never injects, no stamp is written — frozen by `test_compute_baseline` committed green before any feature code). **Deterministic, not generated:** `agent/compute.py` is a closed op set (`sum · avg · min · max · count · rank · pivot · diff · join · pct_change · filter`) computed in-process — the model decides WHAT, never writes the code, never pastes rows; tolerant numbers (`1,234`, `$5.6`, `12%`), ONE numeric column resolves itself (several → a refusal naming them), empty sets honest (`sum` 0 · `avg`/`min`/`max` None · `rank` `[]`). The rows come from a per-session **result-set registry** (`agent/result_sets.py`, numbered in execution order = the theatre's numbering) fed at the two post-success seams every data-running engine passes through (the MCP adapter · the ReAct tool wrapper); framework `TDA_*` tools and row-less results are not statements. **Every figure carries a receipt** (`RECEIPT_FIELDS` → canonical JSON → `receipt_hash`) that is (a) **sealed** into the Ed25519 provenance chain as `compute_step` — `verify_content` re-derives it and names a mismatch either way; Coordinate through its experts) classifies every figure in the delivered answer ONCE — **receipted** / **quoted** (a result-row cell, or the number of rows a statement returned) / **unreceipted** — with numbers the question asked, tokens glued to identifiers and sub-three-digit figures never convicted; the prose is marked (`mark.figure-receipted`/`figure-quoted` = role=button + tabindex + aria-label → the lineage dialog `figureLineage.js`, real `role=dialog`, focus trap, Escape returns focus, en-US formatting so the dialog reads the answer's exact number; `figure-unreceipted` = no colour, no claim), the disclosure is append-only and only under honesty mode `annotate`/`enforce`; the reading is the *Number Lineage* Live Status card (live + reload) and the `compute_lineage` mechanism at **GROUNDED**; `numeric_fidelity` counts a receipted or lineage-quoted figure as grounded ("N by lineage") — the measure moved from flagging arithmetic to verifying it. **The component** (`components/builtin/compute/`, `TDA_Compute`, companion skill `compute-expert`): refusals are recovery-shaped (`spec.error` + `suppress_inline` — never read as success on the Optimize path, never a dead card), the receipt card is pre-rendered html (no renderer.js), `is_profile_relevant` IS the switch. **Optimize planner wiring:** the `compute_insertion` pass (after `text_date_cast`, before `plan_validation`) inserts ONE `TDA_Compute` phase before a synthesis phase whose goal is arithmetic (`total/sum → sum`, `average → avg`, `top N by → rank`, `change since → pct_change`, `minimum`, `maximum`) — never when the SQL already aggregates, a phase already computes, no data phase precedes it, or the component is disabled for the profile; idempotent on replan. **Three defects the live run found, each fixed at the root:** (1) the inserted compute phase ran in the SAME parallel group as the data phase it computes over and computed over nothing — the scheduler gains `_phase_compute_deps` (a compute phase depends on every earlier data phase, the third complement beside the referenced and discovery deps); (2) the figure tokenizer convicted `-5000` out of `FB-5000` and marked every table cell (129 marks on one answer) — `_FIGURE_RE` excludes identifier-glued numbers and cells/`code`/`pre` are masked with LETTER-keyed placeholders (a digit placeholder collided with a figure on the first attempt), row counts ("100 products") became lineage; (3) `compute-expert` auto-injected with the switch OFF because `components/enablement.py` ignored `is_profile_relevant` — relevance is now folded into the ONE enablement rule (`relevant()` in `is_enabled`/`filter_enabled`: an inert component never pulls its skill), which also fixed the pre-existing stale 7-action-tool pin in `test_progressive_skills` (203 green). **Deviations, each deliberate:** no separate `unreceipted_figure` honesty verdict object (one classification lives in the `compute_lineage` event — a second definition of "unreceipted" would drift); at most ONE compute phase per synthesis phase; the bench expectation lives in `conversation_lane_bench.py` (lineage columns), not the airlines KG bench.
