- **Sep 2026**: **S2 — the Attested Cache: pay for the stable prefix once, and a miss on an unchanged prefix is a FINDING (branch `feature/beyond-claude-agent`, spec `BEYOND_CLAUDE_CONVERSATION_AGENT.md` §S2).** Behind the master `APP_CONFIG.PROMPT_CACHING` (env `TDA_PROMPT_CACHING`, default off ⇒ byte-identical, frozen by `test_prompt_cache_baseline` committed green before any feature code). **ONE policy** `llm/cache_policy.py`: capability per provider AND model (`breakpoints` = Anthropic natively or an Anthropic model behind OpenRouter · `automatic` = OpenAI-shaped · `implicit` = Gemini · `none`), breakpoints on the system block + the last HISTORY message and never the question, `read_usage` normalising every provider to `input` = the TOTAL prompt, ONE price rule `CostManager.calculate_cost_with_cache` (read 0.1× Anthropic / 0.25× Google / 0.5× OpenAI-shaped; write 1.25× 5m / 2× 1h), and the attested-prefix rule `miss_is_finding` — the same prefix bytes, inside the TTL, above the provider's minimum, on a provider that caches, nothing served from cache ⇒ a finding; **the Anthropic minimum is PER MODEL** (Haiku 4.5 / Opus 4.5–4.6 = 4096, Opus 4.7 = 2048, Sonnet 5 = 1024, Opus 5 / Fable = 512; an unknown model takes the largest, so it can never produce a false finding). **ONE accumulator** `agent/prompt_cache.py:TurnCache` (a contextvar per turn, armed at the execution seam, seeded from the previous turn's stamp) records every call from the handler lanes AND the two LangChain agents (`langchain_prefix` / `langchain_usage`) and stamps `workflow_history[n].cache` at the persistence chokepoint. **The reading lives at SIGNED** — a miss on an unchanged prefix says something in the signed prefix moved — with `cache_efficiency` as its informational twin at JUDGED's residue (58 dimensions); a `Cached` row on the step cards only when something was served (a warm cache is invisible); a `cacheConfig {enabled, ttl}` profile key (portable, UNSIGNED — a cost setting never moves a badge) with a Prompt Cache editor card. **Two defects the live run found, both closed at the root:** (1) the ReAct lane placed the per-question knowledge/KG enrichment IN the system prompt (Ideate/Focus place it on the user side), so the system block changed every turn and the breakpoint missed on every call — retrieved knowledge now leads the volatile message on that lane too, ONE placement across the engines (a second-turn call went 0 → 10,298 cached tokens); (2) the OpenAI-compatible branch claimed `breakpoints` for a broker-fronted Anthropic model and never placed them (`mark_openai_messages`, the broker's `cache_write_tokens` read). **And the cost consequence:** `turn_cost` on the ReAct lane was a single-model re-price of the summed tokens, so it forgot what the provider served from cache (a turn at 85% cached read $0.0024 where the Σ of its cache-priced steps is $0.00055) — both LangChain agents now hand every priced call to `executor._accumulate_call_cost` (`cost_sink`), the accumulator is complete on every lane and `turn_cost = Σ cache-priced calls` (cost invariant #5); the two suites that pinned the retired partial-accumulator rule were re-pointed and — with `test_rerank_cost_crossclass` — added to the battery they had sat outside of. **Deliberately not built:** stable-first re-ordering of the context-window modules (it changes what the model reads; the CW orchestrator is untouched), the per-module cached hatch (the provider reports one total — a split would be inference), warm-at-session-open (the prefix is engine-composed at turn time), Google explicit cache / Bedrock breakpoints. Honest limit: a LangChain lane in streaming mode cannot see the broker's write count (LangChain drops `token_usage` from streamed responses) — the write surcharge is unbilled there, billed on the native Anthropic branch. Gate `test_prompt_cache` **87** (+ freeze 10), **24 mutations fail by name** (one escaped an `or`-loosened check and was made an AST property); `test_turn_cost` 44, `test_rerank_cost_crossclass` 18; battery green apart from the two pre-existing reds. Live-verified: Gemini implicit (ReAct lane, 65% cached on turn 2), Anthropic breakpoints through OpenRouter (turn-2 share 87%, `turn_cost` $0.0024 → $0.00055), editor card round-trip + step-card row in headless Chrome, both themes, zero page errors. - **Sep 2026**: **S1 — the Governed Stream: the answer arrives as it is written, guarded in flight, and a stopped turn keeps what arrived (branch `feature/beyond-claude-agent`, first of the ten increments of `BEYOND_CLAUDE_CONVERSATION_AGENT.md`).** Built gates-first: `test/test_answer_stream_baseline.py` (15) was committed GREEN against the unmodified code before a line of feature code — it pins, per provider, that `call_llm_api` takes the NON-streaming API with no `stream` argument when no delta sink is supplied and returns the same 5-tuple; it still passes, and the bench proves it live (streaming off ⇒ 0 deltas, no `answer_stream` on the payload). **The mechanism, ONE object per turn:** `agent/answer_stream.py:AnswerStream`, created at the single execution seam (`execution_service.run_agent_execution`, armed only when the caller is a live UI stream — `/ask_stream`, `/invoke_prompt_stream` pass `stream_answer=True`; REST tasks, the scheduler and flows never carry deltas — AND `APP_CONFIG.ANSWER_STREAMING` is on, env `TDA_ANSWER_STREAMING`, **off by default ⇒ byte-identical**) and handed down to every engine: Ideate's answer call and Focus's synthesis pass `on_delta=executor.answer_stream`; the ReAct agent and the genie coordinator feed `on_chat_model_stream` chunks and `reset()` when a model message turns out to be a tool call (a decision is not the answer); Optimize streams the final report's `direct_answer` SENTENCE out of the JSON as it is written (`JsonFieldSink` on the ambient `answer_stream.current()` contextvar — the reader sees the sentence, never the braces), for both report modes. **The provider half** (`llm/streaming.py`): Anthropic `messages.stream` → `get_final_message`, OpenAI-compatible `stream=True` + `stream_options` with the refusal LEARNED from the provider's own error (the `thinking_support` precedent, never a list), Google `generate_content_stream` (the thinking-disable retry kept), Ollama NDJSON, Bedrock-Anthropic `invoke_model_with_response_stream` on a worker thread with deltas marshalled to the loop — every helper returns the SAME response shape the non-streaming branch reads, so the parsing stays single-source; a provider with no stream (the other Bedrock families) hands the sink the whole text once and SAYS so (`provider_streamed: false`); a retry after an overload error resets the sink first. **The guard is the outbound guardrail's own resolution** (`guardrails/runtime.stream_policy`): only an ACTING mode (enforce / review) alters the stream — `StreamGuard` masks PII on a sliding window with an 80-char release lag (agreement with `redact_pii` over the whole text gate-asserted across random chunkings; a span crossing the release boundary is never shown raw) and a toxicity finding withdraws the provisional message; observe/annotate leave the stream exactly as they leave the final answer. **A stop keeps what arrived:** `execution_service` catches `CancelledError`/`Exception` after the seam, persists the partial turn (the executor's `_save_partial_turn_data`, now idempotent and carrying the partial text as the turn's answer; `persist_partial_turn` for genie, tokens honestly unknown) and emits `final_answer{partial:true}` BEFORE the cancel propagates — proven in headless Chrome: the stopped essay stays in place with a *stopped* note, no CANCELLED line, the turn badge present, and it survives a session reload. **Frontend (`ui.js`/`eventHandlers.js`):** a provisional bubble that is deliberately NOT an assistant message (no badge, no `data-turn-id` — the capsule/pin/feedback observers skip it; never written to history — the server writes it once from the final), batched markdown (one parse per frame), the caret at the end of the last text block, duplicate/stale `seq`/`message_index` dropped, a **follow lock** (the view follows only while the reader is at the bottom; scrolling up shows a sticky *new text* pill — one click returns), **Stop is where Send was** (the composer's own control becomes Stop while a turn runs — the Live Status header's Stop was unreachable with that panel collapsed), once-only polite announcements (*Answer complete* / *Answer stopped — the partial answer is kept*), `aria-busy`, reduced-motion honoured; `answer_delta` is handled FIRST in `processStream`'s chain and never reaches Live Status. Deliberately NOT a new surface: the assurance rail and in-place claim marks — the final answer replaces the bubble and already carries the capsule's journey glyph and `mark.claim-unsupported` (contract Rule 3.0). **Bench** (`test/performance/conversation_lane_bench.py`, the fusion_bench precedent, five classes over `/ask_stream`, off → on): TTFT none → 0.9 s (Ideate) · 1.2 s (Focus) · 3.2 s (Optimize) · 5.5 s (ReAct) · 19 s (Coordinate — the expert's run), partial-kept-on-Stop false → **true on every class**, LLM steps/tools/tokens/cost flat. - **Sep 2026**: **The refused fan-out repairs itself — aggregate-then-join at 0 LLM, ranked inside the ranked side.** The fan-out guard (entry below) was working on prod and each turn still paid for it: reading session 940f02fa in full showed the refusal round is not ONE round — the model's own first correction (`(SELECT k, SUM … GROUP BY k) R JOIN member_benefit B`) passed the guard (correct arithmetic) but returned member 2 FIVE times under `TOP 5` (28 distinct tiers across its 149 benefit rows), so it spent one to two further rounds reducing the other side, one of them a 46K-token probe. The doctrine the text-date and reserved-alias rewrites already follow — *a structured refusal that names its own remedy never costs an LLM round* — now applies to the fan-out: ONE pure rewrite `preflight/joins.py:rewrite_fanout_sql` consumed by BOTH chokepoints (`FanoutJoinStrategy` in the Optimize correction chain after `TextDateStrategy`; `fanout_rewrite` in the ReAct tool wrapper on the same seam as the text-date twin). Each holder is aggregated at its OWN grain in a derived table (key + its grouped columns + its aggregates + its own WHERE conjuncts), the aggregates are joined on the key, and a `TOP n … ORDER BY` whose every term belongs to ONE side is pushed INTO that side so the TOP ranks that side's rows rather than the join's repeats — **with the join's membership carried in** (`k IN (SELECT k FROM other [WHERE …])` for an INNER join: the original ranked only keys present on both sides, so a TOP pushed without it could pick a key the join then drops and the result would silently come up short), never into the optional side of a LEFT join, a same-side HAVING moved inside with the TOP (the original filtered before ranking) and an other-side HAVING keeping the TOP outside. **The model's GROUP BY grain is preserved exactly** — a column the other side contributes ungrouped still repeats per key, and the result NAMES the grain and the way to one row per key (aggregate those columns per key, or take the attribute from the owner) instead of guessing a `MAX`. **Everything needing judgement DECLINES to today's refusal**: an expression or predicate mixing both tables, a bare `COUNT(*)` (it counted the multiplied rows), a third table, a subquery/CTE/UNION/window, `SELECT *`, an ON beyond the single key equality, `TOP … WITH TIES/PERCENT`, an unattributable column — so the change can only remove rounds, never add risk; the rewrite re-runs every join check on its own output and the ReAct twin re-preflights the rewritten statement in FULL (a rewrite any check would refuse hands the ORIGINAL refusal back). **Measured before designing:** on live Teradata a derived-table `TOP … ORDER BY` is accepted and `ORDER BY` alone in a subquery is Error 3706 (so the push always carries the TOP); the rewritten prod statements return the top-5 set with exact totals — **17,708 for member 2 where the fan-out read 531,240** — every row accounted for (107 = Σ distinct tiers incl. a NULL group; 774 = Σ distinct balances). **Two guard precision rules the work forced, both class-level:** a holder whose OWN single-column primary key IS the fan-out column is not a holder (`_pk_is_column` — a 1:1 extension table cannot multiply; no such table in any local graph, 82,222 FK edges scanned), and `sql_joins` now resolves ON qualifiers against the join's OWN scope, so a derived table aliased with a holder's name (`… ) AS orders JOIN ( … ) AS shipments`) is a join between aggregates and never the fan-out it replaced — **the guard would have refused the very shape it asked for**, a latent false positive found by the gate's unrelated-schema section (the rule is the CLASS, never the conversation: the prod statements are acceptance fixtures only). **Live on local `@IDAIRL` under enforce**, through the real wrapper → real MCP tool → Teradata: both prod statements refused → rewritten → 17,708 with the tier/balance rows, and the model's reply reads back exactly what the note teaches ("multiple records per member … `ffp_member` is the authoritative source … rerun?"), 2 LLM steps each; on the natural question the local model took the owner-join remedy on its own (never wrote the fan-out), so the twin is exercised deterministically by handing it the statement. Gates: new `test_preflight_fanout_rewrite` (**73**, in the battery — the prod statements, the push truth table, the decline set, both twins through the real guarded coroutine incl. the full re-preflight, an unrelated schema), `test_preflight_joins` 82 → **86** (scope resolution, holder⋈derived, nested scopes), continuity 86 → **89** (the PK rule both ways), bench 41 → **49** (every recorded fan-out statement rewrites from the enrichment's own `fanout_keys`); **eight mutations fail by name** (membership dropped · TOP into the optional LEFT side · HAVING left outside · re-check dropped · twin skips the re-preflight · strategy removed · global qualifier resolution · TOP never pushed), `COUNT(*)` recorded as triply guarded (an equivalent mutant; the `COUNT(1)` assertion carries the property); battery: every touched suite green, the two reds (`extract_trust_inventory` kgTheatre unclassified, `test_product_contract_render` 89/1) pre-existing at HEAD. **Recorded limit at the time — closed the same day by the entry above:** the persisted trace stores a 5,000-char result preview, so on a long result the appended rewrite note reached the model and the log but not the historical Live Status card; the ReAct-lane `conversation_tool_rewrite` event now carries the executed statement. Proven offline on the real subscribed airlines copy, then **live on prod as the demo user** (session 940f02fa, the same two questions through `@IDAIRL` on gemini-3.1-flash-lite): the model still WRITES the fan-out first on both turns, the guard refuses it (`preflight_fanout`, the owner and the remedy named), and the model self-corrects in one round to aggregate-then-join — member 2 reads **17,708** miles redeemed (was 2,638,492) and a 37,491 balance; the render is the first line of defence a weak model can ignore, the guard the one it cannot. Every miss is RECORDED (`missed` kind in `kg_entity_usage`, self-applying column, bumped on the graph's own table entity at the executor's telemetry seam beside `used`) and weighs most in the ranking prior; the carry-over carries the previous turn's **missed** tables ahead of the shown ones (resolved by leaf to the logical entity), and — the cost finding the bench made visible — carried entities now CONSUME seed slots (`_SEED_LIMIT` 15, floor 7) rather than extend the cut: turn 2 **289 → 143 entities, 46K → 24K chars**, every expectation kept. **(3) The column-existence preflight** (`agent/preflight/columns.py`, `PREFLIGHT_COLUMN_MODE`, env `TDA_PREFLIGHT_COLUMN_MODE`, default observe): prod turn 2's first statement was `boarding_event.miles_flown` — a column that does not exist — costing a 3810, an LLM round and a `SELECT *` to learn a schema the graph held. turn 2 *"the names of those customers"* took **7 LLM rounds, 4 SQL statements (2 errors), 99,647 input tokens** and paired names to member ids positionally from a finance table. **Four retrieval defects, each fixed at the root:** **(1) query-only seeding** — "those customers" seeded every `*_name` column in the model and not `ffp_member`, the table turn 1 was about → **conversational carry-over** (`previous_turn_carry_over`, pure): the entities the previous turn's data tool calls REFERENCED (`touched_entities` — the one definition of "used") join the seeds behind the products and ahead of the lexical ranking, tables → descriptive columns → keys, capped at 8, transitive through a turn that read nothing, never on a primer; every enrichment caller threads `session_id` (executor · CW module · genie), the event carries `carry_over`, the Live Status card gains a *Carried over* row. **(2) physical twins** — on a layered graph nine of the first twelve seeds were `airlines_core.*` column copies of logical attributes, competing for the fifteen slots and expanding to NOTHING (only the logical layer is structurally expandable — mileage_accrual/ffp_member were absent from TABLE SCHEMAS locally with semantic seeding off) → `_collapse_layer_twins` at the pool (and the `query` lookup) + the extractor follows a physical seed's `implements` hop to its logical twin. **(3) the join backbone** — the relevance cap filled with twelve `*miles*` columns and `mileage_accrual.ffp_member_id`, the ONE declared key to a table in the same subgraph, was budgeted out, so the FK edge never rendered and the preflight guard had nothing to enforce → `_join_backbone_columns`: a column joining two DISCOVERED tables (or a pk) is kept over the cap, bounded per table; and under a node budget the seeder's ORDER now decides which table gets its columns (a set-ordered tie handed them to the lower node id). **(4) `join_keys` could never be non-empty on this graph class** — `_subgraph_to_dict` emitted edges without endpoint types, so `_declared_join_pairs` never recognised a column-level FK, and it derived a key only from a table's `business_key` (ANDP) → types travel on edges (recovered from the entities for an older shape) and a pair with exactly ONE FK edge naming the SAME column on both sides gets that column as its checkable key; two FKs between one pair or differing names stay un-keyed by construction (rendered as *join on ONE of …*). **The guard now checks each SIDE of the ON** — the turn-1 join named `ffp_member_id` on the wrong side and passed (`sql_joins` carries `by_table`; - **Sep 2026**: **The policing core model's two-column decode is registered faithfully, and a class-level cross-product correspondence reads as one — root-caused from a live @PXPROD turn that answered "0 robberies".** Two defects on the policing cross-product analyst, both fixed at the model/platform layer with no primer workarounds. **(1) Two-column decode (core-model, `policing-data-products/src/core-model/scripts/`):** every coded field in the deployed `Policing_Core.v_*` views is TWO columns — the raw `<field>_code` (the FBI code) and its decoded `<field>` label — but the ISO/IEC 11179 catalog the KG walks had registered ONLY the label column and attached the code value-domain to it, so the agent read "UCR OFFENSE CODE" on the label column and wrote `WHERE offence_type = '120'` → **0 rows** (the label holds `'Robbery'`). The generator now expands each value-domain attribute into the faithful pair — enum + `semantic_type='code'` on the raw `<attr>_code`, a codeless decoded label on `<attr>` (88→120 data elements; the one irregular raw name, `offence_type`→`offence_code`, declared in `model_map.py`). Live: `WHERE offence_code = '120'` → **179,193 robberies**. Locked by a two-column contract test (`test_generate_core_model.py` 36/0). **(2) `type_correspondence` bridge rendering (platform, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/`):** the KG enrichment flattened EVERY `product_bridge` to `"DECLARED LINK, not a verified join"` and rendered only the mechanism code — the rich `basis` was never shown — so the agent tried to `JOIN` the correspondence node as a table, failed, and reported "does not resolve". A `type_correspondence` is a CLASS/KIND-level correspondence, not a per-record link; `_format_subgraph_for_prompt` now renders it as a `CONCEPTUAL CORRESPONDENCE ... never SELECT FROM or JOIN it` and surfaces its basis (other bridges keep their behaviour plus the basis the code's own comment already promised). `probe_bridge` was the sibling half-fix: it read `source_reference`/`target_reference`, which a class correspondence lacks, so it reported `target 'None' does not exist`; both the pure `resolve_bridge_probe` and `_handle_probe_bridge` are now `type_correspondence`-aware (a class correspondence has no row-level overlap to probe — read the basis). The pack's cross-over `basis` was also cleaned of a superseded-history parenthetical ("an earlier crosswalk could not resolve") the weak model misread as this bridge being unresolved. **(3) Primer simplified:** @PXPROD's now-redundant two-column rule was removed — the enrichment teaches it deterministically — and the re-verify with the simplified primer PROVED the correctness is graph-driven (still `offence_code = '120'` → 179,193). Final live answer states the correspondence positively (robbery offences correspond to emails, files, URLs, disk images, registry keys, exhibits — "not a per-record join"). Regression: 9 suites green (`test_bridge_probe` 33 +5, `test_kg_phase_e` 41 +7, `test_kg_enrichment_relevance` 135, `test_declared_model_walker` 56, `test_obda` 93, + `kg_phase_b/c`, `fusion_hardening_aug`, `product_contract_render`). - **Sep 2026**: **The Database Navigator — a world-class database object navigator as a builtin component, built on ONE catalog contract that maximises the traditional database connection.** Operator: *"use the uderia component system to build a worldclass database object navigator component … implement as much deterministic intelligence as possible"*, with the constraint that an MCP connection with catalog-shaped tools can never be assumed, so the direct Database Connection had to be maximised rather than treated as a fallback. **On Teradata it is the RICHER path:** the dictionary (`DBC.DatabasesV/TablesV/ColumnsV/IndicesV/All_RI_ChildrenV/StatsV/TableSizeV`) yields declared referential integrity, primary/unique indexes, statistics with their age, sizes, comments and view text — none of which the `base_*` MCP tools return. **Architecture (`src/trusted_data_agent/dbcatalog/`):** a `CatalogProvider` contract with capability negotiation (the vector-store / graph-store pattern) and two provider families — **direct** (Teradata dictionary; PostgreSQL/MySQL `information_schema`; SQLite `sqlite_master`+PRAGMA) and **mcp** (tool ROLES resolved by name + description — `databaseList`/`tableList`/`columnDescription`/`readQuery` — never a hard-coded tool name); resolution order stated once and reported as `reason` (agent's `componentConfig.database_navigator.sourceId` → default connection → first connection → MCP tools → an honest empty state naming both remedies); enrichment reads degrade to a NAMED *not available from this source* while core reads raise recovery-shaped; **read-only by construction** (`single_select_guard` before any preview/count, identifier shape check). **Deterministic intelligence, zero tokens, provider-independent** (`intelligence.py`): column flags (`key · identifier · pii · text_date · date · code · measure · text`; `text_date` shares `dateforms.is_text_date_attr` with the enrichment + preflight guard), evidence-ranked object roles (`fact · dimension · bridge · lookup · log · staging`, each verdict with its reasons, `unknown` below the evidence floor), key inference (declared wins; else the table's own id, plural-tolerant stems), join inference (declared FKs are facts; name-based candidates are hypotheses with confidence + reason, generic names never join, one verdict per child column), identifier-token search ranking (a plural of the name IS the name; system databases excluded by default), trusted-scope marking, capability-driven actions, role-specific suggested questions and a dialect-correct sample query. **Ontology overlay** (`overlay.py`, fail-open): the bound graph's entity description, validated row counts/key uniqueness, per-attribute PII/decoded values/sampled shapes — ontology-declared PII joins the column flags, so a preview masks it even when the dictionary is silent. **ONE service, two faces** (`service.py`): the `TDA_DatabaseNavigator` tool (`describe · search · preview · suggest_joins · open`, its words composed from the same facts) and the panel's REST (`/v1/database-navigator/*`, every route gated on component availability, failing closed, per-user cache so one user's connection never serves another's tree); previews masked by default (`mask_preview` keeps the first character). **Live-verified** on the local Teradata connection: 107 databases in 1.8 s, a describe in 1.9 s after the runner learned to reuse one connection per host (a describe had cost 13 s on six fresh sockets), NIBRS `Incident` with 393 columns / 12.35M rows from statistics / its primary + join indexes, declared RI on `fitness_db` (`Sales→Customers`, `SaleDetails→Sales/Products`) — and the first live run caught `ct` being a Teradata reserved word in an alias. **UX:** a split panel on the shared `.sp-header` chrome (source picker with the resolution reason · `/`-focused search with keyboard navigation · a tree with system databases hidden and counted · detail with the role chip explaining itself on hover, capability-honest facts, actions, tabs Columns · Keys & joins · Preview · Ask · Definition · Ontology), an inline chat card per tool action, a **Database** resource-rail panel (sources · quick search · recent), a **Source** selector on the profile editor's component row (absent = auto, carried forward on save), companion skill `database-navigator-expert` (auto-assigns with the component), packs default it OFF. **Two more defects the live run caught, both fixed at the root:** (a) the MCP role scorer picked `dba_tableSqlList` as the table lister and `qlty_columnSummary` as the column describer over `base_tableList`/`base_columnDescription` on a real Optimize profile — every object list came back empty; the scorer now disqualifies the analysis/DBA/security/plot families for catalog roles and refuses to GUESS a role its readers do not supply (pinned against the profile's real 31-tool set); (b) the profile's classification snapshot said `base_columnDescription` takes `obj_name` while the redeployed Teradata MCP image takes `table_name` — and `invoke_mcp_tool` realigns every synonym back to the SNAPSHOT's name, so no probe could ever reach the parameter the server accepts; the provider now reads the LIVE schema (one `list_tools` per server, cached) and reconciles that one tool's entry in the adapter's arg map, saying in the log that re-classifying persists it; plus `CType` — the real Teradata MCP type field — was missing from the shared `TYPE_FIELDS`, so every MCP-described column was typeless (no measure flag, wrong role) for the navigator AND the discovery KG constructor alike. **Live-verified end to end on a real IDGGT turn:** the agent called `describe` then `preview` through `TDA_DatabaseNavigator`, reported the declared key, the flags and the referenced table, and its Customers sample came back masked (`G••• R••• g•••`); both navigator cards rendered inline. Gates: `test_dbcatalog` (**187**, in the battery — providers over a replayed dictionary, the MCP provider over a fake invoker incl. the live-schema reconcile, the component and REST faces with the gate EXECUTED), `test_dbnav_renderer.mjs` (**51**, the shipped renderer executed under a DOM stub — a `.map` on the in-flight preview state was caught by the browser, not the gate, and the gate now covers all three preview states); **17 mutations fail by name** (11 Python incl. the REST gate failing OPEN, 6 JS); pins cascaded (`test_version_pins` 82); battery GREEN. - **Sep 2026**: **Model B — release gates agent grounding (Tier 4.3 §1a, the deferred half), plus the `rag_context` module reports what it does.** Tier 4.3's lifecycle *publish* pinned a conformance-stamped snapshot but changed nothing at runtime — every agent kept grounding on the live draft, so for a solo operator release was ceremony (recorded as the open Model B). Built as a per-agent OPT-IN: `componentConfig.knowledge_graph.groundOn: "released"` makes the agent read the ontology's RELEASED version for every KG read — enrichment, the grounding gate's trusted scope, and the `TDA_KnowledgeGraph` tool's reads — never the draft. **Mechanism** (`core/kg_release.py`, ONE decision `resolve_grounding`): the published version is MATERIALISED into a shadow graph `<kg_id>::released` in the same tables, so the entire retrieval path (search, adaptive subgraph, capabilities, semantic index, usage telemetry, grounding-gate scope) runs UNCHANGED over a different kg_id; the shadow row carries `released_of`/`released_version_id` (self-applying columns), is never active, and is hidden from every enumerator (graph lists, pack export's legacy lookup, the published catalog); rebuilt only when `published_version_id` moves — eagerly at publish, lazily on first read. **Rules, each gated:** absent/any other value ⇒ Model A byte-identical (charter #15); released with no release yet ⇒ the live draft AND the event says so (`grounding.fallback: "live"`, the Live Status card warns — an agent never silently reads nothing); a deprecated release stays but is flagged; **KG write actions through a released-mode agent are refused, recovery-shaped** (a release is immutable; an agent editing a draft it cannot see would never observe its own edit); **trust hashes the EFFECTIVE ingredient** — a released-mode agent's ontology hash is the shadow's, so a draft edit does not flip its badge (its behaviour did not change) and a new publish does; `groundOn == released` is itself a signed capability token; the view dies with its graph (KG delete + pack uninstall). The three read seams route through ONE `KnowledgeGraphHandler._resolve_grounding_store`; the profile editor gains a **Ground on** selector on the knowledge-graph row, with the stored value CARRIED FORWARD when the select is not rendered (the F5-class trap). **`rag_context`**: the CW module retrieved from a `ragConfig.collections` key no profile carries and reported `no_collections` on every turn — a module describing a retrieval it never performed; it now reports `planner_owned` (the planner retrieves after assembly, because the ontology-metric champion filter reads the KG enrichment that the `knowledge_graph` module produces after it). Gates: new `test_kg_model_b` (**63**, in the battery — real SQLite, real store, real handler, real trust composition: no doubles for the thing under test), `test_kg_event_title` 47 → **53**; **eight mutations fail by name**; three battery suites went red on the cascade seams and were fixed at the root (a DB predating the column, the versions-cleanup invariant) — plus one implementation-pinning grep converted to its property; KG no-regression 196/196; battery GREEN. **Live-proven locally** on `@CASEDF`: CASE graph published 1.0.0 (conformant) → turn 1 grounded on `…::released` and the tool read was served from it → turn 2's `add_entity` refused with the NEXT-STEP message, the draft untouched, the shadow hidden from the list. **Production is byte-identical** (no agent opted in). - **Sep 2026**: **The semantic seeding channel gets a NUMBER, the enrichment event names its graph, KG seam failures stop dying at DEBUG, and every KG test double is pinned to the real `GraphStore`.** The follow-on to the dead-channel finding (below): the channel had been down for 18 days and *nothing measured it* — the bench disables it for determinism, and no post-turn reading aggregated `bridged`. **(1) `kg_seed_utilization`** — a new informational (non-gating, no threshold) scored dimension: of the entities the question reached ONLY by meaning, the fraction the turn's data tool calls then referenced. Owned by `trusted_scope` (GROUNDED), staged at RETRIEVE, mirrored on the ring + the Guide (`INFORMATIONAL`, 56 → **57** dimensions); abstains — never a pass — when the channel was off/warming/errored, when nothing was bridged, or when the turn ran no data calls. The "did the answer TOUCH this entity" test is ONE rule (`kgstore.usage.touched_entities`: whole-identifier leaf match, case-insensitive, in tool ARGUMENTS only — a row that happens to contain the word is not the agent using the entity; a generic leaf like `count`/`id` is excluded rather than counted everywhere) read by BOTH the scorer and the **`used` telemetry** — a signal `kg_entity_usage` had declared since Phase E and nobody ever recorded; `executor._record_kg_used` now records it beside `_run_obda_scan` at both data-running engines, NOT gated on OBDA, fire-and-forget. Prod evidence that made it worth it: `kg_entity_usage` holds 8,879 rows across 27 graphs, so the priors can now weight real use. **(2)** the enrichment event carries **`kg_id` / `kg_name` / `entity_names`** — the card read `kg: None`; a consumer's pack copy sits beside the publisher's and the two were indistinguishable by owner profile; the Live Status card gains a *Graph* row (omitted, never invented, on an older event). **(3)** four KG seam failures were swallowed at DEBUG (bridge-table discovery · semantic no-embedder · semantic hits · **trusted-scope resolution**, the last found by the gate's own sweep — it silently makes the grounding gate abstain on a whole profile); each now routes through new `core/log_once.warn_once` (ONE WARNING per (key, process), DEBUG after — a per-turn WARNING trains an operator to grep past it; persist/load stay DEBUG because a cache that cannot be written still works). **(4)** `test/kg_double_fidelity.py:double_mismatches(GraphStore, Fake)` — every method a KG test double overrides must agree with the real class on sync/async, BOTH directions — wired into all ten KG suites that double the store (survey: all faithful today; the helper stops the next drift, the third recurrence of this trap). - **Sep 2026**: **The semantic seeding channel failed on exactly the turns it existed for — a sync `GraphStore` read awaited inside the bridging loop.** Operator, reading prod session `fdf94a5f` turn 2 (`@CASEDF`): *"why did the knowledge graph execute Seeded by: Lexical only — semantic seeding did not run?"* The persisted event carried the fingerprint `semantic_seeding: {state: "error", hits: 10, bridged: []}` — the index had answered with its ten nearest entities, and the handler then threw them away. `_semantic_scores` did `await store.get_entity_by_name(name)`, but `GraphStore.get_entity_by_name` is SYNC (only its writes are async), so the await raised `TypeError: object dict can't be used in 'await' expression`, the blanket except reported `error`, and the message was logged at DEBUG — invisible in production. The await sat inside the loop that runs only for a hit NOT already in the lexical pool, which is why turn 1 (the session primer — long text, lexically matching everything) read `ready / semantics agreed` while the short question on turn 2 failed: the channel broke precisely when meaning had something to add, on every such turn since Phase F shipped (2026-08-24). **The gate had missed it for the recorded reason:** its fake store declared `async def get_entity_by_name` — faithful to the wrong convention, the `declare_concept` lesson again. Fixed with the handler's own `_maybe_await` at the one site (a sweep found no other awaited sync read); the swallowed error now logs at WARNING with the exception type; the fake's calling convention is pinned method-by-method to the real `GraphStore` and a bridging turn is asserted to read `ready`, never `error`. Gate `test_kg_phase_f` 68 → **71**; the mutation fails 3 by name; live on the local NIBRS ontology *"how many victims were female"* now bridges `NIBRS_Source.Victim` + the `V40191` sex columns into the pool; KG no-regression 196/196. Files: `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/handler.py`, `test/test_kg_phase_f.py`.

- **Sep 2026**: **A knowledge graph is searched by MEANING, not only by the words a question used — on by default, and fast enough to be.** Operator: *"how do we make sure that entities in the knowledge graph are identified based on semantic meaning of the question?"* — the honest answer was **we did not**: seeding matched entity names/labels/descriptions by substring (`LIKE '%term%'`) with identifier-token scoring, so a question about "customers" against an entity called `Party` found nothing and **ranking can only order what the pool contains**. A semantic channel existed (`kgstore/semantic_index.py`, Aug 2026) but was OFF with **no env var, no compose forwarding and no UI** — reachable only by editing `config.py`. **Why it could not simply be switched on:** the search was a per-entity Python cosine loop, and measuring it settled the design (`test/performance/kg_semantic_bench.py`, committed): at a real graph's size (4,000 entities) **59.9 ms and 49.4 MB per cached graph**, at the 20k cap **275 ms and 247 MB** — four graphs resident was a gigabyte of Python floats. Rebuilt as ONE L2-normalised **float32 matrix** so cosine IS `matrix @ query` with an `argpartition` top-k: **0.086 ms / 6.1 MB** at 4k (**~700x, 8x**). **Three properties make default-on safe, each gate-asserted:** a **cold graph never blocks a turn** (embedding 3,748 entities measures ~3.6 s, plus ~10 s if the process has not loaded the model — so a graph with no index returns **no hits**, lexical seeding stands unchanged, and it builds on a background thread; concurrent turns **join the one build in flight**); a **restart re-loads rather than re-embeds** (the matrix persists per `(kg_id, signature)` under `.cache/kg_semantic`, read back in ~20 ms; the signature is the graph's own `(row count, max updated_at)`, so a rebuild/import supersedes it and stale versions are pruned); and **a graph nobody queries costs no memory** — resident memory is a statement about which graphs are actually being ASKED something: a build triggered by a graph WRITE has nobody waiting on it, so it is persisted and then RELEASED (a deployment importing ten agent packs at startup carries none of their matrices; the first real question reads one back in ~20 ms), the one exception being a matrix that could not be persisted, which is kept rather than throwing the embedding work away. Measured across every route — write 0 MB · backfill 0 MB · five graphs written at startup 0 MB · channel off 0 MB · queried 0.77 MB per 500 entities. **Memory scales with graphs QUERIED, not with users** — the cache is keyed by `(graph, version)` and is process-global, so a hundred people asking one agent questions share ONE matrix (measured: 50 users → 3.07 MB, one matrix; a per-user key would multiply a 30 MB graph by the tenant). **Idle graphs are given back**: the byte ceiling only reclaims under PRESSURE (it runs when a new index is admitted), so a working set that went quiet held its memory indefinitely — measured, 3 untouched graphs kept 9.22 MB forever; `_sweep_idle()` now releases anything unqueried for 30 min, opportunistically on access rather than from a timer thread, which is nearly free to undo BECAUSE the matrix is persisted (a reclaimed graph re-loads in ~10 ms, never re-embeds) and never takes away a graph still being asked things. Honest limit: a process that goes COMPLETELY idle keeps what it last held until something touches the index again. On top of that, resources are bounded in the two directions that matter — **memory in BYTES** (not graph count: a count bounds nothing when one graph is 30 MB and the next 300 KB) and **concurrent builds** (`_MAX_CONCURRENT_BUILDS=2` — one build per graph was already guaranteed; this stops N cold graphs putting N embedding threads on the CPU a live turn is sharing; measured: 8 cold graphs → peak 2, all 8 built). Fails open throughout: no numpy, no embedder, or a changed embedding model against a built index ⇒ no hits, never an error. **Precision is not traded for recall:** hits are UNIONED into the lexical pool and the bonus stays capped at `_SEMANTIC_SCORE_MAX=45`, deliberately between a leading-prefix match (+40) and an exact identifier (+100) — a strong synonym competes, and can never displace an exact match. **Observability — the existing `kg_enrichment` event, extended rather than a second event:** metadata carries `semantic_seeding` per graph, and the event finally got a **details card** (it had none, so it fell through to a raw JSON dump of `table_columns`/`join_keys`/scope — where a reader stopped reading, and where this fact would have been buried), wired into **all three** render paths (a branch missing from one engine flattens the fact for that engine alone — the exact defect this event's own title gate was written for). The reading distinguishes the **three ways the channel contributes nothing** — off · index still warming · ran and found nothing — because as a bare absence they are identical and only one is a finding about the question; and only an entity that was **both** reached by meaning **and** still in the rendered subgraph counts as a contribution (`_semantic_contribution`), a hit ranking or the node budget dropped being counted as `bridged_dropped` rather than credited or hidden. The collapsed step line carries `, N by meaning` (silent when it fired nothing — a clause on every turn is furniture). **UX:** a **Knowledge Graph Retrieval** card in Administration → App Config → AI & Knowledge (sibling of the RAG cards, which own the shared embedding model), applied at runtime, persisted to `system_settings` and restored at startup (`_sync_kg_config_to_config`), plus `TDA_KG_SEMANTIC_SEEDING` / `TDA_KG_SEMANTIC_INDEX_DIR` forwarded through compose. **Encoding happens where the graph CHANGES** (operator: *"isn't encoding done when the knowledge graph is created/updated?"* — it was not, and that is the better moment): `GraphStore.import_bulk` warms the index after a successful write, so the ONE chokepoint every write path reaches (constructors, marketplace install/fork/sync, agent-pack import, PDM deploy — 24 call sites) makes a newly written graph searchable by meaning from its **first** question. Single-entity CRUD deliberately does not — an agent adding entities one at a time would re-embed the whole graph per call; those writes move the signature and the lazy path rebuilds once. The signature became ONE definition shared by the write side and the read side (`semantic_index.graph_signature`, the handler delegates) — two would key a build one way and a lookup the other, so every query would rebuild and never hit. **Existing graphs are NOT migrated by that hook** (a graph nobody rewrites never passes through it) and need no migration: the index has **zero database access** (entities arrive through an injected callable; it writes only its own cache dir), so `kg_entities`/`kg_relationships`/`kg_metadata` are untouched and each graph indexes itself **lazily on first use** — one lexical-only query per graph, once, ever. `maintenance/warm_kg_semantic_indexes.py` pre-builds them for an operator who would rather not spend even that (dry-run default; measured on this instance's 8 real graphs, 30,209 entities: **58 s, 45 MB**). A killed process's half-written temp files are collected on the next prune (age-guarded, so a live writer's file is never taken from it) — junk that only grows would contradict the whole claim. **Proven on a real 3,750-entity NIBRS graph rather than asserted:** the Trust-Membrane content hash is **byte-identical** before and after indexing (`68cfca72…`), row counts and signature unchanged — so **no signed ontology flips 🟠** — and *"which people were arrested"* returns `Arrestee` (0.57), which substring search cannot reach from that phrasing. **Gates:** `test_kg_phase_f` 20 → **68** (rewritten around the new contract, incl. its own header claim), `test_kg_event_title` 18 → **41** (title clause + the card executed under a stub), `test_kg_phase_d` 16 → **18** (its `_kg_signature` check pinned the SQL literal to `handler.py` and broke when the duplication was REMOVED — the ~20th implementation-pinning grep converted to a property, now asserting the signature's shape at its home AND the absence of a second copy). **Thirteen backend + two frontend mutations fail by name — and four ESCAPED the first version and were closed rather than accepted:** a default-flip passed because the check asserted the value the line above had just assigned (a tautology); a corroboration-counted-as-bridge mutation passed because the fixture's `seen_ids` let the id guard mask the name guard under test (fixed with the id-less case where the name guard is genuinely load-bearing); a report-credits-dropped-hits mutation passed a **structural grep** whose token survived elsewhere on the line (fixed by extracting the rule as a pure function the gate EXECUTES); and a removed dispatch passed a count-based check because the function's own **definition** counted as a dispatch site (now asserted per named render path). The last two came from the operator asking *"a graph that isn't queried doesn't consume RAM for the embeddings, correct?"* — it did not: the eager write-build left every written graph's matrix resident, and the gate that tested the release rule never asserted the write path **asks** for it (now executed against the real `GraphStore.warm_semantic_index`). Also recorded: the dimension-mismatch guard is behaviourally equivalent at the return value (a swallowed matmul error returns `[]` too) — what distinguishes it is that it **evicts** the unusable index, which is what the gate now asserts. `test/performance/kg_enrichment_bench.py` pins the flag OFF for the same reason it pins usage priors: a before/after that included index warmth would compare the machine, not the change. Battery green; pins cascaded to a fixpoint (26 modules, `ui.js 1.96` · `adminManager 4.2` · `main 9.39`). Server restart (backend + `index.html`); JS browser-reload. Files: `kgstore/semantic_index.py`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/handler.py`, `api/admin_routes.py`, `auth/database.py`, `core/config.py`, `docker-compose.yml`, `static/js/{ui,adminManager}.js`, `templates/index.html`, `test/{test_kg_phase_f.py,test_kg_event_title.mjs,performance/kg_semantic_bench.py}`, `docs/Architecture/KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

- **Sep 2026**: **The model's answer, with its own reasoning left out — one normaliser, four sites; and the thinking budget becomes a real tri-state.** Follow-on to the entry below, taken in the operator's chosen order (fix the extraction first, then the field). **(1)** LangChain hands a reply back as `.content`, whose SHAPE depends on whether the model reasoned: a plain string, or a LIST of typed parts with `thinking` FIRST and `text` second. Four sites read it and three mishandled the list — the Live Status preview sliced the LIST (`len() == 2` for a 500-word reply), `session_name_generator` stringified the THINKING block **into the session title**, and `extensions/base` passed the list on so `decision.py` ran `json.loads()` on it. **Measuring corrected my own analysis:** this is not a risk that enabling thinking would introduce, it is a LIVE bug — this LangChain version returns a list for Google **even with thinking off** (`gemini-3.5-flash` / `3.1-flash-lite` / `3.5-flash-lite` all `content=list`), so every JSON-mode extension has been raising `TypeError: the JSON object must be str … not list` on any Google model regardless of the budget. `llm/response_text.py` is now the ONE normaliser (pure — it imports nothing from the platform, gate-asserted), **conservative by construction**: a part is kept only if it is plainly TEXT, so a reasoning part a future provider names differently (`reasoning`, `thought`, `redacted_thinking`) can never leak through a name it has not heard of. **(2)** The editor's Thinking Budget field rendered `?? 0` and saved `parseInt(value) || 0`, so a field nobody touched stamped `thinking_budget: 0` on **every save** — silently disabling thinking for every Google model — and the UI could not express "not set", the state the backend already models. Now empty = *model default* (placeholder + hint), `0` = disabled, `-1` = dynamic. **The trap the gate exists for:** `update_llm_configuration` shallow-**merges**, so omitting the key would leave a stored `0` in place and clearing the field would silently do nothing — the cleared state therefore goes over the wire as an **explicit `null`**, which every backend reader already treats as absent (audited: all test `is not None`, none tests key presence), so no backend change was needed. Gates: `test/test_response_text.py` (**29**) + `test/test_thinking_budget_tristate.mjs` (**24**, executing the SHIPPED populate expression and save block, incl. a round-trip per state), both in the battery; **10 mutations fail by name** — one was first caught only by a CRASH and the gate was hardened to report it by name instead. Live-verified through the real extensions path on `gemini-3.5-flash`/`3.7-flash`, thinking on and off: all four combinations parse, where every list previously raised. Pins cascaded (25 modules / 29 files, `configurationHandler 2.28 → 2.29`). Battery GREEN. Files: `llm/response_text.py`, `agent/{conversation_agent,session_name_generator}.py`, `extensions/base.py`, `static/js/handlers/configurationHandler.js`, `test/{test_response_text.py,test_thinking_budget_tristate.mjs,trust_battery.sh}`.

- **Sep 2026**: **A Gemini model that refuses to have thinking DISABLED no longer fails every call — four selectable models were unusable.** Operator: *"if I am using gemini 3.5 flash lite instead of gemini 3.1 flash lite I get `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT`."* **Measured against the live API rather than guessed:** `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` answers **400 `Request contains an invalid argument.`** to any request carrying `thinkingBudget: 0`, while accepting `-1`, `1024` and no budget at all — thinking is configurable on it, it simply cannot be switched **off**. A survey of the nine selectable models shows the refusal is **scattered, not version-ordered**: 2.5-flash-lite ok · 3.1-flash-lite ok · **3.5-flash-lite 400** · 3.5-flash ok · **3.6-flash 400** · 3.7/3.8-flash ok · **3.1-pro-preview 400** · **flash-lite-latest 400** — so no version or family rule can express it, and **the capability is not discoverable** (`GET /v1beta/models/<id>` reports `"thinking": true` for the model that accepts 0 and the one that refuses it alike). The platform sends 0 from two places — session-name generation (always, any gemini ≥ 2.5) and a configured `thinking_budget`, which the LLM-config editor **stamps as 0 on every save** (`parseInt('') || 0`) — so switching a profile's model necessarily switched thinking off and broke every call. **Fix — ONE rule, two lanes:** new `llm/thinking_support.py` is the single registry ("will this model accept a disabled budget?"), deliberately **NOT seeded with a model list** (a list is an arms race that goes stale silently) — it is **learned from the API's own refusal** and consulted by every Google call site, so the doomed request is attempted at most once per model per process. Because disabling thinking is only ever an **optimisation**, a refusal degrades to *thinking enabled* — never to a failed turn — and is recorded **only if dropping the thinking config actually fixes the call** (an unrelated 400 fails the retry too, surfaces as itself, and claims nothing). Wired at both lanes: `handler._google_generate_content` (native SDK — session naming + Optimize/Ideate/Genie) and a lazily-built `_ThinkingAwareChatGoogle` subclass in `langchain_adapter` (**the lane that produced the reported error** — Focus/Conversation/genie session names/judges/extensions), which CONSULTS in `_build_thinking_config` (so a long-lived instance stops paying the round-trip) and LEARNS in `_agenerate`/`_generate`/`_astream`; a mid-stream failure is never re-streamed, since that would duplicate the caller's chunks. A WARNING names the consequence — a configured budget of 0 is **not honoured** on such a model, which is a cost fact the operator set deliberately. **The fallback carried a second defect, found by measuring rather than assuming:** session-name generation caps output at 100 tokens — ample for a 3-5 word title, but not once the model also reasons inside that ceiling, so `gemini-3.6-flash` spent 94 of the 100 thinking and returned the title **`/Draft`** (MAX_TOKENS) and `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` returned a truncated one. `with_thinking_headroom` lifts a ceiling that was sized on the "no thinking" assumption to 1024 whenever that assumption fails; both now return clean titles (STOP), at ~500-1000 thinking tokens per new session on those two models — the honest price of a model that cannot be told not to think. **Measured, and it corrects the warning above for the reported model:** `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` and `gemini-flash-lite-latest` spend **0** thinking tokens even with thinking enabled, so for them the refused setting costs nothing at all; only `gemini-3.6-flash` (1,664) and `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` (1,252) genuinely think — confirmed against a control that accepts the setting (`gemini-3.5-flash`: 0 with budget 0, 1,252 without). **Live-verified end to end:** 3.5-flash-lite / 3.6-flash / 3.1-pro-preview all answer on both lanes, and 3.1-flash-lite / 3.5-flash still receive `0` (**no regression** for every model that accepts it). Gate: `test/test_google_thinking_support.py` (**44**, in the battery); **9 mutations fail by name** — one ESCAPED the first version (the detector fixture let the text fallback mask a removed structured branch) and was closed rather than accepted. **A bug the gate caught in my own fix:** `except … as exc` unbinds `exc` at block exit, so the langchain retry's `raise exc` would have raised `NameError`. Battery GREEN. **Reported, deliberately NOT changed:** the LLM-config editor writes `thinking_budget: 0` on every save even when the field is untouched, so Google models are thinking-disabled by default and the UI offers no way to express "no budget" — a cost/behaviour decision for the operator, not a correctness bug now that a refusal is survivable. Files: `llm/thinking_support.py`, `llm/{handler,langchain_adapter}.py`, `test/{test_google_thinking_support.py,trust_battery.sh}`.

- **Sep 2026**: **A planner repository's count is DERIVED from its store — the card read 6 / 0 / 28 over repositories that held 14.** Operator, after three "fixes" to the policing pack's seeded champion cases: *"the seeded champion cases for the optim class … still not correct and working — neither for admin nor for demo_walkthrough — look at prod and local."* Measured before touching anything, in all four places: the store held **14 vectors and 14 files everywhere** (local admin 8, local demo 55, production admin 527, production fork 529). The cases were seeded and indexed correctly. What the card shows is `collections.chunk_count` (`ui.js:9183` reads `col.count || col.chunk_count`; both list endpoints filled `count` from that column) — and that column was a CACHE with N writers, half of which forgot: the learning loop **incremented** it by one per net-new case, the pack diff and a subscription copy wrote it whole, and the **seeder** (`populate_collection_from_template`), the **dedupe tool** and a **reset** never touched it. So local admin read 6 (an old increment), local demo and the fork read 0 (seeded, never counted), and production admin read **28** — the dedupe removed 14 duplicate vectors and left the column where the doubling had put it. A count with several writers drifts the first time one forgets; that is the class, and the fix is structural: **the count is DERIVED from the store through ONE function, every writer reconciles through that function, and every reader derives.** `RAGRetriever.resolve_store` is the collection's own handle independent of retrieval scope (`resolve_for_write` is it by its old name); `planner_case_count` counts through a **read-only** open (a count must never mint a store) and returns **None for unreadable — never 0**; `refresh_persisted_count` is the one write of the column. Reconciled by the seeder, the learning loop (the increment is gone), the pack diff (routed through the same function, not a private copy), the dedupe tool, `_maintain_vector_store` and `reset_collection` — which also **read the retrieval map** and reported "0 items removed" against a populated repository the process was not serving (the recorded trap, now closed at the root). Both list endpoints serve `_served_count` (planner → derived, reconciling the column on the way; knowledge → persisted, since its backend may be remote and `light` exists for that; unreadable → the last persisted figure), and a served payload carries one number, not a live `count` beside a stale `chunk_count`. **`/rows` — the inspect view — reads the collection's own store** whatever server the process serves (it answered 0 with *"Collection is not loaded"* for a planner keyed to another server, indistinguishable from empty; the top-up that duplicated production's 14 → 28 read exactly that 0), and is now access-checked against the caller's own population (404 for another user's repository). `refresh-counts` never persists 0 over an unreadable store. **A false alarm caught before it became an act:** two production collections matched my `name LIKE '%Policing%'` filter and read as orphaned duplicates — they are the estate endpoint's per-server DEFAULT planner repositories, matched through the account name `policing_estate_agent`; the REST listing named them correctly and nothing was deleted. Gate: `test_planner_indexing` 33 → **67** — the derived count through a real read-only open, unreadable-is-None, the one write, every writer reconciling (AST per function), `_served_count` EXECUTED against a fake retriever (planner derives · knowledge persists · light persists · unreadable keeps the figure), and `/rows` on the store. **Five mutations fail by name** (serving the column · the increment restored · `/rows` back on the retrieval map · a count that mints a store · unreadable persisted as 0); one first crashed the run instead of naming its failure and the assertion was hardened. **Live-verified** on local (both repositories serve 14, `/rows` 14 with no session context, the column healed to 14, cross-user 404) and on production after deploy (527 and 529 both 14 on admin and demo_walkthrough).
