- **Sep 2026**: **A builtin shadow already on disk is IGNORED — the read side of the rule the install guard enforces.** Operator, with a screenshot: `teradata-sql-expert` still rendered with the **User** badge and an *Orphaned · Policing Data Products* tag after being restored as a platform builtin. The earlier fix closed the INFLOW (a pack install naming a builtin id is refused before any write) and deleted the two shadows in the repo — but it did nothing about the copies **already written** to a deployment's state directory, and `_discover_and_load` took a read-dir copy over `skills/builtin/` **unconditionally**: `is_builtin_skill()` existed and was called at exactly ONE site — the install guard — never by the loader that decides what is actually served. So a state copy kept demoting the platform skill to "User", carrying the uninstalled pack's orphan stamp with it, for the life of that instance, and **no migration would ever have cleared it**. Now ONE rule with TWO enforcement points: refuse the write, refuse the read. A read-dir copy of an id the platform SHIPS is ignored and **NAMED** in a warning carrying its path — the copy stays on disk, because deleting an operator's files as a startup side effect is not the loader's call — so an instance **self-heals on restart** with no migration and nothing removed behind the operator's back. The seed carve-out is untouched: a seed may still override an id the platform does NOT ship (`teradata-coordinator`), which is the mechanism's real use; and the duplicate `builtin_dir / plugin_directory` derivation collapses into the one `builtin_dir_for` resolver. **Proven on the running server with a shadow deliberately restored:** the loader names it and `GET /v1/skills` reads `is_user:false · is_builtin:true · pack_origin:null` — the badge is Builtin and the orphan tag cannot resurface. Gate: `test_pack_skill_ownership` 26 → **38**, and the suite is now **in the battery** (it sat outside it — the recorded *a gate the battery does not run is a gate nobody runs* trap, third occurrence). **Four mutations fail by name — and two ESCAPED the first version and were fixed rather than accepted:** an "ignore EVERY state copy" over-reach passed because the no-over-reach assertion was satisfied by the **auto-discovery fallback** rather than the registry path under test (now discriminated on the loader's own log output, which is the only place the two differ), and a **silent** ignore passed because nothing held the warning that gives the operator the path. Production carries no shadow (today's rebuild used the fixed export, which drops the builtin from the bundle); the local copy was removed at the operator's request — byte-identical to the builtin apart from the orphan stamp. Battery **GREEN**, diffed suite-by-suite: zero coverage drops, zero failures, no suite lost. Files: `src/trusted_data_agent/skills/manager.py`, `test/{test_pack_skill_ownership.py,trust_battery.sh}`, `docs/Architecture/SKILL_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

- **Sep 2026**: **The marketplace shows what you may see — and a pack card states what it ships.** Operator: *"I don't see the policing data product in the marketplace for analyst_demo"*, then *"the visibility selector hides behind the agent pack card"*. The second report reframed the first: the filter bar is a `.glass-panel`, and **`backdrop-filter` creates a stacking context**, so the dropdown's `z-index:50` was trapped inside the bar and the cards painted after it covered the menu — measured in a real browser, **every option `hittable:false`**. The control that would have revealed a targeted listing was unusable, so this was never "the wrong filter was selected". Fixed by portalling the menu to `<body>` (`position:fixed`, restored to its exact slot on close) — the mechanism `customSelect.js` and `splitPanelChrome.js` already used; the marketplace `tda-select` was the one hand-rolled dropdown that did not, which is why it was the one that clipped. **The scope the UI never offered:** the backend has always supported `visibility=all` (public ∪ granted-targeted) and the menu had only `public`/`targeted`, with `public` the default — so a listing shared with you personally was hidden with **no sign that anything was missing**. `All` / `All + mine` added and **`all` is now the UI default** (the API default stays `public` — a far wider blast radius); the stored preference key is **versioned** (`marketplace_visibility_v2`), because the option set, labels and default all changed, so an old value would replay the very default that hid the grant — a one-time reset, choices from then on respected. `Targeted` → **"Shared with me"** in the filter only (the publish dialog keeps the publisher's word — two seats, two correct vocabularies), and the collapsed label carries `whitespace-nowrap` after it wrapped to two rows. **`all` was also not a true union in FOUR endpoints** (agent packs, skills, extensions, KGs): each omitted the `publisher_user_id` branch its own `targeted` arm carries, so a publisher's own targeted listing vanished under the name "All" — proven live and isolated (the caller holds zero grants, so the row can only come from the new branch). **Then the pack card itself:** the seal was missing on **both** the consumer's and the publisher's card because the browse endpoint fetched `source_installation_id`, used it internally and **`pop`ped it before serving** — so every card rendered `data-trust-market-id=""` and the publisher's signature could never resolve (a consumer *can* read it: reads are deliberately not owner-scoped, verified → `trusted`); My Assets keyed its seal on that same absent field instead of its own `installation_id`. Cards now also state **how many knowledge graphs the pack ships** (from the publisher's ledger, so listings published earlier need no republish) on all three surfaces, and the two marketplace cards are **harmonized**: `/v1/agent-packs` never served `profile_tags`, so an installed pack showed only its coordinator tag while the listing showed all six — one pack reading as six agents in one place and one agent in the other. Member chips now render **THE profile tag** (`ui.js:renderProfileTag`) in IFOC colours rather than a uniform grey lookalike, driven by a served `{tag: profile_type}` map so the colours are right for a consumer who does not own those profiles; an unknown member is shown as unknown, **never given a guessed class**. Gate: new `test/test_marketplace_visibility.mjs` (**70** assertions, in the battery) executing the shipped builders under a DOM stub — portal/restore, the scope truth table, the defaults, and the card contract; **eight mutations fail by name**. Battery **GREEN**. Verified in a real browser end to end (all six options hittable and unclipped, the label single-row at every viewport, seal reading *"Signed by the publisher"*, `3 knowledge graphs`, chips `#4ade80`/`#3b82f6`/`#9333ea`/`#F15F22`). Files: `api/{agent_pack_routes,skills_routes,kg_marketplace_routes,rest_routes}.py`, `core/agent_pack_manager.py`, `static/js/handlers/{marketplaceHandler,agentPackHandler}.js`, `templates/index.html`, `test/test_marketplace_visibility.mjs`, `docs/Architecture/MARKETPLACE_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/RestAPI/restAPI.md`.

- **Sep 2026**: **A pack graph is resolved by its OWNER — one agent grounding a second agent on a shipped ontology no longer costs the consumer its binding.** Found by verifying the change directly above rather than assuming it: grounding the policing pack's Optimize twin on the NIBRS ontology made that graph active for **two** profiles on the publisher, and the pack manifest's `profile_tag` is **one** tag — whichever ASSIGNED profile the export happened to walk first. When it named the twin, a consumer with no assignment for the twin resolved the entry to nothing, `_refresh_pack_kgs_in_place` skipped it, and `_prune_pack_kg_assignments` then deleted the consumer's **real** binding: an in-place update left `@NIBRS` with **no ontology at all** (observed live on the production demo account, twice — the second run removed the last assignment). A graph is owned by exactly one agent, so the OWNER is the only identity that stays unique once a graph legitimately grounds more than one: the refresh now resolves an entry by `owner_profile_tag` first, then `profile_tag`, then every listed assignee (so an older manifest still resolves), trying each candidate against the consumer's own graphs and skipping the entry only when none resolves. The export also writes the owner as `profile_tag` when it knows it, so new manifests never carry the ambiguous tag — but the consumer-side fix is the load-bearing one, because manifests already in the wild carry it. Gate: `test_agent_pack_kg_refresh` 45 → **51**; the mutation (back to the single-tag lookup) fails 5 by name. Verified end to end on production: both accounts' Optimize twins now answer **5,026,601** with `WHERE V4019 = '0'` — the correct table and the correct QUOTED comparison — where before the twin queried an empty ontology and took a 3807. Files: `core/agent_pack_manager.py`, `test/test_agent_pack_kg_refresh.py`.

- **Sep 2026**: **The Optimize twin grounds on the NIBRS ontology — a deliberate trade, re-decided on measured consequences.** `@NIBRSO` was left out of every `bind_tags` **on purpose**: its lane is the one whose grounding comes from the seeded planner repository, and that contrast with the ontology-grounded Ideate analysts IS the A/B the pack's claims rest on. It was a trade to re-decide, not an oversight to correct. Two consequences, reproduced on both production accounts and locally (2026-09-08), decided it: the knowledge-graph component ships **enabled** for that profile, so the agent calls `TDA_KnowledgeGraph query`, receives an **empty** ontology (`total_entities: 0`), has no schema, guesses a table name and takes a **3807** from the database; and — the sharper half — **the grounding gate derives its trusted scope FROM the bound graph**, so under this pack's `enforce` posture the twin had *no boundary to enforce at all*. An agent that cannot be held to a scope is why this belongs in the pack rather than in an operator's hands. **Fixed in the pack, as data:** new `GROUNDED_ALSO = {"NIBRS": (OPTIMIZE_TWIN_TAG,)}` declares which agents GROUND on a product's graph without OWNING it — the supported shape since the Sep-2026 `owns`/`grounds_on` split — and `graph_plan` reads it in all three layouts, so the twin is grounded on every install rather than by a manual per-instance binding. `CASEDF` and the estate graph are untouched: a product analyst's trusted scope stays one product, and the twin is in the NIBRS lane, so binding it widens nothing by a single database. The planner repository remains the twin's distinguishing ingredient — the lane itself is unchanged. `OPTIMIZE_TWIN_TAG` replaces three string literals, and the bind site skips a tag the run did not create (`--analyst-class optimize` / `--no-optimize-twin`) rather than raising, the `MEMBER_ORDER` convention applied to bindings. **Gate:** `test_policing_pack_graph_layout` 83 → **95** — the per-product assertions were restated from pinned literals (`bind_tags == [["NIBRS"], ["CASEDF"]]`) to the PROPERTY they stood for: a product graph grounds its own analyst plus whatever `GROUNDED_ALSO` declares, and **never an agent from the other product's lane**; plus the twin owns no graph, grounds only on the NIBRS one, and the estate graph never grounds it. Two mutations fail by name (emptying `GROUNDED_ALSO` fails 5; dropping the bind-site filter fails 1). **Also fixed, the same pass:** `@TEFMT` (an admin profile, not a pack member) referenced knowledge repositories **108/109, which have rows in SQLite but no vector store** — so its retrieval from them returned nothing, and after the export hardening it could no longer be packaged silently either. Repointed to the name-identical working copies (**159**/**158**), sending the WHOLE `knowledgeConfig` back because `update_profile` shallow-merges and a partial block would have dropped `enabled`/`maxDocs` — the same defect class this file already records. Production now scans **0** profile- or pack-referenced collections without a vector store. Files: `agent_packs/policing-data-products/build.py`, `test/test_policing_pack_graph_layout.py`.

- **Sep 2026**: **A seeded case is INDEXED, or the run says so — the partial write that reported success.** Follow-on to the entry below, which framed the fault as an ordering trap. That was the symptom; this is the root. In `rag_template_generator.populate_collection_from_template` the disk write was **unconditional** while the vector write was **conditional on the collection happening to be loaded in this process** (`if collection_id in self.rag_retriever.collections`), and the endpoint reported *"14 successful, 0 failed"* either way. On a fresh install nothing has opened a session yet, so the cases reached disk and were never indexed. **The conflation:** *"is this collection in the retrieval working set?"* is not *"may I index into it?"* — the first is scoped by `_planner_keyed_to` so a session cannot retrieve another server's planner; the second is always yes, because a case belongs in its own collection whatever server the process happens to be serving. **Four changes, root first.** (1) New **`RAGRetriever.resolve_for_write`** opens the collection's store regardless of retrieval scope, and deliberately does **not** register it into `self.collections` — that map IS the retrieval working set, and adding an out-of-scope planner to it would leak it into another server's retrieval, the very isolation `_planner_keyed_to` exists to hold. Both it and `ensure_loaded` go through ONE new `_open_chroma_collection`, which resolves the embedder from the collection's **own** `embedding_model` — opening a store with the process default silently produces vectors that can never match the ones already in it, which is almost certainly why the write was made conditional in the first place. (2) The populate loop resolves the target **once, before the loop**, indexes every case, and counts **`indexed`** apart from `successful`; a case that cannot be indexed **fails** rather than passing silently. (3) The endpoint refuses to call a zero-indexed run a success (**500** naming the shortfall) — `successful` counted disk writes, and every caller believed it. (4) **The export now REFUSES a member it cannot ship** (`PackExportIncomplete`) where it previously logged a warning and continued: that is what turned a local indexing fault into a signed artefact that was wrong — the consumer's Optimize twin arrived with `ragCollections: None`, its composition no longer matched what the publisher signed, it read `unsigned`, and the pack seal went down with it (bottom-up), while the publisher's own badge stayed green so nothing on either side pointed at the missing member. Plus a verify-don't-trust floor in `build.py`: the seeded count is read back and a shortfall stops the run before it signs over cases that are invisible. **Deliberately NOT done:** automating "activate before seeding" in the installer — that would encode the workaround and leave the platform broken for every other caller (the UI populate path, other packs); the root fix makes the ordering irrelevant. Gate: new `test/test_planner_indexing.py` (**33**, in the battery) drives the REAL retriever seams and the REAL populate loop with **nothing pre-loaded** — the exact fresh-install state — and asserts both directions of the isolation rule (an out-of-scope planner is writable but still not retrievable, and `ensure_loaded` still loads one that IS keyed here). **Four mutations fail by name** (restore the conditional write · let `resolve_for_write` widen the retrieval map · downgrade the export back to a warning · let the build trust the report). **Live-proven on a real server:** a planner keyed to a server the process was not serving, with no session ever opened, populated `indexed=2` and read back 2 rows — the exact condition that produced 0 before; and a full marketplace fork through the real export+import path still succeeded (`updated_in_place`, `trust_reinstated: 14`, 6 profiles, 3 graphs), so the export refusal does not break a complete pack. Battery **GREEN**, diffed suite-by-suite: **zero coverage drops, zero failures, no suite lost**. Files: `agent/rag_retriever.py`, `agent/rag_template_generator.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `core/agent_pack_manager.py`, `agent_packs/policing-data-products/build.py`, `test/{test_planner_indexing.py,trust_battery.sh}`.

- **Sep 2026**: **A refused planner reset is not a reset — and a fresh install cannot seed a planner until its agent is activated.** Two findings from the production deploy of the policing pack, both about the same seam. **(1)** `build.py --reset-planner` printed the reset's status code and ignored it. A pack-managed repository answers **409** (*"This collection is managed by agent pack(s) … Uninstall the pack(s) to reset it"*), and the run still fell through to `planner_created = True` and seeded the FULL set on top of what was already there — production collection 527 went **14 → 28 cases, every query present exactly twice**. Duplicate champions are not cosmetic: `_reevaluate_champion_for_query` elects one champion per query, so a duplicated query splits its own history and retrieval can serve the same lesson twice while crowding out a different one. The reset now **stops the run** naming the remedy — the operator asked for a reset, and the honest answer to *"it did not happen"* is to stop, not to guess between topping up and re-seeding. **(2) The ordering a fresh install requires, learned the hard way:** the planner's ChromaDB store is created by the first write that happens while the collection is **loaded**, and the retriever loads it only for sessions on the MCP server it is keyed to — which the REST activation firewall refuses until the profile is activated. So on a clean instance the first `build.py` run reports *"14 seeded"* while the vector store is never created, and the pack **export then drops the planner** (`ChromaDB collection not found`), so a consumer's Optimize twin arrives with `ragCollections: None`, its composition no longer matches what the publisher signed, and it reads `unsigned` — taking the pack seal down with it (bottom-up). **The fix is order, not code:** connection-test each profile, add them to `active_for_consumption_profile_ids` (a WHOLE-LIST write — read it first and merge, or everything omitted is silently deactivated), then run the build again; the seeding then lands and the export carries the planner. Verified on production: the consumer's in-place fork update went `resource_reconciliation.added: 1`, **`trust_reinstated: 13`**, and `@NIBRSO` `unsigned` → `trusted` with the pack seal following it. **Also recorded, not fixed:** a `/rows` read against an unloaded planner returns 0 and is indistinguishable from an empty repository — the same "empty vs unreadable" asymmetry the build's own seeding guard already refuses to act on (demo's planner read 0 while holding 14 case files, and read 14 the moment a session loaded it). **New `maintenance/dedupe_planner_cases.py`** removes duplicates already written, from BOTH ChromaDB and the on-disk mirror (a file left behind is one `_run_maintenance` re-adds). Its duplicate test **delegates to `trust.content.case_content_id`** — already THE definition shared by the planner trust baseline and the pack update's change detection — so the tool and the trust layer cannot disagree about what a case SAYS; a third definition here is the drift that module's own docstring warns about. On top of it the dedupe drops only the **mint**: measured on the real pair, two copies of one seed differ on EXACTLY `case_id`, `metadata.case_id`, `metadata.task_id` (literally `template-task-<first 8 of case_id>`) and `metadata.timestamp`. Trust deliberately keeps the last two — they travel verbatim inside the pack export, so publisher and consumer agree on them — which is right for *"is this the case that was signed?"* and wrong for *"is this the same seed written twice?"*. Which copy survives is ordered so nothing is silently undone (elected champion → one carrying user feedback → earliest), and a group whose members genuinely DIFFER while several claim champion is reported and skipped: that is an election anomaly needing a human, not a coin toss. Gate: `test_policing_pack_graph_layout` 79 → **83**; mutation-tested (removing the guard fails 2 by name). Files: `agent_packs/policing-data-products/build.py`, `maintenance/dedupe_planner_cases.py`, `test/test_policing_pack_graph_layout.py`.

- **Sep 2026**: **The classification snapshot is the RECORD, not runtime scratch — the TDA_* leak that made Optimize agents read `changed` forever.** Operator, after months of it: *"@NIBRSO's deployment half reads changed … tools removed: TDA_Canvas, TDA_Charting … I had this all the time with the optim accounts"*, then *"maybe the TDA tools don't travel with the classification — I don't know, you have to find out."* They do not, and they never should have: the adapter states the rule in its own comment — *"CLIENT_SIDE_TOOLS (TDA_*) are always-active platform tools, not MCP server tools. They must not be sent to the LLM for classification or stored in `classification_results`"* — and the adapter honours it (`client_side_names` skip). **Measured live, and the numbers name the bug:** two profiles bound to the SAME MCP server, classified two seconds apart, persisted **63 tools / 0 prompts** (`@NIBRS`, `llm_only`+MCP) versus **48 tools / 12 prompts** (`@NIBRSO`, `tool_enabled`) — a delta of exactly **15 = 7 system + 8 component TDA_\* tools**. **Root cause — reference aliasing through the config cache, in four steps:** `config_manager.load_config()` serves an in-memory cache, so `get_profile_classification()` returns a **live reference into the stored profile**; `load_profile_classification_into_state` assigned those dicts **straight onto `APP_STATE` with no copy**; the injection immediately below wrote `"System Tools"` and `"Component Tools"` **into that same object**; and the next save of that user's config — any `update_profile`, e.g. the `needs_reclassification` clear that runs on the very next line — serialised the polluted snapshot to disk. Because the **deployment half of the trust envelope hashes that snapshot** (`trust.deployment.catalog_from_classification`), an agent then read `changed` over a drift that **was never a deployment change at all**, and re-attesting only held until the next classification moved it back. **Fixed in TWO places, because the leak had two shapes and the first fix only closed one — proven by production re-polluting two `llm_only` profiles hours later.** (a) *Aliasing*: the four `APP_STATE[...]` assignments now `copy.deepcopy` the stored structures, so the injection can no longer mutate the record in place. (b) *Read-back*: the adapter persists `STATE['structured_tools']` **as-is**, and `APP_STATE` is process-global — so when a classification short-circuits (`Forcing light classification mode`), whatever a PREVIOUS profile's activation injected is still sitting there and is written into THIS profile's record. No per-caller guard closes both. **The trigger, once it was named:** `POST /v1/profiles/set_active_for_consumption` classifies `profile_ids[0]` (*"for simplicity, we use the first profile's settings"*), so a whole-list write whose first id happens to be some other agent persisted THAT agent's record from whatever was in `APP_STATE` — which is why exactly ONE profile per account came back polluted, the sorted-first one. So the invariant moved to **`config_manager.save_profile_classification`, the one chokepoint that persists a populated classification** (audited: every other writer — profile creation, a classification-mode change, the pack import — writes an EMPTY block and cannot carry the categories): it strips exactly the two categories the injector creates (`System Tools`, `Component Tools` — never a `TDA_` name heuristic, which would strip a real MCP tool so named), and **copies rather than mutates**, since the caller is handing over the runtime's own live structures. The runtime is deliberately untouched: both categories are re-injected on every activation, so the fix changes what is REMEMBERED, never what runs. **Audited before changing anything:** the loader is the ONLY aliasing site; the adapter builds its structures from scratch (`STATE['structured_tools'] = {}`) and saves them explicitly, so nothing depended on the aliasing. **Blast radius measured, not assumed:** **9 of 40** profiles polluted locally, **26 of 1406** on production — concentrated on `@OPTIM`/`@OPGGT`/`@OPFMT`/`@TDEXO`/`@OPMLX`/`@OPTIL`, exactly the class the operator reported. `maintenance/purge_injected_classification_tools.py` repairs snapshots written before the fix (dry-run default, timestamped backup, drops only the two injected CATEGORIES — never a name-prefix match, which would strip a genuine MCP tool called `TDA_*`); it **refuses** a profile the repair would leave with no tools and no prompts, because an empty snapshot reads to the loader as *never classified* and would silently disarm the profile. **Gate:** new `test/test_classification_snapshot_isolation.py` (**22**, in the battery) drives the REAL loader against a fake config manager that is faithful in the one dimension under test — it hands back a live reference, exactly as the cache-backed manager does, since a fake that copied here would measure nothing. It asserts the record is byte-identical after loading, that no TDA_* is persisted, that APP_STATE still receives both injected categories with their per-profile `disabled` flags (the no-regression half), that the four structures are different objects, that a nested runtime mutation cannot reach the record, and — structurally — that the assignment site copies and the adapter still refuses TDA_* at the source. **Mutation-tested:** removing the deepcopy reproduces the production symptom exactly (the snapshot gains `['Component Tools', 'System Tools']`) and fails **14 assertions by name**. Battery **GREEN**, diffed suite-by-suite against the pre-change run: **zero coverage drops, zero failures, no suite lost**. **A trap in the repair tool itself, found by chasing two false alarms:** `load_config` caches user configs in memory, so running the purge against a LIVE instance is undone by the next profile save writing the stale copy back — the tool now says so and prints a restart reminder, and the production repair was done with the container stopped. Twice during this work I read a dirty baseline as "the fix failed"; the controlled form (repair → restart → replay the exact call → survey) is what settled it, and it reports **0**. Files: `core/{configuration_service,config_manager}.py`, `maintenance/purge_injected_classification_tools.py`, `test/{test_classification_snapshot_isolation.py,trust_battery.sh}`.

- **Sep 2026**: **The publisher's ledger claims the graphs the pack ships — a fork's pack seal reinstates on its own again.** Operator: *"Fix the root first."* A consumer's forked pack read `unsigned` and no amount of signing on the consumer's side could change it — correctly: `portability.reinstate` only re-applies the publisher's signature when the copy's composition matches what was signed, and the two sides were counting **different members**. Measured live: publisher pack declared **8** members (6 agents + the knowledge repo + the planner repo), the fork **11** — the same 8 by content hash **plus the 3 ontologies** — so `composition_hash_for` could never agree (`f20a2501…` vs `9a7cd6aa…`) and the honesty gate refused the claim. Root cause: `create_and_install` (the publisher-registration path behind `build.py --register`) recorded profiles and collections as pack resources but **never the knowledge graphs**, while a consumer's import records its KG copies — `_record_installation` had accepted `kg_ids`/`kg_names` all along and this one caller simply never passed them. **Fixed at the derivation, not the call site:** ONE `_manifest_kg_members(manifest)` reads the graphs from the manifest the export just wrote, so the publisher's ledger and every consumer's ledger name the same member set **by construction**; ids differ between the two sides and the composition hash is taken over each member's **content**, which is exactly what makes them agree. **Two things the fix forced, both real:** (1) the KG deletion loop in `uninstall_pack` was the one member class with **no ownership guard** — profiles and collections already skip what the pack does not own, KGs deleted unconditionally — so recording the publisher's own graphs would have made unregistering the pack **delete the ontologies it was built from**; the guard is scoped to `_registration_origin == "created"` (the origin whose own docstring says it references rather than creates) rather than to `is_owned`, because **subscribe also records copies with `is_owned=0` while genuinely owning them** — a blanket guard would have left a subscriber's copies behind, so every other origin deletes exactly as before; (2) `build.py`'s `register_pack` held a **second idempotency mechanism** ("already registered → skip") that froze the ledger at the first run's membership, so the platform fix could never reach an existing installation — it now always re-registers and lets the platform decide create-vs-update (the row id, and therefore the marketplace listing and every subscriber's pointer, survives). **Proven live end to end on the local pair:** re-registration updated installation 16 in place (ledger 6 profiles · 2 collections · **3 graphs**), `composition_hash_for(16) == composition_hash_for(27)` exactly, the publisher's pack correctly read `changed` over its moved composition and re-signed to `trusted`, and the consumer's ordinary in-place fork update then took the seal on its own — **`unsigned` → `trusted`, `trust_reinstated: 14`, with demo_walkthrough signing nothing and needing no tier change**; full audit: **12/12 admin artefacts and 14/14 consumer artefacts trusted**. Gates: `test_pack_registration_idempotent` 24 → **41** (the property driven through the REAL `member_refs`/`composition_hash_for` over a temp ledger whose two sides hold the same content under different ids — and the inverse: a publisher that does not claim its graphs diverges), `test_policing_pack_graph_layout` 66 → **79**. **Five mutations fail by name** — and one (removing the uninstall guard) was first caught only by a **crash**, which is half a gate, so the ordering assertion was hardened to report by name. Battery **GREEN**, diffed suite-by-suite against the pre-change run: **zero coverage drops, zero failures, no suite lost**. Files: `core/agent_pack_manager.py`, `agent_packs/policing-data-products/build.py`, `test/{test_pack_registration_idempotent,test_policing_pack_graph_layout}.py`.
- **Sep 2026**: **A KG's version history dies with the KG — the purge function had zero callers.** `kg_version_db.delete_versions_for_kg` has existed since version history shipped, with a docstring stating its own contract (*"called when the KG itself is deleted"*) and **not one caller** — so every KG deletion left its snapshots behind: rows in `kg_versions` pointing at a `kg_id` no `kg_metadata` row owns, invisible on every surface, growing forever. Found while clearing local test accounts (5 orphans outliving their graphs). The gzipped payload is the WHOLE graph, so an orphan is not a stray id — it is a full copy of a deleted ontology's entities and relationships retained after the user removed it. **KG deletion has no single chokepoint** — four independent sites issue `DELETE FROM kg_metadata` (the clear endpoint · agent-pack uninstall · the KG-subscription copy delete · the marketplace install rollback), each with its own transaction and cascade list — so the purge is explicit at each site, beside the cascade already there; the agent-pack site already carries the same shape for the attestation, which is the precedent this follows. **Fail-soft everywhere** (losing a snapshot must never block a removal the user asked for): three sites log a named warning; the rollback path is silent because it removes a KG that was never established, so there is normally nothing to purge — the DELETE is kept for the rule rather than its effect, since carrying an exemption list is where the next deletion site would hide. Now the phrase is tried first, then its **meaningful terms** (each with its singular) ranked by how many a node satisfies — the sentence surfaces the nodes it is about; a true miss is **recovery-shaped** (size, types, sample names, what a lookup matches, "the graph is supportive, never required") and carries `suppress_inline`, so no dead card reaches the reader. **(3) Enrichment:** a DATE deployed as text now says so — *ORDER BY / TOP / GROUP BY follow STRING order; SELECT one value first, then CAST with the FORMAT matching its shape (31-OCT-2023 → 'DD-MMM-YYYY' …)* — the product's own metadata for `INCDATE` claims `MM/DD/YYYY` while the data holds `31-OCT-2023`, which is why the rule says sample, never trust the declared form. **(4) ReAct parity with the Optimize path:** ONE `sql_dialect.teradata_top_rewrite` (LIMIT n or a misplaced trailing TOP n → `SELECT TOP n`; declines DISTINCT / existing TOP / OFFSET / multi-statement) now serves `TeradataLimitStrategy` AND a one-shot retry in the ReAct tool wrapper, which hands the model the successful result with a note naming the rewrite. **The local rehearsal found a fifth, deeper gap:** `langchain_mcp_adapters` raises `ToolException` on any MCP error result and LangGraph's default handler re-raises it, so on this install ONE failed SQL statement ended the whole ReAct turn with a canned "I encountered an error" answer — the model never saw the error it could have corrected. The wrapper now turns a raised tool error into recovery-shaped tool CONTENT (cancellation still propagates); the second rehearsal turn showed the model receiving Error 3707 as a result and self-correcting in the next round. - **Sep 2026**: **The Live Status assurance dial settles at the stream's OWN end — a completed turn no longer depends on a single later score delivery; JUDGED's "pending" is bounded by turn age**. Operator: *"if the live status panel is collapsed and I execute a query, and then open up the live status panel after query execution, the trust circle is either not showing up at all or … spinning forever with the status 'not in yet' — after a page refresh it shows up as normal."* The collapse itself was not the mechanism — every code path is identical collapsed or expanded, no stale-pin fork existed on the dial path (audited across the last 80 content commits per module), and a headless-browser reproduction with the panel collapsed settled fine LOCALLY. **The prod reproduction found it:** at the moment the stream closed (composer re-enabled) the dial still carried all 35 pending marks; it settled ~20 s later when the score arrived over the notification channel. Root cause: `settle()` was called ONLY by the Stop handler; a normally completed turn left the live model (pending words + the pulsing phase dot) on screen and waited on `turn_score_complete` alone — which, once the stream has closed, rides the notification channel; locally the score rode the still-open stream, which is why it never reproduced there. One lost delivery (a reconnect gap, a tab that was not the one the event reached) → "not in yet" forever; and on the NEXT turn `begin()` bailed on that stale `_live` (its guard could only ever match a previous turn's model once the caller ran it once per stream) after the status window had been cleared → no dial at all. Both halves of the report, one root. **Fix — the stream's own end settles the dial:** `processStream` returns the turn it DELIVERED (from `final_answer`); the stream's `finally` calls the new `AssuranceDial.complete(sid, turn)` for a delivered turn (render the persisted, authoritative reading — with bounded fetch retries, since the turn persists AFTER `final_answer` is emitted — JUDGED honestly pending until scored) or `settle()` for an undelivered one (error/cancel → "not recorded", never a pass); `inject()` gains `force` (the score that lands later must be allowed to re-render the same turn, or the settle would have become a lock via `_isOnScreen`), `retry`, `scored`, and a truthful return; both score paths (stream + notification) force the re-render; a **bounded score fallback** re-fetches at 45 s (a lost notification) and 200 s (past the registry's window) while no score has landed; `begin()` always starts fresh. **Registry:** `EVAL_PENDING_WINDOW_SECONDS = 180` + `turn_within_scoring_window()` — an unscored turn past the window reads the truthful `absent` ("no score recorded") instead of a pending that never resolves; a turn with no/unparseable timestamp keeps pending (a legacy shape must not be pushed into absent on a field it never carried). **Gates:** dial 441 → **454** (stream returns the delivered turn · the stream's end completes/settles · complete = force+retry, falls back to settle, arms the fallback · both score paths force · begin clears the timers), assurance_points 354 → **362** (the pending-window truth table incl. Z-suffixed times and the injected clock); **three mutations fail by name** (stream end stops completing · notification score loses force · begin bails on a stale model); the `_isOnScreen` and begin assertions re-pinned to the new forms; pins cascaded through 24 modules by script. Battery GREEN. Browser reload + server restart (registry). Files: `static/js/handlers/assuranceDial.js`, `static/js/{eventHandlers,notifications}.js`, `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/assurance_points.py`, `templates/index.html` + importer pins, `test/{test_assurance_dial.mjs,test_assurance_points.py}`, `docs/Architecture/ASSURANCE_INSTRUMENTS_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

- **Sep 2026**: **An imported document keeps the exporting instance's id — and on one instance the subscriber's rows overwrote the publisher's.** Found refreshing the policing pack's documentation corpus after release 2.2.0: the demo account's collection listed ZERO documents while a live search on it returned the new content, and the admin's 20 rows all carried the demo import's timestamp. `knowledge_documents.document_id` is unique across the table; the fresh-install path had already learned to mint instance-local ids (randomly), but `update_in_place` kept the ZIP's source ids, so its `ON CONFLICT(document_id)` upsert UPDATED THE PUBLISHER'S rows and the copy's chunks were written twice under ids no row owned. **Fix — ONE derivation for both paths:** `collection_utils.local_document_id(scope, source_id)` (uuid5, keyed on the target's vector collection NAME — known before the first batch, whereas the row id only exists after; different scope ⇒ different id, so publisher and subscriber on one instance never share one) via `_LocalIdMap`, a dict whose `setdefault` derives instead of taking the random default the call sites pass; `_handle_update_in_place` localizes what it reads from the ZIP (`_localize_incoming`: re-keyed map, chunk metadata and chunk ids rewritten, `source_document_id` kept) and `_diff_and_patch_collection` sweeps chunks left under a source id before adding. The policing product's own release 2.2.0 carries the product side (`QC-DOMAIN-003` states the declared key and names the batch-header columns as NOT keys; the Uderia trial logged it in the fork with `Change_Log` rows for the performance and access layers that had none). Files: `agent/preflight/{joins,guard}.py`, `agent/executor.py`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/handler.py`, `core/config.py`, `docker-compose.yml`, `test/test_preflight_joins.py`.

- **Sep 2026**: **The "connection timeout" class, found on the database: a runaway join with no ceiling wedges the whole MCP endpoint; closed at the driver, at the chokepoint, and in the enrichment.** A trial pass on the policing product turned into three identical 120 s tool timeouts per turn from one run onward. Teradata's `MonitorSession` showed two requests from the endpoint's sessions running for three hours (6,000 CPU-s each) with every later request `DELAYED` behind them; direct calls proved the endpoint answered `initialize` but hung on `SELECT 1`. The runaway was `Incident JOIN Arrestee ON BH010 = BH010 AND BH012 = BH012` — batch-header fields both tables carry — instead of the declared `(ORI, INCNUM)`. **Three fixes, each a class:** (1) the endpoint's `DATABASE_URI` carries the driver's own `request_timeout=110`, under the platform's `TDA_MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` (120 s), so a request the platform has abandoned is aborted where it lives — proven (abort at 110.3 s, next query 0.2 s); recorded in `deploy/mcp/README.md` with the trap that `docker restart` does not re-read `.env`. (2) The adapter's timeout error is **recovery-shaped** (the loop-guard precedent): it names the ceiling, says a verbatim resend will time out again, and names the two moves that change the outcome. (3) The KG enrichment's declared-key block said "FK declared between these tables" **without the columns** when the column-level key edge (physical layer) was outside the extracted subgraph, while the JOINABLE hint offered the coincidence columns beside it; now a declared pair names its join columns from the two tables' declared keys (and marks a wider key's extra columns as not joining), and a column shared by name only between keyed tables is listed as **NOT JOIN KEYS**. Validated per the operator's cost rule with ONE targeted turn, not a pass: the question that ran away answered the acceptance figure in 20.5 s joining on `(ORI, INCNUM)`. Gates: `test_kg_phase_e` 28 → 34, KG no-regression 196/196. Files: `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/handler.py`, `mcp_adapter/adapter.py`, `deploy/mcp/README.md`, `test/test_kg_phase_e.py`, `test/performance/kg_enrichment_bench.py`.

- **Sep 2026**: **A pack install labelled two profiles with each other's tag — and the next in-place update wrote each manifest entry onto the wrong profile.** Found while diagnosing why `update_in_place` refreshed no graph for a consumer: the installation ledger (`agent_pack_resources`) said `profile-3f62… = @POLICE` while the live profile, the harness that had addressed it for three trial passes, and the graph's owner row all said `@NIBRS`. **Root cause, class-level:** the fresh install recorded ids in CREATION order (non-genie first, coordinator last) zipped against tags in MANIFEST order — any manifest not listing its coordinator last mislabels two profiles, silently (found on two production installs, one of them untouched since Aug 28). The re-import then trusted the ledger: the coordinator's entry landed on the analyst (which lost its graph — assignments key on the id, which was right) and the analyst's entry on the coordinator, leaving a stale `genieConfig` on an `llm_only` profile. **Fixed at four seams:** ONE tag-keyed walk records the ledger (`_aligned_recording`, aligned by construction whatever the creation order); `update_in_place` **heals** a mislabelled ledger from the live tags before reading it (`_heal_ledger_tags` — pure; adopts a live tag only when the manifest ships it, so an out-of-band rename is still updated as installed; a pack-managed profile's tag cannot be changed through the API, so a disagreement is always the ledger's); a profile whose type the pack changes **sheds** the previous type's exclusive block (`_TYPE_EXCLUSIVE_KEYS`, via new `config_manager.remove_profile_keys` — a merge cannot remove a key); and the pack-KG lookup reads the assignments table's REAL columns (`assigned_profile_id`) through `sqlite_util`. `maintenance/repair_pack_ledger_tags.py` heals installs recorded before the fix (same rule; dry-run default) — applied on production. **Also fixed the same hour:** `declare_concept` awaited `GraphStore.get_entity_by_name`, which is synchronous — the gate had passed because its fake store made every method async, unfaithful in the exact dimension under test; the handler guards the mixed surface (`_maybe_await`) and the fake's calling convention is now pinned method-by-method to the real `GraphStore` (mutation reproduces the production traceback). Gates: `test_pack_ledger_tag_alignment` (28, in the battery), `test_kg_concepts` 27 → 31. Files: `core/agent_pack_manager.py`, `core/config_manager.py`, `maintenance/repair_pack_ledger_tags.py`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/handler.py`, `test/{test_pack_ledger_tag_alignment,test_kg_concepts}.py`.

- **Sep 2026**: **The ANDP constructor derives a codebook's structure as a CLASS; a concept can be DECLARED; the policing product gets its performance layer.** Three defects the NIBRS trial exposed were fixed as rules of the constructor for ANY product — none naming a column, prefix or product: **repeating groups** (attributes of one entity whose description titles are equal once their trailing position numbers are stripped → `family`/`positions`/`family_axes`/`family_members`; the seeder treats a family as one concept and the enrichment renders a relevance-gated REPEATING GROUPS block — an agent shown only "LOCATION TYPE - 1" had never learned "- 2/3" existed); **column references** (a description naming another attribute of the same entity → `refers_to`, a PROPERTY deliberately not an edge: as an edge the extractor walked it and every prompt grew a third); **range codes** (`-5 to -9` expanded to members, folded back at render); `module`/`product` stamps. Measured against the old walker on the same database: worst +6.7% tokens on one question, every target kept, airlines/fitness byte-identical (they declare none of it); gate `test_kg_repeating_groups` 23. **`declare_concept`** (`components/builtin/knowledge_graph/concepts.py`, pure; `TDA_KnowledgeGraph` action + `POST /v1/knowledge-graph/declare-concept`): a use case names concepts a product never declared ("digital channel"), so every agent re-derived the rule and any of several defensible readings came back — the declaration makes ONE term, ONE compilable metric (`SUM(CASE WHEN <predicate> …)`, consumed by the existing compiler) and ONE recipe, grounded in the entity's declared columns (an undeclared column refuses, naming it), and returns the product's Memory-module statements as TEXT — the platform never writes to a product's database; gate `test_kg_concepts` 21 incl. a real-backend round trip. **Performance layer** (`agent_packs/policing-data-products/scripts/apply_performance_layer.py`, idempotent, measured): statistics on every declared natural key + the agents' predicate columns, and a COVERING join index (not a sparse one — a sparse index bakes one reading of a definition into the database) — the digital-channel scan 20.4 s → 3.0 s; recorded as `DD-PERF-001` in the product's own Memory module. Also: the benchmark's ceiling is measured against an old-walker run on the SAME database (`kg_bench_oldwalker_newhandler_2026-09-04.json`), because the product catalogue itself moved between baselines.

- **Sep 2026**: **NIBRS loaded at 100% (58,586,198 rows) — and the load's real obstacle was a FATAL AMP nobody knew was down**. Raising the policing product from a 10% sample to the full ICPSR 39270 extract exposed four defects, three of them in the loader and one in the machine. **(1) The Domain load had been broken since the v2 uplift**: `uplift_v2.py` added `created_dts`/`updated_dts` to every Domain table, so `03-domain/02-load.sql` — a positional `INSERT ... SELECT *` — put 391 values into 393 columns. `EXPLAIN` against the live schema failed on **all six** entities; any reload, at any percentage, would have died. Both paths now generate the INSERT **by column name**, stamping the audit columns, which also survives whatever column Domain gains next. **(2) PERM is a per-AMP constraint, not a pool.** Sizing on totals starves the busiest AMP: `resize()` hit Error 3541 twice, and the first fix was wrong (clamping on `SUM(CurrentPerm)` still gave the busiest AMP less than it held). The floor is `MAX(CurrentPerm) × divisor`; `perm_for()` replaced the ×1.25 factor at every site; and `db_space()` stopped reading grants from `SUM(MaxPerm)` over `DiskSpaceV`, which has a row only per POPULATED AMP and so under-reported every grant by a quarter — mixing units with `perm_for`, which reasons in whole grants. **(3) A single Domain `INSERT-SELECT` redistributes every row** (NoPI staging → PI'd Domain) and needs its own size again in spool, at once, on the tightest AMP — Error 2644 after all 58.6M rows had staged. Large inserts now split on `HASHBUCKET(HASHROW(<PI>))`, each chunk committing independently and skipping groups already present, so an interruption resumes instead of duplicating (proven four times; the MOD groups partition the staging table exactly). **(4) The machine**: `HASHAMP()+1` said 4 AMPs, `DiskSpaceV` showed 3, and the derivation of that gap led to **`AMP vproc 2 = FATAL/Down`** — long enough to predate the retained logs (crash count 0, uptime 238 days), **completely masked by FALLBACK** since vproc 3 served its dead partner's rows. Cost: 25% of every PERM grant unreachable, vproc 3 chronically full carrying cluster 1's fallback alone, and **zero redundancy for that cluster**. Recovered mid-run — `BOOT` → `REBUILD AMP 2 ALL TABLES ALL DATA` → `tpareset`, ~20 min, 52-second outage, zero data loss; the procedure came from the `rebuild` binary's own help strings after two wrong syntax guesses. **Also fixed:** two primary indexes keyed on CONSTANT columns (`V1001='1'` on all 1.24M Administrative rows, `BH001='BH'` on all 21,908) — Remi's optimisation pass had corrected the four big tables and skipped these two because they lack ORI/INCNUM; the right keys were already declared in `entity_metadata`, and `ALTER … MODIFY PRIMARY INDEX` preserved the `_NoPII` views a drop/recreate would have broken. **Observability was fiction**: `04-observability/03-load-metadata.sql` writes literals — `ROWCOUNT_RECONCILIATION` was the constant `1.0000` while the product claimed 21,908 rows for a table holding 2,190 — so `step_validate` gained a `rowcount_reconciliation` check (ERROR, not CRITICAL: the RECORD is wrong, not the rows) and `refresh_observability()` now measures, reconciling **source-to-Domain** since staging is emptied as the load proceeds. **Result:** 6/6 tables exact, skew 1.004–1.020 across four AMPs, all six reconciling 1.0000, gate **TRUSTED 8/8**. **Recorded, not hidden:** three wrong predictions (ramp-up rates read as trends, "comfortable headroom" from a per-AMP limit that was not the constraint, a grant increase that made things worse by reserving spool space), and `pkill -f` killing my own monitors three times. **Backups taken before the recovery**: all 166 deployed objects' DDL + 8 access-layer roles committed to the fork (`deployed-ddl/`), and 3,520 rows of non-reproducible product metadata exported. Change_Log now carries 9 entries across v1.0.0/v2.0.0/v2.1.0 — the entire v1→v2 uplift had never been recorded there. **Query logging was the other half of the space problem**: DBQL logged `EXPLAIN + OBJECTS + SQL + STEPINFO + XMLPLAN + STATSUSAGE` for ALL users with **nothing purging it**, reaching 14.12 GB (XMLPLAN alone 8.24 GB) against a tightest AMP holding 1.68 GB — purging it returned 4.74 GB and was what let the load continue. Fixed at both ends: re-enabled without the two options that were 62% of the volume, and bounded by a weekly 90-day purge. Those maintenance scripts were created directly on the database host — the same state `base_teradataQuery` was in for six months — so they are version-controlled at **`deploy/teradata/`** (mirroring `deploy/mcp/`), pulled from the deployed files so what is committed is what runs; the BTEQ credential file is deliberately excluded. Files: `agent_packs/policing-data-products/scripts/{load_nibrs,uplift_v2}.py`, `agent_packs/policing-data-products/docs/V2-MIGRATION.md`, `deploy/teradata/*`.

- **Aug 2026**: **White-label branding layer — one server, N DNS names, N product identities; default deployment byte-identical (branch `feature/brand-layer`)**. The platform can now present itself as an application-specific product (first brand: **Teradata Evidentia**, the policing-pack skin at `teradata-evidentia.uderia.com`) with zero forks. **ONE resolver** `core/branding.py` (the `get_app_version()` pattern): a frozen `Brand` dataclass whose **defaults ARE the pre-branding template literals character-for-character** (the no-regression contract, byte-pinned in CI); brands are DATA (`static/branding/<key>/brand.json` + assets, welcome partial at `templates/branding/<key>/welcome.html`) — adding a brand touches no Python and no existing template; resolution per request `UDERIA_BRAND` env pin > Host-header match > default, fail-open everywhere, registry cached at startup. **ONE context processor** in `main.py` hands `brand` to every template — no per-route kwargs. Hand-tuned default markup (inline nav/welcome logo SVGs with `mix-blend-mode`, Tailwind-arbitrary-class gradients, the GitHub star button + Uderia-only links) stays via `{% if brand.is_default %}` — branded mode uses asset files + inline accent styles; on a branded host the LLM Model Guide link keeps its target but drops the "Uderia" prefix and the © reads the brand's (Evidentia: **© 2026 Teradata**). **Branding ≠ tenancy** (documented): host branding is for demos; a real customer gets a dedicated instance with the env pin. **Never brand-resolved:** `uderia:` event namespace, `uderia-*` connector ids, RDF vocab, salts. **Gate:** `test/test_branding.py` (**125** — default byte-pins, resolution truth table incl. fail-open + the code-owned-default refusal, window.BRAND escaping, both email builders through a fake provider, and **the real templates rendered both ways via jinja2**); no-regression **proven by rendering `main`'s templates vs the branch's under the default brand** — the only content deltas are the declared additives (window.BRAND script; auth-page favicons). Live-verified on one running server: default host all-Uderia, `Host: teradata-evidentia.uderia.com` all-Evidentia (title, wordmark, kicker, hero, © Teradata, welcome partial, branded favicon), all 5 brand assets 200, version-pins gate 42 green. **Open:** deep-JS literal sweep via `window.BRAND` (batched — pin cascade), Evidentia `attribution` decision, marketing-final welcome copy, Teradata legal clearance. - **Aug 2026**: **Every turn froze the whole server for ~27 s after the answer — the recommender's follow-up retrieval ran unscoped, synchronously, on the event loop.** Operator report (prod session `5103e93a`, a @POLICE coordinator with a session primer): *"the assurance circle turns for ages until it delivers a result … and a new session afterwards takes ages to respond."* The prod log showed the shape on **every** turn since Aug 22: `✅ execution completed` → `ChromaDBBackend initialized (persist=in-memory)` → **23–30 s of silence** → `rag_retriever: No candidate cases found across all collections`. Measured inside the container: the recommender's Tier B call (`retrieve_examples`, awaited in `run_agent_execution` **before** the online-eval dispatch that emits `turn_score_complete`) took **0.59 s with an access context and 26.7 s without one** — and it was ALWAYS running without one: `recommender.py` imported `RAGAccessContext` from `agent.rag_retriever`, where it does not exist (it lives in `agent/rag_access_context.py`), and the `ImportError` was swallowed by a bare `except → rag_context = None`. `None` means *no scope*, so `retrieve_examples` scanned **all 283 loaded planner collections** — 259 of them the one-per-user "Default Collection" every login provisions for the bootstrap MCP server — calling `collection.query(query_texts=…)`, which **re-embeds the same query inside every call** (~0.1 s each on CPU), **synchronously on the event loop**. Three consequences from one root: the dial spun until the turn's tail finished (the primer turn was simply the FIRST turn of every such session, so it was where the operator saw it); every other request — a fresh session, a poll, a login — queued behind the frozen loop; and **every user's private champion cases were candidates for another user's follow-up chips** (a privacy defect the scan made real; the test stub had planted `RAGAccessContext` onto the fake `rag_retriever` module, faithful to the wrong import, so it could never catch it). **Fix, at the root and at the seam:** (1) the recommender imports the context from its real module, **fails closed** when it cannot build one (no context ⇒ no follow-ups, never an unscoped scan), and bounds the call with `APP_CONFIG.RECOMMENDER_TIER_B_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (5 s) — the seam is awaited in the turn path; (2) `RAGRetriever.retrieve_examples` embeds the query **once per embedding model** and passes `query_embeddings` (ranking + distances proven byte-identical to `query_texts` on real Chroma), with the encode and every `collection.query` moved off the loop via `asyncio.to_thread` (encoder failure degrades to per-collection `query_texts`, never to silence) — so the all-collections path is now ~0.7 s instead of 27 s, and even that can no longer stall the server. The primer turn itself was never the defect (its turn IS persisted — `workflow_history` lives under `last_turn_data`). **Recorded, not changed:** the 259 per-user empty planner collections are by design (per-user isolation, created at login in `auth_routes.py`) — the fix makes retrieval cost independent of their number rather than pruning them. **Gates:** new `test/test_rag_retrieve_embed_once.py` (14 — embed-once · off-loop-thread asserted · scoped · fallback · AST: no sync `collection.query` in the function) + `test_recommender.py::test_tier_b_access_scope` (context always passed with the requesting user · fail closed with the retriever never called · bounded); both added to `trust_battery.sh` (the recommender suite had sat outside it). **Four mutations fail by name** (wrong import module · swallowed context · per-collection `query_texts` · sync query on the loop). Regression-clean: rag_learning_loop 20 · champion_authority 27 · corpus_quarantine 13 · signed_knowledge 19 · fusion_hardening_aug 74. **Server restart** (backend). Files: `agent/recommender.py`, `agent/rag_retriever.py`, `core/config.py`, `test/{test_recommender,test_rag_retrieve_embed_once}.py`, `test/trust_battery.sh`, `docs/Architecture/NEXT_STEP_RECOMMENDER_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

- **Aug 2026**: **Component enablement — one rule, three enforcement points (the "Pin to Dashboard on a dashboard-disabled agent" report)**. An operator on production found `@POLICE` (Coordinate, Dashboard switched off) still offered **Pin to Dashboard**. The assessment (`docs/assessments/COMPONENT_ENABLEMENT_ASSESSMENT_2026-08.md`) found the pin button was the smallest of it: *"is component X enabled for profile P"* had **four independent re-derivations** that disagreed — **A** `recommender._component_enabled_for_profile` (chips, companion skills), **B** `GET /v1/profiles/<id>/components` → `profile_enabled` (every panel), **C** `ComponentManager.get_active_components` (**what actually runs**), **D** the editor/component-manager/KG-panel toggles. **C was blind to admin governance** (`components/manager.py` imported `components/settings.py` nowhere) and defaulted an absent entry to `True`; **D read a SECOND manifest key** (`profile_defaults.default_enabled`) that contradicted the first (`enabled_for`) for six of nine components. Proven live: an admin's global disable left the tool bound to the model (the agent kept the capability and lost its companion skill — worse than either state), and **`TDA_Memory` was bound on every shipped bootstrap profile** while every UI reported memory off (their `componentConfig` predates the key, and absent meant `True`) — writes landing in a write-only limbo since recall was correctly gated by A. **Fix — ONE rule** (`components/enablement.py`, pure `decide()` + batch wrappers that read each lookup once): global admin gate + per-user override → explicit `componentConfig` → manifest `enabled_for`. All four sites delegate; the second manifest key is retired from all nine manifests. **Three enforcement points** replace advertise-time-only gating: the runtime surface (`get_active_components`, now `user_uuid`-aware and threaded through every consumer), the **effect site** (`enforce_component_call` at both chokepoints — `mcp_adapter.adapter` for Optimize and `_run_component` for ReAct — so a replayed champion plan, pack-authored plan, `@TAG` override or hallucinated call can no longer execute a disabled component; recovery-shaped refusal, fails open on internal error), and the **affordance** (`static/js/handlers/componentGate.js` — reads the server's resolved `profile_enabled`, never re-derives, **fails closed**, primed on profile switch and invalidated on save; both leaking pin paths now gated, and `ui.js`'s origin walk was extracted to `_deriveTableOrigin` so the profile is derived once rather than twice). REST creation is gated on `is_component_available` (dashboard create + add_tile, flow create + execute, canvas create, memory POST, scheduler create — replacing its hand-rolled global-only copy); **reads, updates and deletes of existing instances stay open** so a user can always inspect and erase their own data, and memory reads/erase are explicitly ungated (data-subject rights outrank a feature flag). **Policy change (operator decision):** memory is now **enabled by default for every profile type** — an explicit `componentConfig.memory.enabled:false` still wins. **Two things implementation changed about the plan, both recorded:** per-user `component_profile_defaults` was **rejected** as a runtime resolution step (it is a *creation* default; folding it in would make a saved profile's behaviour drift with a later setting and put a bootstrapping — i.e. writing — config read on the per-turn path, which raised a live FK violation), and `conflicts_with` hard enforcement is **open** (chart and dashboard declare each other exclusive yet are both default-on for all four types, so the default state violates the declaration and a warning fired on every turn — removed rather than shipped as a false alarm). **A regression this caused, caught by the gate not by review:** `skill_library` declared `enabled_for: []` *because* absent-entry-True made it irrelevant — its real gate is the `is_profile_relevant` hook — so collapsing the rule silenced it permanently; `enabled_for` now means **eligible** (relevance narrows further) and both halves are pinned. **Gates:** `test/test_component_enablement.py` (75) + `test/test_component_gate.mjs` (16, executes the shipped module under a stubbed fetch — a substring rule had let a fail-OPEN mutation escape); **10 mutations, all caught**. Version pins bumped to a fixed point across the importer cascade (41 → 53 assertions). **The regression baseline also surfaced 19 suites already red at HEAD — every one root-caused (assessment §13): 14 fixed (12 were stale pins on deliberate, documented changes — most went red the DAY the change shipped and stayed red because they sat outside the battery; 3 orphaned assurance suites are now IN `trust_battery.sh`), 2 March relics retired with reasons, 3 are environment-dependent by design. Two real product defects fell out: `SurfaceViolationScorer` violated the substrate's one-grader-per-property contract (fixed in the scorer, reason recorded), and the corpus second-chance support test was punctuation-brittle — `ae8473be`'s correct quote-extraction fix revealed the published FP=0.0 had rested on a truncated mis-extraction; ONE shared `corpus.span_supported()` (strips terminal sentence punctuation, conservative) now serves the runtime AND the benchmark harness, restoring the published numbers for the right reason.** **Server restart** (backend + `index.html`); JS browser-reload. Files: `components/enablement.py`, `components/manager.py`, `agent/recommender.py`, `api/{rest_routes,dashboard_routes,flow_routes,canvas_routes}.py`, `mcp_adapter/adapter.py`, `components/builtin/*/manifest.json`, `components/builtin/memory/adapter.py`, `static/js/handlers/{componentGate,dashboardHandler,configurationHandler,knowledgeGraphPanelHandler}.js`, `static/js/{ui,main}.js`, `templates/index.html`.

- **Aug 2026**: **A forked pack's owner could never clear `deployment_unattested` — the attest authority is ownership, not signer tier**. Operator, after forking the policing pack on prod as a non-admin OAuth user, read the Trust Circle's SIGNED station: *"not attested here — the portable half is vouched for; the local half is not"*. The state itself was correct (the two-hash envelope working as designed: `portability.reinstate` re-applied the publisher's signature byte-identically, while the deployment half — resolved LLM, reachable MCP tool/prompt catalog, connector opt-ins — deliberately never travels). **The defect was that they could not act on it:** the footnote in the panel was `trustBadge.js`'s 403 string, i.e. the button had already been pressed and refused. `attest-deployment` routed through `_authorize_signer` (the **ontology governance** approver-tier policy — a category error; this act has nothing to do with the ontology lifecycle, it just borrowed the nearest gate), while the badge popover hid the button entirely behind `canSign`. **Three facts made the tier gate wrong rather than merely strict**, and each is now pinned so it is not reinstated: (1) **it could never enable a reviewer** — the handler resolves the profile via `get_profile(profile_id, user.id)` and profiles live per-user in `user_preferences`, so an approver-tier user reaches only their OWN profiles; an admin could not attest a subscriber's fork on their behalf, so the gate could only lock the owner out (the codebase's own TC-30 row had already noted `attest-deployment` resolves under `user.id`); (2) **it disabled the protection it appeared to provide** — the attestation's value is drift detection (once a baseline exists, a model swap, a server quietly gaining a write tool, or a connector opt-in flips 🟠 with `describe_drift` naming it), so with nobody able to take the baseline the detector never armed: the gate did not stop a user pointing a fork at an uncensored local model, it guaranteed nobody would notice; (3) **separation of duties is incoherent here** — `_authorize_signer` refuses ALL self-signing while `require_approval` is on, and attesting is always self, so that policy made deployment attestation impossible platform-wide for **every** tier including admin. **The fix follows the provenance-vs-policy split every trust system makes** (a build system signs the artefact; the deploying org attests its own admission policy): the **portable** half stays approver-tier gated (a third party can vouch that this is the artefact that was validated), the **deployment** half becomes **ownership**-authorized (*"this model, this tool catalog, these connector opt-ins are what I intend here"* is a statement about a surface only its owner controls). New `_authorize_deployment_attester()` makes the ownership check **explicit** rather than an incidental side effect of the handler's lookup — the TC-30 lesson is that an unstated invariant is one a refactor removes — and fails **deny** (unreadable config or unknown profile → 404; a non-owner gets **404, never 403**, which would confirm another user's profile id exists). Frontend: the badge popover's attest button is no longer gated on `canSign` (the dialog only ever opens for the caller's own profiles); sign-off in the same dialog stays tier-gated; the refusal copy says the true thing (ownership) instead of "admin-only", preferring the server's own reason so a policy change never needs a copy edit on the other side. **Deliberately NOT a config flag:** an escalation toggle was designed and rejected — its ON state has no valid workflow (since only the owner can resolve their profile, "require approver tier" means *nobody* can attest a non-admin's agent), so it would ship a supported configuration that re-creates the bug. **Gate:** new `test/test_deployment_attest_authority.py` (**22 assertions**, CI-pure) — helper truth table incl. the non-owner-gets-404 rule and fail-deny, AST-level wiring (a comment naming a helper cannot satisfy the rule), the portable half still tier-gated, and the two `_authorize_signer` refusals that prove the old gate could not have worked; **4 mutations fail by name** (reinstate the tier gate · re-gate the button on `canSign` · restore the admin-only copy · un-scope the ownership lookup). **One escape caught in my own gate:** route handlers are `async def` → `ast.AsyncFunctionDef`, so matching only `FunctionDef` made every call-set empty and three assertions passed **vacuously** — caught by the paired "attest exists" assertion, which is why a rule asserted over a possibly-empty set is not a rule. **No regression:** battery run before AND after, diffed per suite — 53 → 55 suites, **zero coverage drops, zero failures**, only `test_version_pins` 41→42 (the bumped pin); `test_trust_deployment` (114) was **not in the battery** and is now added alongside the new suite (a gate the battery does not run is a gate nobody runs). **Docs — a sweep, not a spot-fix** (every surface that asserts the authority or the state): membrane arch §3b gains an **Authority** column + the three-reason record; the manual's sign-vs-attest table + walkthrough step corrected (it said "admin only"); `restAPI.md` row corrected (it said "signer (admin)"); a one-source row in the status contract; **`trust_routes.py`'s own module header** (it declared the whole seam "admin-gated, with separation of duties" and omitted `attest-deployment` from its endpoint list entirely); a pointer in `deployment.py`'s canonical docstring; a FAQ §9 row (the FAQ had **no** coverage of `deployment_unattested`); **the README claimed "Three verifiable states" and omitted ◒ — the very state a fork lands in** — now four, with the fork case named; - **Aug 2026**: **Knowledge Graph ingestion & retrieval — deep assessment** (`docs/assessments/KG_INGESTION_ASSESSMENT_2026-08.md`). Measured offline on the two large graphs (policing/ANDP 3,183 nodes; airlines/industry-model 15,797), class-independent. **Headline:** the ANDP walker records entity→attribute as `has_property` while the renderer/extractor/`_table_columns_map` read only `contains` (and conformance demands the opposite), so on ANDP graphs the compact `TABLE SCHEMAS` never renders, column expansion fills the 500-node cap with two tables' columns, and every turn injects **~74K tokens ≈ $0.019 on Gemini** (15–20× a whole @OPGGT turn); on 128K/32K models the line-trim drops relationships/entities/the target column.
