- **Aug 2026**: **Fusion Optimizer hardening — driven and validated through `@OPGGT` (Optimize on the Entry-Frontier model, one MCP tool, KG-enabled)**. Method: 106 persisted `@OPGGT` turns as ground truth + a fixed 8-query benchmark (`test/performance/fusion_bench.py`, fresh session per query, reads the persisted turn) run before/after. **Stability:** `CorrectionHandler` returned after the FIRST `can_handle()` match, and `TeradataLimitStrategy` claims any "Syntax error" — so on every non-`LIMIT` syntax error it declined and **aborted all correction** (the LLM fallback was unreachable; live: "technical error" answers). Now a `(None, [])` decline CONTINUES the chain. The `column_not_found` regex never matched Teradata's 3810/5628 messages (every column error paid a Generic LLM round) → matched, and resolved **deterministically against the KG schema** first (same-table case/underscore/fuzzy match → mechanical rewrite, 0 LLM; else the real columns + JOINABLE keys are handed to the LLM as facts instead of "describe the table", which a 1-tool profile cannot). Correction output is validated against the catalog (`{"prompt_name": "base_readQuery"}` — a TOOL — was run as a sub-prompt and failed). A bare `result_of_phase_N` EMBEDDED in a SQL string reached the database verbatim → substituted when the phase is a scalar; SQL date binds (`:start_date`…) that `base_readQuery` can never take are wired from the turn's `TDA_DateRange`/`TDA_CurrentDate`; raw-SQL phases now DEPEND on those temporal phases (they were racing ahead in a parallel group). **Quality (the headline):** for "top 5 products by revenue" the KG enrichment seeded only `Products` — `_match_score` rewarded prefix matches, so the `TotalRevenue` metric scored 0 for "revenue" — the model invented `Price * StockQuantity`, the error-free turn was SEEDED as a champion, and the champion then taught the wrong arithmetic on every later revenue question. Fixed at three layers: identifier-token scoring + reserved seed slots for matched metrics (and a rescue that never evicts a better-ranked reserved row — the first version did exactly that), metric lines render the `formula:` as authoritative (`compile_metric` advertised only when compilable; the compiler's refusal now carries the formula), **bridge tables** discovered through shared column names (`SaleDetails —SaleID— Sales —CustomerID— Customers`; this KG has no FK edges) and the JOINABLE COLUMNS block un-broken (it compared full `Table.Column` names — dead on every layered graph); and `champion_contradicts_metric` (0-token, fail-open) — a champion whose SQL contradicts an ontology metric the question names is not offered. Live: both revenue queries now implement `SUM(SaleDetails.UnitPrice * SaleDetails.Quantity)` with the correct joins (a DIFFERENT top-5 list — the old one was wrong). **Cost:** the strategic planning call carried the master system prompt's full capability catalog on top of the planning prompt's own (`strip_capabilities=True`, planning −10%); Gemini `cached_content_token_count` read + discounted (`CACHED_INPUT_PRICE_FACTOR=0.25`; **no cache hits were observed on gemini-3.1-flash-lite in any run** — instrumented, not a claimed saving); `mcp_system_name` sqlite read cached (was on EVERY LLM call + the planner); the per-turn 2000-char `[DEBUG]` INFO log removed. **Honesty:** new `fabricated_after_failure` kind — a quantitative claim when every data query failed and the answer does not disclose it ("30 days of sales activity recorded" from zero rows). **Bench (8 queries, before → final):** input tokens 91,265 → 83,637 (−8.4%), cost −7.0%, tool errors 1 → 0, self-corrections 0, 8/8 success, latency flat. Gate: `test/test_fusion_hardening_aug.py` (**74**, in the battery); regression-clean across 20 suites (honesty fixture "All good, 40 rows." updated — a figure after total failure is now correctly acted on). The `fusion-hardening` skill was materially outdated (12 vs 13 passes, wrong strategy order, stale anchors) and is re-synced (v1.9.0). Files: `agent/{phase_executor,executor,planner,rag_retriever}.py`, `agent/honesty/gate.py`, `llm/handler.py`, `core/config.py`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/{handler,metric_api}.py`, `test/{test_fusion_hardening_aug.py,test_honesty_gate.py,trust_battery.sh}`, `test/performance/fusion_bench.py`, `.claude/skills/fusion-hardening/SKILL.md`.

- **Aug 2026**: **Consumption time windows made self-healing — "Tokens Used Today" showed months of accumulation, and every reset path had a hole**. Operator, with a screenshot of Administration → Users → User Consumption: *"the tokens used today column is showing wrong content"* — 10.7M/14.2M "today", then: *"i would prefer a sum tokens consumed column instead anyhow."* **Three independent defects, one root shape** (a reset that only fires if something else happens to run): (1) the lazy daily/hourly reset lived ONLY in `check_rate_limits`, which never runs when rate limiting is disabled — the default — so `tokens_today` accumulated forever on most installs; (2) the platform daily maintenance job (`maintenance/consumption_periodic_jobs.py`) reset `requests_today` but **silently omitted the `*_tokens_today` counters** (an inline copy predating the columns — the hand-maintained-duplicate defect class again), so even a 24/7 production server accumulated; (3) APScheduler's jobstore is **in-memory**, so a midnight firing missed while the server was down is invisible after restart (`misfire_grace_time=60` never helps across restarts) — the local dev DB sat with `day_reset_at` 8 days stale and `current_period` at **2026-05**, monthly quota rollover included. **Fix — ONE set of reset semantics, three delivery paths:** `ConsumptionManager.apply_hourly_reset` / `apply_daily_reset` / `_rollover` are the single definition; a **lazy healer** (`heal_time_windows`, called from `get_or_create_consumption`) brings every record current on ANY consumption access (rate check, quota check, turn recording, summary reads — all consumers route through that chokepoint), so quotas now enforce against the right period even with no scheduler at all; the maintenance jobs call the same `apply_*` helpers (inline copies deleted, gate-asserted); and a **startup catch-up sweep** in `task_scheduler.start_scheduler` runs `run_all_jobs()` once (timestamp-guarded → no-op when current) to cover idle users and missed boundaries. Platform jobs get `misfire_grace_time=3600` (idempotent + guarded, so a late catch-up is always correct); in-process maintenance runs now receive a **managed `get_db_session()` session** instead of building a private engine that bypassed `sqlite_util`'s process-wide lock (SQLITE_CONCURRENCY rule; the private-engine path remains for standalone CLI use). One trap caught by the gate: tz-normalizing naive datetimes must not count as "changed" — SQLite returns naive datetimes on every load, so writing tzinfo back would have made every read a write, forever. **The admin column, per the operator's preference:** "Tokens Used Today" → **"Tokens Consumed"** (all-time), computed as `SUM(consumption_periods_archive) + current period` — the rollover invariant makes this exact and **cleanup-proof** (`cleanup_old_turns` prunes the turn ledger to 90 days at each rollover, so the first-draft `SUM(consumption_turns)` would have silently shrunk the moment healing enabled rollovers — proven live: 230 turns pruned, column unchanged at 26,505,197). Also fixed: the column's `data-sort="tokens_used_today"` matched **no case** in the sort switch (sorting was a silent no-op; now wired to `total`, and the equally dead `usage_percentage` key got a real case), "Daily Limit" renamed **"Monthly Limit"** (it always displayed `input_tokens_per_month`), and the KPI tiles' scope labels read "All time" instead of a month. **Honest consequence, stated:** with rollovers healing, the 90-day turn-ledger retention is now actually enforced — surfaces that COUNT from `consumption_turns` (the v1.19 "Total Sessions" figure, model-distribution panels) become 90-day windows on long-broken instances; the retention span is the operator's call. **Gate:** `test/test_consumption_healing.py` (**52** — daily heal resets tokens · fresh-window guard · rollover archives-then-resets + idempotent · the all-time invariant across rollover AND ledger pruning · `record_turn` lands in the healed window · naive datetimes tolerated · rate limits still enforce · both maintenance jobs through the real `ConsumptionPeriodicJobs(session=)` · one-source structural checks). Live-verified end to end on the genuinely-broken dev DB: startup sweep ran `daily_reset, monthly_rollover` for 2 users, periods 2026-05 → 2026-08, archive rows carry the exact finished totals, endpoint `lifetime_total_tokens` byte-identical across the rollover. Server restart (backend + `index.html`); `adminManager.js 3.9 → 4.0`. Files: `auth/consumption_manager.py`, `maintenance/consumption_periodic_jobs.py`, `core/task_scheduler.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `static/js/adminManager.js`, `templates/index.html`, `docs/RestAPI/restAPI.md`, `test/test_consumption_healing.py`.

- **Aug 2026**: **BOUNDED reported "acting as the user" on every autonomous turn — and the gate battery had a false-green**. Operator, reading a live genie coordinator's Trust Circle (session 3cba1f54): *"why are 4 of the 8 trust segments deactivated?"* Running the real registry over the persisted turn confirmed the four (GROUNDED · BOUNDED · TRUSTED · REVIEWED) — a station is dashed only when EVERY mechanism reads `na` (`ATTN_RANK` na:0 < pass:1) — and three are honest structural absences for a coordinator (no ontology bound — it lives on the experts; `provisional`, 6 turns of 10; no gate armed with retention). **The fourth was a defect.** `_read_authority` decided autonomy from `turn["origin"]`, a key `execution_service` puts on the returned payload and on the user MESSAGE but which **no engine writes onto the turn** — while an authoritative, execution-time-sealed `authority` stamp was ALREADY being built and thrown away on the payload. Blast radius: **0 of 1540 production turns carried the stamp, 2 carried `origin`**, so every genie / flow / scheduler turn read *"interactive turn — acting as the user"*. **Fix — one builder, one seam each:** `agent_authority.build_authority_stamp()` is THE shape (both copies built from it, so they cannot drift); a `set/get/reset_turn_authority` contextvar is sealed beside the existing principal **before** the engine runs (nothing in the stamp depends on the outcome) and released in the `finally`; `session_manager.update_last_turn_data` — THE chokepoint every engine's turn lands in — stamps it with `setdefault`, so all five engines inherit with no signature plumbing; `_read_authority` reads the sealed stamp (`applied` distinguishes *the boundary held* from *never in force*), keeping `origin` as an any-era fallback. Unset contextvar ⇒ no stamp ⇒ **byte-identical baseline**. Historical turns are NOT re-resolved (the same retroactive-falsification trap the SIGNED stamp was sealed to avoid). **One trap caught mid-fix:** the first version deserialized the stamp with `parse_scope`, which reads `dataSurface` while `to_dict()` emits `data_surface` — it would have **silently dropped the data surface**, the constraint that most narrows an agent, and re-resolved `OBDA_ENABLED` against today's switch; replaced with a true inverse `scope_from_stamp()` living beside `to_dict()`. Live-verified on the real turn: BOUNDED `na → pass`, that ring 4 → 5 of 8. **The battery it was verified against was itself broken.** `run_py` derived a suite's verdict from the printed COUNT and **discarded the process exit code** — proven live, a suite printing `100 passed, 0 failed` then exiting 1 was reported **GREEN**; `run_js` honoured the exit code but never required a count (`${line:-ok}`), so a JS suite that stopped printing its total read "ok" and its coverage guarantee evaporated. Same battery, opposite holes, one root cause (one fact doing two jobs). **The contract now encoded:** a suite reports two INDEPENDENT facts — **verdict** (the exit code: unforgeable by a print, survives crashes/import errors) and **coverage** (the printed count: catches silent coverage loss) — both read, neither substituting for the other, and **disagreement is itself a finding** (Rule 3.0c applied to the gate), with named verdicts `CRASHED AFTER PASSING` / `BROKEN EXIT DISCIPLINE` / `NO COUNT`. Both runners route through ONE pure `classify_suite`. **The two suites that had been red for this reason:** `test_citation_fidelity` was a FALSE red (119 checks passing, printed `(N checks)` instead of the canonical count) → one machine-readable format; `test_product_agent_face` took the first `LIKE '%Fitness%'` KG, which on this box is pinned to a **dead Neo4j Aura host** → DNS traceback — now picks a locally-backed target resolved **without instantiating** the backend (building a remote one is what dials the network) via a new `kgstore.factory.resolve_backend_choice` extracted as the selection half of `get_backend_for_profile`, so a reader can never disagree with the factory. Two further defects inside that suite: it authored its fixture to an explicit `kg_id` while the handler resolved its OWN store (they coincided only by luck), and two assertions still granted a LIVE product (`support_load`) — the piggybacking fragility its own header says it fixed for measure names. **Gates:** `test_agent_authority` 64 → **101** (5 mutations; one ESCAPED — the round-trip was asserted on the inverse but the READING only asserted `read-only`, which both shapes recover, so the surface-only case is now driven through `_read_authority`); new `test_trust_battery_contract` **34** (the truth table + the REAL runners end-to-end against throwaway suites; 8 mutations). **Three escapes closed in my own gates, not accepted:** an assertion grepped a COMMENT about the retired code (the "prose about the code is not the code" trap already recorded in `test_quality_card_partition`); `"sys.exit" in text` was satisfied by `sys.exit(0)` — a suite that can never report failure; and driving only the classifier let a runner that computes the right verdict and reports a CONSTANT slip past. **Two bugs of my own, found by reading output rather than trusting green:** `[^\n]` in POSIX ERE means "not backslash, not the letter **n**", truncating every JS summary at its first `n` (`ALL PASS — 1829 assertio`), and the sourced script `cd`'d on `$0` (= `bash` when sourced), walking out of the repo — the meta-test now reads the shipped patterns FROM the script rather than keeping the copy that had already drifted. Battery **GREEN**. Files: `core/agent_authority.py`, `agent/execution_service.py`, `core/session_manager.py`, `agent/assurance_points.py`, `kgstore/factory.py`, `test/{trust_battery.sh,test_trust_battery_contract.py,test_agent_authority.py,test_citation_fidelity.py,test_product_agent_face.py}`.

- **Aug 2026 (v1.23)**: **Release** — the progressive-disclosure release: 21 commits since v1.22. The headline is **progressive disclosure skills** — a skill may now be a lean always-injected root plus a governed on-demand library the agent opens section-by-section mid-turn (`TDA_SkillLibrary`), built under a gates-first zero-regression contract whose baseline-freeze suite was committed green against unmodified code *before* any feature work. With it: the **anchor grant** made visible and operable through one shared library-access dialog reachable from both the profile editor and the Skill Library component; **pack provenance** on skills (recorded at install, tagged in the UX, kept-and-marked-orphaned on uninstall); the skill editor no longer deleting a skill's library on save (carry-forward, the hand-maintained-key-list defect class again); and **PROP-004 Phase 1 + Phase 3** — the ANDP pack re-sourced to the open-source ANDP and its Option-A role mirror, where `@ANDPA-DESIGN`'s grant is *computed* as every non-teradata anchor so the design/implementation boundary is structural rather than requested. Alongside: **profile activation could never succeed** (`/v1/profiles/<id>/activate` imported a module that does not exist, so the LLM check always errored) — fixed by reusing the one shared validator, and the activation list gained the **`GET` half it never had**, so adding one profile no longer requires knowing the whole list (a partial write had silently deactivated everything else). Docs gained the progressive-disclosure **control model** — who decides what is loaded (author: what exists · operator: the boundary · the model: which section now), the contrast with retrieval, and the honest weak point that nothing verifies a read happened — plus a **§4b authoring guide**, which did not exist. Also `mcp_custom_objects/` — `base_writeQuery` as a version-controlled custom MCP object loaded via `CONFIG_DIR`, so the teradata-mcp-server fork can stay a pure mirror of upstream. Version surfaces bumped together per [docs/RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md): `pyproject` 1.23.0 · compose `uderia-v1-23` + build-arg default `v1.23` · annotated tag `v1.23`.

- **Aug 2026**: **Progressive disclosure skills become visible, governable and documented — the follow-on wave (branch `feature/andp-refresh`)**. PROP-005 shipped the mechanism; this wave makes it *operable by a person*. Every item was an operator finding, and three were the same defect class the codebase keeps paying for — a hand-maintained key list where a carry-forward belongs. **(1) Invisible capability → tagged on both surfaces:** `list_skills()` now reports `progressive` + `library_sections`, rendered as a **Library** tag (skill list + resource panel) — a skill that behaves fundamentally differently at runtime looked identical to one that does not. **(2) Pack-installed skills were fire-and-forget:** an agent pack installed skills that the ledger never recorded, so uninstall could not reason about them at all. Now stamped `uderia.pack_origin` + recorded in `agent_pack_resources` (`resource_type='skill'`), and on uninstall **kept and marked orphaned** (operator's call — a skill may be assigned to profiles outside the pack, and deleting it would break them); both surfaces carry a pack tag and a muted *orphaned* tag, response carries `skills_orphaned`. **(3) The anchor grant was real but unreachable** — enforced fail-closed in the handler since day one, editable only by hand-writing JSON into a profile. Now **ONE dialog, two entry points** (`skillGrantDialog.js`): the profile editor's skill row and the Skill Library component's **Libraries** tab; the dialog owns editing, each caller owns only persistence via `onSave(grant)`, so they cannot drift. Built to the `openPackGovernDialog` bar — plain-language hero naming what is excluded, mode cards, tri-state group toggles over the library's own path structure (the real decision is "this half, not that half" — one click, not sixty), glob chips with live match counts, dirty-state Save. Three semantics are load-bearing and gate-asserted: **"All" saves NO key** (an exhaustive list freezes the grant and silently excludes sections a later update adds), **globs are stored verbatim, never expanded** (they grant forward; an anchor granted *by* a glob is marked un-untickable — it would silently do nothing), and a save before the async list renders **carries the STORED grant forward** ("an empty UI is not an empty choice", applied to governance data). **(4) The skill editor was DELETING the library on save** — it rebuilt the manifest from the fields it models, so `uderia.progressive`, `uderia.pack_origin`, `version`, `author` and `keywords` all vanished on any edit of a progressive skill's body; fixed by carrying forward every unmodelled key (the `core/profile_config_contract.py` lesson, fourth recurrence this session), plus an editor notice stating the split (root is editable, library is packaged and survives). **(5) The component detail's first tab was labelled "Chart Types" for every component** — a generic label inherited from the chart component, lying on six cards — and also dumped internals; retitled from content and curated. **(6) Param pills overflowed their card** (fixed-height single line + character budget). **(7) PROP-004 Phase 3 — the roles shape** (`build.py --shape roles`): 4 role agents over ONE 77-section `andp-corpus`, where the design/implementation boundary is **structural** — `@ANDPA-DESIGN`'s grant is *computed* as every non-teradata anchor, so it cannot drift; `verify_roles_build.py` (29) asserts the boundary **live** through the real handler over the real installed skill, both directions. **(8) Docs, the gap the mechanism exposed:** SKILL_ARCHITECTURE §4a gains **the control model** — *who decides what is loaded* (author: what exists + the procedure · operator: the grant, a **boundary not a selection** · the model: which section now), the contrast with RAG (the platform never selects; no scoring, no pre-fetch — verified by grep, not assumption), and the honest weak point (**nothing verifies a read happened**; skip-read is the metric that matters, and the deterministic remedy — a planner-inserted load phase — is deliberately not built); new **§4b authoring guide** (there was none anywhere — the format is the contract, `skills/package.py` is the one serializer, anchors are prompt surface and renaming one breaks operators' grants); `restAPI.md` **§3.21.3a** documents `GET /v1/skills/<id>/library-index` (undocumented; my first draft got its response shape wrong and was corrected against the code); welcome screen + README feature entries; and the component's own card description de-jargoned (it leaked an internal proposal ID and "structurally inert" to users) — closed as a **class**, not an instance: `test_component_manifests.py` **32 → 50** now refuses a proposal id / tier / issue key in any builtin manifest's `description` or `display_name` (both are rendered verbatim on the card), mutation-tested against the exact string that shipped. **Gate:** `test_progressive_skills.py` **92 → 203** (+§U surfacing · §K provenance · §G editor grant · §V card layout · §E skill editor · §D detail dialog · §W shared dialog), every semantic mutation-tested; two §G assertions were **re-pointed, not deleted**, when their semantics moved into the shared dialog. syntax widens, meaning never). the store's own natural experiment: the tickets question's champion taught `query_product` → later turns governed; the customers champion taught raw SQL → free-form every time); (2) the contract **never named its measures** (manifest stores LISTS, the renderer tested `isinstance(dict)` — the model guessed `count`/`CustomerID`/`TicketID` across four runs because it was never told `ticket_count` exists); - **Aug 2026**: **OBDA V7 — live probes: a product signature becomes empirically verified, and a lie in the manifest can no longer be signed (branch `feature/obda-phase-a`)**. Scope §5 V7, closing the soft spot the Phase-B acceptance leaned on (the manifest *declared* the joins the gate only verified structurally). **Three probe families, built deterministically from the manifest's own declarations** (`build_probe_plan`, pure — builds SQL, never runs it): every V6 battery query executed with limit 1 at the REAL target (TOP form on Teradata — syntax-valid where it will actually run); every declared N:1/1:1 spot-checked empirically — the one-side must be UNIQUE on the join's to-columns, via the composite-safe `GROUP BY … HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 → zero groups` form (a bare `COUNT(DISTINCT)` cannot check a composite key), a 1:1 additionally checking the from-side; - **Aug 2026**: **The "not recorded" ring on OPTIM turns — silence is absence (`na`), never an alarm (`unknown`); the two-kinds-of-silence rule retired against production evidence**. Operator, with a screenshot of session 06e4a8da: *"almost all segments of the trust ring show not recorded — why is this?"* — GROUNDED/GUARDED/BOUNDED all read "not recorded" while four of GROUNDED's own mechanisms sat green directly beneath. **Root cause:** several gate readers in `assurance_points.py` returned **`unknown`** ("should have recorded and did not") when the turn carried no stamp for them, and `unknown` (rank 3) outranks `pass` (rank 1) in the station's worst-of fold — so ONE absent reading buried a station full of passing mechanisms. On the operator's clean SQL turn the three **retrieval-hygiene** readers (corpus quarantine · retrieval firewall · sensitivity ceiling) all fired on the absent `retrieval_hygiene` stamp: an OPTIM turn that does SQL, not RAG, never writes that stamp. **The first fix was too narrow and the correction is the story:** the original design (test-pinned in TWO suites) split silence deliberately — no stamps at all = pre-tracing (`na`), SOME stamps but not this gate's = "a real gap" (`unknown`) — and that model is right ONLY for gates that stamp unconditionally. Verified per gate at the stamping seams: outbound/inbound/grounding stamp `{ran:False}` even when their master switch is off, but **preflight** stamps only when a SQL call reaches the chokepoint, **retrieval_hygiene** only when retrieval happens, and **honesty**'s RAG path returns no stamp when retrieval never ran. Then the production sweep settled it: real turns carry **every partial shape** — `['grounding']` alone, `['guardrail_inbound']` alone, `['honesty']` alone — benign engine-path variance, not silent skips, so `unknown`-on-absence was the false-alarm-teaches-operators-to-ignore-alarms failure the codebase's own `turn_refused_inbound` docstring warns about. **Fix (the whole class, not the symptom):** every absent-stamp branch reads **`na` with the reason named** ("did not run on this turn" / "no knowledge was retrieved on this turn") — `_guard_reading` (outbound+inbound), `_read_preflight`, `_read_grounding`, `_read_honesty`, and the three retrieval-hygiene readers; exactly the rule `_read_integrity` already documented for its own stamp. **The precise gap signal survives where it belongs:** a gate that RAN and ERRORED stamps `action:"error"` itself and still reads `unknown` from there (gate-asserted for outbound/grounding/honesty). Verified on the operator's real turn: GROUNDED/GUARDED/BOUNDED fold `pass` (were "not recorded"), SIGNED/TRUSTED honestly `na`. **Gates:** `test_assurance_points` §[4b] rewritten with the retirement HISTORY recorded in the test itself + a new §[N] (349 → **354**: all eight absent-stamp readers read `na`, a gates-off turn alarms NO station, errored still alarms, stamped-clean unchanged, the operator's scenario folds green); `test_assurance_tally` updated to the same model (30). **Two mutations, both fail by name** (reverting `_read_preflight` or `_guard_reading` to `unknown`-on-absent). Full battery green (18 Python + 6 JS gates + inventory + docs). Docs: `ASSURANCE_INSTRUMENTS_ARCHITECTURE.md` **V4** rewritten (absence is not an alarm; the retired rule and its refuting evidence recorded); the manual/FAQ errored-guard passages were already correct (they describe the preserved `action:"error"` path). - **Aug 2026**: **OBDA gets the master switch its two peers already had — and it defaults OFF, so the "Governed data" advisory can't permanently redden GROUNDED**. Operator, immediately after the re-home below: *"i always have the grounded segment orange (as data is currently almost always free formed and so governed data is false) with no chance to turn this measurement off — what is your recommendation?"* They were right on both counts. **The flaw:** `governed_data` is a non-gating **incentive** — a carrot rewarding the governed-metrics lane — but its free-formed reading renders `warn`, and a station's colour is worst-of its mechanisms, so on any deployment without a governed-metric layer (almost all of them: OBDA is Phase 0/1, validate/execute/provenance still deferred) it warns on **every** turn → GROUNDED permanently amber, burying that station's REAL signals (scope drift, unsupported claims, honesty). The exact *"a station that can never go green gets ignored"* failure the contract warns about. **The inconsistency that clinched it:** the two MATURE enforcement lanes — grounding (`GROUNDING_GATE_ENABLED`) and guardrails (`GUARDRAILS_ENABLED`) — both **default OFF** and are admin-gated in the Trust panel, while OBDA, the LEAST-finished lane, was the ONLY one always-on with no switch. The subscriber/forker's coordinator therefore pointed at profiles that do not exist in their account: no checkmarks in the editor, and `Genie profile has no child profiles configured` / `Child profile(s) not found` on activate. New `apply_to_manifest` is the source-side mirror of `apply_from_manifest` (the two `entry.update(project_to_manifest(...))` sites were themselves the source half of the same clobber). The sink's exclusion list is deleted — order-independence replaces it. **Existing `.agentpack` files need no rebuild:** their `child_tags` are correct and the stale publisher ids they carry are now ignored (gate-asserted). Trust is unaffected — hashing reads live profiles, never `manifest_json`, so no attestation flips. **Gate:** `test_profile_config_contract` 102 → **117**, driving both directions plus the stale-manifest case; 3 mutations fail by name (sink stops honouring the declared paths · write replaces instead of merges · `knowledgeConfig` loses its declaration). - **Aug 2026**: **The ANDP Access Layer — the agent's write boundary enforced by the DATABASE, and PII made unreachable**. Until now every consumer of the policing products connected as **DBC**, so the agent held full DBA rights over the instance and `deny_writes` in Agent Authority was the ONLY thing between a prompt injection and a write to a policing dataset — one layer of defence, in application code. New pure emitter `agent_packs/policing-data-products/scripts/access_layer.py` (+ `apply_access_layer.py`) builds the layer our `@ANDP-ACCESS` designer prescribes: **`{P}_ROLE_READ`** (SELECT everywhere) · **`{P}_ROLE_AGENT`** (SELECT everywhere, **INSERT on Memory + Observability ONLY** — deliberately not uniformly read-only, since the agent writes its own conversations, learned strategies, usage events and quality feedback back into the product, and nothing else) · **`{P}_ROLE_ADMIN`** · **`{P}_ROLE_READ_NOPII`** (SELECT on PII-free VIEWS only, **no grant on any base table**). Applied to **both** products: 8 roles, 48 PII-free views, `DD-ACCESS-001` in each product's Memory module. **Verified by LOGGING IN as each role, not by the DDL succeeding** — agent reads Domain/Semantic but cannot write either, can write Memory, cannot DROP; the restricted role reads its view but cannot reach the base table or `V4019` at all. **The restricted role is the deterministic PII control** the ten-question pass showed was needed: prompting proved unreliable (one run decoded values and said "a sample", the next returned raw codes with no remark), and a role cannot be talked out of it. Teradata has no column-level SELECT, so a view is the mechanism — and the dropped columns are read from the product's own `column_metadata.is_pii`, making the Access Layer a **projection of the semantic module** that follows the product as it evolves. **Every table gets a view, including PII-free ones, on purpose:** granting base tables directly where there is no PII *today* FAILS OPEN when a PII column is later added, while the invariant "this role holds no grant on any base table, ever" survives it. **Two constraints only the database could teach**, both found by applying: Teradata refuses `GRANT ALL` to a role (**5615** — ALL implies CREATE USER) and `WITH GRANT OPTION` to a role (**5613**), so ROLE_ADMIN holds an explicit product-scoped privilege list **established empirically** (24 offered, 24 accepted) and delegation moved to `GRANT <role> TO <user> WITH ADMIN OPTION` — *the gate had asserted "admin can delegate" via WITH GRANT OPTION, an **impossible expectation that passed happily**, because a pure test cannot know what the database will refuse*; and the two products implement the Memory module's `Design_Decision` **differently** (NIBRS: context/rationale/is_current/decision_version; CASE: context_description/decision_taken/is_active), so the record is **projected onto whatever columns the target actually has** — the same principle as the type rule, read what is deployed rather than what is declared. **Gate:** `test_access_layer` (**57**), six mutations fail by name (agent given INSERT on Domain/Semantic · agent losing its Memory write-back · restricted role granted a whole database · PII left in a view · case-sensitive PII matching · service account with no DEFAULT ROLE). Recorded about the gate itself: one assertion swept up `CREATE ROLE` and the decision prose as if they were grants — matching substrings rather than privilege, since only a GRANT can widen access; and a mutation initially "passed" because the replacement used single quotes where the source has double, so **it matched nothing and mutated nothing** — the third time that no-op has cost this repo a round. **Provenance corrected in our own docs:** DEPLOYMENT-STATE/PROGRESS said "the ANDP standard makes Access Layer DCL a mandatory deliverable", implying it came from the source product's spec — it does not (`CREATE ROLE`, `ROLE_AGENT` and `3523` appear NOWHERE in that repo, which declares no Access module); the requirement is **ours**, so this completes OUR standard on a colleague's product, and saying otherwise would misrepresent their work. **And it is now load-bearing** (same day): three MCP servers on the production host, one identity each — an admin endpoint (LAN only) · **8888** `FITNESS_MANAGER` · **8889** `ANDP_AGENT` (policing, since retired). The two public endpoints were **mutually exclusive by database enforcement**: each is denied the other's data, so the only endpoint that reaches everything is the one not exposed. Duplicated as separate compose projects reusing the same image, so the existing container was never touched and rollback is `docker compose down` (8888's original DBC env kept as a timestamped `.env.bak`). **Verified by a real turn through the policing endpoint**: 477,466, `WHERE V4019 = '0'`, on an account that cannot write Domain or Semantic and cannot see `fitness_db` — which closes the ten-question pass's **scope-drift** finding by construction (as DBC the agent had answered a "quarterly sales" question out of `fitness_db`; it now physically cannot). A redundant `fitness_agent` account was created and **dropped** when the operator pointed out `fitness_manager` already existed — checked rather than assumed, two accounts for one job removed. Recorded for later: a denied cross-scope query **killed the MCP session** (TaskGroup error) rather than returning a clean denial — the boundary held, but an agent hitting a permission error mid-turn may lose its session. Also: CASE_Source declares **zero** PII columns, so its `_NoPII` views are currently full copies — the product's own metadata gap (`column_metadata` covers 4 of ~120 columns), reported rather than papered over. Files: `agent_packs/policing-data-products/scripts/{access_layer,apply_access_layer}.py`, `agent_packs/policing-data-products/docs/{PROGRESS,DEPLOYMENT-STATE,NEXT-STEPS}.md`, `test/test_access_layer.py`.
- **Aug 2026**: **The decoded values were right and the comparison was wrong — 900,719 vs 477,466 — plus multi-product builds and three silent-bridge faults**. The NIBRS load landed (5.86M rows at 10%), and a **ten-question test pass** against the combined two-product graph found the flagship answer was WRONG, caused by our own feature. `V4019` declares `INTEGER` and is **deployed as `VARCHAR(2)`** — one of the **1,425 divergences in 1,508 columns** the constructor already counts. We surfaced the decoded values (`0=Female`) but never the deployed type, so the agent wrote `WHERE V4019 = 0`; the database CAST the column and **a blank casts to zero**: 900,719 returned where the truth is **477,466**, the other 423,253 being blank rows. Nothing errored and the number looked plausible. The type rule already had both facts — they were never joined at the point of use. **Fixed deterministically:** the walker stamps `deployed_type` on the LOGICAL attribute (it computed it for the mismatch count and threw it away) and the enrichment renders a character column's codes **quoted** with the trap stated (`values: '0'=Female …; deployed as VARCHAR(2) — compare as strings; a numeric comparison also matches blank rows`) — the agent copies the form it is shown, so the form it is shown is the safe one. **This is a NORMATIVE exception to [ONTOLOGY_ARCHITECTURE §2.4c](Architecture/ONTOLOGY_ARCHITECTURE.md)** (storage type belongs on the physical node, *never* the logical one) and is documented there with its boundary: it is unambiguous **only** because §2.4b guarantees exactly one deployed physical layer; with two PDMs it must be omitted or keyed by `infrastructure`, never "whichever was walked last". Re-asked: **477,466**; the cross-product count stopped counting `nibrs_crosswalk` (“2”) and now reads `investigative_action` (**1**) beside 1,235,155 incidents. **The bridges were silent, in three places, each invisible alone:** search is a SUBSTRING match so the gap is one-directional (`victim` is inside `Victims`, but `investigations` matches nothing named `Investigation`) → plural terms returned **zero** hits and the node never entered the pool; singularizing only the SEARCH put the bridge in the pool and then **scored it zero** (a fix to one half of a two-stage pipeline is not a fix); and scoring both forms still lost — the bridge scored **100** while a dozen interchangeable `Incident.BH04x` columns at **130** displaced it, so matched bridges now hold bounded **reserved seed slots**. Lexical similarity is the wrong judge for a node that carries a *warning* rather than a fact. **Multi-select data products** in the ANDP constructor: `products: [...]` (the single `product` string unchanged), one act → one graph, **per-product** outcomes with `status:"partial"` when some fail (a graph missing a product looks identical to a complete one until an agent is asked something it can no longer answer — the rule lives in `overall_status()` under a name a test can hold), and a **bridge re-resolution pass** so the result no longer depends on which product you listed first; it only ever UPGRADES a dangling bridge, because a declared link whose target does not exist IS the finding. The notice is consequence-based and silent when nothing is surprising — the dangerous case is the DEFAULT one: building into “a new knowledge graph” **deactivates** the graph the agent is currently grounded on (kept, not deleted), which is how this instance grew two 3,111-entity NIBRS graphs. Also: `Build into` listed raw UUIDs (read `g.name`/`g.entity_count`; the endpoint returns `kg_name`/`total_entities`) so every option looked identical on the one control where picking wrong matters. **Gates:** `test_kg_enrichment_relevance` 22 → **63**, `test_andp_multiselect` **23** (new), `test_kg_andp_modal` 18 → **39**, `test_nibrs_loader` **37** (new); ~20 mutations fail by name. **Two escaped first and both are recorded:** a “partial rounded up to success” mutation passed all 39 JS assertions because the assertion grepped the **JavaScript** for a rule living in **Python** — coverage of the wrong file reads exactly like coverage (hence `overall_status()` + a Python gate); and `t_the_estimate_is_not_optimistic` asserted `STAGING_FACTOR >= 1.0` on plausible reasoning about VARCHAR overhead — measurement refuted it (staging landed at **×0.30**, NIBRS being extremely sparse), so the assertion was pinning a GUESS and broke the moment evidence replaced it, the very failure mode it existed to prevent. Restated against the observation instead. **Recorded operational traps:** a stale `.pyc` survived a mutation restore because `1.6`→`0.6` changes neither mtime-second nor byte length, so a gate went red for code no longer on disk; and `pkill -f "python -m trusted_data_agent.main"` does **not** match `python3 -m …`, so several “restarts” were silent no-ops and one rebuild ran on 8-hour-old code — kill by PID and verify the pid changed. **Open, not papered over:** row-level output of PII-classified columns is **not reliably preventable by prompt** (one run decoded the values and called it “a sample”, the next returned raw codes with no remark — same question, same model), so it needs a deterministic control per the Component → LLM → Skill priority; and scope drift to an unrelated database is SEEN by the grounding gate (`out_of_scope_dbs`) but passes under `observe`. Files: `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/handler.py`, `agent/kg_constructors/{andp_semantic,andp_semantic_walker}.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `static/js/handlers/rag/kgAndpSemanticModal.js`, `skills/builtin/andp-consumer/andp-consumer.md`, `agent_packs/policing-data-products/{scripts/load_nibrs.py,docs/PROGRESS.md}`.
- **Aug 2026**: **"0 rows matched" is not "there are none" — the honesty gate learns the empty-relation case**. Operator, reading a live answer: *"can this be correct?"* The agent had answered *"There are 0 female victims recorded in the database"* from `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM NIBRS_Source_Domain.Victim WHERE V4019 = 0` — **literally true of the result, materially false about the world**, because the table has no rows loaded at all. The next turn asked about male victims and also got 0, which is the tell. **Why the existing gate stayed silent, correctly:** it fires when an answer asserts non-existence AND every data query errored; here the query *succeeded*. And there is a deliberate invariant behind that — *a legitimate empty result is never altered* — so a real "no matching rows" is not second-guessed. This is a **third** case neither branch covers: query succeeded, but against a relation nothing showed holds data. New `primitives.unestablished_relations()` + a second `assess()` branch (`kind="empty_relation"`), deterministic and **0-token, needing no execution**: a filtered aggregate returning zero only supports "no rows matched" unless the turn *established* the relation has data — an unfiltered count coming back positive, or the table returning real rows. It goes **silent** the moment either appears, so a meaningful filtered zero is untouched. The rewrite says what the evidence supports: *"…this turn did not establish whether nibrs_source_domain.victim contains any data at all — an empty table produces exactly the same result… this does NOT confirm that no such records exist."* **A second gap found en route:** the answer said **"0"**, not "no", so `asserts_nonexistence` never matched it — a numeric zero is a non-existence claim in substance, now detected, while `\b0\b` cannot match inside 10/120 so ordinary counts are unaffected (asserted both directions). Conservative throughout: an unreadable result is never assumed zero, a multi-column row is not read as an aggregate, an unfiltered zero is not a filtered claim, and a failed query stays the retrieval-failure case. **Gates:** honesty 42 → **64**, three mutations fail by name (ignoring the established-relation evidence · dropping numeric-zero detection · treating an unreadable result as zero); grounding 149 / guardrails 109 / review-queue 116 regression-clean. **Worth recording about the gate work itself:** two successive edits wrote **nothing** — this suite uses inline checks, not a `for fn in [...]` runner, so both replacements matched no anchor and the file still reported **42 passed, green** with the new test functions absent entirely. Caught only by grepping for the new check names rather than trusting the pass count; the third time this session that "green" meant "did not run". The invocation is now explicit and a raising test is reported as a NAMED failure rather than aborting the run. **Also added:** `agent_packs/policing-data-products/scripts/load_nibrs.py` — one command from ICPSR TSVs to queryable facts, wrapping the source repo's own resumable loader (nothing reimplemented), resolving credentials from Uderia's encrypted store (no `tq`, no secrets on disk), running the Domain INSERT-SELECT and verifying. Its **pre-flight space check refuses rather than failing hours in**: the data lands twice (Staging all-VARCHAR, then Domain), so it computes the requirement against live free PERM and, when it will not fit, names the percentage that would. **Space reclaimed on the reference box while preparing this:** the system had **59.5 GB allocated but only 17.1 GB in use** — `PERM` is a quota carved from the parent, not reserved storage, so several databases held large claims against almost nothing (`airlines_mvm` 7.5 GB against 30 MB, `PDCRADM` 6 GB against 0). Shrinking them to generous floors and dropping one empty leftover took free space **6.5 GB → 28.9 GB with no data deleted and no disk added**, which lifts the practical ceiling from a 10% sample to ~50%. (`TDMaps` needed `MODIFY USER`, not `MODIFY DATABASE` — it is a user.) Files: `agent/honesty/{gate,primitives}.py`, `agent_packs/policing-data-products/scripts/load_nibrs.py`, `test/test_honesty_gate.py`.
- **Aug 2026**: **The enrichment was handing the agent near-misses and no codes — three bugs, each a layer deeper**. Operator ran the first live question against the combined graph (*"How many victims are female?"*) and showed the result: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM NIBRS_Source_Domain.Victim WHERE V40191 = 'F' OR V40192 = 'F' OR V40193 = 'F'`. **My first diagnosis was wrong and is corrected here:** those are **real columns** — "SEX OF VICTIM-1/2/3", because NIBRS denormalises up to N victims per incident — they simply belong to **Arrestee** and **Incident**, not `Victim`. The agent did not hallucinate; it picked real columns from the wrong table, which is subtler and more instructive. **(1) Decoded values were never rendered.** `allowed_values` appeared **zero times** in `handler.py`: codes were put on 1,349 attributes by the constructor and dropped on the way to the prompt, so a coded column read as an opaque identifier and `= 'F'` was the only guess available. Fixed in **both** rendering paths — the entity listing and the `TABLE SCHEMAS` block, which is `name(type)` only and now carries a bounded `CODED / SENSITIVE COLUMNS` section — along with `is_pii`/classification, also being dropped. Same class of omission as the bridge caveat fixed hours earlier, which should have prompted a sweep then. **(2) Seed ranking by type — a fix aimed at the wrong layer.** Ranking entities above fields is reasonable and didn't help: the right answer *is* a field. **(3) The real cause: `search_entities` has no relevance ranking and truncates first.** It returns matches in arbitrary backend order, so at limit 25 `Victim.V4019` **was not in the candidate pool at all** — the handler was ranking a list that never contained the answer (at limit 100 it appears). And even with it present, `Victim.V4019` and `Arrestee.V40191` **scored identically**: same description text, same value labels. The missing signal is structural — the question is about *victims*, and only the **owning entity** separates them. Scoring now weighs owner match (+60, singular/plural tolerant), exact-identifier match, description-leads-with vs merely-mentions, and **decoded value labels as evidence** ("female" identifies a sex column through its values, not its name). Result: the enrichment now delivers `NIBRS_Source.Victim.V4019 (SEX OF VICTIM …; values: -9=Undetermined, -6=Not applicable, 0=Female, 1=Male; PII; CONFIDENTIAL)` in 1.1 s, with the bridge and evidence queries still resolving correctly (23-node focused subgraph for the evidence question). **Gates:** new `test_kg_enrichment_relevance` (**22**) — codes/PII rendering incl. graceful degradation on malformed input, the owner signal, incidental-mention weakness, value-labels-as-evidence, exact-match precedence, and ranking stability/bounds; 2 mutations fail by name (reverting the owner signal fails 3 assertions, dropping the codes fails 1). Nine KG suites regression-clean. **Open, not closed:** the observed query *hung* rather than erroring on a non-existent column, which suggests the MCP server (`uderia.com:8888`) may not target the same Teradata the graph was built from — worth confirming before trusting any execution result. Files: `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/handler.py`, `test/test_kg_enrichment_relevance.py`.
- **Aug 2026**: **The `andp-consumer` skill — and the two things that had to become CODE before it could be written**. Operator: *"shall we create a skill that finds bridges … or a more generic ANDP-Consumer skill where this is one of the sub skills?"* **Neither, quite — and the reason is the platform's own layering rule.** Running Component → LLM → Skill over "finding bridges" collapses most of it into code that already exists (does the target exist? what is the basis? is this product bi-temporal? what does code `0` mean? — all already on nodes), leaving one genuine gap: *do the two columns actually share values?* Telling an LLM in prose to write and interpret that query is exactly the shortcut the component doctrine forbids. So: **(1) `probe_bridge`**, a new `TDA_KnowledgeGraph` action backed by a pure `bridge_probe.py` — resolves both sides of a declared link to their deployed identifiers and compiles an overlap probe reporting **three** counts (distinct each side + shared), because a bare intersection count is unreadable without its denominators. **It COMPILES rather than executes, deliberately**: the KG component holds no warehouse connection and must not acquire one, since executing SQL from inside a component bypasses the MCP tool catalog where **Agent Authority** enforces `deny_writes` / denied tools / connector allow-lists — a read-only probe is harmless but the precedent is a governance hole the next feature walks through. Mirrors `compile_metric`: the component does the hard resolution, the agent runs it through its governed path. An unresolvable bridge yields the **reason, not SQL** — *"there is nothing to measure"* IS the answer — and an ambiguous bare label (two products both having an `Incident`) is **declined rather than resolved arbitrarily**, since attaching a probe to the wrong product's table is worse than declining. **(2) The caveat now travels with the node**: `_format_subgraph_for_prompt` renders a bridge as *"DECLARED LINK, not a verified join; declared basis: Synthetic Crosswalk Key; target does not exist in this graph (incident_Current) — unusable for a join"*, so an agent meets the caveat while planning instead of having to go looking. Also fixed a pre-existing correctness gap found en route: **`compile_metric` was missing from the manifest's action list**, and `entity_type` listed only the original eight types. **Then the skill.** One `andp-consumer` skill, bridges as one section — not a bridge-only skill (it would never load alone and would duplicate framing; skills cost tokens every turn). The stronger argument for it: ANDP consumption knowledge existed **only as a session primer** on the pack's Consumer profile, which cannot be assigned to another agent, shared, or published — as a skill it is reusable by any agent consuming any conformant product, and it **subsumes plan item B3** (instead of forking the primer into a source-image variant, the skill says *read the declared `temporal_pattern`*). Scope boundary against the existing `knowledge-graph-expert` (which stays untouched): that one is how to act on KG enrichment generally; this one is how to consume a *data product*, and applies **with or without** a KG. Content is judgement only — read declarations rather than assume conventions, decoded values are given so never guess a code, sensitivity is instruction not metadata, and the cross-product rules: an unresolved target means the link is unusable; a resolved one means *get evidence before relying on it*; **value overlap never upgrades a declared basis**; and never invent a link from similar-looking column names. Deliberately carries **no `component_id`**, so it never auto-assigns — packs and profiles opt in, and the ANDP pack's `skillsConfig` (previously empty) now bundles it on `@ANDP-CONSUMER`. Gates: new `test_bridge_probe` (**28**); 3 mutations fail by name — guessing an ambiguous label, emitting SQL for a missing target, and dropping the "evidence does not upgrade the basis" note. **The harness itself was fixed mid-run**: one mutation *crashed* rather than naming a failure, aborting every assertion after it, so each test function is now wrapped to report a raising test as a named failure — a gate that dies without saying what broke is half a gate. Files: `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/{bridge_probe.py,handler.py,manifest.json,instructions.json}`, `skills/builtin/andp-consumer/*`, `skills/skill_registry.json`, `agent_packs/andp/manifest.json`, `test/test_bridge_probe.py`.
- **Aug 2026**: **Linking two data products in ONE knowledge graph — declared bridges surfaced with their basis, never as joins**. Operator: *"more important to me is if there is a way to link both knowledge graphs"*, then *"currently a single agent can only be assigned to one knowledge graph — is this a problem?"* **The answer to the second question shaped the first.** One-active-KG-per-agent is correct and stays: the grounding gate derives ONE trusted scope from the bound graph, and that scope IS the guarantee — several bound graphs would need a scope union that blurs what an agent may talk about (for genuinely separate domains the coordinator pattern is the better answer, each expert tightly scoped). So multi-product capability comes from **one graph holding several products**, which is safe because the walker qualifies every name by product (gate-asserted: zero key collisions between NIBRS and CASE). New `target_kg_id` on the constructor + a **Build into** selector in the modal. **The question exposed a data-loss-shaped bug in that plan:** a KG stores exactly ONE `source_descriptor`, so appending a second product would have OVERWRITTEN the first — and the next resync would rebuild only the last product, **silently dropping every node of the other from the graph**. Fixed with `_merge_descriptor`: a multi-product graph carries a `products` list, `rebuild()` walks all of them, re-adding a product replaces rather than duplicates its entry, and a legacy flat descriptor is folded in rather than discarded (single-product graphs keep the flat shape, so nothing existing changes). **The bridges themselves — the honest half.** The reference CASE product declares a `nibrs_crosswalk` and is candid about it: one row's own `linkage_mechanism` reads **"Synthetic Crosswalk Key"**. Two problems, both now surfaced rather than hidden: the *view* wrapping that honest table appends **hardcoded string literals** (`'20181119-001-001-01'`, `'202300008138'`) as if they were resolved sample ids — so the constructor reads the **table**, never the view; and the declared targets (`incident_Current`, `offender_Current`) **do not exist** — they are the ANDP bi-temporal convention, while the target product is a source image that deployed `Incident`/`Offender`, i.e. the crosswalk was authored against an *assumed* product and never run against the real one. The rule encoded: **surface the claim, state its basis, say whether its targets resolved** — never normalise `X_Current` → `X` (that is guessing), never emit an edge to a node that does not exist, and still attach the bridge to the side that DOES resolve so it remains findable. Live on the combined graph: *"links: InvestigativeAction → incident_Current · basis: Synthetic Crosswalk Key · resolution: target 'incident_Current' not found in this graph · declared_in: nibrs_crosswalk"* — with **both products in the same graph**, so "not found" is a genuine governance finding rather than a scoping artefact. Cross-product resolution IS supported (`known_entities`) so a bridge naming a real entity of another product in the graph links to it. **Fifth entity type `product_bridge`**, deliberately NOT filed under `business_concept`: a glossary term is an authoritative definition, a bridge is an unverified claim, and mixing them would hide exactly the distinction a reader needs. Added through the documented four-edit process (§2.4d) — and the vocabulary gate immediately caught the missing default-lens entry, which is the gate working. Crosswalk tables are discovered by the shared **word** rather than a hardcoded `nibrs_crosswalk`, so the next product's crosswalk is picked up with no code change; the wrapping view is excluded by name. **Live-verified:** NIBRS built into a new graph (3,111/4,654) → CASE **appended to the same graph** (+70/+92) → one graph with **2 database roots, 41 entities, 1,512 attributes, 21 design decisions, 10 query recipes, 2 bridges**, descriptor declaring `['NIBRS_Source','CASE_Source']` for resync. Gates: walker 130 → **149** (dangling bridge, resolvable bridge, cross-product resolution, undeclared-basis naming, and the descriptor-merge trap incl. the legacy shape), vocabulary 65 → **67**; KG suites regression-clean. Files: `agent/kg_constructors/{andp_semantic_walker,andp_semantic_source,andp_semantic}.py`, `kgstore/types.py`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/{handler,renderer.js}`, `semantic_interchange/vocab.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `static/js/{api.js,handlers/rag/kgAndpSemanticModal.js}`.
- **Aug 2026**: **The ANDP Knowledge Graph Constructor — a deployed AI-Native Data Product becomes a grounded agent surface, deterministically and with zero tokens**. Operator ask, in stages: *"can you use remis repo to build the product on our uderia teradata database connection?"* → *"i really would like to have a andp knowledge graph constructor in the ux"* → *"make sure the constructor is exploiting all relevant assets of the foundation product"* → *"andp should be one of the drivers on how our knowledge graphs are structured"*. **Why it matters:** any product built to the AI-Native Data Product standard already publishes an agent-discoverable catalog of ITSELF, so consuming that catalog directly makes every conformant product usable on Uderia with **zero bespoke modelling** — the design framework becomes a supply channel rather than a one-off integration. New `discovery_mode="andp_semantic"` in the `KGConstructorStrategy` registry, split the same way as the industry-model constructor: a **pure walker** (`andp_semantic_walker.py`, no I/O, the unit-test target), a **fetcher** (`andp_semantic_source.py`), and a **strategy** (`andp_semantic.py`, `supports_resync=True` so a product's own evolution flows through to every agent bound to it). **THE TYPE RULE (the load-bearing decision):** *meaning comes from the ontology; types come from the data dictionary*. A product's declared `column_metadata.data_type` drifts from what was deployed — on the reference NIBRS product **1,425 of 1,508 columns** declare a type the deployed schema contradicts (it lands its source losslessly as characters). Physical `column` nodes therefore carry the `DBC.ColumnsV` type; the logical `attribute` keeps the declared type as the semantic fact it is; the divergence is **counted and surfaced in the UI**, never silently reconciled — a divergence is a finding about the product. **It consumes the WHOLE product, not just the schema** (the operator's correction — the first cut read 4 catalog tables and left the rest on the table): Semantic (`data_product_map`/`entity_metadata`/`column_metadata`/`table_relationship`/`naming_standard`) + **Memory** (`Business_Glossary`, `Query_Cookbook`, `Design_Decision`, `Module_Registry`) + **Observability** (`data_lineage`, `data_quality_metric`). Every asset is **attached to what it describes** — an unattached node is a footnote the agent never meets: a glossary term links to the attribute it defines, a recipe to the entities it queries, a decision to the table it shaped, a quality reading by `measures`. **Four new logical entity types** (`query_recipe`, `design_decision`, `quality_metric`, `naming_standard`) — named source-neutrally, since any KG may carry them — and critically added to **`SEMANTIC_TYPES`**, without which they render in the inspector but are **invisible to the agent**, making the whole enrichment decorative. **The vocabulary is now defined ONCE** (`kgstore/types.py`): it existed as **three hand-maintained copies** (`graph_store.py`, `sqlite_backend.py`, `conformance.py`), each commented "identical to" another — three copies of one contract drift the first time a type is added, and the failure is silent. All three now import and re-export; `test_kg_vocabulary` asserts **identity, not equality**, so a fresh literal copy fails CI even when its contents match. **Frontend/backend parity is enforced mechanically** (standing imperative): a type the backend can emit but `renderer.js` cannot colour, or that has no filter-pill position, or no RDF class for the standards export, fails the build. **Three real defects found by testing, not review:** (1) `kg_generate` defaulted **any unrecognised `discovery_mode` into the agent-discovery constructor** — building a completely different graph with no error; now refused by name, closing the class for every future constructor. (2) Teradata returns `Decimal`/`date` for quality readings → `Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable` killed the **entire** import; fixed centrally in `add_entity`/`add_rel` (a per-field fix only protects the fields someone remembered). (3) The module registry cases module names differently from the product map (`DOMAIN` vs `Domain`), silently losing all enrichment. **Honest lineage:** the reference product loads from files, so `source_database` is NULL — an external source becomes **provenance on the target table** (`derives_from_external`, `load_job`) rather than an invented node for a `.tsv`. **UX (the explicit ask):** a purpose-built modal — pick a Teradata connection → it **scans and lists the products actually deployed there** (discovery is deterministic, so the list is real, not free text) → choose → four include-toggles → build. Because "Build" is no longer an act that is **owed** after success (clicking it would create a silent duplicate graph), the footer swaps to **Build another / Done** and the form locks; a *failed* build keeps the form usable, because there the retry IS owed. The **inspector** was fixed too: the default lens excluded the new types (hiding the most distinctive content behind a pill click) and the tooltip rendered a hardcoded whitelist, so a recipe showed no SQL, a decision no rationale, and an `attribute` **neither its PII classification nor its decoded values** — now a declarative `KG_TIP_FIELDS` map plus governance badges and inline value codes. Also caught: the success path dispatched a `uderia:kg-created` event with **zero listeners**, so a built graph didn't appear in the Intelligence tab until a manual reload. **Live-verified end to end** on two real deployed products: NIBRS_Source → **3,111 entities / 4,654 relationships** (26 entities · 1,508 attributes · **511 PII-classified** · **1,349 with decoded values** · 5 glossary terms · 4 recipes · 9 decisions · 4 standards · 12 quality readings), CASE_Source → 68/90; one connected component, imported through the real `GraphStore` in 0.3 s. **Gates:** new `test_andp_semantic_walker` (**130**), `test_kg_vocabulary` (**65**), `test_kg_andp_modal.mjs` (**18**, executing the shipped footer state machine under a DOM stub); 13 KG suites regression-clean. Mutation-tested throughout — reverting the type rule, guessing an ambiguous table name, emitting a dangling FK endpoint, re-duplicating the vocabulary, dropping a colour, making a type agent-invisible, or restoring the duplicate-build footer each fail **by name**. One mutation **escaped** the first pass (a dangling physical-FK endpoint the fixtures never exercised) and the missing scenario was added rather than the result accepted. Docs: `ONTOLOGY_ARCHITECTURE` §2.4d (**the vocabulary is defined once** + the four coordinated edits adding a type requires) and the product-description layer table. Server restart (backend + template registry); browser reload for the modal/renderer.
