- **Aug 2026**: **`.sr-only` was a no-op for every input in the app — proven, fixed, and the judge toggle moved onto a shared slider**. Operator, with a screenshot of two controls where one belongs: *"showing up as two — this is a common issue."* Correct, and it was never about this card. **Root cause (measured, not asserted):** `.sr-only` is specificity **(0,1,0)** and `input[type="checkbox"]` in `main.css` is **(0,1,1)**, so the global rule won on `width`/`height`/`position` — and because `position` was forced back to `relative`, the `clip: rect(0,0,0,0)` that *did* apply was **inert** (clipping only affects absolutely-positioned boxes). Computed styles in a headless browser against the real stylesheet: the "hidden" checkbox measured **18×18, 324px² — pixel-identical to a fully visible one**. So the utility silently did nothing, app-wide: the **existing agent-pack tri-state toggle had the same duplicate**, live. Fixed at the utility (`!important` on the layout properties + `clip-path` + neutralising the platform's checkbox chrome — the same reasoning as Bootstrap's `.visually-hidden`): both fall to **1px²** while an ordinary checkbox stays untouched at 18px. **The hand-rolled switch is retired** for a shared **`.u-switch`** component in the platform's existing slider language (the tri-state toggle's geometry and palette), **driven entirely by CSS sibling selectors** — no script paints it, so the control cannot show one state while a different one is saved; focus ring on the track, light theme included. **A scope error the operator caught in the copy:** *"is 'On the panel that scores answer quality' not too narrow — it is also the panel that judges in-flight controls?"* — **right, and materially so.** `build_panel` is what the **grounding gate escalates to in flight**, where a ruling can *withhold an answer*; describing the switch as measurement-only understated what turning it off does. Card now reads **`Judges answers in flight and after the turn`** under a **Judging role** heading (was "Evaluation role"), the opt-out rationale leads with the in-flight consequence, and the same correction was applied to the architecture doc, the REST reference, the operator manual and the FAQ. One switch deliberately governs both layers (they ask the same models the same kind of question) — now stated rather than implied. Verified headlessly on the shipped markup + real `paint()` with the real stylesheet: **one control, card height 64px identical across on/off × dark/light**. Gate 22 → **31** (the sr-only authority per property, the CSS-driven switch, no-script-paints-it, and the both-layers copy); 3 mutations caught (stripping `!important` fails 6 · painting the switch from script · narrowing the copy back). Pins: `main.css 3.0` · `configurationHandler 1.1` · `main.js 8.1`.

- **Aug 2026**: **A model can be excluded from the judge panel, per LLM configuration**. Follow-up to the judge-layer fix below, from what the live re-run exposed: `Friendli/meta-llama-3.3-70b-instruct` timed out on **every** judge of **every** turn (three 20 s timeouts on one turn once the judges ran concurrently), contributing no vote while **setting the latency of the whole evaluation layer** — the panel waits for every member on every judged turn. Operator's call, so an explicit **opt-out**, never an auto-eviction: a model that is merely slow today may be the panel's most valuable member tomorrow. **One rule, stated once** (`judge.judge_panel_enabled(cfg)`) and read by `build_panel` — the **single selection path** behind all four judge consumers (online hook · manual *Score this turn* · CLI · **the grounding gate's in-path escalation**, the one that can withhold an answer), so one flag governs every one of them. **ABSENT means participating**, so every configuration that predates the option is byte-identical; only an explicit `False` opts out, and any other value (a hand-edited string, `None`) is treated as participation because *the failure direction that matters is silently losing a judge, not gaining one*. Exclusion is per **configuration**, not per provider family (asserted — the loop's family de-dup runs after the opt-out, so a second config of an excluded family can still be picked). **The empty-panel log now names the real reason** — it only ever said "no LLM config has usable credentials", which would have sent an operator to fix a key that is perfectly fine. **UX (world-class pass, on the operator's ask):** the control is a **role card**, not a checkbox with a paragraph — its own *Evaluation role* group (this is the model's second job, not a credential), the platform's **own scales glyph** reused from the Live Status judges control rather than a new icon, a real switch, and **one renderer** (`paint()`) driving the switch + state line + icon + border + hint so the toggle and the sentence beside it can never disagree (the defect a dialog cannot afford: reading "On" while it saves Off). **Progressive disclosure** — the rationale appears *only* when you switch it off, exactly when it is actionable. Both state lines are one line, so the card height is **identical** in both states (measured at 64 px in a headless render of the shipped markup + real `paint()`; the first draft wrapped and made the card jump on toggle). Theme-aware via CSS vars, keyboard focus ring drawn on the switch that replaces the `sr-only` checkbox, and the LLM card carries a muted **Not a judge** badge — marking the **exception**, never the rule. **A latent deployment hazard fixed en route:** `configurationHandler.js` was imported **unpinned** at all three sites, so a normal reload would have served the cached module and the new card would silently not appear — the "the fix didn't take" trap this repo has burned rounds on; now pinned (`?v=1.0`) with the cache root bumped (`main.js 8.0`). **Gates:** new `test_llm_judge_panel_optout.mjs` (**22**, executes the shipped markup + real `paint()` with a DOM-free stub — no browser) wired into `trust_battery.sh` so it cannot go stale; `test_eval_judges` 74 → **84**. Four mutations, each caught: flipping the default to opt-**in** (which would silently disable judging for every existing config) · writing the key only in the opt-out branch (so a model could never be re-enabled) · letting the switch stop agreeing with its own sentence · `build_panel` ignoring the flag. Battery green. Docs: `AGENT_OPS_EVAL_ARCHITECTURE` (panel composition + §6.4 rewritten — it still described the retired discard-everything timeout), `restAPI.md` (the field on POST/PUT, incl. that a partial update must send `true` to restore), the operator manual (control map + reading the panel), the FAQ (**§7.9/§7.10**, 64 → 66 entries), and the **public trust site regenerated** (3 of 5 renders were stale). Files: `eval/judge.py`, `static/js/handlers/configurationHandler.js`, `static/js/{main,conversationInitializer}.js`, `templates/index.html`, `test/{test_llm_judge_panel_optout.mjs,test_eval_judges.py,trust_battery.sh}`.

- **Aug 2026**: **The judge layer billed for rulings it then threw away — every judge run this deployment ever paid for**. Operator, on a real production turn: *"session 4a2169f3 judged the agent quality through an LLM post execution — looking at the agent roster row I don't see any indication of that judgement call."* The roster was telling the truth: the span carried `eval.judged=False`, **20 verdicts, zero of them judge-kind** — while `eval.cost_usd=0.0194065 / 4566 in / 430 out` matched the Live-Status "Agent Quality Judged" card **exactly**. Two surfaces, both honest about different things: the card reports **spend** (deliberately billed whatever the panel actually consumed), the roster reports **rulings** — and the disagreement between them WAS the defect signal. **Root cause, named by the production log to the second:** panel assembled 17:59:12.455 (3 models) → `Friendli/meta-llama-3.3-70b-instruct timed out after 20s` at :32.458 → `judges timed out after 25s` at :37.458. Three things compounded: **(1)** `run_judges` was a sequential `for … await` (rag_focused registers 4 judges, tool_enabled 5); **(2)** the per-call timeout was 80% of the whole-layer cap (`ONLINE_EVAL_JUDGE_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=20` inside `ONLINE_EVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=25`), so ONE hung panel member consumed the entire budget inside the FIRST judge and starved every judge after it; **(3)** the recovery was `verdicts.extend(await wait_for(...))` — on `TimeoutError` the `extend` never runs, so completed rulings died with the cancelled coroutine **while their tokens were still charged**. Blast radius across the whole production sink: **4 of 4 spans that paid for judges kept 0 verdicts ($0.0399 for nothing); `eval.judged=True` appears on zero spans.** The contrast that clinched it: the **manual** "Score this turn" path — same panel, same hanging model, no outer `wait_for` — records verdicts fine and degrades the hung model honestly to `panel 2✓/0✗/1?`. **Fixes:** judges run **concurrently** (`asyncio.gather`, per-judge isolation — a raising judge becomes a named abstention instead of taking the panel down), so the layer costs ONE call window instead of N; a **partial-results sink** (`make_judge_fn(panel, sink=…)`) lets a timeout keep what completed AND was paid for; the layer cap is floored at `per-call + _JUDGE_LAYER_MARGIN_SECONDS` so the budget is **satisfiable by construction** rather than by whoever last edited the two numbers apart. **A fourth defect the tests surfaced:** a judge the cut-off silenced simply VANISHED from the record — a reader could not tell *"never applicable"* from *"tried and lost"* — so `_mark_judges_cut` now backfills an abstention **naming the cut-off** for every applicable dimension (an abstention never asserts a pass). **`eval.judged` now states what the RECORD holds, not what was attempted** — one named rule `judged_from_record()` used by BOTH writers (online hook + manual re-score, which previously computed it apart and stamped "we assembled a panel"), so the runs-ledger LABEL and its judge CHIPS can never contradict each other. **The card is honest about absence:** spend with no ruling now reads `LLM judge panel — no ruling` + *"no ruling recorded — the panel did not return … the tokens above were still spent"* instead of announcing a panel and an empty per-model disclosure over a real bill. **Gates:** eval_online 100 → **126**, grammar 1815 → **1821**; **8 mutations, and two ESCAPED the first pass and had to be re-armed** — counting judge *dimensions* passed on the backfilled placeholders, so the assertion now demands a **real ruling** (`passed is not None`, explanation not the cut-off text) survive; and the "attempted vs recorded" flag proved an **equivalent mutant** (backfill makes the two coincide in every reachable state), so the rule was extracted into a named function and asserted directly rather than shipping a tautological scenario test. Also recorded: `git checkout <file>` inside the mutation copy silently reverted the **uncommitted** fix, so a "caught" mutation was really testing the old code — mutation harnesses must restore from the working tree, not from HEAD. Full battery green (18 Python suites + 6 JS gates). JS pins bumped `ui.js 1.68` (45 importers) · `main.js 7.9` · `notifications 4.12` · `genieHandler 4.0` · `agentAnatomy 6.0` · `agentPerformanceHandler 14.1`. **Server restart** (backend + `index.html`). Files: `eval/scorers/judges.py`, `eval/online.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `static/js/ui.js`, `test/{test_eval_online.py,test_trust_circle_grammar.mjs}`.

- **Aug 2026 (v1.20)**: **Release** — 316 commits since v1.19 (250 files, +65,973/−2,554). The headline is the **assurance module plane**: third parties can build for the Trust Circle end to end, shipping their own checks AND their own controls, dormant on arrival and signed before they can be bound. Alongside it: the trust substrate's one-assessment-two-lanes model, measurement counted once at JUDGED and grouped by the moment of the turn, three checks promoted from reports to in-flight protections (loop guard · budget cap · fluent-fabrication detection), the Trust panel rebuilt around the ring, and the developer contract at [BUILDING_ASSURANCE_MODULES.md](manuals/BUILDING_ASSURANCE_MODULES.md). Version surfaces bumped together per [docs/RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md): `pyproject` 1.20.0 · compose `uderia-v1-20` + build-arg default `v1.20` · annotated tag `v1.20`.

- **Aug 2026**: **The universal vote signal — a rating now reaches every engine, and one defect it exposed in the champion store**. Operator ask: *"we only make use of this ability in the optim profile class … lay out a strategy to make use of this across all engines"*. The vote was already stored engine-agnostically (`update_turn_feedback` writes `turn["feedback"]` for every engine) with exactly ONE consumer — the RAG champion score — so the substrate existed and everything else discarded the signal. **The framing that shaped it:** a vote is the scarcest signal the platform receives (free human ground truth on a fully-instrumented turn), and the two directions are **not symmetric** — downvote = *don't repeat this* (exclude/demote/deactivate/diagnose), upvote = *do this again* (promote/protect/seed). New **`agent/feedback/`** (sibling of `grounding/`/`guardrails/`/`honesty/`): a frozen `VoteEvent`, ONE dispatcher (sequential, per-consumer isolation, never raises, fire-and-forget so the HTTP response never waits), and six consumers — `champion` (a verbatim move of the pre-existing behaviour), `annotation`, `genie`, `retrieval`, `memory`, `diagnosis`. **`session_manager` keeps ONE line of vote code**; nothing vote-related may be added there again (structurally gate-asserted). **Per engine:** *Optimize* gains the missing upvote half (promotion via re-election + a replay-counter reset); *Focus* gains the learning loop it never had (per-document feedback surfacing in **Corpus Health** — records only, never reranks, never auto-quarantines); *Coordinate* propagates a vote to its expert **only when exactly ONE expert produced the answer** (a synthesis cannot be attributed, and the rule is one pure function `eligible_slave`); *Ideate/Conversation* pause facts the extractor auto-learned from a rejected turn. **Universal:** every vote writes an append-only `eval_annotations` row (`judge_passed` FROZEN at vote time — a re-score must not rewrite what the human reacted to; never-scored and refused turns record `NULL`, the honest value), feeding judge + threshold calibration. **A vote is a PREFERENCE, not a measurement** — the third axis beside intervention and quality (Rule 3bb): the runs-ledger word chip and the roster's `user feedback — N up · M down · K disagree with the scorecard` sit BESIDE the pass rate and can never move it (proven live: `pass_rate` byte-identical at 0.4474/38 across down → up → clear → down). **Disagreement is the point** — a turn the scorers passed that the user rejected is the only place a human says the bands are miscalibrated. **A REAL production defect found while building the upvote half:** champion re-election filters on `user_feedback_score >= 0` **read from the store**, and it ran BEFORE the new score was written — so a just-downvoted case was still eligible, could win its OWN re-election, and was then stamped `is_most_efficient=False` by the write that followed, **leaving the query with no champion at all**. Re-election now runs after the write, on every change including a cleared vote (election is a pure recompute, which is what makes the vote reversible). **Governance:** one `APP_CONFIG.FEEDBACK_SIGNALS` block; every default-on consumer is deterministic and **0 tokens**; the ONLY spender (`judge_on_downvote`, an opt-in judge run explaining a downvote) ships **OFF**, never overrides a profile's judge opt-out, never runs on a propagated vote, once per turn, and routes through `evaluate_turn_online(force_judges=True)` — the same timeouts, span, Live-Status step and **canonical cost sink** (no second judge path). **UX:** the vote buttons now say what the vote will DO, per engine, in a two-tier tooltip (consequence as the lead, the boundary as a quieter note) opening ABOVE the pill; the pill and *"Why trust this answer?"* share ONE action row. **Harness fidelity findings, each recorded:** the fake ChromaDB returned aliased dicts so the ordering defect could not reproduce (the first mutation ESCAPED because of it — *a fake unfaithful in the dimension under test measures nothing*); `test_feedback_dispatch` drove the real consumer chain and appended **72 fixture rows to the deployment's own `tda_eval.db`** (the table judge calibration reads) until the store was isolated; `resolve_profile` reached the real config manager and tried to bootstrap a `user_preferences` row; two scoping mutations escaped because the fixture gave each user a different session id, so the filter was never load-bearing (fixed with a collision case); and two CSS assertions used an unbounded `[\s\S]*?` that matched a property hundreds of lines later — *a bound is not an assertion*. Also converted the **~20th** implementation-pinning grep (the chips-row assertion pinned the exact call list rather than "every chip is in the shrinking slot"). **Gates:** 7 new CI-pure suites (`feedback_dispatch` 51 · `feedback_annotation` 42 · `feedback_champion` 19 · `feedback_genie` 27 · `retrieval_feedback` 41 · `feedback_memory` 28 · `feedback_diagnosis` 26) + `test_vote_tooltip.mjs` (**121**, executing the real renderer under a DOM); `eval_analysis` 129 → **155**, grammar 1800 → **1815**, pins 44, inventory re-baselined **614** (growth classified in the ledger). **53 mutations, every one fails by name.** Battery green; live-verified end to end. Server restart (backend + `index.html`). Docs: [FEEDBACK_SIGNAL_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/FEEDBACK_SIGNAL_ARCHITECTURE.md), plan + per-increment record `VOTE_SIGNAL_PLAN.md`. - **Aug 2026**: **Third-party CONTROLS, control postures, the studio as the ring, and one save model** — the second half of PROP-003, plus the audit that found what was missing. Operator: *"we must open this also to third parties — as i want to allow customers and third parties to implement their own controls"*, then *"think deep about it — as we must deliver a consistent solution"*. The plane had opened assessment and stopped, on the grounds that the posture ladder took five recorded contract breaches *by platform code* to get right. **That reasoning conflated the act with the CHOICE of act.** Four things, only two of which must stay the platform's: the assessment (third party) · the policy — when to act, which act (third party, **declared as data**) · the act itself (**platform performs it**) · the ladder, parking, retention, event and reading (**platform**). A pack now ships a real control — answers are genuinely withheld or altered because of it — while `ACTS` (withhold · alter · annotate) and `CHOKEPOINTS` (outbound_answer · inbound_request) stay closed, both because the platform must be able to DESCRIBE what happened, not from distrust. **`Control` is a frozen dataclass with no callable field**: the thing with POWER never carries logic, and the thing with logic (an assessor) never has power directly. **DORMANT ON ARRIVAL replaces the lock and is a better guarantee** — it moves the decision from the vendor to the operator: a third-party control installs at `observe`, records what it would have done, and changes nothing until an admin raises it; **installing a pack can never, by itself, withhold an answer**. **`enforced_by` became sugar for a control rather than a second runtime path** — left as its own mechanism it inherited the GATE's posture, so installing a pack routed to an already-enforcing gate made it act immediately, with no dormancy and no separate decision. **`fires_on` IS the routing** (a control's declaration is what makes its property consulted at that chokepoint, so a pack declares the fact once), and a bare name is namespaced to the pack — so naming a PLATFORM property, or a plain typo, produced a control that registers, signs, is raised to `enforce` and **never fires, forever, with nothing explaining why**; refused at load now, naming the pack's own properties. **The audit before the build found three gaps and disproved one.** *Disproved:* on paper a control has no signing gate while `check_binding` refuses an unsigned module's assessor — the weaker gate on the machinery with more power. Three probes say otherwise: a control is only ever offered `augment()`'s output (findings from BOUND modules), so `signed → bindable → produces a Finding → a control may act`, and an unsigned pack's control is inert at any posture including the escalating `withhold`. Right property, held through a call-site detail one refactor could have undone silently, asserted nowhere; now asserted from both ends. *Closed:* the `fires_on` trap above; **no REST or UI for posture** (settable only from Python — so the dormancy guarantee was absolute in the unhelpful direction); and **posture was invisible to the deployment envelope** while a REBIND, a smaller change by the envelope's own reasoning, was carried — `control_postures_state()` now carries only deviations and is **omitted when empty**, so adding it flips no existing attestation and the record appears the day it first means something. `POST/DELETE /v1/assurance/controls/<key>/posture` fails **closed** on an unrecognised posture; clearing is a distinct act from setting `observe` ("nobody decided" vs "decided the default" — only the first should leave the attestation). **The studio became the ring.** Two views over one model — *By guarantee* (eight segments) answers "what upholds this promise?", *By capability* (the matrix) answers "where is this capability used?"; neither contains the other, both reach every action, and `_propRowsHtml`/`_controlRowsHtml` take a subset so there is ONE renderer. **Deliberately a different instrument from the Agents lens's ring**: there colour means attention priority on live data, and a config page has no live agent — a coloured ring here would be the same shape under different rules, and an operator would read "GROUNDED is red" as "GROUNDED is misconfigured", the exact drift the trust grammar exists to prevent. So no state fill, structural strokes only, selection is the one fill, each segment labelled with what it HOLDS. **Found in the browser: "what acts on it" was the third-party registry alone**, so every guarantee said nothing acts on it on a fresh install — including GUARDED, which three gates uphold — and the honest-absence sentence made the emptiness look considered rather than broken; the same dogfooding gap the modules had, one layer out. Platform mechanisms are served per station and merged first; they carry **no** deployment-wide posture switch (a gate's mode is per-agent) and say where theirs is set instead. **The Trust panel's five containers collapse** (matching AI & Knowledge exactly), Assessment modules moved out from below the Save row into the sequence, and **module changes are now STAGED and applied by Save** — one save model in one column. Staging normally moves refusals to Save; it does not here, because eligibility is decided at PICK time (`conformance.candidates()` returns eligible/blocked with reasons before any write, and the picker never offers a blocked module) and the server re-checks on apply, still fail-closed. Applied **sequentially, never as a batch** (one act, one audit event, a refusal attributable to its row), a refused change **stays staged with its reason rendered on that row**, plus per-change undo, discard-all, a running count and a `beforeunload` guard (an accordion hides the row, so a staged change would be invisible AND lost). Also: the capability matrix now says when there is **nothing to remap** — with no pack installed each property has one shipped module, the bound one is correctly not offered as a change, so only unbind (a weakening) and restore remained; a control surface with an empty control space presented as though it were full, and the one absence on these surfaces that was never rendered. **What the gates caught that review did not:** two mutations ESCAPED the first staging assertions (an ordering check passed a mutation that moved a delete out of its success branch; `/beforeunload/` passed one that deleted the ADD and left the REMOVE) — both rewritten to assert the shape; a `_cellHtml` edit **silently matched nothing** (wrong parameter names), so the staged cell never rendered while every other part of staging did; the DOM stub had `querySelectorAll` but not `querySelector`, so the first path to use it died in the harness instead of failing an assertion; and the distance-bounded-regex trap bit **twice more** (a 900-char bound broke on a comment growing between two functions while the property held) — that trap has now cost this repo four fixes, and the lesson is recorded in the gate: **a bound is not an assertion**. **Recorded, not hidden:** I committed once while the battery was RED (the failures were stale assertions encoding the placement decision the move overturned, not defects — but the point of a gate is finding out *before* the commit); and an inventory **DROP** (fact-html 7 → 5) is justified in the ledger rather than re-baselined — two imperative `.innerHTML` pokes into the open picker are gone, and the refusal now renders declaratively on the staged row, which needs no picker to be open, survives every re-render and shows all of them: fewer writes, more of the fact reaching the operator. **New third-party developer guide** — [docs/manuals/BUILDING_ASSURANCE_MODULES.md](manuals/BUILDING_ASSURANCE_MODULES.md): the four-way split, the tiers, the manifest, siblings, getting signed, and the honest limits. Gates: new `test_assurance_controls` (**48**), studio 42 → **75**, bindings_rest 32 → **44**, grammar 1800 (its `#65` note said to flip when built, and it is flipped rather than deleted), inventory 575 → **598**; ten mutations fail by name. Battery green across 18 Python suites and 6 JS gates. Live-verified against a real server: a real installed pack's control is served dormant, the apply endpoints are unchanged, and a refusal still returns its reason. **Browser-verified** (operator click-through of the Trust panel, Aug 2026) — in addition to the renderer being executed under a DOM by 75 assertions and the payloads checked live. Server restart (rest_routes + template); `assuranceBindings 1.9`, `adminManager 3.7`. - **Aug 2026**: **PROP-003 · the IN-FLIGHT half — a third-party module can now MOVE an answer, as a sibling of the one that grades it**. Operator, on the shipped plane: *"but the whole purpose of this exercise was to enable 3rd parties to create plugins for both inflight and postflight capabilities"* — correct, and the shipped plane was half of one: only two of ten properties were consulted during a turn, so a pack could measure an answer and never affect one. Then the sharper framing: *"with shared modules — so basically siblings."* **That reframing is the design.** The intended shape is not "replace the platform's PII scan" but: a pack declares its OWN property (`acmeref.custref` — *does the answer expose an internal customer reference?*), routes it to a gate (`enforced_by`), and an operator binds ONE module to BOTH lanes — so the gate acts on it in flight and the SAME module grades it afterwards. `registry.symmetry()` then reads **`shared`** and the Guide draws the **S badge**: the thing that acted and the thing that graded are not two implementations that agree today, they are one that *cannot* disagree. It also dissolves the question that would otherwise have to be answered — *may a plugin replace the platform's own detector, and so weaken it?* — because a pack ADDS a property and nothing native is displaced. **ONE seam, union-only by construction:** `agent/assurance/inflight.py:augment(mechanism, own_properties, ctx)` returns what a bound module CONTRIBUTES; there is no return value that can REMOVE a native finding, so *a plugin may tighten, never loosen* is structural rather than remembered at four call sites. A shipped module contributes nothing through it (the gate already made that assessment natively; running it twice would double-count one finding), and every failure path returns `[]` so a gate behaves exactly as before. **Wired at four gates:** the outbound guardrail (findings merged before `decide_outbound`, so the platform's ladder — and only it — decides), the inbound guardrail (`request_integrity` ships with NO platform assessor, so this is the one property a pack can be the FIRST to assess), and the grounding gate (a pack finding ESCALATES to the judge, exactly as `context_use` does and for the same reason). **Classification is assessment; the act is policy:** a pattern rule declares `finding_category ∈ {pii, toxicity, exfil}` and supplies `(label, start, end, value)` spans — the pack says *this is personal data*, the platform says *personal data is redacted in enforce, noted in annotate, untouched in observe*. The raw matched value rides `payload`, which no surface renders and which the seam strips before anything is reported, so a plugin can drive a mask without its value ever reaching an event. **Proven live end to end**: `Contact Jane at jane@acme.com regarding CUST-48219 and CUST-77031.` → with the pack bound, `[REDACTED:email]` **and** `[REDACTED:CUSTREF]` ×2 — the platform's own detection still firing alongside it (the union rule), the action still `redact` (the platform's, not the pack's), symmetry `shared`, the same module scoring the turn afterwards, the raw reference absent from the event, and unbinding restoring the previous behaviour byte-for-byte. **The studio gained a third reading**, because two could not express it: a gate may RESOLVE a property itself, may consult it through the SEAM (its own assessment plus a plugin's), or may not consult it at all — collapsing any two loses a fact, so a seam cell now names the gate that acts on it and states the union rule in its tooltip. `INFLIGHT_CONSUMERS` grew from 2 to 6 and is still pinned against the gates' own source; a bound-but-unconsulted lane still says *no gate consults this in flight yet*. **Mutation-tested, and the fourth mutation found a hole in my own gate**: narrowing the seam's `except` changed nothing, because `Assessor.run()` already absorbs a raising `assess()` — the seam's guard is for a broken ENVELOPE, which no test drove; added, and it now fails by name. Gates: substrate 168 → **183**, studio 38 → **42**, new `test_assurance_inflight_live` (**21**); bindings_rest 32 (one assertion converted from pinning the map's exact contents to pinning its property — it froze at two entries and broke the moment more properties became genuinely consulted, while the thing that matters held perfectly). Battery green across guardrails 109 · grounding 149 · honesty 42 · review_queue 116 · corpus_grounding 75 · exfil 23 · membrane 208 · deployment 114 · grammar 1800 · inventory 575/0. Files: `agent/assurance/{inflight,__init__}.py`, `agent/guardrails/{runtime,policy}.py`, `agent/grounding/gate.py`, `assurance_modules/{manager,declarative}.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `static/js/handlers/assuranceBindings.js`.
- **Aug 2026**: **PROP-003 — the Assurance Module Plane: third parties can build for the Trust Circle, and an operator assigns what assesses what**. Operator directive: *"enable 3rd parties to develop functionality for the trust circle stations (properties, measures, controls) … a smart contract … a visual interface that allows us to assign platform-native and 3rd-party components dynamically."* **The hard part was already built:** `agent/assurance/` already defines the third-party surface (a `Property`, the `Assessor` ABC with its guarded envelope, `conformance.check_binding` whose refusals are already written for humans), and `registry.bindings()/bind()` + `conformance.candidates()` existed with **zero callers** — the binding table's own comment reads *"Data, not code. Each row is what a remapping UX will edit."* So this serves, persists, packages and gates the EXISTING contract rather than inventing a second one; because the Guide and the dial already render the LIVE binding, a rebound or third-party module appears on every trust surface with no frontend work. **Two tenets decide everything else. (A) Third parties ASSESS; the platform ACTS.** Of the operator's trio, controls do not open as third-party code — the posture ladder, HITL parking and the act grammar are guarantees that took five recorded contract breaches *by platform code* to get right. Control extensibility comes **through binding**: a third-party assessor bound to a property a native gate consults changes what the gate SEES (and so when it acts), while the act, its posture, its event and its rendering stay native. A module can tighten what an agent says; it can never loosen it silently (an unbound property reads NOT ASSESSED, never assessed-clean). **(B) Privilege by PROOF, not declaration.** The lane-capability model is the sandbox policy, so capability is *verified*: **T0 declarative** (no third-party Python at all — pattern rules, metric expressions through the flow `safe_expression` sandbox, and judge rubrics; expected to cover most real demand), **T1 verified** (a statically-verified pure subset — AST + import allowlist, no dunder traversal, the escape that makes a naive "strip builtins" sandbox worthless), **T2 scanned** (full Python, confined to post-hoc). **Phase 0 — the substrate persisted + served:** `assurance/store.py` with THREE distinct states a simpler design would collapse (no row = shipped default · a key = rebound · **NULL = explicitly not assessed**), so `delete` means *restore the default* and is a different act from unbinding; overrides fail **soft and loud** (a stale row is logged and skipped — startup dying to protect a preference would take every gate down); three latent gaps closed (`tool_outputs` was in the support set but in NO lane's supply, so an assessor requiring it could never bind ANYWHERE; capabilities were declared-but-unenforced; the assessor package was a hardcoded list). `INFLIGHT_CONSUMERS` declares which properties a gate really resolves in flight (**two of ten**) — a bound-but-unconsulted lane is a decoration wearing a control's clothes, and the studio renders that difference. **Phase 1 — the binding studio** (Config → Trust): properties × lanes, the two in-flight lanes as ONE column (they are alternatives, and a third would read as a gap that is not one), absence rendered rather than blank, the picker quoting `conformance`'s refusals verbatim, and nothing applied without a confirm step naming the consequence. **Phase 2 — the plane:** manifest + manager + `~/.tda/` + settings KV + the `assurance_module` trust kind. **Signed to bind** — the gate lives in `check_binding`, not the REST layer, so every caller inherits it; the validator checks **capability honesty** (a pack claiming the pure tier while failing it cannot be signed, so it can never reach the in-flight lane on an unchecked claim); **drift never auto-unbinds** (it is reported, because removing a running protection without a decision is worse than running a changed one visibly). Third parties write **no eval code**: `PropertyScorer` generalises the idiom nine native scorers share, and both lanes resolve the SAME binding, so symmetry is structural. The binding table folds into the **deployment** half of the trust envelope (never the portable half — a subscriber's bindings are their own decision), carrying each module's content hash so an in-place edit is drift a key-only record would miss. **Phase 3 — rubric judges + marketplace:** a rubric becomes a subclass of the platform's own `JudgeScorer`, inheriting the panel, the timeout, the consensus rule AND the **canonical cost sink** (a rubric billing through its own path would break the one-sink imperative on day one); publish/install/rate mirrors the extension plane, but an install grants **availability, never authority** — the pack still cannot be bound until it is signed HERE. **Six defects found by the gates or the browser, each fixed:** stripping `PURE` did NOT confine a scanned module (`LANE_REQUIREMENTS` asks nothing of the TRIGGERED lane, so unsandboxed Python could still run during a turn); the scorer discarded a triggered finding when no threshold was configured; the registry's `disabled` status was defeated by auto-discovery (the reference pack shipped disabled and loaded anyway); `INSERT OR IGNORE` silently swallowed a NOT NULL violation so no install was ever recorded and nobody could rate; an over-wide template edit deleted the Save Trust Settings row; and — in my own gate — a mutation that "passed" because the first version exercised `reload_overrides` alone while `bootstrap` ignored the override layer entirely. **Master switch OFF by default ⇒ byte-identical baseline.** New gates: `test_assurance_substrate` 132 → **168**, `test_assurance_bindings_rest` **30** (through the real auth stack — it immediately caught `@require_admin` not injecting `current_user`), `test_assurance_bindings_studio.mjs` **38** (the shipped module executed under a DOM), `test_assurance_modules` **67**, `test_assurance_modules_live` **22** (install → refused → sign → bind → score → drift), `test_assurance_marketplace` **32**; every security-bearing rule mutation-tested to fail by name. Battery green: assurance_points 327 · membrane 208 · deployment 114 · grounding 149 · guardrails 109 · eval_online 100 · grammar **1800** · dial 424 · partition 279 · pins 38 · inventory 574/0. Verified in headless Chrome against a real server with a real third-party pack installed. - **Aug 2026**: **Hovering a module described the property it routes to** — reported with a screenshot: a chip labelled *Data scope adherence* showing the tooltip *"Answer scope — Does the answer stay inside the data scope…"*. **Root cause is general, not cosmetic:** the Guide's one tooltip renderer builds from `data-dim`, and on a **routing** element `data-dim` is the DESTINATION — so every element that carries a route described where it GOES rather than what it IS. The two facts had been collapsed into one slot and the destination won. Fixed at the renderer: a module now gets a module-shaped tooltip (title from the MODULE, the description of what a module is, and *"Opens **Answer scope**, the property it assesses"* as a **separate** slot) — the contract's own rule that no slot may restate another, applied to a slot that was answering the wrong question entirely. The M badge's competing `u-tip` is removed: two tooltip systems on one hover render two boxes. **A probe artifact that nearly became a false bug report:** the tooltip measured as *never visible* on the module — until instrumenting the event order showed only ONE `mouseover` and no `mouseout`, which pointed at the `scroll → hideTip` handler; Playwright's `hover` scrolls the element into view and hides it. Scrolling first, then moving the pointer, renders it at **opacity 1** with the right text. The reading was mine to get wrong, and the event log is what settled it. Inventory **549 → 547** — a DROP, justified in the ledger: the badge's own tip is gone and the explanation moved to the whole button, richer and with more reach, not less. Gate: partition 275 → **279** (module branch exists · titled from the MODULE not the destination · destination named separately as a route · no competing badge tooltip). - **Aug 2026**: **A stale cache pin the pins gate could not see — freshness, not just consistency**. Operator: *"did you restart the server?"* The restart was current; the **pin** was not. `qualityDimensions.js` changed **four times** while `index.html` still said `?v=6.5`: the first `sed` bump matched nothing (a `sed` that matches nothing exits **0**), so every later bump matched nothing either, and the file sat at 6.5 through four content changes. Playwright never caught it — a fresh browser has no cache, so it always fetched current content while a **returning** browser would keep serving the old module through any number of restarts. That is the "the fix didn't take" failure this repo has burned three debugging rounds on. **`test_version_pins` passed the whole time** because it asserts *one pin everywhere* — consistency, which was intact; the pin was simply the wrong one. - **Aug 2026**: **No two chips share a verb, and no ruling is stated twice**. Operator, with a screenshot: *"look at the inconsistent conflicting messaging."* Two conflicts, different in kind. **(1) One ruling, two chips.** A row carried **`judge-flagged`** beside **`1 judge flagged this`** — and both came from the SAME `groundedness` verdict: one naming the Rule 3.0c disagreement, the other counting the panel's finding. - **Aug 2026**: **The judge step in Live Status names its layer — in-flight or post-hoc**. Operator: *"can we make sure in the live status window event that the llm judge event contains the information if it's an inflight judge or a posthoc judge."* **The ambiguity was real and structural**: `judge_evaluation_complete` is emitted by ONE canonical sink (`_record_score_usage`) for **all three** judge paths — the online panel, the manual re-score, and the grounding gate's in-path escalation (which defers its cost until the turn is persisted) — because that is what makes every judge token sum into the turn total. So a ruling that **could have withheld the answer** and a measurement that **changed nothing** rendered as the same step, with the same title, and nothing in the payload told them apart. New `layer` field, **declared by the caller and never inferred**: the deferral defaults to `in_flight` (it exists FOR that case) but still carries it per entry so a future deferring caller declares its own; the online hook and the re-score endpoint state `post_hoc` explicitly rather than leaning on the default; an unrecognised value degrades to the norm. It drives the **step's own name** (`Gate Consulted a Judge` / `Agent Quality Judged`) so the Live Status LIST distinguishes them — on the live stream **and on reload**, which meant all four per-engine title functions had to resolve it (one hardcoding it would flatten the distinction for that engine alone, which is worse than not having it) — plus a **When** row on the card stating what each layer *means* rather than the wire token. An older event carries no layer and gets **no row**, rather than claiming a certainty the record does not have. **Gates:** eval_online 91 → **100** (the sink/deferral signatures, the declared-not-inferred rule, the degrade), grammar 1723 → **1741** (all four title functions executed across in-flight/post-hoc/legacy, the card's three renderings, and *no surface leaks the wire token*); 6 mutations, each caught (hardcoding one engine's title · dropping the card row · leaking `in_flight` as user-facing text · claiming a layer for legacy events · letting an unknown value through · defaulting the deferral the wrong way). **Version-pin discipline**: `ui.js` and `eventHandlers.js` both changed, so their own pins and every importer's were bumped up to `main.js` — including **4 inline `import()` calls in `index.html`** that the sweep of `static/js` cannot see and that the pins gate caught. **Server restart** (`eval/online.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`) + browser reload (`ui 1.57` ×21 · `eventHandlers 4.4` · `main 6.8`). - **Aug 2026**: **The size channel restored on the operator's model, and a judge's colour is worst-of its PANEL**. Operator, after I removed the size channel one commit earlier: *"i am now totally confused — diamonds are solely used by judges — this is what we agreed on — and judges that are sampled after the turn execution are smaller in shape … all other judges that are executed during a turn have regular diamond shape … correct?"* **Correct, and my removal was the wrong call.** I had retired it under *mark the exception, never the rule* (48 of 52 judge marks are sampled, so nearly every diamond wore the modifier) — but that reasoning inverts here: **the regular diamond is the BASELINE and the shrink means *lighter*, so the consequential judge is the one that stands out**. Marking the exception is achieved BY modifying the common case, not violated by it; the maxim's real content is narrower — *a modifier must not make the exception harder to see* — and the contract now says so rather than the over-broad form. Re-encoded the way the operator framed it: `.ap-sq-j` is the judge diamond and `.ap-sq-js` is the **sampled** modifier (a step down from .82 to .62), so the in-path judge wears the regular, unmodified shape. **Then, asked for a colour recommendation, the operator set the rule themselves:** *"if any one of the judges votes false, the diamond turns red otherwise green."* Implemented as **worst-of the panel** — which is the house rule for aggregation (5.1), and which Rule 3.0c already implies one level down: a panel is N measures of one property, and a disagreement between them is REPORTED, never weighted away. A recorded judge verdict is the panel's **consensus**, so a dissenting model previously vanished into a majority. **The one guard that matters:** a red mark beside a chip reading *upheld* with nothing explaining the difference is the contradiction this grammar exists to prevent, so a split panel is NAMED on both — the chip gains `·split 2/3` and the mark's tooltip reads *"the panel upheld this 2 to 1; the mark shows the dissent"*. An **abstention stays in the absence family even if a vote inside it said fail** — a judge that declined to rule is an absence, not a finding (gate-asserted; it was the one mutation that escaped the first pass). **No behaviour change today**: every panel in the live sink is a single model (52 verdicts, 0 splits), so the rule is identical to the current reading and becomes meaningful the moment a multi-model panel is configured — which is the lever recommended after the false positive we traced. **Gate:** grammar 1675 → **1691**; the retirement assertions became the channel's rule (both are judges · the in-path one is unmodified · the shrink is smaller · resolved per verdict from `gate.judge_family`), plus the panel truth table; 7 mutations, each caught (dropping the shrink 5 · inverting it 4 · ignoring dissent · repainting rules by a panel they do not have · painting an abstention red · hiding the split). Fixed **structurally** (the chip slot is the only flexible member and it SHRINKS with `text-overflow:ellipsis` — its full text is in the tooltip either way; every fixed member refuses to wrap; the strip never shrinks) **and** by shortening the labels to the row's short form (`withheld · parked`, `judged in-path 2/3` — longest combined chip text 65 → **38 chars**), with the sentence moved into the tooltip where there is room for it. **(2)** *"the dots at the beginning are misleading — remove them."* Correct, and it was a grammar conflict I created: once the acted dot landed, the row carried **two dots side by side meaning different things** — the exact misreading **Rule 9.3** exists to prevent. The key never said this — and worse, it demonstrated *shape* with two GREEN samples, hiding the only case where the distinction bites. Operator: *"I am confused about the 7 failed — I count more."* Correct, and the two numbers came from two rules. The headline uses `analysis.turn_failed` (fixed earlier: gate-eligible danger, or a grounding block), but `runBand()` re-derived the band **client-side** as `gating_failures > 0 || vs.some(v => v.passed === false)` — the **pre-`Verdict.gating` rule**, under which an ADVISORY check convicts a whole run. One fact, two surfaces, two answers — and the ledger sat directly beneath the headline that contradicted it. **Fixed by reading, not re-deriving:** the row now keys danger on the backend's `gating_failures` alone (computed against the current registry) and treats an advisory failure as **review** — the Scorecard's own rule, that an advisory check is flagged and never a conviction. **The subtle half:** persisted verdict events carry **no `gating` key** (the flag became a derived property after these spans were written), so a naive frontend check would never fire and an advisory-failed turn would have fallen through to **healthy** — hiding the finding, strictly worse than over-convicting it. `analysis._verdicts` now **back-fills** each verdict's `gating` from `is_gating_dimension`, the same precedent `/v1/evals/turn-score` already uses when replaying an older span, so the renderer reads a resolved fact instead of guessing. - **Aug 2026**: **Every Trust Circle station opens its own Guide entry — one declaration, either scope**. Operator: *"can we have an additional button to open the Assurance Guide focused on the selected station (Guarantee), regardless of whether an agent is selected or the star reflects the whole estate?"* The station panel could route to the runs and the posture matrix but not to the **guarantee's own definition** — the one surface that says what upholds it and what grades it (the `upheld by` / `graded by` rows added earlier the same day). **Declared ONCE in the renderer**, not eight times in the model: all eight stations have a `station_<key>` Guide entry, so the route is a property of BEING a station. It rides the **same `explain-dim:` channel** the derivation's dimension chips already use — which resolves the station from the same model the panel rendered from, so the Guide opens on the GUARANTEE scoped to exactly the dimensions listed above it, with their live bands. **Scope-independent by construction** — the route names the station, never the agent; driven at both scopes it produces the identical `openGuide("station_grounded")` with the identical scoped rows. Guarded on the Guide being loaded (Rule 8.5 — a button that cannot open anything reads as the route). **The gate work is the notable part, and it was mine to fix twice.** (1) My first three assertions were **source greps** — they searched for the route string, which survives both `if (false)` and a neutered guard, so **two of the three mutations passed**. Rewritten to EXECUTE `stationPanel` and assert the rendered output: route present when the Guide is loaded, **absent when it is not**, existing routes surviving either way. (2) Sharpening Rule 3b.7 — which banned any mention of `QualityDimensions` in the ring, and so banned *asking whether the Guide exists*, though a capability check defines nothing — I replaced the blunt ban with the property: the ring may route, and must never call `openGuide`/`.label`/`.desc` or read `DIM`/`LONG`. (3) That left the "second glossary" mutation crashing the gate instead of naming a failure, because an EARLIER harness executed the same panel without a `window`. Both harnesses now share ONE **faithful stub**: a Proxy exposing only `openGuide` and throwing *"Rule 3b.7 — the ring must not use QualityDimensions.label: it routes to the Guide, it never looks a dimension up itself"* on anything else. A permissive stub would have let exactly that through; a crashing gate still fails CI but names nothing, and **a gate that cannot say WHAT broke is half a gate**. Final mutation results: disabling the route → 2 named failures · neutering the guard → 1 · reaching for a second glossary → the rule, by name. **Gate:** grammar 1578 → **1593**. - **Aug 2026**: **ONE palette, ONE tag chip, ONE settled fold — and the shortcut I took while fixing the tag**. Operator: *"make sure you use Uderia-conform @Tag colour coding"* + *"where do all the acknowledge/confirmed messages go to?"* + the design imperative *"apply best practice, never do a shortcut"*. **The colour was never wrong** — `@RESTO` is `tool_enabled` → `#9333ea`, Optimize purple; it *read* as an arbitrary magenta because the inbox printed the tag as **bare 10px coloured text**, which is not the platform's tag. **And my first fix was itself the shortcut**: I hand-rolled a second copy of the chip markup in the Agents lens while `ui.js` **already exports `renderProfileTag()`** — reproducing, inside a session spent removing duplicate vocabularies, the very defect. The copy had already diverged (it dropped the builder's `--profile-tag-bg-hover`), and it came with a `.ai-tag` rule overriding font-size, padding **and** the border-width `main.css` calls *"industrial 2px for strength"* — a local re-design of shared tokens to make a copy fit, when `.profile-tag--sm` is already 10px/`0.125rem 0.375rem`, exactly the inbox's scale. **Fixed at the root, four copies removed:** `ui.js` publishes `window.renderProfileTag` (the dual-surface pattern `profileColors.js` already uses for IIFE handlers); the lens **deletes its local `IFOC` map** (copy #3 — `profileColors.js`'s own header records the map *"historically drifted across ~5 handlers"*, and this file was one) and reads `window.ProfileColors`; **`FAMILY_COLOR` — a FOURTH copy keyed by IFOC *label* instead of type, which is exactly why it survived a search for the copy keyed by type — is now DERIVED** from the same source (verified value-identical); `_agentIfocColor` returns the CLASS colour per the rule `profileColors.js` states, rather than the profile's own `color` field (they agree today; preferring the field would make this the one surface able to disagree with the declared palette); and **both** row kinds (inbox + review) render through the one chip. The absent-builder fallback is the **plain tag**, never a styled lookalike — a fallback that reproduces the design is the duplication wearing a safety net. **Where acknowledged items go:** into a collapsed **settled** fold, beside the existing "below the reporting level" and "recoverable originals" folds. The queue lists what is OWED; an acknowledged notice and a decided item are finished work, and mixing them made the operator re-read the same rows every visit to find the two that mattered. Folded, never dropped — each keeps its disposition AND its route, and the fact that a *condition* can outlive its *notice* is safe here because that state lives on the ring, not the queue. **Gate:** grammar 1564 → **1578** — the four IFOC hexes are declared once, and no expression in the lens pairs three or more of them (**precision on purpose**: a single hex may legitimately reappear as a chart series colour, and a blunter ban would be worked around rather than obeyed); the builder is owned by ui.js, published, delegated to, with no local chip markup and no local re-styling of its tokens. **Mutation-tested**: restoring the palette copy fails 1, reintroducing a local chip fails 3. **12th implementation-pinning grep converted** — `P2-10b` grepped two exact call expressions (`_agentIfocColor(e.profile_tag)`), so routing through the shared chip broke it while the property held *better* than before; its replacement extracts the resolver and reads its BODY, because a comment growing between the name and the call had nearly decided a distance-bounded regex. **The trust inventory is green for the first time in several sessions**: `data-batch` classified as request plumbing (the documented precedent for the derived-ack key), `uTip.js` classified NOT_A_SURFACE (it renders each surface's own `data-tip`, already inventoried there — the trustGrammar.js reasoning), and **both count DROPS justified in a new ledger note before re-baselining**: `delegate 23 → 20` is the three stale `.closest('div.flex.items-start')` selectors that WERE the dead-button defect (reach restored, not lost), and `route 38 → 37` is `data-event-id` giving way to `data-batch`, which names every occurrence rather than one. - **Aug 2026**: **No inbox row is a dead end — an acknowledged `needs you now` offered nothing at all (Rule 8.5)**. Operator: *"don't I need buttons for the needs you now messages?"* Those two rows were correctly acknowledged (`seen`) and therefore offered no action — but that is only correct if `Ack` resolves the finding, and **it does not: an ack disposes of the NOTICE, never of the CONDITION**. A station shortfall is recomputed from the window, so it persists and re-derives after every acknowledgment; ticking it again achieves nothing. The row therefore read *"urgent, and there is nothing to do"* — the exact shape the contract's **Rule 8.5** bans (the offered act must be the act that is OWED, and an act that cannot move the state is worse than none because it reads as the fix). **Every row now offers the place it is WORKED**, routed by what the row is, using machinery that already existed: a **turn-scoped** finding opens that turn's trace (`data-ap-open-session` — the lens's own route, so the inbox and the runs ledger reach a turn the same way), an **agent-scoped** one opens the agent's roster detail, where the failing dimension bars are. Offered whether or not the item is disposed — a disposition settles the notice, and the place it is worked stays worth reaching. Live shapes: an acked `@RESTO` shortfall now offers `Open @RESTO` (and correctly does NOT re-offer the ack it already has); a grounding block offers `Open turn · Ack`; the grouped defusals offer `Open @UDERIA · Quarantine doc · Ack all 3`. **Gate:** grammar 1553 → **1564** (the acked-danger row is not a dead end and routes to the agent without re-offering its ack; a turn-scoped row routes to its turn through the shared route; and the full severity × disposition matrix — 6 combinations — each still offers something). **Mutation-tested**: removing the route fails 6 assertions. - **Aug 2026**: **The inbox's buttons were dead — a row selected by its layout classes — and collapsing now keeps its precision**. Operator: *"none of the buttons work (Quarantine doc / Ack)"* + *"the right approach is to enable collapsing but have the buttons execute the task for ALL — still with the option to expand and execute individually"*. **Root cause of the dead buttons:** the three handlers ended with `btn.closest('div.flex.items-start')` — the OLD row's *utility classes*. The redesign renamed the row, so the POST fired, the server recorded the ack/quarantine, and **nothing on screen moved**: indistinguishable from a broken button, and worse, because the operator clicks again. Selecting a row by its layout classes was the defect; all three now call ONE `refreshInbox()` that re-renders from the source — a removed row was a lie anyway, since the badges, severity counts and agent pills all move with a disposition and DOM surgery left every one of them stale. **The design ask, built:** a collapsed row's buttons act on **every** occurrence it collapsed (`Ack all 3`), and **expanding gives each occurrence its own actions** — grouping that could only be acted on wholesale would trade precision for tidiness, which a triage queue may not do. **ONE batch contract serves both**: a single item and a group of twelve hand the same `data-batch` list to the same executor, so there is no group-only branch to drift from the far better-exercised single case. The list carries whichever key the source needs — a STORED incident by id, a DERIVED observation by (session, turn, event_type), since the sealed trace is never rewritten and the ack is a disposition ABOUT it. Sequential, so each item gets its own audit record, with an honest partial-failure tally (`Acknowledged 2 of 3`) rather than a reported success. A settled occurrence is never re-offered. Quarantine acks the whole batch — the document is part of the grouping signature, so one quarantine covers every occurrence and leaving N−1 open against an already-excluded document would be false work. Two ack functions collapsed into one; the now-unreachable `ackDerivedObservation` deleted. **Also corrected, not a regression:** the two `needs you now` rows have no buttons because they are already acknowledged (they wear `seen`) — verified against the pre-redesign screenshot, which shows the same. **Gate:** grammar 1543 → **1553** (collapsed-row-acts-on-all, per-occurrence rows all individually actionable and none skipped, one executor with no surviving single-item action, settled-not-re-offered, and the row-selector ban). **Mutation-tested**: making the group act on one fails 1, removing per-occurrence actions fails 3. **Three more gate assertions repaired**, two of them mine: `P2-6 derived observations are ack-able` grepped two FUNCTION NAMES, so unifying the ack paths broke it while the property held perfectly — now asserted on the rendered row (the 11th pinning grep converted this session); my own occurrence assertion still counted `<li>`; and my CSS slice anchored on `.ai-btn{`, which `.ai-occ-act .ai-btn{` also contains — it silently inverted the moment the occurrence rows landed. Browser reload only (`agentPerformanceHandler 10.7`). Files: `static/js/handlers/agentPerformanceHandler.js`, `templates/index.html`, `test/test_trust_circle_grammar.mjs`.

- **Aug 2026**: **The Assurance Inbox rebuilt as a triage queue — titles, recurrence grouping, one filter bar**. Operator: *"the layout really looks ugly"* + *"I want clear titles for the rows"*. The queue was **one run-on sentence per row in a single weight**, preceded by four competing left-side markers (dot · severity chip · station chip · text), with four IDENTICAL retrieval-firewall findings listed flat — so the two `needs you now` items were pushed off the first screen by repetition of a warning, on a surface whose entire job is "what do I look at first". **(1) Row anatomy is now title-first.** New declared `_INBOX_TITLE` — every event type the backend can raise gets a scannable heading (`Answer withheld — unsupported by its sources` · `Retrieval firewall defused a chunk` · `Request refused at the door` …), with the parameterised `station_shortfall_*` family BUILT from its station rather than listed five times, and an unknown type degrading to a humanised key rather than a wire string. **Titles are declared, never parsed out of the summary** — a heading derived from prose breaks the moment the prose is reworded. The backend summary becomes the DETAIL line, with the title's own leading words stripped (longest shared word-prefix, so a reworded summary degrades to showing MORE rather than to a mangled fragment) plus a redundant `for @TAG —` lead-in dropped, since the agent has its own slot in the meta (Rule 3.0 — no slot restates another). **(2) Recurrence collapses.** `_groupInbox` folds identical findings into one row with `×N` and every occurrence still reachable behind a disclosure; the signature is *"the same thing"* as an operator would mean it (event kind · agent · the payload's own subject · labels) and deliberately excludes TIME, since recurrence over time is exactly what is being collapsed. A decided or acked item never folds into an open group — that would hide a completed act — and the same finding on two agents stays two rows. Real data: **5 rows → 2**. **(3) One filter bar** replaces two labelled rows (the `Agent:` / `Show:` prefixes were furniture — the pills say what they are); both pill families now share `.ai-pill` so they cannot drift in size, radius or focus ring. **(4) Relative time** with the absolute one hover away, replacing raw `3.8.2026, 19:03:44` locale output. Actions are quiet until hover but **never `display:none`** — an action reachable only by mouse is unreachable for anyone else, and these actions are the queue's whole purpose (gate-asserted, plus `:focus-within`). **The gate caught a regression in my own redesign, which is the notable part:** the first draft moved severity onto a coloured left EDGE and dropped the word chip — making severity **colour-alone**, the exact Rule 9.4a violation fixed on the band strip hours earlier. The edge now differs in **border WEIGHT** per level (3px/2px/1px) AND the severity **word** leads the meta line, so the three levels are readable in greyscale and under CVD. **Also converted the 10th implementation-pinning grep of the session:** the assertion read `/_sevDot\(e\.severity\)/ && /_sevChip\(e\.severity\)/` — it pinned ONE rendering of severity, so it broke on a redesign while the property it stood for (severity legible without hue) went unprotected; worse, any surviving call would have satisfied it while the first draft violated the property. Now executed: every level states its word from the ONE vocabulary, and the three edges are asserted to differ in weight. **Gate:** grammar 1505 → **1543** (+38: a declared title per event type with none leaking a wire key, the built shortfall title, the unknown-type fallback, detail-never-restates-title, the agent lead-in strip, grouping/no-merge/decided-stays-solo, row anatomy, keyboard-reachable actions, and the severity property). **Mutation-tested**: dropping the severity word fails 3 assertions, disabling grouping fails 3. Battery green (grammar 1543 · dial 400 · partition 164 · routes 99 · pins 37 · eval_analysis 101 · guardrails 99 · assurance_points 261 · trust_events 50). Browser reload only (`agentPerformanceHandler 10.6`); no backend change. **Not done, deliberately:** the row is rebuilt but has NOT been seen in a browser — the markup and grouping were verified by executing the real renderer over the screenshot's own data. - **Aug 2026**: **One malformed config block silently disabled ALL FOUR gates on a turn — found by chasing an "errored guard" display note**. Closing the two open items from the session above turned up a real protection failure, not the display gap it was filed as. **The chase:** two turns carried `eval.gate.{outbound,inbound} = "error"`. Reading the code first **corrected my own earlier claim** that "nothing distinguishes an errored guard from a clean pass" — the per-turn instrument had always been honest (`assurance_points` → `unknown`, *"the guard failed — not recorded as a pass"*; the live dial maps `action==='error'` the same way). What was missing was only the AGGREGATE. But the turn stamps showed **`inbound · outbound · grounding · honesty` ALL errored together with the same `AttributeError`** — four independent gates cannot fail identically by coincidence, so something shared was raising. **Root cause:** every gate resolves its posture by walking into the profile's config (`profile["guardrailConfig"]["outbound"]["mode"]`), and those walks assumed dict shape **at every level**. A block that is not a dict — the exact drift an editor change or config migration produces, and the posture-model rework landed that same day — raised `AttributeError` **outside the resolver's own guard** and therefore **inside the caller's fail-open `except`**. Result: one bad block, every protection silently off, the answer still delivered. (First probe reported a break on the normal shape too; that was the probe passing a raw string where a `Direction` enum belongs — checked before reporting, so no false alarm shipped.) **Fixed** with ONE shape-tolerant reader `profile_config_contract.config_block(profile, *path)` — always a dict, never raises, for any input at any depth — routed through both `guardrails/adapter` and `grounding/adapter`; every malformed shape now degrades to `observe` (the safe default) instead of taking the gates with it, and a well-formed block still resolves to `enforce` untouched. **The two filed items, delivered:** (1) an **`errored` counter** on the aggregate (`_gate`), counted **once per turn** however many gates errored — the turn is the unit, and on the real occurrence all four failed from one cause; (2) the **intervention reading** on the roster (`interventionNote()`, on the card AND the detail panel): *"2 of 18 answers altered or withheld · 2 parked for review · 4 escalated to a judge · 2 turns where a guard did not run"*, reporting only what happened so an agent nothing acted on says so plainly rather than showing a decorative zero. **The errored count is deliberately NOT in the pass rate** — a guard that could not run is not a quality failure, and folding it in would repeat the exact conflation Rule 3bb was written to prevent one commit earlier. **Deferred with a reason:** the "pass rate" → "answer quality" rename was ranked LAST and left to the operator, because once the intervention reading sits beside it the ambiguity largely dissolves — the reader can see there are two axes — so the rename became optional rather than necessary; doing it alone would have been the worst order (relabel one number, leave the other question unanswerable). **Gates:** guardrails 77 → **99** (every malformed shape × all three resolvers degrades-not-raises, well-formed config still honoured, and the helper's own always-a-dict property); eval_analysis 93 → **101** (counted once per turn · never a quality failure · pass rate untouched · the roster reading names it in words). **Mutation-tested**: restoring the naive `.get()` chain fails 8 assertions, dropping the counter fails 2. Battery green across guardrails 99 · eval_analysis 101 · grounding 133 · review_queue 116 · posture_modes 78 · assurance_points 261 · membrane 208 · contract 102 · grammar 1505 · dial 400 · partition 164 · routes 99 · pins 37. Docs: contract gains two one-source rows (the config reader; the intervention reading), the FAQ's **§9 open items are now closed and answered as §4.5**, the operator manual's §3.0b gains the intervention paragraph, public trust site re-rendered. **Server restart** for `core/profile_config_contract.py` + both adapters + `eval/analysis.py`; browser reload for `agentPerformanceHandler 10.5`. - **Aug 2026**: **Intervention and quality are two dimensions — documented as such across the contract, the eval architecture, the operator manual and the FAQ**. Operator conclusion after tracing the pass rate: *"an event that changed the answer through triggering the gates in GROUNDED and GUARDED is a different dimension than the valid/invalid turns (that is based on measurements and associated bands)"* — exactly right, and nothing said so in writing. Their call on the behaviour: **leave the fold as it is, document the difference clearly** — so this is a docs-only change, no code. **The evidence that shaped it:** the 2×2 across one real agent's 18 turns shows the axes are near-**orthogonal in practice**, not merely distinct in theory — `acted+flagged 0` · `acted+clean 2` · **`nothing acted+flagged 5`** · `nothing acted+clean 11`. Every intervention landed on a turn whose measurements were otherwise clean; every measurement failure landed on a turn no control touched. The third cell is the one an operator should act on (the answer was DELIVERED and grades poorly — nothing caught it) and it is precisely the cell an intervention count reads `0` on. **Written down, in four places:** (1) contract **§3bb** (Rules 3bb.1–3bb.3) — the two readings side by side, the 2×2, why the rate is measurement-driven (a mechanism-driven rate reads a comfortable-and-dishonest **89%** on that agent, since 16 of 18 turns had no mechanism act), and the ONE deliberate crossing stated as an exception rather than left to be discovered; (2) `AGENT_OPS_EVAL_ARCHITECTURE` **§6.4b** — the predicate, the current-registry resolution, and the **asymmetry table**: an inbound refusal is EXCLUDED from the quality denominator (`eval.gate_only`, *"never measured against"*) while a grounding block is COUNTED as a failure; (3) the operator manual **§3.0b** "Reading the Agent Roster — two readings, not one"; (4) the **Trust UX FAQ**. **The honest consequence, now stated wherever the rate is explained:** on a blocked turn the delivered text is the platform's own withholding notice, so the delivered-text scorers deliberately ABSTAIN — and the turn is then counted as a quality failure **on evidence the platform chose not to gather**. Both blocked turns in the sample had ZERO failing gate-eligible measurements; the entire failure was the fold. Intended (a withheld answer must not read clean), and an undocumented exception to a stated rule is indistinguishable from a defect. **FAQ pass (the session's questions, verbatim):** +7 entries — §1.7 *who decides whether a turn passed*, §1.8 *the two readings + the 2×2*, §2.5 *does an amber measurement colour the station* (with the pre-Aug-2026 screenshot caveat), plus a **new §4 "The Agent Roster"** section (what the pass rate measures · what makes a bar green or red · why there is no amber bar · the run-row squares · *"my pass rate went UP after an update — was it wrong before?"* → yes, and why); 5 new troubleshooting rows (the unsupported-claim-without-a-gate-act = the ≥3 identifier floor; the amber square that looks red; the blocked turn that also counts as a quality failure; the sparkline's two heights); 2 new **known open items** (a guard that ERRORED reads like a guard that passed — `eval.gate.{outbound,inbound}="error"` on 2 real turns; and the roster names a quality figure with validity words while the mechanism axis has no surface at all). **Also repaired: the FAQ's section numbering was already inconsistent before this pass** — §4 held `6.x` entries, §5 held `4.x`, §6 held `5.x`, and there were TWO §5s; all sections and entries renumbered by scoped bounds, index anchors updated, and every in-page anchor verified to resolve (11 sections · 37 entries · 0 broken). Public trust site re-rendered (`render_trust_docs.py --check` → all 5 current). Docs-only: no code, no schema, no REST, no version pin. - **Aug 2026**: **The roster pass rate convicted turns under a RETIRED rule — a derived scalar frozen on the span outlived the policy that produced it**. Operator question while reading @UDERIA's roster card (`44% live pass rate · 18 turns · 10 failed · Danger`): *"who defines if a turn is failed — the mechanisms or the measurements? I would assume the mechanisms."* The code says the opposite, and answering it empirically found a defect. **The rule** (`eval/online.py:gating_failures`) is: a turn fails iff a **gate-eligible MEASUREMENT** landed in the danger band, **or** a runtime grounding gate BLOCKED — so measurements are the primary driver and a mechanism enters only as a block. Correct for a *quality* rate (the detail panel labels the section LIVE QUALITY), and it cannot be mechanism-driven: 16 of the operator's 18 turns had no mechanism act at all, so an intervention-based rate would read a comfortable-and-dishonest **89%** on an agent whose grounding measurements are the worst thing about it. **The defect:** `eval.gating_failures` is a DERIVED value **stored on the span at write time**, and a sink outlives a policy change. The recent `Verdict.gating` fix (making it a derived property because *"a stored field is a second copy every site must remember"*) stopped one level short — of this copy. So the sink held two eras side by side: spans where a failing `groundedness` correctly did NOT convict, beside spans where it did. On the live agent, **3 of the 10 "failures" were convicted by advisory dimensions alone** (`grounded_overlap` ×3, `groundedness` ×2, `context_utilization` ×1 across those turns; only `retrieval_relevance` is gate-eligible). Recomputed against the current registry: **7 failed of 18 → 61%**, which crosses the REVIEW floor — **the card should be AMBER, not red**. - **Aug 2026**: **An amber measurement could not colour its station — a band is not a state, and a station's measurements are now allocated, not delivered**. Operator finding on a real Focus turn: the Scorecard read `Context Utilization ·metric 0.56` in amber under **GROUNDED**, while the ring's GROUNDED segment beside it read **quiet** — contradicting the invariant that a segment is worst-of everything the station holds. **Root cause: two vocabularies collapsed into one field, overlapping on exactly one value.** A quality BAND (`healthy · review · danger`) is not a turn STATE (`pass · warn · danger · na · pending · unknown`); they share only `danger`. `assuranceDial.js` converted between them with **three hand-written aliases** — `b === 'healthy' ?
