Three symptoms, one cause: the station stayed green; the chip rendered grey (`ad-meas-review` matches no CSS rule); and it sorted LAST in a row specified worst-first. The companion `sc` field worked only by accident — `REFINEMENT_STATE` already emits states, so `sc || b` mixed two vocabularies in one expression. **The rule was stated four times** (`trustGrammar.BAND_STATE`, the three dial aliases, `routes.py`'s `band in ("review","danger")`, `assurance_points`'s `bad = {"danger","review"}`) and one of them was wrong — which is why JUDGED honoured review bands (server-side) while GROUNDED could not (client-side): one fact, two surfaces, two answers. **Fixed at the root, not the alias** (the operator's framing: *"we decided measurements are allocated to stations — the allocated station measurements must drive the ring"*). **(1) One bridge.** `assurance_points.BAND_STATE` ≡ `trustGrammar.BAND_STATE`, pinned byte-equal by a node-driven assertion. The registry resolves each measurement server-side into **`st`** (its station CONTRIBUTION, `dimension_state` — honours Rule 3.0c) and **`bst`** (the band as a state for its OWN chip, `band_state`), while `b` stays exactly as measured. The dial now converts **nothing**; the reverse relation it needs (a mechanism's state → a band, for Guide context rows) is derived by INVERTING the one map instead of being written out a fourth time. **(2) Allocation by ownership, not by courier.** New `allocate_measurements()` / `read_turn_measures()` assign each scored dimension to its station via `station_dimensions()` — owned to its owner, unowned residue to JUDGED — served as `assurance.measures`. Dimensions previously travelled as *cargo on a mechanism `Reading`*, which made the partition's totality an **emergent agreement between two independently-maintained lists** (`Scorer.applies_to` vs `AssurancePoint.applies`): a dimension whose scorer applied more widely than its owning mechanism was filtered out of JUDGED as foreign AND carried by nobody — **counted nowhere, invisibly**. Verified no such dimension exists today across all five classes (`rag_focused` comes within one list of it: `governed_data_ratio`/`no_tool_loops`/`tool_success_rate` are owned by non-applying mechanisms and simply are not scored there) — latent, not live, and now asserted. The renderer's `seen`-set union over `p.dims` is deleted: that was the renderer re-deriving station ownership by hand, and it is exactly the code that would have dropped an orphan. `apply_refinements()` extracted so `read_turn` and the allocation resolve a Rule 3.0c pair identically. **(3) The verb follows the state.** `"X is failing"` was written when only `danger` could reach that sentence — because `review` could not fold at all — so it convicted a review band the moment amber started arriving; now `"is in the review band"`. **Gates (the ones that would have caught it):** **G1** — per profile class, every dimension any scorer produces is allocated exactly once, disjoint, each record carrying a valid `st`/`bst` (`test_assurance_points` 229→**261**); **G2** — a `review`-band measurement raises **every one of the eight stations** to warn, is NAMED in the reading, and is not called a failure (`test_assurance_dial` 387→**400**); **G3** — the dial declares no band alias and reads the resolved contribution. En route the dial harness was found to load `trustCircle.js` but **never `trustGrammar.js`**, despite a comment claiming it exercised "the real attention vocabulary" — so it silently ran on literal fallbacks and could not have detected them drifting. **Three more implementation-pinning greps converted** (the seventh, eighth and ninth): `test_quality_card_partition` asserted the chip/sort behaviour by grepping two exact source lines — pinning an implementation, and they would have sailed through this very rewrite; both are now executed against the real extracted renderer (which now also extracts the shipped `_st` reader, the exact seam where a conversion would reappear). **And the two long-standing `test_trust_circle_routes` failures are closed** — stale greps for `tc-acted-tick`, a class the renderer stopped emitting when the count channel died; asserted as properties now (99 assertions, gate green for the first time in several sessions). **Battery:** dial 400 · partition 164 · grammar 1488 · routes 99 · pins 37 · assurance_points 261 · tally 30 · integrity 35 · gate_outcome · trust_events 50 · eval_online 91 · eval_analysis 83 · grounding 133 · guardrails 77 · review_queue 116 · posture_modes 78 · membrane 208 · trust_behavior 63 — all green. **Known pre-existing, not introduced:** `extract_trust_inventory` reports growth-only drift on `assuranceDial.js` (`tip-trust 1→3`, `aria 8→9`) — byte-identical with and without this change, left over from the prior session's icon-button/tooltip work and never re-baselined. **Server restart** for `agent/assurance_points.py` + `api/routes.py` + `templates/index.html`; JS `assuranceDial 5.4`. - **Aug 2026**: **The station partition rendered wrong on two surfaces — two latch/merge defects, both order-dependent, both root-caused**. An operator reading a real Focus turn found the Quality card listing all 20 checks under **JUDGED · 20 checks counted here** — attributing GROUNDED's two red chips (`grounded_overlap` 0.46, `numeric_fidelity` 0.60) to the wrong station, contradicting the dial beside it. The partition itself was intact throughout (`partition_conflicts()` → NONE); **both defects were in how the partition was READ.** **(1) The vocabulary latch recorded the attempt, not the success.** `stationOf` resolves through `ENTRY_STATION`, filled by one fetch. `ensureVocabulary` set `_vocabLoaded = true` at CALL ENTRY, so a second caller during flight got `Promise.resolve()` over an EMPTY table; and because the fetch's own `catch` resolves, a 401-before-login latched that emptiness for the whole page session. `ui.js` then kept a SECOND latch (`_stationVocabReady`) recording the same non-fact, so one miss disabled the warm for every later card. Fixes: `ensureVocabulary` memoises the **in-flight promise** and **un-latches unless entries actually registered** (retryable on 401/offline/empty payload); the ui.js latch is **deleted** — two latches over one fact IS the defect — and readiness is asked of the owner via a new `QD.stationsReady()`, the predicate that was missing (`stationOf` returning `'scored'` is indistinguishable from "no answer", which is exactly how an empty vocabulary rendered as a confident all-JUDGED card). **(2) Registration was first-writer-wins with a partial payload.** Two producers feed the same registry: the assurance dial registers the CURRENT TURN's points on every render (`guide_entry` — dims, **no station**), the vocabulary endpoint serves the full registry (dims AND station) when the Guide opens. `registerEntries` bailed on a known key (`if (DIM[e.k]) return;`) — right for the DEFINITION, silently "whoever registered first wins" for everything else. The dial always renders first, so a mechanism present on the turn was registered **station-less** and the richer vocabulary entry behind it was DISCARDED: `authority` kept its dims (its MEASURES chip rendered) and lost its station → `tool_subset`/`must_not_call` fell to the JUDGED residue, while `tool_enforcement` — absent from a Focus turn, never pre-registered — read BOUNDED correctly. **One partition, two answers, decided by load order.** Fixed at both ends: `registerEntries` is now **additive** (first DEFINITION wins; every other field fills in when missing — a richer payload completes an entry, a poorer one never downgrades it), and `guide_entry()` carries its `station`, completing a projection of the same registry that had been structurally incomplete. Each half stands alone (verified). **Also confirmed NOT a defect:** a measurement with no MEASURES row (e.g. `self_correction`) is correct — it measures the execution, not any mechanism's guarantee, so it is the JUDGED residue by definition. **Proof:** partition gate 77→**101** (§6 the warm path the old gate structurally could not see — it injected a working resolver: in-flight race, success-latches-once, failure-and-empty-payload-are-retryable, the banned second latch, and the REAL extracted `_paintQualityResults` through four repaint scenarios; §7 additive/order-independent registration + the complete backend projection); dial gate 386→**387** (its "registration never overwrites a real dimension" assertion was a grep for the guard's exact SOURCE LINE — it pinned an implementation, not a behaviour, and passed while that very guard discarded stations; now executes the module, and its localStorage stub is scoped so the pin assertions still read the gate's real one). **Mutation-tested**: reverting each of the four fixes fails exactly the intended assertions. Root: the gating fact is declared ONCE (`Scorer.gating` in the registry) but `Verdict.gating` was an implicit `True` default that **no construction site ever set**, so `eval.advisory_failures` (reading `gating is False`) could only ever be **0** — a dead field on a signed span whose own comment claimed "a dimension that merely wants a look is still visible". Fixed by making `Verdict.gating` a **derived property** resolving from the registry (a stored field is a second copy every site must remember; a property cannot be forgotten) — ONE change corrected three consumers at once (`gating_failures` ✓, `advisory_failures` 0→real, and the flag now serializes in `to_dict()`); `GET /v1/evals/turn-score` back-fills it when replaying spans persisted before the serialization, so no surface guesses. The headline now convicts only what is gate-eligible AND **drops nothing** — an advisory failure joins the review-band checks in one "flagged for review" count (gate-asserted: convictions + flagged == every non-clean verdict). Live: the real turn now reads `gating failures=0 · flagged for review=3`. **(4) "Quality" → "Scorecard".** It is the turn's FULL scorecard grouped by station, not the JUDGED station's card — the old name beside a JUDGED group invited exactly that misreading (and did: the operator read it as "the quality card, which reflects the judged station"). **(5) A station segment now lists BOTH its populations.** A station holds MECHANISMS (what ran) and MEASUREMENTS (what grades them) and its colour is worst-of both — but the dial's station panel drew one row per mechanism and none per measurement, so a station turned red by a measurement showed nothing but green dots, and the panel and the scorecard listed *different things under one station name* with nothing on screen saying they were different KINDS of thing. `measuresHtml()` renders the station's owned dimensions worst-first as Guide-routed chips (`data-dim`, the one navigation channel) under a "what it measures · N counted here" label, beside a "what ran" label on the mechanism rows; the chip shows the MEASUREMENT band (`b`), never the station contribution (`sc`), so Rule 3.0c's "the measurement is never rewritten" holds. Gate: **101 → 125** (§8 the summary arithmetic driven through advisory/gating/absent-flag/nothing-dropped; §9 `measuresHtml` executed against the REAL TrustGrammar rank — dedup across mechanisms, driver leads, empty station renders nothing). **(6) The measurements went blind exactly when the gate acted — ONE rule, stated once.** Driving a real blocked turn (judge panel `0✓/3✗`, answer withheld and parked) the operator asked why the measurements don't explain the block. They couldn't: once a gate acts, the delivered text is **Uderia's own withholding notice** — ~30 words that QUOTE the spans being reported as unsupported — and every scorer comparing delivered text against its sources then grades the platform's prose as the model's. `grounded_overlap` alone knew to abstain; `numeric_fidelity` scored **0.125 danger** and `context_utilization` **0.03** on that notice. So the gate acting manufactured a second failure at its own station AND blinded the diagnosis at the one moment it is wanted. Root: the rule lived inside ONE scorer instead of being stated once. New `RunRecord.platform_authored_answer()` — the single declaration, on the record every scorer already holds — returns *why* the delivered text is not the model's (grounding block/annotate · honesty rewrite · outbound-guardrail block; a guardrail REDACT is deliberately EXCLUDED — values are masked inside otherwise model-authored text, and abstaining would discard real signal). All three scorers ask it; none keeps a copy. Live-verified on the real blocked turn: the three delivered-text scorers now abstain while `retrieval_relevance` / `retrieval_performed` / `knowledge_freshness` still report — **the retrieval measurements are precisely the ones that explain the block**, and they survive. Delivered-turn baseline byte-identical (0.4634 / 0.6 / 0.234). **(7) The panel now STATES which population acts.** Listing both was not enough: with no statement of the relationship, proximity reads as causation, and the operator concluded the measurements open and close the gates — nothing on screen corrected it. `what ran · acted during the turn` / `what it measures · graded after · N counted here`, with the full rule one hover away from ONE `SUB_TIP` declaration ("nothing here can open or close a gate"), via the platform tooltip. Gate **125 → 138** (§10 the acts-vs-grades statement, executed with the REAL SUB_TIP strings; §11 one declaration, all three call sites, REDACT excluded, no private copies). **Mutation-tested**: reverting each of the five fails exactly the intended assertions. **(8) The Assurance Guide separated what DECIDES from what GRADES, and retired the label that caused the confusion.** `MEASURED BY` listed all nine of the grounding gate's dimensions under one heading — including the two judges it actually ESCALATES TO in-path (`groundedness` is what returned `0✓/3✗` and withheld the answer) beside the seven scorers that only grade it. A label ambiguous about direction over a list ambiguous about role. New `POINT_JUDGES` **declares** the in-path subset per mechanism (never inferred — a `…_judge` name pattern would catch purely post-hoc judges like `answer_correctness`), guarded by `judge_partition_conflicts()` (a declared judge the mechanism does not own is unreachable) and served on `guide_entry`. The Guide now renders **`escalates to`** (decisive) · **`checks on it`** (report-only), with a judge EXCLUDED from the second list, and the REVERSE direction carries the same split — **`decides for`** vs **`checks`** — because `groundedness` reading *"grades: Grounding gate"* while the gate read *"escalates to: Groundedness"* is one relation described two ways with the decisive half demoted. **Label:** `measured by` → **`graded by`** / **`grades`**. An active-voice variant (`checks on it` / `checks`) was tried to dodge the passive construction and **reverted** — the passive was never the problem, the conflated list was: once `escalates to` gives the decisive half its own name, "graded by" carries exactly the after-the-fact role a grade implies (a grade is awarded ON work already done and never becomes part of it). Worked example that settled it: on a turn the gate PASSED, `numeric_fidelity` then read "6/10 numbers grounded" — a report card on the gate's own decision, written after the answer had already shipped, changing nothing; one turn is noise, but 60% across 50 turns says the gate is too lenient for that agent, which the gate alone can never reveal. Gate **138 → 155**. Two more implementation-pinning greps found and converted: the dial ledger asserted the bidirectional-link property by grepping the exact `chipRow('measured by', RELATED[k])` source line, so renaming a misleading label broke two assertions while the property held perfectly — `relatedChips` is now an exported test seam and both are behavioural (this also removed a string-replace hack the partition gate needed to reach it). **(9) The acted dot said "a gate acted" — it is not gate-scoped.** Operator catch while reading the ring's grammar. `acted` is set by **nine** mechanisms and only **four** are gates: the other five are a tool DENIED by Agent Authority, a quarantined corpus document, documents withheld by the sensitivity ceiling, a retrieval-firewall chunk labelled untrusted, an item parked for review, and an integrity mismatch. The computation was always right; the WORD narrowed it and would send a reader hunting a gate that never fired. Corrected to **"a mechanism acted"** at all 15 sites across 5 files + the contract's Rule 9.3 (with the reason recorded). En route the legend was found to hardcode its own copy of the phrase instead of reading `TrustGrammar.TICK_ARIA[2]` — the same word could be spoken one way to a screen reader and another in the key beneath the mark, and the two DID drift the moment the noun changed; new `_actedWord()` reads the one vocabulary. Four operator findings on the new band, each fixed at the root. **(1) The dial stayed "still running" after completion (refresh fixed it).** `AssuranceDial.begin(sid,'live')` ran for EVERY SSE message, guarded only by `_live` — which the authoritative `inject()` clears. The cluster is now three 24px monochrome icon buttons (info / scales / target) with `u-tip` tooltips; state changes NEVER write `textContent` (the busy state spins the svg + retitles the tip; the judges toggle styles via `[aria-pressed]` CSS — no inline writes); `.ad-sub` became the row's flexible member (flex:1, min-width:0, ellipsis). **The dial is pinned by default** (built-in fallback true; a locked preference still wins both ways). **(3) ONE mark family — dots (PROP-002 §tick amendment).** PROP-002 had split the channels: owed → accent dot, engraving → KEPT ticks (I=detail, II=acted). Operator confusion proved the split failed: the engraved ticks were visually identical to the ring's retired owed double-tick, so the old grammar looked alive beside the new one. Guarded by a new verbatim-extraction gate **`test/test_posture_editor_roundtrip.mjs` (32 assertions)** pinning the F5-class contract: every stored mode round-trips populate→save unchanged (a stale checked property on the other posture can never leak into a save). Pinned rule: **enforce must do everything annotate does, plus suppression** — numeric-only concern now ANNOTATEs in enforce (0 tokens, never a judge escalation), and the judge-pass fold (`enforce.py`) re-attaches the numeric-only disclosure when the judge clears the scope trigger (the cleared refs are NOT re-accused); `GroundingVerdict.numeric_concern` carries the flag through `to_event()`. **(3) Retention default (`APP_CONFIG.REVIEW_RETAIN_ENFORCED_BLOCKS`, default ON):** a FULL withholding under plain enforce (grounding BLOCK, outbound toxicity BLOCK) parks its original as a new **`retained`** review-queue status — a *recovery ledger*: recoverable + dispositionable but **never owed** (excluded from `pending_count`, the inbox badge, and the REVIEWED station, whose config stays keyed on `review` mode — collapsing them would make "we have human oversight" indistinguishable from "we keep a trash can"). Grounding parks through the ONE `_park_review` seam (status param), guardrails through `_park(status=)`. **(4) Retention bounds (the queue grew forever):** settled + retained items age out after `RETENTION_DAYS`=90, `retained` capped per user at `RETAINED_CAP`=200 oldest-first, **`pending` never auto-pruned** (owed work must not silently vanish); pruning is opportunistic on each park. **Surfaces kept honest:** the reviews endpoint returns a separate `retained` count and accepts `?status=retained`; `decide()` accepts retained (409 message → "not open"); the Assurance Inbox renders a collapsed "N recoverable originals retained (no action owed)" section that never touches badges/severity folds/station ticks; the answer capsule gained a `retained` branch ("withheld — original retained · no action owed" — previously it would have fallen through to "withholding upheld by the owner", a decision nobody made); trust-history + agent-story label retained items distinctly; `disposition_index` already whitelists approved/rejected (unaffected). Operator finding: the trust rings read "inconsistent and hard to understand" — root-caused to the grammar being defined bottom-up per surface: trust.css openly declared TWO colour idioms (verdict vs triage) for the same three colours; the double-tick meant *a gate acted* on the dial and *an act is owed* on the ring (same mark, opposite tense); the dial spoke six states while the ring's legend named four and the mini glyph rendered `pending`/`unknown` as **invisible segments** (missing CSS); `pending` carried three different words at three sites (one branch unreachable); the Quality chips used private theme-invariant band hexes beside the tokens; and the inbox printed raw wire severities while an honesty block read `warning` there and `danger` on the dial for the identical stamp. - **Aug 2026**: **Rule 3.0c — when two measures of ONE property disagree, the disagreement is REPORTED, never resolved by weighting**. Campaign 1 left one design question open: `grounded_overlap` (coarse lexical, median 0.27) disagreed with `groundedness` (the judge that by its own description *refines* it, median 1.00) on 12 of 14 turns, so GROUNDED took worst-of and read `danger` permanently — **a station that can never go green gets ignored** (§8's reasoning, applied to a measure instead of an act). Both obvious fixes are dishonest: **weighting the judge** builds a composite with invisible arithmetic (Rule 4.3 permits one only because the drill-down names its driver) and makes the colour depend on whether a *sampled* judge ran (a Rule 3.5 denominator problem wearing a fix's clothes); **demoting the pre-signal** silences a check that runs on every turn in favour of one that runs on some, so a lenient verdict becomes a green station. Both answer *"which measure is right?"* — the wrong question. Rule 3.0b had already written the answer (*"a corroborated failure … vs the check disagreeing with the judge"*); this completes that sentence at the station's reading. **Declared** `REFINEMENT_PAIRS = {grounded_overlap: groundedness}` beside the partition, with a five-row truth table: both fail → **danger** (corroborated) · judge only → **danger** (it reads meaning) · **coarse only → warn (DISPUTED)** · both pass → quiet · judge didn't run → the coarse check stands alone at full weight. No new state, no weighting. **Three constraints keep it honest:** (1) the measurement is NEVER rewritten — the dimension reports the band it measured (`b`, what the chip shows) and a separate *station contribution* (`sc`) is what the station folds in; (2) nothing is silenced — a disputed turn still colours amber, still counts, and is **named** in the qualifier ("N turns flagged by the coarse lexical check and cleared by the judge that refines it") and the derivation; (3) the pair is declared, never inferred, and must live on ONE station. **One declaration, two server-side computations, renderers hold no opinion:** `read_turn` emits per-turn `sc`/`disp` for the dial, and `eval/analysis` emits `turn_disputed_dims` for the ring's window — the aggregator is the only place that can tell *"the judge passed"* from *"the judge never ran"*, and it IMPORTS the map rather than restating it. The ring's disputed-only turns leave the rate alone and **floor** the station at warn (never lowering a danger); an older payload without `turn_disputed_dims` keeps the pre-rule reading byte-identical. **Why this is the transparent choice, concretely:** had the surface reported the disagreement, the C5 scorer defect would have announced itself instead of needing a forensic dig — a rule that makes a latent defect self-reporting beats one that makes a number look better. Explicitly **does not weaken worst-of (Rule 5.1)**, which governs aggregation *across agents* where one agent's health cannot excuse another's exposure; this governs two measures of one property on one turn, where a disagreement is evidence *about the measures*. **Live-verified on real turns** (all five rows: G5 disputed→warn+named · G3 corroborated→danger · G7 judge-only→danger · G2/G4/G6 agreed→pass · G1 no pair). CI: assurance_points 145→**167** (truth table, the band-never-rewritten assertion, judge-absent), grammar 1,350→**1,357** (disputed/corroborated/legacy-payload fixtures); regression-clean across eval_analysis 75 · eval_deterministic 58 · posture_modes 60 · grounding 110 · dial 377 · routes 97 · inventory 498. - **Aug 2026**: **Live Trust-Circle campaign (Focus) — a reproducible suite, and the five reporting defects it found**. New `test/trust_campaign/` (approach README · `suite.py` cases+invariants · `run_campaign.py` runner · `analyse.py` · `FINDINGS.md`): 16 live cases through @UDERIA (`rag_focused`), **one new session per case**, judges forced ON at rate 1.0 and restored in a `finally`, posture untouched so the signed baseline stays valid. It measures the three surfaces that must agree about one turn — the assurance dial (`assurance.by_station`), the Quality card (scored verdicts) and the ring (aggregate) — with **nine universal invariants per case** plus a per-turn partition audit. Final: **16/16 cases, 128/128 invariant checks, 0 double counts**; the gate blocked judge-confirmed hallucination on 5 turns and parked each; both injection shapes were refused at the door; the privacy invariant held (labels only, never a matched value). **Five defects found, fixed, pinned.** **(C1)** a `review`-armed gate stamped the `enforce` it resolves to internally, so REVIEWED read *"no gate is set to park answers for a human"* on an agent with three gates in review — while the ring, reading profile config, said it could park (two instruments, one fact, two answers). Fixed with ONE helper `posture_modes.stamped_mode()` routed through all four runtimes rather than four inline copies. **(C2)** a request **refused at the door** left six downstream mechanisms reading `unknown` ("should have recorded and did not"), putting GROUNDED and BOUNDED into attention on the *best* outcome the guard can produce; their silence is structural (nothing to screen, ground or seal), so `turn_refused_inbound` + `_POST_DOOR_POINTS` now read `na` **with the cause named**. **(C3)** JUDGED's pass sentence appended a count to a finished clause (*"every check this station owns passed of 10 checks owned here"*). **(C4)** a turn that scored **nothing** read *"every check passed"* — the vacuous clean Rule 3.7 bans — now `na`, *"no check ran on this turn"*. **(C5, the deepest)** `grounded_overlap` was measuring **text the model never wrote**: when the gate blocks, the delivered text is Uderia's own withholding notice — which *quotes the unsupported spans it is reporting*, so it is engineered to fail an overlap check and the gate acting **manufactured a second grounding failure at the same station**; and the support set was the retrieved documents ALONE while `corpus.assess` has always included the question, so an answer echoing the user's terms was scored as invention. Both fixed (abstain on platform-generated text; question joins the support set) — on the same 14 answers 4 correctly abstain and real answers score honestly (0.40→**0.60 healthy**, 0.33→0.44, 0.00→0.20), no bare 0.0 remains. **A third change was tried and REVERTED the same hour, and the revert is the more useful lesson**: gating on "does the answer make a groundable claim" made `FOCUS_HALLUCINATION` (*"Quantum entanglement enables faster-than-light teleportation of refunds"*) **abstain**, because a fluent fabrication carries no number, quote or identifier — the existing CI fixture caught it; a refusal and a fabrication are lexically alike and separating them is the *judge's* job, which is why this scorer is documented as the pre-signal the judge refines (reasoning recorded in-code so it is not re-attempted). **Reported, deliberately NOT acted on (governance):** GROUNDED still reads danger on 13/16 because `grounded_overlap` (median 0.27 vs a 0.5 default) and `retrieval_relevance` (0.46 vs 0.4) are calibrated for a different answer style and embedding model than this deployment's (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2` + a paraphrasing model over technical prose), while the judge that refines them reads 1.00 — a station that can never go green gets ignored, so the operator tunes the thresholds (Trust → GROUNDED) or takes up the design proposal (weight the judge / drop the pre-signal to informational once a judge verdict exists). Docs synced: `qualityDimensions.js` LONG (user-facing Guide) + `AGENT_QUALITY_DIMENSIONS.md` row + a measurement-contract note in `AGENT_OPS_EVAL_ARCHITECTURE.md` + the contract's one-source row for `stamped_mode` + the operator manual & public trust site (reading REVIEWED armed, and refused-at-the-door). Three related trust-surface changes. **(1) Trust Trip** (`docs/roadmap/TRUST_TRIP_RESET.md`): the odometer (whole record) never resets; a **trip reset** appends an audited per-agent MARKER (who/when/note/the agent's integrity state at that moment via `turn_integrity_stamp`) and the **trip lens** re-windows the ring's execution readings to "since the marker" — after fixing an agent, "how is it doing *since* the fix" is answerable immediately, and the derivation explainers compare the leg against the previous one (*did the fix work?*). Marker store `core/trust_trip.py` (self-applying `trust_trip_markers`, **append-only by design** — no UPDATE/DELETE path exists; reads fail-open, the write fails loud; NOT part of the removable Ontology Suite). REST: `POST /v1/assurance/trust-trip/<tag>/reset` (owner-scoped) + `GET …/trust-trip/<tag>` (leg logbook); resets appear in Trust History (`trip_reset`) + the agent story (`trip` block + an "Interlude · A new leg" chapter). **The trip cell is the SAME aggregator run twice** (W4 — never a second implementation): the dashboard runs `online_quality_by_agent` over `trust_trip.spans_since(spans, markers)` and attaches `by_agent[key].trip` (same shape + `since`/`note`/`leg_n`/`integrity_state` + a `prev` previous-leg sub-cell), so the whole focused-ring machinery consumes it unchanged via one frontend seam (`_lensCell`). UX: *Whole record · This leg* pill-pair + leg chip on the ring's stage (`trustCircle.js` `model.lens`, absence-tolerant), "Start a new leg" act with inline two-step confirm + recorded note in the narrative panel (`model.trip.onReset` → `_startNewLeg` → auto-switch to the honest EMPTY leg). **Contract rules** ([TRUST_STATUS_COMMUNICATION.md §10](Architecture/TRUST_STATUS_COMMUNICATION.md)): a lens re-windows, never re-writes (total lens byte-identical, CI-pinned); every lens-scoped reading names its boundary ("since 30 Jul"; an empty leg reads "empty, not clean", never "no data"); canonical trust (TRUSTED composite, breaker, audit pack, attestations) NEVER re-windows — the leg is one labelled informational line beside it; chip-less surfaces (roster/tree mini-glyphs) are never lens-scoped (the one derivation site is lens-guarded + gated). Estate trip = each agent since ITS OWN reset where one exists, mix disclosed ("4 of 9 have an open leg"). **(2) Turn-sealed SIGNED**: the turn dial's `integrity` stamp is sealed AT ANSWER TIME (`composition.turn_integrity_stamp` via the assurance tally in `executor.run()` + genie's own turn assembly); the turn endpoint's live-resolve is REMOVED (it retroactively flipped historical turns' SIGNED when an agent changed); absent stamp = honest "not recorded when this turn ran"; `resolve_profile_trust` is CI-banned from `api/routes.py`. **(3) Estate ring worst-of**: GROUNDED/GUARDED/JUDGED estate execution = worst-of over per-agent bands (`_estateExecRollup`, same banding as the focused ring → the estate never reads better than the worst drill-down; was proportional — 9/10 clean rendered green over a red agent). **Proof:** `test_trust_trip.py` (23) new; grammar gate → **1,300** (trip-lens + estate worst-of sections, full grammar asserted under the lens), routes 89, dial 376, assurance points/integrity 100/35 (§4c replay + §5b live-resolve ban); live-verified end-to-end (reset → empty leg → turn accrues 1/0 vs prev 33/21 · story/history/logbook · historical turn reads "not recorded" instead of today's badge). Server restart; JS versions `agentPerformanceHandler 9.0`, `trustCircle 5.0`, `trust.css 9.3`. - **Aug 2026**: **Trust Circle — the "?" derivation explainer, and JUDGED renamed SCORED**. Two changes from one question: *how do the ring's figures relate to the Quality card's?* **(1) The explainer.** Pinning a station now surfaces a `?` opening a distinct zone — **never a fifth slot** (Rule 3.0) — carrying the **population** the figure was measured over (the fact that actually resolves the confusion: *the ring counts TURNS, the Quality card counts CHECKS*), how each attribute was derived, and the contributing quality dimensions as **clickable chips** that open the existing Dimension Guide, scoped to that station with each dimension's live band. The ring never defines a dimension itself — it routes `explain-dim:<key>` through the one navigation channel to `QualityDimensions.openGuide`, because a second glossary is the drift this codebase keeps paying for. **Four of the eight stations read no quality dimensions at all** (SIGNED · BOUNDED · REVIEWED · PROVEN) and now say so — leaving it unsaid implied the ring is a view onto the Quality card, which it is not. A dimension the agent's class never produces renders **dashed**, not dropped (dropping overstates what the station watches; showing it as a pass would be worse). Each derivation is built from the **same variables that produced the figure**, so the prose cannot drift from the number above it; `trust_dims`/`trust_dim_weight` now travel on the trust-behavior payload so TRUSTED names the real weighted list instead of hardcoding a second copy. **(2) JUDGED → SCORED**, label *and* key. Of the 51 dimensions **42 are deterministic code and only 9 are LLM judges** — "Judged" over-claimed the judge layer (its own subtitle existed to walk the name back) and collided with the platform's *literal* judges, which the Quality card marks with dashed chips; the backend has always said *score* (`eval/scorers/`, `score-turn`, `turn-score`), so the ring was the surface that lagged. **A proposed reorder (SCORED to position 2) was assessed and NOT made, with reasons:** the ring encodes the **runtime** order — grounding and guardrails run *in-path during* the turn (they can withhold an answer), scoring runs *after* it as a background task — so moving the post-hoc measurement ahead of the in-path controls would be factually backwards, and the "Play its life" chapters narrate the ring order as a biography ("born → scored → learned to be grounded" is not a life). The real relationship is **containment, not sequence**: SCORED is the *union* over every applicable dimension, and GROUNDED/GUARDED are **lenses onto the same turns** — so their turns are a subset and SCORED can never read better than they do. Position on a ring cannot express that; the explainer states it **on both sides**, since a relationship visible from only one end reads as a coincidence. **Swept for completeness:** every `judged` occurrence across code, tests, docs and the public trust site was classified — the station renamed, the *judge concept* and the eval payload's `judged` flag deliberately untouched; the two historical records (this changelog's Jul-2026 entries, `TRUST_CIRCLE_WALKTHROUGH_STATUS.md`) are **preserved, not rewritten**, with a naming note added so a reader isn't confused. Also fixed en route: a genuine `(s)` placeholder in the Trust Journey strip (a contract ban the gate does not scan). Gate **855 → 934** (+79), mutation-tested — reverting the label, dropping a station's honesty note, dropping a containment claim, and silently dropping an unmeasured dimension each fail exactly the intended assertions; the harness now also extracts the real `HEALTHY`/`REVIEW` floors and loads the real `qualityDimensions.js` under Node. Contract gains **§3b** (Rules 3b.1–3b.6 + the naming rationale), two one-source rows and a checklist step; the operator manual and the **public trust site** gain a "Where the numbers come from" section. JS: `agentPerformanceHandler 7.5` · `trustCircle 3.6` · `trustJourney 1.9` · `trust.css 5.7`. Server restart for `rest_routes.py` + `index.html`; JS/CSS browser-reload. - **Aug 2026**: **Trust Circle deep-assessment remediation — the seal must not lie (Wave 1–3, tested)**. A four-lens adversarial audit (frontend ring · backend trust core · API/data-flow · docs+gate) of every Trust-Circle artefact surfaced **1 Critical, 12 High, ~30 Medium** defects — *all blind spots of the seven green gates*, which was the audit's second-loudest result. Full record: `docs/assessments/TRUST_CIRCLE_DEEP_ASSESSMENT_2026-08.md` (living status table at the top). **The Critical (TC-1):** signing a **genie coordinator hashed `genieConfig.slaveProfiles` in raw-id space while the badge resolved in tag space**, so every coordinator read 🟠 CHANGED the instant it was signed and no coordinator pack member could ever reinstate — the exact "coordinator packs permanently amber" failure the tag-space mechanism was built to prevent, unfixed on three of four hash surfaces. Fixed by threading the id→tag resolver through `sign_agent`, `pack.agent_live_hash` and the REST `_artifact_live_hash` (one canonical call, as the docstring already claimed); the mirror test had stubbed both sides without `id_to_tag`, which is why 183 assertions missed it. **The seal-must-not-lie cluster (fail-open where design says fail-closed):** the artifact badge **returned TRUSTED when the live hash could not be computed** (opposite fail direction from the composition path that BLOCKS the same fault) — now a `_NO_LIVE_HASH` sentinel distinguishes "kind has no resolver" (TRUSTED fallback) from "resolver ran and could not confirm" (→ CHANGED); an attestation recorded with **`signed=0`** (provenance key absent) **still read green** — `attested_hash` now honours the signed flag everywhere (mirroring `portability.capture`); the **downgrade guard was bypassable** by omitting a mode/flag sub-path from a present block (shallow `dict.update` reverts it to the weaker default) — now compared to the runtime default like floors already were; **knowledge-repo applicability didn't mirror the runtime** in either direction (composition defaulted `enabled` True, engines default False, Focus ignores it) so a `rag_focused` agent with `enabled:false` could **sign 🟢 without its entire corpus** (the F1 hole reopened) — now per-class; and **composition/deployment fetch failures silently narrowed the signature** (a whole ingredient class or connector opt-in vanishing while the badge read intact) — per-collection failures now emit a blocking `unresolved` ingredient, planner repos gained the empty-vs-unreadable asymmetry, connector-state failure marks `UNRESOLVED` not `[]`, and `describe_drift` now names intra-connector tool widening + UNRESOLVED transitions instead of showing an empty amber. **API perimeter:** the Ed25519-**signed audit pack shipped with an always-empty derived-incidents section** (a `dispositions` NameError swallowed by a blanket except — the compliance artifact attested an understated record) → fixed + no longer hidden; **`GET /v1/evals/online` leaked all users' quality spans** (session ids, judge evidence quoting answers) with no gate → scoped to the caller, `scope=system` behind VIEW_ALL_SESSIONS; the **TRUSTED station narrated "circuit breaker off" even under `freeze_autonomy`** (the endpoint never returned `breaker_mode`) → added; **live-redteam ownership failed open on NULL-owner collections** (any user could ingest adversarial docs into a shared collection and have cleanup delete its rows) → fails closed. **Frontend grammar (the ring is the differentiator):** the **posture matrix could crash the entire Agents view** from one malformed profile, hand-rolled a mode ladder **omitting `review`** (the exact §0 defect class), and ignored the deployment masters → all routed through the canonical `_cfgMode`/`_actingMode`/masters; **raw wire tokens** `deployment_unattested` and `at_risk` rendered verbatim on user-facing chips → human labels via the seal vocabulary (`TrustBadge.META`) + `TRUST_STATE_LABEL`, with `changed` severity aligned to danger on both surfaces; the roster mark + coordination-tree glyph **collapsed `deployment_unattested` into the unsigned seal** (a publisher-signed agent looked never-signed) → four distinct seal shapes + `--trust-seal-unattested`; `api()` **discarded error bodies** (a refused review-release showed "HTTP 400") → parses the server reason; **all `(s)` placeholders** on rendered surfaces (story chapters, sparkline, matrix, probe) → routed through `_plural`; an **unescaped `p.color`** style-attribute sink → `esc()`; stale inbox counters on fetch failure → zeroed; emoji (`🟢`/`⚠`/`✗`/`✓`) → words / monochrome SVG. **The gate that missed all of this is now stronger:** `test/test_trust_circle_grammar.mjs` extracts `TRUST_STATE_LABEL` verbatim (faithful, fails loud on rename) and gained a focused-`at_risk` fixture proving no wire token leaks — **804 assertions** (was 801). **Proof:** every fix landed with the assertion that would have caught it — trust_membrane **201** (+18: TC-1 genie sign/resolve, TC-3/4/5/21), trust_deployment **114** (+6: TC-25/26), profile_config_contract **102** (+3, two buggy-behaviour assertions corrected), grammar gate **804** (+3); regression-clean across posture_modes 51 · trust_events 29 · review_queue 70 · grounding 102 · guardrails 57 · agent_authority 58. **Pass 2 (same day) closed the entire remaining backlog — nothing from the findings list is open.** **AuthZ:** leaf sign-offs now enforce per-kind OWNERSHIP (`trust_routes._assert_owner` — ontology/collections/flow/dashboard/canvas/pack resolve their owner and fail **CLOSED** on a lookup error or NULL owner, the TC-33 lesson; skill/extension stay tier-gated — platform-level, no owner exists); the six offline eval-store endpoints (`runs`/`scores`/`clusters`/`diff`/`annotations`) sit behind `_eval_store_gate` (VIEW_ALL_SESSIONS — instance-global ops data, and annotations feed judge calibration); system-scope trust-behavior keys cells **`tag::uuid`** (`assess_agents(per_user=True)` — two users' same-tag agents never merge, requester integrity caps only the requester's own cells) with ONE frontend resolver `_tbAgent()` covering both key shapes; every sign/attest now **broadcasts live** (`_notify_sign_off` → `broadcast_notice` — the last gap in the standing live-emission rule). **TC-8 closed for real:** `_selfDash()` restricts system-scope execution cells to the caller before ANY station reads them, so both attributes of an estate reading share one subject — gate-asserted as *subject invariance* (foreign cells change nothing on all 8 stations) and **mutation-tested** (disabling it fails exactly the 4 intended assertions). **Gate 804 → 855:** the attention vocabulary is asserted identical across all four sites that carry it (handler `_ATTN_WORD` ↔ ring chip ↔ legend ↔ routing summary); the gate now loads the REAL `qualityDimensions.js` under Node so CI exercises `QD.label()` — and its own two-name regex (`/Grounded Overlap|Grounding Overlap/`, the exact forbidden defect) is killed; extraction-anchor uniqueness; PROVEN `1 sealed` (never a dressed bare count); Rule 5.4 laggard naming; a Rule 3.3 doctrine sweep over every slot; `stationPanel` pin lifecycle (actions only when pinned, routes survive pinning); `glyph()` per-state segments + `_attentionSummary` na-exclusion on the RENDERED tally; renderer STATIONS ≡ STATION_KEYS. **The Low backlog (TC-60..97) is closed** — highlights: unreferenced `create_task(q.put(...))` notification emits → `put_nowait` at all 5 sites (GC-droppable-task class); `review_queue` named columns + tri-state `decide` (store failure → 503, never "item is not pending"); connector-state/profile-id failures hash UNRESOLVED; `verify()` returns `key_source` (carried vs local key — never mistakable for publisher authentication); trust-history never mixes epoch-strings into the ISO sort; agent-story reads BOTH repo binding fields (knowledge-typed); `::` foreign-agent guards on story/history; live-redteam derives its self-call URL from the real port; ring Escape/story timers guarded by visibility; trustBadge caches keyed to the auth token (user-switch), topmost-only dialog Escape, u-tip conversions, `Re-sign` label preserved on failure; HEALTH palette routed through the trust tokens via color-mix (one green vocabulary in light mode); `BAND_ICON` ✓/✕ dingbats → currentColor SVGs in both consumers; `_applyGlyph` whitelists to `TrustBadge.META` icons. Five Lows are recorded as **deliberate design limits** with in-code documentation (60/68 hash-substrate — a fix invalidates every existing attestation; 64 license fail-open until the Enterprise flip, search key `TRUST_LICENSE_FAIL_OPEN`; 69 sign TOCTOU — fail-safe direction; 79 verify enumeration). Contract gains Rules **3.5/3.6/3.7** (figure-carries-denominator · structural-zero · no-vacuous-clean) + **4b.8** (leading route follows the driver) + gate-coupled one-source rows. - **Jul 2026**: **Trust Circle — the offered act follows the state; shape carries integrity; both attributes share one subject (walkthrough closeout)**. Driving the ring through a real signing cycle on @UDERIA (Focus) and contrasting it with an unsigned @IDEAT surfaced three defects, all of the same family the earlier waves kept finding — *a reading that looks settled while the decision-relevant fact is missing or wrong*. **(1) The most prominent action performed an act that could not help.** SIGNED offered **"Sign this agent"** for a `deployment_unattested` agent — which is already publisher-signed and intact. What is outstanding there is the *other* half of the two-hash envelope: this instance attesting its own resolved model, reachable tool catalog and connector opt-ins, which never travel with a pack. A primary CTA that cannot move the state is worse than none, because it reads as the fix. Fixed by deriving the act from the state (`attest` vs `sign` vs `re-sign` vs `verify`) — and, critically, by **exporting the attest act as `TrustBadge.attestDeployment()` so ONE implementation serves both callers** (the badge popover, which already had it inline, and the ring); the ring routes to it exactly as it routes `sign-agent`, in place, so the reading you acted on stays on screen. Guarded so an older trust package without the deployment half offers no button rather than one that fails on click. **(2) Unsigned and unattested were visually identical.** Colour is committed to *attention priority*, so two states that need you equally are the same amber — correct by the declared grammar, but it left two genuinely different jobs indistinguishable. The answer was **not a fifth state**: SIGNED is the one station whose subject already has a published visual vocabulary — the Trust Membrane seal on profile cards, marketplace listings and the badge popover — and the ring was the single surface disagreeing with it. The station now **borrows `TrustBadge.META[state].icon`**: *shape carries integrity, colour carries attention*, neither encodes the other (shield+check = attested · shield with dashed lower half = not attested here · warning triangle = changed · dashed circle = unsigned). **Deliberately SIGNED-only** — the other seven have no vocabulary to inherit, and inventing one per station is the drift this grammar exists to prevent; a station may supply an optional `glyph`, and absent one the renderer keeps its own icon (absence-tolerant: the trust package is removable, and the grammar gate executes this code under Node where `window` is a ReferenceError). Estate scope supplies none — no single integrity state can stand for ten agents. **(3) REVIEWED mixed two scopes in one pair.** Its configuration side is per-agent by construction (this agent's gate modes) while its execution side read the estate badge, so a focused agent with an empty queue reported the estate's three items as its own — the exact confusion the two-attribute model was introduced to end. Fixed by attributing inbox items to agents **at the single point the estate count is computed** (one pass, one source, so the focused reading can never disagree with the badge above it); the estate figure and any **estate-level items belonging to no agent** are still named in the hover, so a focused zero can never read as "the inbox is empty". **Also fixed, same family:** a focused SIGNED rendered `0/1` — the scope size wearing a ratio's clothes, identical for a never-signed agent and one owing only the local attestation — now the state word (`unsigned` / `not attested here` / `attested` / `changed`), with the ratio kept for estate scope where it is real; and the `deployment_unattested` headline claimed *"no baseline exists"* while the Why slot on the same panel said the publisher signature was intact. **De-noised:** `trust.composition` logged an identical WARNING on every badge resolution for a profile bound to a deleted collection (~40 lines/session for one `@FOCUS` fault) — which does not make the fault more visible, it makes every other warning less visible; now once per (profile, collection) per process, first line carrying the full fact and naming the consequence ("its retrieval is silently inert"). **Gate strengthened where it had been blind:** all three `deployment_unattested` defects were **prose contradicting the state it described**, and the 548-assertion suite caught none of them because it asserted structure only. `test/test_trust_circle_grammar.mjs` now also asserts subject-consistency across both scopes, state-derived actions, the borrowed-not-invented seal, and an explicit **prose-vs-state contradiction** class — **572 assertions**, mutation-tested (reverting the CTA, reinstating the contradicting headline, and re-leaking the estate count each fail exactly the intended assertion). Regression-clean: trust_membrane 183 / trust_deployment 108 / posture_modes 51 / profile_config_contract 99. Docs: `TRUST_STATUS_COMMUNICATION.md` gains **Rule 8.4** (use an existing second channel rather than a fifth state) and **Rule 8.5** (the offered act must be the act that is owed), two rows in the one-source table, and two checklist steps; the operator manual gains the seal-shape table and the same-subject rule. **Residue kept honest:** outstanding work still shares amber with a measured shortfall, distinguished by shape at SIGNED and by text elsewhere — a general fifth state should still wait for evidence operators confuse *"a control under-performed"* with *"an act is owed"*; and the dangling-binding fault has no UI surface yet (where it belongs — profile editor vs posture matrix — remains open). Server restart for `composition.py` + `index.html`; JS versions `trustCircle 3.1` / `agentPerformanceHandler 5.1` / `trustBadge 1.3`. - **Jul 2026**: **Trust Circle station grammar — two attributes, attention-priority colour, and the contract made enforceable (walkthrough findings 4–7)**. A station-by-station walkthrough of the Trust Circle for the Focus class (@UDERIA / Uderia Expert) surfaced four defects; the first was a live bug, the rest were communication defects in the same family — *a comfortable-looking reading that hides the thing you need*. **(F5, live bug) Inbound guardrail `review` could not be saved.** The profile editor's *population* validator for the inbound mode read `['observe','annotate','enforce']` — omitting `review`, so a stored `review` **displayed as Observe** and the next Save then persisted that downgrade: *a protection silently weakened by opening and saving a form*. The value was reaching the DB correctly all along; only the redisplay was wrong, which is why it read as "it doesn't save". Root cause was **five hand-rolled copies** of the posture-mode ladder in `configurationHandler.js` (four had `review`, the inbound one — added in a later wave — did not, 35 lines below a comment explicitly warning about this exact trap). Fixed with ONE `POSTURE_MODES` + `pickMode()` mirroring `core/posture_modes.py`; no inline copy remains. **(F6) Estate GROUNDED/GUARDED reported a false green.** `_modeLadderState` used `.some()` over the whole estate, so **1 acting agent of 10 rendered green** — the strongest member reported as the state of the whole, while SIGNED and BOUNDED in the same panel already aggregated worst-of. Fixed with ONE declared policy `_postureAggregate` (classify per agent → aggregate worst-of; `danger` reserved for a *detected discrepancy*, never a chosen default, or a fresh install would ship red and teach operators to ignore red), applied by all four config stations. Amber is made actionable by naming the laggards (`not acting: @IDEAT, @OPTIM +6 more`). **Proven to move only what it should: exactly 2 of 88 station rows changed** (estate grounded/guarded `pass→warn`); all 80 per-agent rows byte-identical, so focused rings and roster mini-glyphs did not shift. **(F4) REVIEWED read "the Assurance Inbox is clear — every layer quiet" while a danger-severity item sat in that inbox.** The counter was *correct* (`pendingReviews + unacked`; derived observations are recomputed from the sealed trace and carry no disposition, and counting them would make a badge that can never reach zero — the same rationale used elsewhere). The defect was that no slot existed in which the finding *could* appear. **(F7) Configuration and execution were mixed in one value slot.** Three stations rendered `profiles.length` / `states.length` — always `1` for a focused agent: a constant that reads like a measurement, while the decision-relevant fact (the mode) hid in the hover. **The fix for F4+F7 is one model:** every station now carries **two attributes** — *configuration* (design effectiveness: would it work?) and *execution* (operating effectiveness: did it?) — rendered as a fixed-order pair `config · execution` where an absent side is an explicit `—`, never collapsed (SIGNED has no dial: signing is an act; BOUNDED has no execution data: denials aren't aggregated). Hover = four fixed slots **Configuration · Execution · Why · Evidence**, with **Evidence mandatory** — which closes F4 *structurally* rather than by wording. Doctrine ("graded in code first — 51 dimensions", "receipts export from every capsule") was removed: true, but not a reading. **Colour was re-purposed to ATTENTION PRIORITY, not a dimension** — with eight stations the only decision is *where to look next*, so the highest-salience channel is spent on that (`quiet` / `worth a look` / `needs you now` / `not turned on`; the existing words already said "needs attention" and "quiet"). Attention = `worst-of(design, execution)` and **a composite is honest only because the drill-down names its driver** — a colour ramp needs an ordinal scale, and while `(config, execution)` pairs have no legitimate ordering, attention does; `_assemble()` writes the driver unconditionally so no call site can omit it. This **corrected an earlier recommendation in this same review** to colour by design with an exception badge: the badge existed only because colour was spent on the wrong job. A **routing summary** ("1 needs you now — JUDGED · 3 worth a look") removes the visual-search task, `na` is excluded from the tally (a chosen default must not put a fresh install in alarm), and a danger-only pulse respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. Also folded in: `deployment_unattested` now reads **amber** rather than dashed (publisher-signed but not attested *here* is genuinely partial; dashed implies nothing is left to do — zero blast radius today, and it is the exact state an operator enters mid-signing), and an **unresolvable** `authorityScope` classifies `warn`, never `na` (unknown authority must not read as "nothing enabled"). **Assessed and NOT changed, with reasons:** a proposed second matrix surface was **rejected** — the eight stations are non-commensurable (`3/4 grounded` vs `0 open` share no scale), so column alignment buys nothing, the commensurable comparison (agents × controls) is already the existing posture matrix, and a second renderer of the same model is the drift risk this very review kept finding; risk-weighting the aggregate was rejected as a fabricated composite that would break the named-driver contract. **Known gap left open, not papered over:** the four-state grammar has no state for *"a required act has not been performed"* — an unsigned agent reads `not turned on`, implying nothing is left to do, while `warn` would overstate it; resolving it needs a fifth state or a relabel (CSS, glyph shapes, legend, mini-glyph, story chapters). Two other open findings recorded: the acknowledge-finding path uses a native `window.prompt()` (violates the platform's no-native-dialogs standard, on the critical corpus-signing gate), and the ring/posture matrix can *show* unsigned but cannot sign — signing lives only on the profile trust seal. **Verification (method matters here):** the real `_circleStationsFor()` was extracted verbatim and executed against **live REST payloads** for all ten agents in both scopes — which caught five defects a reimplementation would have missed, including estate JUDGED asserting *"every scored dimension passed"* while 8 of 14 turns had failed. Promoted to a committed, self-contained gate: **`test/test_trust_circle_grammar.mjs` (329 assertions**, no server/network) covering the four slots, the pair value, the attention word + driver, worst-of boundaries, all four `TrustState` wire strings + an unknown one, unresolvable scope, empty scope, and a regression on bare scope-size values — **mutation-tested** (renaming the Evidence slot → 72 failures; reverting attention to best-of → caught) so the gate provably cannot pass a broken contract. Docs: new **[TRUST_STATUS_COMMUNICATION.md](Architecture/TRUST_STATUS_COMMUNICATION.md)** (the contract + add-a-station checklist + one-source-per-rule table), corrected `trust.css` header (it declares itself the single source of the grammar and described the levels as verdicts — they are now verdict semantics on verdict surfaces and *triage* semantics on the ring), and a new operator section **§3.0 "Reading the Trust Circle"** in [AGENT_TRUST_AND_ASSURANCE.md](manuals/AGENT_TRUST_AND_ASSURANCE.md) (the ring had **no** operator documentation at all). JS/CSS browser-reload only — no backend change, no schema change, no REST change. - **Jul 2026**: **Two-hash trust envelope — portable capability + deployment surface (marketplace-ready)**. Widens the membrane from "the three answer gates" to the whole configured envelope minus deployment-bound access, on the stated design intent: *no silent widening of what an agent can do or say, wherever that change is stored*. **The constraint that shaped it** is the marketplace honesty gate — `portability.reinstate` only re-applies a signature when the copy's live hash equals what was signed, so anything in the hash must reproduce byte-identically after an id remap. The three changes most worth catching (**model swap · MCP catalog drift · connector opt-in**) are exactly the three that *cannot*: a subscriber uses their own LLM, their own server, and has opted into nothing. One hash would either make every installed pack permanently 🟠 or let real widening hide behind green. **So an agent now has two signable halves:** **portable** = composition + posture + **capability** (travels, reinstates on install, preserves publisher provenance) and **deployment** = resolved LLM identity · reachable MCP tool/prompt catalog · per-profile connector opt-in (never travels; each instance attests its own). The badge composes both — the portable half dominates (an unsigned or drifted artefact is not rescued by local attestation), and only then does the deployment half speak. **New `capability` dimension** (all portable, one registry): `profile_type`, `session_primer`, `tools`, `prompts`, `useMcpTools`, `useKnowledgeCollections`, `componentConfig`, `genieConfig`, `dualModelConfig`. `skillsConfig` stays **unsigned** — active skills are already ingredients, so signing the block would double-count and flip on inert edits. **Enablement is content** (a disabled→enabled flip changes capability while changing no artefact) and conversely **absent must equal inert** — per-spec canonicalizers make a disabled session primer, an opted-out connector and a component's intensity dial hash as though absent, because a badge that flips on tuning is one people learn to ignore. **Portability normalisation:** `genieConfig` is hashed in **tag space** via an injected id→tag resolver (hashing raw profile ids would make every coordinator pack permanently 🟠); instance-local pointers (`llmConfigurationId`, `mcpServerId`) never enter the portable hash — the *resolved identity* lives in the deployment half. **New `TrustState.DEPLOYMENT_UNATTESTED`** as a real state: collapsing it into `changed` would claim drift where none occurred, into `unsigned` would discard a verified publisher signature. **The MCP catalog is read from the persisted classification snapshot**, not a live connection, so badge resolution works offline — honest limit, documented: an upstream server change is caught when the profile next re-classifies, not instantaneously (the timestamp is excluded so re-classifying an unchanged server does not flip the badge). **Drift is described, not merely detected** (`describe_drift` → *"tools appeared: base_writeQuery(sql)"*, *"connectors enabled: uderia-shell"*) because an unexplained amber trains operators to click through it. **Live bug found by live testing that unit tests structurally could not catch:** `_connector_state` re-derived the auth-DB path instead of reusing `store._db_path`, missing the `sqlite:///` prefix strip — in the running server the path was unopenable and, behind a fail-soft `except`, **connector opt-in silently vanished from the signature while the badge still read intact**. Fixed by reuse (not by copying the rule), the failure is now logged at WARNING, and a structural regression test pins *one resolver, loud failure*. **Verified:** full lifecycle live through REST (`unsigned → deployment_unattested → trusted`), all three drift cases caught and named with the portable half intact throughout, and a simulated publish→install where **every** id differs (profiles, KG, collection, LLM, MCP server) hashes identically so `reinstate` takes — while weakened posture, an edited corpus and a dropped expert are still caught. Capability behaviour validated across **all five IFOC classes**. **+108 CI assertions** (`test/test_trust_deployment.py`); regression-clean across trust_membrane 176 / profile_config_contract 99 / agent_authority 58 / pack_component_config 35 / posture_modes 51 / guardrails 56 / grounding 102 / corpus_grounding 68 / review_queue 70 / trust_events 29 / sqlite_util 16. **Deferred (honest):** a real publish→fork cycle driven through the marketplace endpoints (the property is proven by simulation + unit tests, not by clicking the endpoints); browser click-verification of the new badge state. Server restart for backend + `index.html`; JS `trustBadge ?v=1.1`. - **Jul 2026**: **Repositories become trust ingredients + BOUNDED reports constraint, not presence (Trust-Circle walkthrough, findings F1/F2/F4)**. A station-by-station walkthrough of the Trust Circle for the Focus class (@UDERIA / Uderia Expert) surfaced three structural defects, all fixed at the root. **(F1) A Focus agent's corpus was not part of its trust composition.** `core/trust/composition.py` composed an agent over exactly two kinds — active KG + active skills — so a `rag_focused` agent with no KG and no active skills resolved with `ingredients: []` while its 144-doc / 4,715-chunk corpus sat *outside* the composition. Consequences: the bottom-up gate ("refuse unless every ingredient is 🟢") was **vacuous** — `sign_agent` succeeded instantly with the corpus unsigned and unscreened; the badge could not flip when the corpus changed; and `knowledgeConfig` being portable-but-unsigned meant re-pointing the agent at a *different* corpus disturbed nothing. The `knowledge` kind was separately signable all along (validator + earned-signature v2 with `scan_report_hash`) — it simply had no path into the agent badge. **The hole was estate-wide, not Focus-only**: every agent binds a planner repo, and champion cases steer the planner exactly as a corpus steers retrieval. Fix: **knowledge + planner repositories are first-class ingredients**, typed by each collection's own `repository_type` (never by which field named it — `ragCollections` and `knowledgeConfig.collections` overlap), with applicability **mirroring the runtime rather than a new rule**: knowledge counts only while `knowledgeConfig.enabled`, planner only for planning classes (`tool_enabled`/`genie`) — the convention already encoded in `planner.py`, `agent_pack_manager` (`uses_tools`) and `platform_ontology.projection`. Attesting an artefact the agent never consults would make the badge claim more than it verifies. **Empty ≠ unreadable** (deliberate asymmetry): a repository with no content has nothing to attest and is omitted (so the default empty planner repo can't make every agent unsignable), while one that demonstrably holds content whose hash could not be computed is emitted **`unresolved`** and blocks — silently omitting it would reopen exactly this gap under any transient read error. `IngredientRef` gained an explicit `unresolved` flag plus ONE shared `ingredient_state()` resolver used by **both** the badge and the signing gate, so what you see and what blocks can never disagree (the alternative — a sentinel hash string — was rejected as smuggling state into a hash field). A dangling binding (a profile pointing at a deleted collection) is warned and skipped, never silently counted. **Accepted, honest flip:** adding ingredients changes `agent_version_hash`, so an agent with a bound repository whose prior signature did *not* cover that repository correctly reads 🟠 until re-signed. **(F1b) `knowledgeConfig.sufficiencyThreshold` is now signed** — the honesty gate reads it to decide when the agent must answer "the knowledge base does not cover this", which is *what the agent will and will not say*, the documented signing criterion. **`maxSensitivity` deliberately stays unsigned** (the contract's existing rationale is correct: a retrieval-*access* ceiling whose meaning depends on local collection labels — the same trust≠access logic as `authorityConfig`), as does retrieval tuning (`maxDocs`/`maxTokens`/`minRelevanceScore`) so ordinary tweaks cannot flip a badge; *which* repositories are bound is covered far better than a hash could — they are ingredients in their own right. `posture_is_acting` now considers only ladder-bearing blocks, so a signed non-gate key cannot surface in the agent validator's "observe-only" list. **(F2) BOUNDED counted the presence of a config block, not the presence of a constraint.** `Object.keys(authorityConfig).length` rendered an agent with `autonomous:true`, no denials and no caps as **green**, under the headline "a strict subset of yours" — while it was the *least*-bounded agent in the estate; the eight profiles with `authorityConfig: null` behave identically at runtime yet rendered honest `na`. The station rewarded *touching* authority in the direction of more autonomy. The correct predicate `AgentScope.is_restricted` (which already handles the asymmetries — `allowed_connectors: []` = deny-all, `max_cost_per_run: 0` = a real cap) existed and was simply never asked. Fix: new `scope_for_profile()` + `describe_scope()` in `core/agent_authority.py` (wording lives with the model so ring, posture matrix, editor and enforcer describe a scope identically), surfaced as a computed read-only `authorityScope {restricted, autonomous, constraints[]}` on `GET /v1/profiles`; the ring and `_authoritySummary` now render it instead of re-deriving. Ladder: all constrained → pass · any unconstrained → **warn** ("N would act with your full authority if run unattended"). **(F4)** an unknown artefact kind returned a plausible `unsigned` — indistinguishable from a real never-signed artefact, so a mis-wired badge would look honest forever; `registered_kinds()` now backs a `400 unknown_kind` (batch endpoint reports `unknown_kinds` and still serves the rest). **Bonus gap closed by the same mechanism:** the downgrade guard gained declarative `floor_paths`/`ceiling_paths`, so `groundingConfig.minNumericFidelity` and `maxOutOfScopeDbs` — signed but **unguarded** — can no longer be relaxed by a pack that holds the gate at `enforce` while changing the numbers it fires on. **Assessed and closed as NOT a defect:** the three prompt-injection findings on the Uderia doc corpus (`README.md`, `TIER_1.3_GUARDRAILS.md`, `TIER_5.2_VALIDATORS.md`) are the *correct* output of a detector that must not be weakened — documentation *about* injection trips injection detectors — and `acknowledge-finding` (required written reason, frozen into the scan record and therefore into the earned signature) is exactly the path built for it. **Live-verified:** @UDERIA now carries `knowledge:2` and its sign-off returns `unsigned_ingredients` naming the corpus (it previously signed instantly); the corpus's own sign-off returns `blocked/unsafe` naming the three documents; planner repos attach to planning agents only; BOUNDED reads 1/10 amber where presence-counting showed 2/10 green. **+47 CI assertions** (trust_membrane 160→176, profile_config_contract 75→93, agent_authority 46→58, agent_pack_component_config 34→35 — two stale assertions pinning the old "signed = exactly three gates" invariant replaced with stronger ones asserting the produced *signature contents*); regression-clean across guardrails 56 / grounding 102 / corpus_grounding 68 / honesty 28 / review_queue 70 / ingest_firewall 36 / corpus_quarantine 13 / trust_events 29 / posture_modes 51. **Deferred (honest):** the dangling-binding warning is logged but has no UI surface yet (where it belongs — profile editor vs posture matrix — is an open design decision); browser click-verification of the new amber BOUNDED rendering still pending. Server restart for backend + `index.html`; JS `agentPerformanceHandler ?v=4.7`.
