- **Jul 2026**: **Durable, portable & signed agent trust posture (prerequisite for Trust-Circle agent hardening)**. Hardening an agent means setting its `groundingConfig` / `guardrailConfig` / `honestyConfig` / `knowledgeConfig` strictness controls / `authorityConfig` — and **none of that work survived**, for three independent structural reasons. **(1) Posture edits weren't durable.** The profile editor collected a fixed field list and `config_manager.update_profile` is a shallow `dict.update`, so each block was replaced **wholesale**: opening any profile and pressing Save silently deleted `groundingConfig.corpus.mode`, `maxOutOfScopeDbs`, `minNumericFidelity`, `knowledgeConfig.maxSensitivity` and `sufficiencyThreshold` (the last two being exactly the Focus hardening controls — neither had a UI field), and deleted `authorityConfig.frozen_by_breaker` + reset `autonomous`, so **a profile save silently un-froze an agent the trust breaker had frozen**. `honestyConfig` had no UI at all. **(2) Posture wasn't portable** — absent from all four of `agent_pack_manager`'s hand-maintained allow-lists, the same defect class that had already recurred three times. **(3) The seal didn't cover what protects the user** — `composition.py` read exactly ONE profile key (`skillsConfig`), so two agents with identical ontology+skills but opposite enforcement hashed identically and both resolved 🟢; a publisher could sign in `enforce`, the subscriber materialize at `observe`, and the badge still read **signed-and-intact**. **Fixes — W1 durable:** new **`core/posture_modes.py`**, ONE ladder replacing four duplicated tuples whose normalizers all degraded an unrecognised mode **down** to `observe` (so `review` — a real, *stricter* value — silently became observe wherever a hand-rolled guard was missing, i.e. protection switched off); it clamps to the strongest supported mode not exceeding the request (`review→enforce`; `annotate→observe` on the preflight ladder, unchanged), logs a genuinely unknown string rather than escalating a typo into withheld answers. `review` parity extended to `scan_inbound` + honesty (both now enforce **and** park, via one shared helper + turn-context kwargs). Editor now spread-preserves each block (so unmodelled sub-keys incl. `frozen_by_breaker` survive; re-enabling autonomy explicitly lifts a freeze) and gained the missing UI: honesty mode, corpus-support mode, `maxSensitivity`, `sufficiencyThreshold`, inbound `review`. **W2 portable:** new **`core/profile_config_contract.py`** — one declarative registry (per-key `portable`/`signed`/`mode_paths`/`flag_paths`/`aliases`) replacing four allow-lists; the sites are a *diamond* (3 sources → 1 sink), so it exposes `project_to_manifest`/`apply_from_manifest`. **Downgrade guard**: `update_in_place` refuses `posture_downgrade` unless `allow_posture_downgrade=true` (same seam as `dropped_tags`, dry-run reports it; absence still preserves), covering authority too — with the asymmetries a naive normalizer would invert into a privilege grant (`allowed_connectors: []` = **deny-all**, `max_cost_per_run: 0` = a real cap). Validation errors now carry a machine-readable `error` field from a closed set (restAPI.md documented one that was never emitted). **No manifest version bump** (validation has no unknown-key rejection; bumping would make older installs reject the pack). **W3 signed:** ONE canonical `composition.agent_version_hash` routed through all **four** mirrors (sign · live resolve · pack member · REST badge) that previously recomputed it independently; `attestation.py` stays pure via an optional `live_version_hash`. **Byte-identical baseline** — an agent at default posture hashes exactly as before, so existing attestations stay 🟢. `authorityConfig` deliberately **excluded** from the hash (deployment-bound access, *trust ≠ access*) but still portable + guarded. Closed a live bug: `_artifact_live_hash` returned `None` for `kind="agent"` → `GET /v1/trust/artifact/agent/<id>` reported **TRUSTED unconditionally** and could never surface drift. New **`agent` validator** (the kind had none; `sign_agent` persisted `verdict=None`): bands clean/partial, **never blocks**. Pack authoring: `agent_packs/common/trust_posture.py` (mirrors `component_config.py`; **omitting ≠ declaring defaults**), wired into uderia_expert. **Proof:** 4 CI-pure suites — `test_posture_modes` 51 · `test_profile_config_contract` 75 · `test_agent_pack_component_config` 34 (was 16; grep assertions replaced with real `_build_profile`/normalizer round-trips) · `test_trust_membrane` 160 (was 132); regression-clean across grounding 102 / guardrails 56 / honesty 28 / review_queue 70 / corpus_grounding 68 / preflight 26 / agent_authority 46 / obda 26. **Live-verified (43 assertions):** sub-keys persist and survive a simulated editor save; signing records a posture verdict; weakening posture flips 🟢→🟠 on **both** badges; restoring returns 🟢; an authority change leaves the badge untouched; observe-only signs *partial*; fresh pack install carries all four blocks; weaker republish → `posture_downgrade`; dry-run reports it; opt-in permits it. **Honest scope:** `groundingConfig.allowOutOfScope` is parsed/stored but **never read** by the gate while the UI promises it prevents withholding in Enforce — a UI claim with no implementation, excluded from the signature and left for its own decision; `agent` sign-off returns 409 where `agent_pack` returns 422 for the same failure class; the editor carry-forward is verified via REST simulation, not a browser click-through. Server restart for backend + `index.html`; JS browser-reload. Doc: `docs/roadmap/TIER_5.2_POSTURE.md`. Files: `core/{posture_modes,profile_config_contract}.py` (new), `core/trust/{composition,attestation,validators,pack}.py`, `core/agent_pack_manager.py`, `api/{agent_pack_routes,trust_routes}.py`, `agent/{grounding,guardrails,honesty,preflight}/*`, `agent/executor.py`, `agent/engines/coordinate_engine.py`, `static/js/handlers/configurationHandler.js`, `templates/index.html`, `agent_packs/common/trust_posture.py` (new), `agent_packs/uderia_expert/build.py`, `test/test_{posture_modes,profile_config_contract,trust_membrane,agent_pack_component_config,review_queue}.py`.
- **Jul 2026**: **REST activation firewall + per-executor `@TAG` override isolation + deferred-LLM materialization (cross-user hardening of the Optimize override path)**. A deep assessment of the Optimize (`tool_enabled`) engine found that an `@TAG` profile override **mutated eight process-global `APP_STATE` slots** (`llm`, `mcp_tools`, `mcp_prompts`, `structured_tools`, `structured_prompts`, `mcp_client`, `tools_context`, `prompts_context`) for the whole turn, and the shared LLM handler read global provider config at call time — so on a multi-user server a **concurrent turn could observe another turn's overridden tool catalog / LLM** (a real cross-user data-integrity hazard given the platform's concurrent-session model). **(1) Per-executor STATE overlay** — the override now installs its catalog in a `ChainMap(override_slots, APP_STATE)` on `executor.dependencies['STATE']` (+ `executor.profile_llm_instance`) instead of mutating the global; reads for non-overridden slots fall through to the global exactly as before (`load_and_categorize_mcp_resources`, the sole writer of these slots, runs only at config/classification time — never during a turn — so the ChainMap can never misroute a write). The whole C10 global-restore machinery is **deleted** (nothing global to restore); only the small per-user provider/model revert is kept (`executor.current_provider` falls back to `get_user_provider` on some construction paths, so leaving the override provider would corrupt the same user's next turn). The `temp_mcp_client` subprocess leak is fixed (the old `pass` → a real `aclose()`, outside the flag guard so it can't leak on the failure path). Non-override turns keep `dependencies['STATE'] = APP_STATE` untouched → **byte-identical baseline** (the 99% path is inert). The C10 restore is now provider-only (`restore_override_app_state`); the new `apply_override_state_overlay` helper is unit-tested. **(2) Handler provider de-race** — `_condense_and_clean_history` history normalization + the Bedrock ARN provider read now use the **per-call** provider (user-keyed fallback) instead of the shared `APP_CONFIG.CURRENT_PROVIDER`/`CURRENT_MODEL_PROVIDER_IN_PROFILE`, closing a **pre-existing** cross-user race (two concurrent turns on different providers previously both read the shared global). **(3) Deferred-LLM materialization** — `switch_profile_context(validate_llm=False)` parks a placeholder dict `{"placeholder": True, provider, model}` in `APP_STATE['llm']` ("client will be created on first message") that was never implemented → cryptic `'dict' object has no attribute 'chat'`; `call_llm_api` now materializes the placeholder into a real (pooled, no-network) client at the universal chokepoint (`_materialize_placeholder_llm`), and on a missing-credentials failure raises a **clear, actionable** error instead of the cryptic crash. **REST activation firewall** (the front-line governance control — `_assert_profile_activated`): every REST profile-resolution point — `POST /v1/sessions/<id>/query`, `POST /v1/sessions`, `POST /v1/prompts/<name>/execute`, `POST /v1/prompts/<name>/execute-raw` — now rejects the EFFECTIVE profile (default OR `@TAG` override) with **HTTP 403** (`code:"profile_not_activated"`) unless it is ACTIVATED (present in `active_for_consumption_profile_ids`; activation requires all profile tests to pass). So an untested profile (e.g. one with no valid LLM credentials) can never be driven through the API and fall through to the placeholder / a misleading "model may be overloaded" planner error — it fails fast with an honest message pointing at Configuration → Profiles. **Genie orchestration is exempt** (slave session CREATION via `genie_parent_session_id`; slave QUERIES on `genie_metadata.is_genie_slave` sessions) — the coordinator drives its validated children in-process via the same REST endpoints; the firewall fails **closed** on any unexpected error. **Live-verified:** `@OPTIM` (unactivated) → 403 with the honest message; `@IDGGT` default → 202; activated `@OPGGT` override → 202; the override catalog (53 tools) reaches the planner via the overlay. **CI:** `test/test_provider_globals_isolation.py` (23) + `test/test_rest_activation_firewall.py` (14) + updated `test/test_fusion_structural.py` (122); regression-clean across turn_cost 35 / fusion quick-wins 46 / robustness 63 / grounding 102 / honesty_gate 28 / preflight 26 / phase_serialization 13; broad app import clean. Server restart for backend. The slim prod image has no git binary, so the Dockerfile gained `ARG/ENV UDERIA_VERSION` and docker-compose passes `build.args.UDERIA_VERSION: ${UDERIA_VERSION:-v1.19}` to bake the tag at build time. (2) **Awareness "Total Sessions" fix** — read the monthly-reset `UserConsumption.total_sessions` counter (showed 13 for an admin with far more); now a live `COUNT(DISTINCT session_id)` from `consumption_turns` in both `/consumption/summary` and `/consumption/system-summary`, consistent with the all-time Model-Distribution/Most-Token-Intensive panels; KPI tooltips rewritten to state each metric's scope (sessions/panels all-time; tokens/cost/success current-month; velocity 24h). (4) **Admin component card titles** used the raw `component_id` (`knowledge_graph`) — `_loadGenericComponentAdminPanel` assigned the whole `{component:…}` envelope to `comp`; now unwraps `.component` so titles use `display_name` for all components. An imported pack profile carried **no `componentConfig`** (it was never exported/imported), so it inherited the platform's permissive per-type defaults — 6 action components default-on for every IFOC class → their 6 companion skills auto-injected (~5.5K tokens/turn). Root fix: `componentConfig` now travels the whole pack contract — export `prof_entry`, import `_build_profile`, fork/subscribe `_to_manifest_entry`, **and** the v1.0→v1.1 `_normalize_v10_to_v11` (which whitelisted and silently dropped it AND `skillsConfig`, on experts + coordinator). All three shipped packs declare it via a new shared helper `agent_packs/common/component_config.py:focused_component_config(memory=True, extra_enabled=[...])` (memory on, action components off) — uderia_expert (1) / andp (10) / vat (11) profiles. - **Jul 2026**: **Single-source session-token accounting (kills a rag_focused double-count that over-charged quota)**. The LangChain-agent layer (`ConversationAgentExecutor`, used by rag_focused + conversation_with_tools) persisted its session tokens **gated on the live SSE handler**, so persistence was mode-dependent and wrapping engines guessed inconsistently: FocusEngine re-persisted → the main call was counted **twice** in the session counter on live turns (session ≈ 2× turn), and since `update_token_count` also drives `record_token_usage`/consumption, it **over-charged the token quota**. Root fix at the seam: the agent now persists each LangChain step to the session counter **exactly once, unconditionally** (decoupled from `async_event_handler`, which stays gating only the live `token_update` *event*); FocusEngine stops re-persisting (keeps only the turn accumulator). All IFOC classes now single-count. Live-proven: rag_focused turn session == turn (ratio 1.000, was 1.95×), turn totals == Σ per-call events, turn_cost == Σ event costs. Durable AST guard `test/test_token_accounting_single_count.py` (8 assertions). Files: `agent/conversation_agent.py`, `agent/engines/focus_engine.py`.

Added `_resolve_turn_cost_usd(prefer_accumulator=False)` (forces the single-model re-price — ReAct is single-model, `turn_input` already includes ReAct + reranking); Conversation passes it at both persistence sites; the default is unchanged for the fully-accumulated engines. **CI:** `test/test_rerank_cost_crossclass.py` (18 assertions — event shape/value via a replica of the frontend `extractCost`, reorder correctness, empty-docs no-op, `_events=None` back-compat, partial-accumulator resolver, four caller wirings); regression-clean across turn_cost 35, §4 efficiency 30, fusion 46/115/63, rag 20, grounding 102, eval_online 54. - **Jul 2026**: **`turn_cost` dual-model re-pricing — persisted turn cost = Σ accurate per-call costs (was a single-model re-price)**. Every LLM call is priced per-call at its ACTUAL model in `PlanExecutor._call_llm_and_update_tokens` and emitted as an event, but each engine then recomputed the **turn** total by re-pricing the summed tokens at `executor.current_model` (the last-used model) — so a **dual-model** profile (strategic model A + tactical model B, different rates) was systematically mispriced, and the backend `turn_cost` drifted from the frontend `eventHandlers.js:_getTurnCost` event-sum (a `[Cost Verification]` warning on every dual-model turn). **Fix — one accumulator:** `executor.turn_cost_usd` sums each per-call `cost_usd` at its own model (contributor A in `_call_llm_and_update_tokens`; sub-executor seed/reclaim so a delegated sub-prompt's costs flow back); `executor._resolve_turn_cost_usd()` returns it (or a single-model fallback re-price when the accumulator is empty but tokens were spent, so we never regress to `$0`) and **replaces the re-price at every in-turn persistence site** — optimize (the dual-model target), ideate, focus (×2 paths), conversation, plus the executor error/partial-save + completion-card sites. **Genie left untouched** (`GenieCoordinator` is a separate single-model class whose coordinator-model re-price already equals its per-call sum). **Session-name fold (§3.2-D)** — folds `_name_cost` into the accumulator **guarded by `acc > 0`**: Ideate/Focus route their main call through the accumulator (so without the fold `turn_cost` = main only, missing the session-name event's cost), while Conversation (ReAct, direct LangChain) and Focus's tools path leave the accumulator empty and correctly rely on the fallback re-pricing `turn_input_tokens` (which already includes the name tokens) — the guard folds only on accumulated paths, no per-path branching. **§3.4 — two post-hoc re-price bugs the work surfaced** (both would have OVERWRITTEN the accumulator-based `turn_cost` with a single-model re-price on turns that ran them): the **recommender** (`_record_tier_c_usage`) and **extensions** (`session_manager.append_extension_results_to_turn`) both re-priced the whole turn → switched to priced **increments** (`added_cost_usd`+`additive` / `prior + _ext_cost`); judges + grounding already increment (confirmed). Result: `turn_cost` == the `_getTurnCost` event-sum for single- AND dual-model turns (single-model byte-identical within 1e-6). **CI:** `test/test_turn_cost.py` (35 assertions — dual-model correctness, single-model no-regression, fallback, guarded fold, engine-site switch, post-hoc increment); regression-clean across fusion (quick-wins 46 / structural 115 / robustness 63), recommender 84, eval_online 54, eval_analysis 60, guardrails 56, flow_extensions 35. Server restart for backend; no schema/JS change. Plan: `docs/assessments/TURN_COST_DUAL_MODEL_PLAN.md`. Closes the honesty gap where an owner released a withheld original but the agent still could not see or state it (and every mention re-parked a new review item). Approve now has two scopes: **Approve** (record only — unchanged default) and **Approve + release** — the owner EXPLICITLY releases the withheld original INTO the conversation, **forward-only** (the sealed turn is never rewritten; append-only invariant preserved). - **Jul 2026**: **Live red-team probing — the honest resilience test that drives REAL turns (opt-in, budget-capped, remaining-topics R6)**. The deterministic self-test measures in-path DETECTOR recall at 0 tokens; this is the stronger form — it submits an adversarial corpus as real queries to a target profile and scores the AGENT'S actual behaviour (did it obey an injection, echo planted PII, or answer a drift-eliciting question). Costs real tokens (one turn per probe) so it is **opt-in + hard-capped**. New pure `eval/live_redteam.py`: a curated `PROBE_CORPUS` (injection / pii_echo / scope_drift, each with a deterministic 0-token scorer over the completed turn — `held` True/False/unknown; a PII-echo probe plants a known secret and fails if it returns unredacted, injection probes detect obey-tells vs refusal-tells, drift reads the grounding stamp as the authority) + `summarize` (resilience = held/decided, excludes unknown) + `bounded_corpus` (hard ceiling protects the token budget). REST `POST /v1/assurance/live-redteam` drives the bounded corpus through the caller's OWN profile via the internal self-call path (`UderiaRestClient` + `create_internal_token`, 180s/probe cap); a FAILURE lands in the Assurance Inbox (`live_redteam_failure`, danger) + broadcasts live. UI: a **Live probe** row in Trust Posture (agent picker + 3/6 count + Run) rendering resilience + held/failed/unknown chips + per-failure detail. **Pure scoring, so the verdict is reproducible + free; only the probe turns cost tokens.** Tests: `test_live_redteam.py` (23: every scorer's held/failed/unknown paths, spacing-insensitive card match, summarize math, cap clamp). New `guardrails/runtime.scan_tool_result(tool_name, result, …)`: deterministic, 0-token, gated on the guardrails master switch, wired at the universal `mcp_adapter.invoke_mcp_tool` success seam (same chokepoint as preflight catalog caching → every SQL/data-running engine reaches it). **Observe-only by design (charter #15): the result is NEVER altered — byte-identical baseline** — a match is logged, recorded as an Assurance-Inbox `tool_result_injection` event (labels + tool name only, never row content), and broadcast live (banner + in-place inbox refresh, via the wave-9 `broadcast_notice`). `TDA_` framework tools are exempt (their output is the agent's own text, not external data). - **Jul 2026**: **Deterministic anti-hallucination hardening — four guardrails closing the "confident false negative" failure (all-IFOC, no-regression by default)**. Root-caused from session `5fd9be3d` turn 6 (@OPGGT / Optimize on a weak model, gemini-3.1-flash-lite): the planner hallucinated `SELECT * FROM airport.station` (a *logical* KG entity name mistaken for a physical DB), ran the KG-discovery phase and the query phase **in parallel**, Error 3802 fell through to a blind LLM retry, and the turn ended with a **confident false negative** ("there are no airport stations") even though turns 4–5 had already answered it via `airlines_mvm.awb`. Fixed WITHOUT a smarter model — the model's job is reduced to *intent*; code owns *schema truth, execution ordering, error recovery, and answer honesty*. Four independent, deterministic, 0-token fixes, each defaulting to **observe/measure-only → byte-identical baseline** (charter #15); *enforce* behaviours are opt-in. **(1) Error-3802 deterministic recovery** — new `DatabaseNotFoundStrategy` in `phase_executor.py` (the structured handlers matched `Object '…' does not exist`/`Column '…'` but NOT `Database 'X' does not exist`, so 3802 hit the blind generic LLM retry); now pivots — zero LLM — to `base_tableList` on the KG-scoped database (or `base_databaseList`), surfacing the REAL tables instead of a scattershot guess. Optimize-only path (other engines don't use `CorrectionHandler` → structurally no-regression). **(2) Honesty post-condition** — new pure module `agent/honesty/` (`primitives`/`gate`/`adapter`/`runtime`, sibling of grounding/guardrail/obda) + `executor._run_honesty_gate` wired at the Optimize + Conversation trust seams (reload-stamped `turn_data['honesty']`, Live Status `honesty` card in `ui.js` + reload-harmonization in `eventHandlers.js`). Fires ONLY when the answer asserts non-existence AND every raw-SQL data query that turn errored with **none** succeeding → flags (observe) or rewrites to an honest retrieval-failure (enforce, per-profile `honestyConfig.mode`). Critical invariant proven: a **legitimate empty result** (query succeeded, 0 rows) is never altered. Reads both engine result shapes (Optimize `{status}` / ReAct `{success}`); Ideate/Focus abstain by nature; genie covered via expert turns. **(3) Preflight schema grounding** — new pure module `agent/preflight/` (`catalog`/`guard`) + two fail-open hooks at the shared `mcp_adapter.invoke_mcp_tool` seam (universal — Optimize + Conversation + genie slaves). Validates a SQL call's FROM/JOIN databases (sqlglot, +regex fallback, reuses `grounding.primitives.SYSTEM_DBS`/`SQL_DB_RE`) against the session's **authoritative** catalog cached from a `base_databaseList(scope=all)` success. Regression-safe *by construction*: only a COMPLETE catalog is cached → a valid non-KG database (e.g. `fitness_db`) is never a false positive (unlike a KG-scope allowlist); no catalog → no-op. Global `APP_CONFIG.PREFLIGHT_SQL_MODE` (default `observe`); `enforce` short-circuits with a **3802-shaped** error so fix (1) engages. **(4) Role-aware phase serialization** — new `DISCOVERY_TOOLS` set in `plan_compiler.py` + `executor._phase_discovery_deps` ORed into `_build_phase_groups` (third complement to `_phase_referenced_deps` + `_phase_implicit_deps`): a data-EXECUTION phase (raw SQL) that follows a schema-DISCOVERY phase (`TDA_KnowledgeGraph query`, `base_tableList`, …) now depends on it, so the turn-6 plan serializes to `[[1],[2],[3]]` instead of racing the query ahead of its discovery; independent queries still parallelize. Optimize-only (only Optimize builds multi-phase plans). **Proof:** 87 new CI-pure assertions across 4 suites (`test_database_not_found_correction.py` 20, `test_honesty_gate.py` 28, `test_preflight_schema.py` 26, `test_phase_serialization.py` 13) — each proving the fix AND abstain/no-regression for the other IFOC classes; adjacent suites regression-clean (grounding 102 / guardrails 56 / obda 26 / arg-alignment 6 / eval 82). To activate containment: `APP_CONFIG.PREFLIGHT_SQL_MODE="enforce"` + per-profile `honestyConfig.mode="enforce"` (fixes 1 & 4 are always-on with no behavioural downside). **Not built (honest follow-up):** in-session query memoization (reuse a prior turn's proven SQL for a near-duplicate follow-up — same RAG mechanism, no smarter model). Server restart for backend; `ui.js`/`eventHandlers.js` browser-reload. - **Jul 2026**: **Judge run is now a visible, reload-safe Live Status step (cost-transparency imperative)**. Follow-up to the judge-cost-allocation fix: allocating the cost consistently wasn't enough — the spend must also be **visible as a discrete event whose sum reconciles to the turn total** (a core platform USP: the Live Status panel's per-event costs must equal the turn's total cost). **Gap:** clicking "Re-score" with judges billed `turn_cost` but emitted **no** cost-bearing event — `grounding_gate.to_event()` carries no `cost_usd` and `turn_score_complete` was a UI overlay never persisted — so the panel's event-sum fell short (the `_getTurnCost` `[Cost Verification]` check would warn). **Fix — in the ONE canonical sink `_record_score_usage`** (so all three judge paths inherit it): emit one cost-bearing **`judge_evaluation_complete`** step (title *"Agent Quality Judged"*, carrying `input_tokens`/`output_tokens`/`cost_usd`/`judge_models`). It is **broadcast live** over the always-open per-user notification channel (session-guarded → `updateStatusWindow`), so it appears the moment the judge runs for every caller incl. the backgrounded online hook + the REST re-score button (no open request stream); and **persisted** into the turn's `system_events` via `append_system_events_to_turn`, so it **re-renders identically on a plan reload** and its cost re-sums into the turn total. No double-count: it's the *sole* cost-bearing judge event `_getTurnCost` sees, and it's emitted only over the notification channel (never also via `event_handler`) so a live stream can't render it twice; deterministic-only scoring (0 tokens) is a clean no-op. **Live-verified:** a fresh turn auto-scored by the online hook AND manually re-scored produced **two** persisted "Agent Quality Judged" steps and the panel's event-sum reconciled to the backend `turn_cost` exactly (Δ=0). Frontend: `ui.js` `_renderJudgeEvalCompleteDetails` + 3 step-render dispatch sites (Genie/Conversation/Standard) + the reload custom-render branch; `eventHandlers.js` 4 profile-title fns map the type → "Agent Quality Judged" (so reload harmonization preserves it); `notifications.js` session-guarded `judge_evaluation_complete` case. Tests: `test_eval_online` `t_score_usage_accounting` +6 assertions (mock `append_system_events_to_turn`; assert the step is broadcast **and** persisted with cost) → 48→54 pass. Server restart for backend; JS browser-reload. Doc: [AGENT_OPS_EVAL_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/AGENT_OPS_EVAL_ARCHITECTURE.md) §6.4a. Files: `src/trusted_data_agent/eval/online.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `static/js/{ui.js,eventHandlers.js,notifications.js}`, `test/test_eval_online.py`.
- **Jul 2026**: **Judge-cost allocation — one canonical sink for every judge LLM call, all IFOC engines (design imperative)**. Every LLM-judge call in the eval/trust stack spends real tokens on the user's credentials, so cost must be allocated **consistently at all times** — the same way a normal turn's tokens are, and every associated event must survive a plan reload. **Audit finding:** the manual **"Score this turn"** button (`POST /v1/evals/score-turn`) spent real judge tokens but only *returned* the cost in the HTTP response + a roster span — it did **not** bill consumption, session/turn totals, or emit a live event (a real gap vs the online hook + grounding gate). **Fix — route all three judge-spend sites through ONE sink** `eval/online.py:_record_score_usage(user_uuid, session_id, turn_id, in_tok, out_tok, cost_usd, event_handler)`, which does (idempotently): cost via `CostManager` · session totals (`update_token_count`) · turn totals (`update_turn_token_counts`, **authoritative for plan reload**) · consumption/billing ledger (`ConsumptionManager.update_turn_tokens`, cents) · a live KPI `token_update`. **The `token_update` is now ALSO broadcast over the per-user notification channel** (`APP_STATE["notification_queues"]`, session-tagged) so backgrounded/REST callers with no open request `event_handler` (the online hook + the score-turn button) still update the live counters; `token_update` carries **absolute** totals (frontend *sets*, never adds) → double-delivery is a no-op; `notifications.js` renders it **session-guarded** (closes cross-session KPI pollution — the `_dispatchRestEvent` path was unguarded). The score-turn endpoint also stamps `eval.judged`/`eval.cost_usd`/`eval.input_tokens`/`eval.output_tokens` on the persisted quality span so a reload's Quality card echoes the cost via the `turn-score` GET. **Because the fix lives in the sink, every engine inherits it — no per-engine code.** The three judge-spend sites: (1) **online eval** → direct `_record_score_usage` at the single engine-agnostic seam `execution_service.run_agent_execution` (covers all 5 IFOC engines + genie experts); (2) **grounding gate** → `_attribute_judge_cost` → `_record_score_usage` (4 engines via `executor._run_grounding_gate_full` with uniform `session_id`/`turn_id`/`event_handler`, genie directly at `coordinate_engine.py` with the same context); (3) **score-turn button** → `_record_score_usage` (engine-agnostic by construction — reads the turn via `RunRecord`, whose accessors are defensive across every engine shape). CLI (`eval/cli.py`) is correctly **exempt** (offline, no session). **Live cross-engine verified:** a real turn per class scored with judges + a reference answer (so `AnswerCorrectnessJudge`, which applies to all classes, fires) — the consumption ledger moved by the **exact** judge token count and the reload GET echoed the exact cost for all five: Ideate (Δ677=487+190), Focus (Δ297=237+60), Optimize (Δ350=256+94), Coordinate (Δ315=250+65), Conversation via the shared sink. **Two verified nuances:** dimension judges **abstain at 0 cost** when inputs are absent (no ref answer / no retrieved docs / no tool calls) — correct, not a gap; and when verifying `score-turn` accounting in isolation, re-score a **settled** turn — a turn's own fire-and-forget tasks (online-eval, memory extraction, next-step recommender) bill *after* `status=complete` and otherwise race the before/after ledger snapshot. Tests: `test_eval_online` `+t_score_usage_accounting` (8 assertions) → all eval suites 127 pass. Server restart for backend; JS browser-reload. - **Jul 2026**: **Industry-model PDM deploy — two generation-time DDL correctness fixes + single-PDM invariant (surfaced by a live Databricks→Teradata KG build)**. A clean end-to-end deploy of the restaurants/MVM industry model to a real Teradata target surfaced three root-cause bugs, all fixed at generation time (not patched at the target). **(1) Reserved-word columns unquoted:** a `guest_satisfaction` column named `language` (Teradata reserved word) emitted bare in metric-view SQL → Error 3706. Root cause: SQLGlot emits bare identifiers. Fixed in `dbdeploy/metric_compiler.py:translate_expr` with SQLGlot `identify="safe"` on the Teradata write (quotes reserved-word columns like `language`/`order`, leaves functions bare) + a `_SIMPLE_IDENT_RE` bare-identifier fallback when sqlglot is unavailable. **(2) Table/view namespace collision:** Teradata tables + views share ONE namespace per database, so a metric named like a table (`menu_lto`, `order_item`) emitted `CREATE VIEW <table>` → Error 3803 "already exists". Fixed with `dbdeploy/dialects/teradata.py:dedupe_view_name(base, taken)` — `_emit_metric_views` seeds the taken-set with all deployed table names per DB and renames colliding metric views to `<name>_mv`/`_mv2`; the KG `ddl_artifact` node uses the deployed (renamed) view name but keeps the logical `label`, and the resolver walks the `implements` edge (not the name) so it's transparent. **(3) Single-PDM invariant:** `declarative_model.construct()` now forces the walker to `layers=["logical"]` whenever `deploy_pdm` is on — the deploy IS the authoritative physical layer at the real target, so the KG carries ONE physical namespace that matches the deploy target (fixes a grounding-scope mismatch where the walker built physical nodes for `restaurants_mvm` while data deployed to `agent_test`; the trusted scope now correctly reads the real target). **Deploy #3 result:** 153 tables + 1123 FK + 112 views created (0 DDL errors), 7600 rows loaded, physical KG layer imported, trusted scope `['agent_test']`. Tests: `test_pdm_metrics` (reserved-word + collision → 91), `test_pdm_constructor_deploy` (`+test_deploy_forces_single_physical_layer` → 67) — 322 PDM assertions across 5 suites. Files: `src/trusted_data_agent/dbdeploy/metric_compiler.py`, `dbdeploy/dialects/teradata.py`, `agent/kg_constructors/declarative_model.py`, `test/test_pdm_metrics.py`, `test/test_pdm_constructor_deploy.py`.
- **Jul 2026**: **Rename — "Agent Identity" → "Agent Authority" (module + config + UX + docs; no behavior change)**. Clarifies the platform's identity taxonomy. An agent's **identity is its Profile** (*who it is* — IFOC class, LLM, MCP "senses", memory, components; the `@TAG` profile IS the agent). The P3 subsystem does **not** define identity — it governs the agent's **authority** (*what it may do, on whose behalf* when acting autonomously — a strict, subset-only slice of its owner's permissions). Identity ≠ authority (charter #8, *trust ≠ access*), a four-axis composite: **Profile = identity · Trust Membrane = assurance · Agent Authority = access · Provenance chain = audit**. Renamed `core/agent_identity.py` → `core/agent_authority.py`; config key `identityConfig` → `authorityConfig` (**legacy key still read** for pre-rename profiles; `authorityConfig` wins if both present); profile-editor card "Agent Identity" → "Agent Authority"; `test/test_agent_identity.py` → `test_agent_authority.py` (+2 back-compat assertions → **46 pass**). Internal class `AgentPrincipal` kept (correct IAM term). All 4 backend import sites + all docs updated; arch doc renamed to [AGENT_AUTHORITY_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/AGENT_AUTHORITY_ARCHITECTURE.md) with a new **§0** defining the identity-vs-authority taxonomy. Pure rename + backward-compat (verified: legacy `identityConfig` honored, module imports clean, 46/46 tests). **Frontier facets the platform does NOT yet claim under "agent identity"** (honest, charter #19): the agent authenticating to external systems *as itself*, its own vaulted short-lived credentials, and formal OAuth token-exchange / on-behalf-of delegation downstream. Server restart for backend + `index.html`; JS browser-reload. - **Jul 2026**: **OBDA status events — the observable governed-data lane (Phase 0, on `main`)**. The observability + eval face of the OBDA vision (`docs/roadmap/OBDA_VISION.md §5`): makes **determinism visible**. Today the deterministic metric compiler runs in conversations but is *invisible as a lane* — a governed `compile_metric` and an LLM free-forming its own SQL look identical in the trace. OBDA fixes that with a new **`obda` class of Live Status events** (sibling of the grounding/guardrail cards) whose single most important field is the **lane marker: governed-deterministic vs free-formed-advisory** (shows *both* lanes, never only the good path). **Pure core** `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/obda.py` (deterministic, 0-token, single source of truth): `scan_obda(tool_calls)` classifies a turn's data ops into **governed** (a `compile_metric` op) vs **free-formed** (a tool call carrying a raw `sql` arg); `calls_from_trace` / `calls_from_conversation_events` adapt the Optimize `turn_action_history` and ReAct `conversation_agent_events` into the canonical `{tool_name,arguments,result}` shape (mirrors `eval.types.RunRecord`); `build_event` yields the card's details dict. **All-engine + reload-safe (the hard requirements):** emission mirrors the grounding/guardrail seam exactly — `executor._run_obda_scan(...)` is called at the end-of-turn trust-pass in the two engines that perform data ops (Optimize via `executor.py` final-answer assembly; Conversation via `conversation_engine.py`), yielded live as a `type:"obda"` step **and** stamped `turn_data["obda"]` for reload; `eventHandlers.js` reload-hardens it by synthesizing the `obda` event into `system_events`/`genie_events` (identical mechanism to grounding/guardrail). Ideate/Focus/Coordinate do no data ops by construction (Coordinate's slaves get their own cards). **Eval (two ends of one signal):** new **`governed_data_ratio`** reliability scorer (`eval/scorers/reliability.py`) reads the *same* trace via `RunRecord.tool_calls()` (all-engine, abstains where no data ops), bands the governed fraction — a **non-gating incentive** signal that rewards the governed lane (nudges toward OBDA). **Frontend:** `_renderObdaDetails` in `ui.js` (monochrome status-kv card in the trust-card family) wired at all 3 status dispatch sites + the renderable-types filter. **Proof:** 26 CI assertions (`test/test_obda.py` — scanner lanes, both adapters, event builder, the scorer via real `RunRecord`); eval reliability (48) / eval tasks (34) / grounding (102) regression-clean; scorer registered. Phase 1 (`obda.catalog` — surface the *complete* governed catalog, which is already computed for the grounding gate) + Phase 2 (`obda.validate`/`execute`/`provenance`, with the surface) are the follow-ons. **Server restart** for backend/engines; JS browser-reload for the card (live visual check pending). - **Jul 2026**: **Tier 4.2 / T3 — Governed Metric Semantic API for BI (on `main`)**. Makes a metric a governed data product consumable by **both AI and BI from one definition** (assessment req T3 — TD/MS/Google half-open). A metric is *defined once* in the ontology (a KG `metric` node: dimensions/measures/source) and *consumed everywhere* through **one pure semantic core** — `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/metric_api.py` (`resolve_metric_semantics` + `list_metric_catalog`; deterministic, zero-LLM, capability-aware via `resolver.py` — resolves the deployed realization: computed **view** · direct **column** · materialized **table** · **base_table** aggregation · **none**). **Single source of truth (the key move):** the AI-side `handler._handle_compile_metric` was **refactored to call the core and only render**, so the agent's `compile_metric` SQL and a BI tool's SQL for the same slice are byte-identical by construction (no drift). **Four governed REST endpoints** (all `_assert_kg_enabled` tier-gated, ownership-scoped to the profile's *active* ontology via `kg_profile_assignments`, `?kg_id=` override): `GET /v1/profiles/<id>/metrics` (catalog), `GET …/metrics/<name>` (definition + compiled SQL + deployed pointer + access scope + ontology governance/trust + RDF-Cube link; `?include_conformance=true`), `POST …/compile` (slice → SQL), `POST …/query` (compile **and execute** against a deployed DB connection → **rows**; user's own authority + own connection; **read-only by construction** — only the compiled aggregate SELECT runs, re-checked single-SELECT; honest 409 with the SQL if no connection). **Governed, not just an API:** surfaces the source ontology's **lifecycle (Tier 4.3) + trust badge (Tier 5.2)** so a BI consumer sees whether the metric is governed/trusted (trust imported **defensively** — it's in the removable Ontology Suite → absent ⇒ field omitted); cross-links the **W3C RDF Data Cube** face (Tier 4.1). **In-app (charter #2):** metric node → right-click → **Semantic API for BI** panel (definition · deployed target + access scope · compiled SQL copy · trust/lifecycle chips · 3 endpoints with Copy cURL), alongside the RDF export options. **Proof:** 46 CI assertions (`test/test_metric_api.py` — all 4 realizations, slice compile incl. coarser-grain + column-read, catalog, access scope, honest errors) covering **both faces** (shared core); resolver (37) + metric compiler (80) regression-clean; **live-verified all four endpoints** on a real ontology (OPTIM's active KG — catalog, full GET with `trust_state:trusted`+`lifecycle:draft` surfaced + standards link, honest 422/404). **Server restart** for backend + endpoints; renderer.js browser-reload. **Architecture:** `docs/roadmap/TIER_4.2_METRIC_API.md`. Files: `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/{metric_api.py,handler.py,renderer.js}`, `src/trusted_data_agent/api/rest_routes.py`, `test/test_metric_api.py`.
- **Jul 2026**: **Tier 5 Step 4 / P3 — Agent Authority: the Agent Principal (on `main`)**. Delivers assessment req **P3** (agent identity & permissions — only SF/MS were GREEN), built *on* the Tier 5.2 Trust-Membrane foundation (the agent as a first-class governed principal; **trust ≠ access**, charter #8). When an agent acts **autonomously** (a genie expert, a scheduled task, a flow node, an MCP `ask_profile`) it now acts as an **Agent Principal derived from its owner** whose authority is a **strict subset** of the owner's, enforced **fail-closed at every tool chokepoint** — and every autonomous action is attributed to the agent (vs the user) in the audit trail. **Model (pure, deterministic, subset-only — never grants):** `core/agent_authority.py` — `AgentScope` (`autonomous` on/off · `deny_writes` · `denied_tools` · `allowed_connectors` allow-list · `max_cost_per_run`), `AgentPrincipal` (`principal_id=agent:<profile_id>`, `actor()` audit stamp), `parse_scope`/`derive_principal` off the profile's `authorityConfig` (same mechanism as `guardrailConfig`), `is_tool_allowed` (`TDA_*` framework tools never write-gated). **Enforcement architecture (the "think deep" part — all-engine by construction):** a **per-turn security context via `contextvars`** (async-task-local, non-racy) — the principal is set **once** at the autonomous-turn boundary in `execution_service.run_agent_execution` and read at every chokepoint; `contextvars` propagate into awaited coroutines + child tasks so concurrent sessions stay isolated and **no signature threading** is needed (an interactive user turn leaves it unset → baseline). Three chokepoints read the ambient principal and **deny before executing**: `invoke_mcp_tool` (MCP tools), `_run_component` (component tools), `invoke_connector_tool` (connectors); `enforce_tool()` **fails closed** (error → deny), denials return a **terminal non-retryable** result stamped `agent_denied`. Origin→principal: `genie_parent`/`genie_child`/`flow`/`scheduler`/`mcp` are autonomous; a scheduled task's `source=scheduler` now maps to the scheduler origin. Genie *slaves* run as separate HTTP requests (own task/context) → no cross-task leak. **UX:** a world-class, process-focused **Agent Authority** profile-editor card (frames the model, then allow-autonomous · read-only · denied-tools · connector allow-list · per-run budget; theme-aware, monochrome, collapsed by default). **Honest scope (charter #19):** this is the *attainable* form — capability scoping + audit + enforcement; the **fuller OBDA data-slice form** ("cannot query outside its graph slice") is **deferred to Tier 5 Step 5** (prerequisite absent). Default (no `authorityConfig`) = **byte-identical baseline**. **Proof:** 46 CI assertions (`test/test_agent_authority.py` — decision · subset invariant · contextvar propagation-across-awaits · **concurrent-turn isolation** · fail-closed enforce · denial shape) + a **live integration proof** through the real `invoke_mcp_tool` chokepoint (owner passes; autonomous agent denied `base_writeQuery` before touching MCP; permitted read passes) + the real stored-profile→scope loop (`@OPTIM`). **Server restart** for backend + `index.html`; JS browser-reload. **Architecture:** [docs/Architecture/AGENT_AUTHORITY_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/AGENT_AUTHORITY_ARCHITECTURE.md). Files: `core/agent_authority.py`, `agent/execution_service.py`, `mcp_adapter/adapter.py`, `components/manager.py`, `core/platform_connector_registry.py`, `static/js/handlers/configurationHandler.js`, `templates/index.html`, `test/test_agent_authority.py`.

Tier 5 Step 2, reframed by design review from "governed-segment *gate*" to **trust as a visible, cryptographically-verifiable badge on the agent** (⚪ unsigned · 🟢 signed-and-intact · 🟠 signed-but-changed). **The agent is the sole unit of trusted exposure/consumption**, and trust is **compositional** — *a signed agent contains only signed ingredients* (ontology, skills, …); Ed25519 sign/verify reusing `eval/online.py:sign_payload` — the **same provenance key** as EPC + eval attestations); `composition.py` (real profile → active KG + active skills → live badge; `sign_agent` enforces the bottom-up gate); **51 CI assertions** (`test/test_trust_membrane.py`); default (no attestations) = **byte-identical baseline** (every agent ⚪). **Terminology settled:** KG = ontology (one object); **publish = share** (marketplace) vs **sign off = attest trust**; the estate nav recommended rename **"Platform Map"** (not yet renamed in code). **Trust is orthogonal to access** (badge = validated, not authorized; secrets/identity never travel with a shared agent — self-describing, not self-authorizing). **Not built:** the badge UI (Platform-Map agent node + guided bottom-up signing), Model B grounding, ingredient validators beyond ontology. - **Jun 2026**: **Tier 4.1 — Open Semantic-Interchange Standards (T4): bidirectional, lossless KG/metric ↔ W3C standards**. The leapfrog roadmap's T4 epic — the cheapest leapfrog on the board (*all six vendors AMBER, nobody GREEN*). Uderia's KG (a navigable ontology) and metrics (a real semantic layer) were locked in a proprietary `export_version 2.0` JSON; this ships a **pure, deterministic, zero-LLM, bidirectional** adapter that re-serializes them into recognised **W3C open standards** *and parses them losslessly back*. New module **`src/trusted_data_agent/semantic_interchange/`** (`vocab`/`kg_to_rdf`/`rdf_to_kg`/`metric_to_qb`/`catalog`/`serializers`/`__init__`) built on `rdflib>=7`: **SKOS** (concept/taxonomy layer → `skos:Concept`/`narrower`/`broader`), **RDFS/OWL** (logical `entity`→`owl:Class`, `attribute`→`owl:DatatypeProperty`+`rdfs:domain`), **RDF Data Cube / QB** (metric → `qb:DataStructureDefinition` with `qb:DimensionProperty`/`qb:MeasureProperty` components — the exact structural fit for dimensions+measures), **PROV-O** (`implements`/`derives_from`/deployed views → `prov:wasDerivedFrom`), **DCAT** (KG + each metric as `dcat:Dataset`/`dcat:DataService`); serialized as **Turtle / JSON-LD / RDF-XML / N-Triples**. **The round-trip backbone is a dual-layer serialization** (charter #6, #20): every triple set carries (a) the **standard predicate** for *interoperability* — a Protégé / SPARQL / DCAT consumer reads only SKOS/OWL/QB and never touches Uderia internals — and (b) a parallel **`uderia:` annotation layer** (`entityType`, the full properties dict as one canonical JSON literal, reified relationships with type/cardinality/metadata) for *lossless reversibility*; relationships are emitted **both** as a direct standard-predicate edge (interop) and a reified `uderia:Relationship` resource (re-import). Standard predicates are used **only where the semantics are exact** (`contains`→`skos:narrower`, `is_a`→`rdfs:subClassOf`, `implements`/`derives_from`→`prov:wasDerivedFrom`); types without an exact standard predicate fall back to a `uderia:` predicate rather than misusing a standard one (charter #1 — no shortcuts). Import is **deterministic too**: the `uderia:` layer is read straight back (exact); a *foreign* graph with no `uderia:` layer degrades to a best-effort standard-predicate mapping that records what it couldn't place in `warnings` (honest, never silent — arbitrary external-ontology import stays deferred since precise mapping needs judgement / an LLM). **REST seam (additive):** `GET /v1/knowledge-graph/export` extended with `?format=json|skos|owl|rdf` (default `json` **unchanged**) + `?serialization=`; new `GET /v1/knowledge-graph/metrics/<name>/export?format=qb|prov|dcat|all` (+`?include_sql`); new `POST /v1/knowledge-graph/import-rdf` (create|merge, reuses the existing `import_bulk` migration chokepoint). Reuses the existing `_assert_kg_enabled` tier gate + `kg_id`→owner-profile resolution — **no new master switch** (re-serializing data the user can already export adds no authority). **Side-fix:** the existing JSON export called the now-`async` `list_entities`/`list_relationships`/`get_stats` (May-2026 KG-store abstraction) **without `await`** — a latent bug serializing coroutine objects; now awaited (verified live: 86 real entities). **Live-verified (2026-06-29):** a real 86-entity / 128-relationship KG (logical+physical+metric) → Turtle → `POST /import-rdf` into a fresh KG → **entity set identical, relationship set identical, 0 property mismatches, 0 warnings**; all four serializations 200; metric export emits valid QB+PROV+DCAT; `format=json` regression intact; errors 400/404. **79 CI assertions** (`test/test_semantic_interchange.py` — type mapping, `uderia:` layer, lossless reconstruct across all four serializations, graph isomorphism, metric↔QB, foreign-graph fallback+warnings, vocab filtering, determinism, input non-mutation) + a **standalone offline verifier** (`docs/proof-packs/samples/verify_open_standards.py`, runnable with only `pip install rdflib`, **23/23**: round-trip · re-importability · QB structural conformance · third-party SPARQL consumption of dims/measures · tamper-evidence). **UX surfaces (charter #2 — reachable in the app, not just REST):** three theme-aware frontend affordances (CSS vars + monochrome SVG icons + `localStorage` token) — **(1)** the KG-panel **Export** button is now a format-menu popover (JSON · Turtle · JSON-LD · RDF/XML · N-Triples · OWL-only · SKOS-only); **(2)** the **Import** dialog accepts `.ttl/.jsonld/.rdf/.nt/.xml` (serialization auto-detected by extension) → `import-rdf`, surfacing returned `warnings[]`; **(3)** **right-click → Export as RDF Data Cube** on `metric` nodes in the KG inspector (+ tooltip hint). JS is **browser-reload only** (no restart): `static/js/api.js`, `static/js/handlers/knowledgeGraphPanelHandler.js`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/renderer.js`. **Server restart** for the REST seam; the converter is import-only. Roadmap: `LEAPFROG_ROADMAP.md` Tier 4.1 ✅ (T4 → GREEN). Design: `TIER_4.1_OPEN_STANDARDS.md`. Proof: [docs/proof-packs/T4_OPEN_STANDARDS.md](proof-packs/T4_OPEN_STANDARDS.md). Consolidated platform-wide posture: [OPEN_STANDARDS_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/OPEN_STANDARDS_ARCHITECTURE.md) (semantic interchange + MCP + OTLP + OAuth/OIDC/SAML + Ed25519/Fernet). - **Jun 2026**: **Knowledge Graph enrichment promoted to a budget-managed context module + registry-default activation fix**. KG enrichment was previously appended **raw onto the `knowledge_context` channel** by each engine — bounded by a fixed 500-**node** cap (not tokens), with no independent budget, no condensation policy, and no bar in the `context_window_snapshot` (a recorded case hit ~21 KB / ~5–6K tokens in one turn). Promoted into a first-class **11th builtin module** `knowledge_graph_context` (P72, sibling of `knowledge_context`): the subgraph node count now **scales to the module's token allocation** (`max_nodes = clamp(budget/~30, 20, 500)`); condensation re-trims trailing (least-critical) lines, preserving the TABLE SCHEMAS / JOIN backbone. **Single-source** — the extraction/format/scope logic stays in the KG **component** (`components/builtin/knowledge_graph/handler.py:get_context_enrichment` gained an additive `max_nodes` param, threaded through `ComponentManager.get_context_enrichment` inspect-gated so 3-arg handlers never break); the module is a thin seam over `get_component_context_enrichment`. **All-engine (IFOC):** the four direct engines read the orchestrator-cached output via `executor._get_kg_enrichment()` (cache-with-fallback, mirroring `_cw_component_instructions`; falls back to the legacy direct fetch when assembly is off → **zero regression**); genie is covered through its slaves (real I/F/O engines) and injects no KG text of its own, so it's excluded from `applies_to`. The contribution's `metadata.kg_enrichment_event` (`scope_databases`/`scope_entities`) is preserved verbatim so the **grounding gate (Tier 1.1) is unchanged** (regression-verified). **Activation fix (the real blocker):** the Context Window Type's `modules` dict was a strict **allowlist** — Pass 1 only iterated CWT-listed modules, and CWTs live per-user in `user_preferences` (seeded once from bootstrap `tda_config.json`, never re-read). So registered-but-unlisted modules — **both `user_memory` and the new KG module** — were dormant on existing instances (registered → shown in the "Installed Context Modules" UI, but never run in the five-pass). Fixed by making Pass 1 **registry-aware**: it activates the **union** of (CWT-listed) ∪ (all registered) modules, registered-but-unlisted ones running with their manifest defaults; the CWT dict became an **override** layer (deactivate/retune), not an allowlist. No per-user migration; `tda_config.json` untouched. Safe because every module self-gates to an empty contribution when its feature is off (this also activated the previously-dormant `user_memory`). `condensation_order` is append-augmented so merged condensable modules stay reducible. **42 CI assertions** (`test/test_kg_context_module.py` — module contribute/condense/abstain, grounding-event parity, budget→nodes, registry-default merge, explicit-deactivation override, inspect-gated pass-through); grounding 102 / kg_scope_derivation 17 / memory 77 regression-clean. **Server restart** (backend). - **Jun 2026**: **Tier 2.2 — Agent Memory (A7): managed, governed, inspectable cross-session memory**. The leapfrog roadmap's A7 epic — promotes Uderia's implicit memory substrates into a **named product**, built as a **component** (KG precedent: the action component owns a tool + backend store + a context contribution). **Naming (deliberate, two layers):** **Agent Memory** = durable facts *about the user* (preferences/identity/style), recalled into every session; **Context Window** = this session's working/conversation memory (the industry term, kept). "Long-term" retired — both are long-term; the axis is *user* vs *conversation*. Surfaced as two sub-tabs (**Context Window** + **Agent Memory**) under the Configuration **Memory** tab. **Architecture:** `components/builtin/memory/` backend (`types`/`store`/`recall`/`adapter`/`extractor`/`runtime`, imported from `src` as `components.builtin.memory.*` — KG precedent) over a dedicated **`agent_memory` table** (SQLAlchemy model in `auth/models.py`, self-applying `create_all`, cascade-on-user-delete; row-level so each fact is independently scoped/inspectable/erasable — NOT crammed into `preferences_json`). **Scope model — per-agent by default + a shared pool:** every write (tool/manual/learned) defaults to **agent-scoped** (`profile_id` set → only that agent recalls it); an explicit `scope:global` stores it **shared** (`profile_id=NULL` → all the user's agents recall it, for genuine user-level facts). An agent's recall view = its own items ∪ shared. A **flow owns no memory** — each LLM node is an individual agent (its profile) recalling/writing its own memory via the normal `/query` path (flow_executor.py:745); "a flow's memory" = the composition of its node-agents' memories (flow durable *state* is the separate `flow_variables` feature). **Recall is the all-engine headline (charter #14):** a 10th builtin context module `components/builtin/context_window/modules/user_memory/` ranks the user's memory **deterministically** (scope filter + keyword overlap + recency + confidence + recall-count — charter #20, zero LLM) and injects a `[Remembered about this user]` block for **every** profile type; observability rides the existing `context_window_snapshot` (recalled item contents in `Contribution.metadata`). **Three write paths**, each abstaining cleanly where N/A: (1) explicit `TDA_Memory` tool (`remember`/`forget`/`list_memories`, deterministic 0-token, companion `memory-expert` skill); (2) **opt-in** background learned-extraction (the *one* LLM use — `componentConfig.memory.learn`, fire-and-forget at the `execution_service` eval seam mirroring `_dispatch_online_eval`, never blocks/throws, **cost-accounted via `CostManager`** with a `memory_extraction` call_id + `memory_write` event); (3) manual REST/UI CRUD. **Governance = standard component chain (no bespoke master switch):** `enabled_for: []` ⇒ **off by default ⇒ byte-identical baseline (#15)** *(superseded Aug 2026 — memory is now `enabled_for` all four profile types, i.e. default-ON, per an explicit operator decision; an explicit `componentConfig.memory.enabled:false` still wins)*; `componentConfig.memory = {enabled, learn, scope, maxItems}`; resolution reuses the authoritative `_component_enabled_for_profile` logic (`is_component_available` → explicit `enabled` → manifest `enabled_for`), **never** `get_active_components`. **UX — a standard Workspace component (no dedicated resource-rail tab):** Agent Memory behaves exactly like the other components (canvas/dashboard/flow/scheduler/KG — shared `sp-header` chrome, registered in `splitPanelResizer.js` for the shared resize bar, fullscreen button). The Workspace **Agent Memory** section lists two launcher rows (**Local** / **Global**, `GET /v1/memory/buckets`) opening a **world-class two-pane read/write manager** (`#memory-split-panel`, `openMemorySplitPanel`): **owner rail** (Global + every agent, IFOC-coloured, counts, active marker — `GET /v1/memory/owners`) | **item manager** (inline edit, kind select, pause/activate via `active`, **move/promote** to another agent or Global via `PUT profile_id`, provenance *source·used N×·recalled Xago*, search/kind-filter/sort, multi-select bulk, add, clear-view) + **recall-preview transparency** (per-agent query → the exact rank-ordered items that would be injected, `POST /v1/memory/recall-preview`). **Intelligent-component (principle #1):** the LLM `remember` surface needs only `content` — the component **deterministically infers `kind`** (`types.infer_kind`), defaults scope, handles dedup, and applies a **global-scope safety net** (`types.detect_global_scope` reads `comp_context["user_query"]` and forces `scope=global` on phrasing like "global … memory"/"all my agents" that weak models ignore); `instructions.json` is the thin contract, judgement lives in the `memory-expert` skill. The open canvas **live-refreshes** on a `uderia:turn-complete` event when the agent writes memory mid-conversation. **Inline chat card (same UX as the other components):** `renderMemory` is registered in `componentRenderers.js` and renders a compact high-level card (summary + the stored fact(s) + scope + **stat chips**: total / global / this-agent / kind breakdown from `spec.stats` computed by the handler) with a "View in Canvas → / Expanded in side panel →" toggle. All cards' buttons stay in sync with the panel via `_syncMemCards` (open ⇒ "Expanded…", close ⇒ "View in Canvas →") — mirroring scheduler's shared-class button reset. It **auto-opens the canvas when `window.__canvasSplitMode` is on** (mirrors flow/dashboard/scheduler) and opens to the item's owner (global vs agent). The canvas presentation is a refined two-pane design (owner rail with IFOC dots/active marker, hover-revealed row actions, compact kind chip-selects, centered content column, empty/preview states). Close + close-on-session-switch match the other panels (`splitPanelResizer` registration, `display:none` after transition). The Configuration **Memory** tab carries two sub-tabs — **Context Window** (the existing session/working-memory budget config, industry term kept) and **Agent Memory** (informational: an industrial Global-vs-Local visual + an "Agent Memory component settings →" link that opens the Components view on the memory component via `componentHandler.openComponentDetail('memory')`; no config here). **GDPR (charter #8):** clear-view per bucket + 6 REST endpoints (`GET/POST /v1/memory`, `PUT/DELETE /v1/memory/<id>`, `DELETE /v1/memory/all`, `POST /v1/memory/recall-preview`); reads + erase are **never gated by the component flag**. **Live-verified (2026-06-28):** component + `user_memory` module discovered; untouched profile recalls **0** (baseline preserved); enabled profile recalls; **cross-session recall reaches the LLM** (stored "EMEA" → fresh session "Which region?" → "You report on the EMEA region."); agent self-write via `TDA_Memory` (`source=explicit`); inspect/erase round-trip. **68 CI assertions** (`test/test_memory.py`). Server restart (backend + `index.html`); JS browser-reload. Design/architecture: `docs/roadmap/TIER_2.2_AGENT_MEMORY.md`. - **Jun 2026**: **Process-wide SQLite serialization — root-cause fix for a multi-thread deadlock that froze the whole server**. The server is a single asyncio loop but SQLite was touched from many OS threads (the loop + `run_in_executor`/`to_thread` workers + the SQLAlchemy pool). SQLite's unix VFS coordinates **every** connection in a process through a **process-global mutex** that **every** op takes (WAL read `walTryBeginRead → unixShmBarrier`, write commit, open `findReusableFd`, close `unixLock`); two of these on different threads at once hit a file-lock⇄VFS-mutex **lock-order inversion** and **deadlock** — and the event-loop thread being one of the wedged callers froze the entire server (login/polls/everything). Confirmed by repeated live `sample <pid>` stack captures (loop wedged in connection-init, then a WAL read, while other threads sat in open/close). WAL + `busy_timeout` + a `QueuePool` (replacing the cross-thread-shared `StaticPool`) each *reduced probability* but **cannot fix a cross-thread hazard**. **Fix — new canonical access layer [`core/sqlite_util.py`](../src/trusted_data_agent/core/sqlite_util.py)** enforcing two invariants: (1) **no two threads inside libsqlite3 at once** — every C-call (open, each `execute`/`fetch` on a connection AND its cursors, commit, rollback, close) holds one process-wide re-entrant `_DB_LOCK`, held only around short C-calls, **never across an `await`**; (2) **write transactions atomic under the lock** — once a statement opens a write transaction the connection keeps `_DB_LOCK` until commit/rollback/close (via `in_transaction`), so writers never busy-wait into `database is locked`. `connect()` returns a transparent drop-in `sqlite3.Connection` wrapper (no `__del__` — would break chained `connect().execute()`). **SQLAlchemy routes through the same lock** (pool `creator` returns the wrapped connection; `auth/database.py` switched file-DB pool `StaticPool`→`QueuePool`, `:memory:` keeps `StaticPool`). **CANONICAL RULE: always open SQLite via `sqlite_util.connect()` — never `sqlite3.connect` directly.** All **203 `sqlite3.connect(` sites across 45 files migrated** (module-level import verified via `ast`). **16 CI assertions** (`test/test_sqlite_util.py`) incl. an 8-reader/4-writer open/close/read/write storm reproduction (completes, no deadlock, no lock-errors) + concurrent-ORM-write correctness (90/90 rows). **Live-proven**: the Tier 1.4 grounding benchmark (36 back-to-back sessions — the exact load that froze the server 3×) ran to completion with the server responsive on every poll, incl. cases 13 & 27 that previously wedged it. Server restart. Doc: [docs/Architecture/SQLITE_CONCURRENCY.md](Architecture/SQLITE_CONCURRENCY.md). Files: `core/sqlite_util.py`, `auth/database.py` + 43 migrated modules, `test/test_sqlite_util.py`.
- **Jun 2026**: **Grounding gate → judge-backed enforce + recall-first trigger; anti-hallucination benchmark VALIDATED (Tier 1.1 / 1.4)**. The first benchmark run **disproved** the deterministic-block gate (it over-blocks honest "not in scope" refusals and misses prose-phrased answer-drift). Re-architected to **judge-backed enforce**: the deterministic gate is **observe-only + a recall-first trigger** (`needs_judge`), and the **`scope_faithfulness` LLM judge** makes the real **block (drifted) · pass (faithful, incl. honest refusals) · annotate (judge unavailable, fail-safe)** call — bounded by `ONLINE_EVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, cost via `CostManager`, runs only on the opt-in `enforce` path. Pure decision in `agent/grounding/enforce.py:resolve_enforced_verdict`; executor `_enforce_grounding_with_judge` + `_attribute_grounding_judge_cost`; wired through one shared `executor._run_grounding_gate_full` across all five engines. The trigger became **recall-first / allowlist-based** (`answer_out_of_scope_refs`): instead of matching known out-of-scope *phrasings* (a leaky regex arms race), it flags any **structural data reference** (dotted `db.table`, a quoted identifier, or a technical identifier near a container word) **not in `scope_databases ∪ scope_entities ∪ SYSTEM_DBS`** — `scope_entities` threaded `RunRecord.kg_scope_entities()` → `GroundingInputs`. Self-maintaining, degrades to DB-only. New `ScopeFaithfulnessJudge` (domain-only rubric). **Final live benchmark (36 cases, $0.031): trigger recall 0% → 25% → 100%, 0 false negatives, net governance drift 6% → 0%.** Benchmark report re-framed to score the trigger's recall of judge-confirmed drift (`trigger_decision`, pinned to the gate's `needs_judge`); dataset grew to 36 cases (12/18/6) with 6 drift-eliciting cases. **98 CI assertions** (`test_grounding.py`), +17 `test_kg_scope_derivation.py`, +34 `test_grounding_benchmark.py`; all eval suites regression-clean. Docs: [AGENT_OPS_EVAL_ARCHITECTURE.md §6a/§6b](Architecture/AGENT_OPS_EVAL_ARCHITECTURE.md), `TIER_1.1`, `TIER_1.4`. Server restart. - **Jun 2026**: **Tier 2.1 — Uderia as an MCP server (A3)**. Uderia becomes an MCP **provider**: any external MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, another agent) can call a governed Uderia profile *as a tool*. The differentiator is trust — `ask_profile` runs the full pipeline, so the answer is **grounding-gated (Tier 1.1) + guardrailed (Tier 1.3)** before it leaves the building. New module **`src/trusted_data_agent/mcp_server/`** is a **thin facade over the REST API** (adds zero new execution path): `client.py` = `UderiaRestClient` (pure httpx: `create_session → submit_query → poll_task` + `list_profiles`/`resolve_profile_id`/`list_knowledge_graphs`, no fastmcp imports → unit-testable with `httpx.MockTransport`); `server.py` = the `FastMCP` app + `@mcp.tool()` functions (`ask_profile`, `list_profiles`, `list_knowledge_graphs`); `__main__.py` = CLI (`python -m trusted_data_agent.mcp_server [--transport stdio|http]`, STDIO default — the `google_search.py` pattern). **Auth = a Uderia 90-day access token** via `UDERIA_ACCESS_TOKEN` env (the STDIO-subprocess model); `UDERIA_BASE_URL` (default `http://localhost:5050`) targets the instance. **Governance is enforced server-side by the REST layer** — the token's user, profile/component access, consumption limits, and per-profile grounding/guardrail modes all apply; the MCP server holds no policy. `result.guardrail_blocked` is surfaced so a caller distinguishes a refused turn from an answer. **Consumer-tier tool segmentation (HARD GATE):** `--profile user|developer|admin|all` (`UDERIA_MCP_PROFILE`) selects the tool surface; the CLI resolves the token's actual tier from `GET /auth/me` at startup and clamps to `min(launch profile, token tier)` **before any tool is served** — a user-tier token launched with `--profile admin` can never even see developer/admin tools; resolution **fails safe to `user`** (least privilege). Tiered catalog (`server.py:TOOL_CATALOG`): `user`={ask_profile, list_profiles, list_knowledge_graphs}, `developer`+={list_collections, list_sessions, get_my_usage}, `admin`+={system_usage, list_user_usage}; `all`=full. **39 CI assertions** (`test/test_mcp_server.py`, MockTransport — full ask flow, tag resolution, poll timeout/failure, 401, guardrail pass-through, tool registration, `/auth/me` tier resolution, tier segmentation, hard-gate clamp, fail-safe). **Live-verified (2026-06-28):** a real `fastmcp.Client` over streamable-HTTP returned 26 real profiles + `ask_profile(IDEAT)` answered; `--profile user/developer/admin` → 2/6/8 tools (admin token). The down-clamp is **live-verified**: a real **developer**-tier access token + `--profile admin` clamped to exactly the 6 developer tools (admin tools absent, `clamped to token tier 'developer'`); an unauthenticatable token also fails safe to the 2 user tools (CI: `t_hard_gate_clamp`). The live developer token was minted via the admin **"create as pre-verified"** option (below). *(Historical note: an apparent "tier not reflecting" symptom investigated 2026-06-28 was NOT a bug — a freshly admin-created user failed `email_verified` at login → empty token, and an error-response parsing artifact made `/auth/me` look like it returned null tier. `verify_access_token`/tier resolution are correct; the pre-verified option removes the provisioning friction that caused it.)* **Boundaries (honest):** single-token-per-process auth (multi-user per-request Bearer is a follow-up the facade already supports); reads + the ask flow only (write/`TDA_*`/`compile_metric` promotion is the next increment — each endpoint's tier is pre-recorded in the matrix); runs standalone (not yet mounted into the Quart app). **Full REST→MCP tier matrix:** [docs/RestAPI/MCP_TIER_MATRIX.md](RestAPI/MCP_TIER_MATRIX.md) (552 endpoints classified all/developer/admin/N-A). **restAPI.md** updated: new §3.33 (MCP server) + §3.34–3.38 (previously-undocumented families: Evals, KG management + KG Store, Database Connections, Platform Connectors + Registry, Component Instances + Knowledge-repo documents) + audit findings (§9). - **Jun 2026**: **Online-eval hardening — the hook no longer blocks a turn + admin agent-eval settings persist across restart**. Two production fixes after enabling banded thresholds + judges hung a live turn (the server went unresponsive, Stop couldn't interrupt). **Root cause:** `evaluate_turn_online` was **`await`ed inline** in `run_agent_execution`'s critical path with **no timeout**; with judges on, a stalled judge LLM call froze turn completion indefinitely (contradicting the documented "never blocks a turn"). **Fix 1 (never blocks):** the hook is now dispatched as a **tracked background task** (`execution_service._dispatch_online_eval`, strong-ref'd to avoid GC, discarded on done) — the answer is already delivered, scoring is pure observability and runs off-path. Inside the hook, **deterministic scoring runs first (instant, always persists the bands)**, then the judge layer runs **bounded by `asyncio.wait_for(ONLINE_EVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=25)`**; the turn is selected **by `turn_id`** (not `wf[-1]`, since a fast next turn may have appended). The panel now calls every judge model **concurrently** (`asyncio.gather`), each bounded by `ONLINE_EVAL_JUDGE_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=20` → a hung model degrades to `unknown` instead of stalling the panel or blocking on N sequential timeouts. **Live Quality card preserved:** since backgrounding closes the per-request `/ask_stream` before scoring finishes (so `processStream` no longer sees `turn_score_complete` → card only showed on reload), the hook now ALSO broadcasts the event over the **per-user notification channel** (`APP_STATE["notification_queues"]`); `notifications.js` renders it session-guarded and the idempotent overlay prevents double-render — verified live (event delivered with all 21 verdicts, correct session/turn). **Fix 2 (persistence):** the whole `agent_eval` block (online toggle, judges, judge rate, 14 banded thresholds) is now **persisted to the `system_settings` table** (key `agent_eval`, JSON) on save and **restored into `APP_CONFIG` at startup** via `_sync_agent_eval_to_config()` (mirrors the `tts_mode` pattern; `SystemSettings.setting_value` widened `String(255)`→`Text` so the threshold JSON fits) — an admin's saved Balanced set survives a restart instead of resetting to the `config.py` seed. **Verified live:** the exact config that hung before (judges on, sample 1.0, Balanced) now **completes in ~7s** with the server responsive, the backgrounded judges still score (span carries all deterministic + 4 judge dims), and judges/thresholds **survive a restart**. All 8 eval suites green. Server restart for backend. Doc: [AGENT_OPS_EVAL_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/AGENT_OPS_EVAL_ARCHITECTURE.md) §6.4. The KG/ontology is **strictly additive support** — it enriches the engines, never alters them (a design imperative: deleting the KG → all four IFOC engines run identically; the KG produces identifiers + SQL *text*, the engines execute). **(1) Deterministic logical→deployed resolver** (`components/builtin/knowledge_graph/resolver.py`, new): resolves each logical `table`/`metric` to its real, queryable **deployed** identifier (+ metric-view/compilable capability), preferring the deployed Teradata layer over the Databricks *reference* layer. The constructor modal gated *deploy* on "Include physical layer (PDM)", which made the walker emit the **Databricks reference** physical layer (per-domain catalog/schema), so deploying produced **two** physical layers (Databricks reference + Teradata deployed) — doubling physical nodes (e.g. `schema 4` = 3 Databricks + 1 Teradata; `physical_table 68` = 34 + 34) and leaving a layer that isn't actually queryable, with ambiguous `implements` linkage. **Removed the Databricks reference PDM option entirely**: the modal now makes **deploy the sole physical path** (always available, sends `layers=["logical"]`), so the KG↔warehouse `implements` edges target the **deployed Teradata schema**. The three deploy controls (`comments`/`replace_existing`/`deploy_metric_views`) and the dry-run/result summaries were de-coupled from the removed checkbox and the stale per-domain labels fixed. **Validation (the key concern — "does anything context-relevant live only on Databricks?"): NO.** Compared all property keys across logical vs Databricks-physical vs Teradata-physical columns: every property maps to the logical node and/or the deployed Teradata node. **Layering rule (now documented):** *storage type is physical* (`physical_column.datatype` = `DECIMAL(15,2)`/`VARCHAR(4000)`, per backend) — never on the logical node; *semantic meaning is logical* (`column.semantic_type`, 100% column coverage; `value_regex`; `references`). Confirmed the walker with `layers=["logical"]` emits zero physical nodes and the deploy supplies a Teradata-only physical layer → one clean PDM. **Data-domain / logical-type-class concept added to the docs (deliberately deferred, not built):** the formal logical analog of a physical type is a reusable normalized type class (a `taxonomy` node columns `is_a`) — deferred because `semantic_type` already carries most of the signal, source models don't declare domains (would be derived), and no consumer needs it yet. - **Jun 2026**: **PDM deploy — DDL throughput: batching is impossible on Teradata; the real lever is comment verbosity (default now `none`)**. Investigated batching the ~1,464 single-round-trip DDL statements (~164s table phase). **Finding (empirically proven against live Teradata): DDL throughput batching is not achievable.** (1) Teradata **forbids multiple DDL statements in one multi-statement request** — "Only an ET/COMMIT WORK or null statement is legal after a DDL" (Error 3932 in BTET mode, 3722 in ANSI). (2) **Parallel sessions give only ~1.2×** — Teradata serializes DDL on the per-database dictionary lock, so concurrent CREATEs in the single flat database contend (a naive fresh-connection-per-statement pool was actually *slower*). (3) `teradataml.execute_sql` vs a raw persistent cursor: 2 ms/statement difference — negligible. The ~150 ms/statement is inherent DDL latency. **The only real lever is reducing statement count, and `COMMENT ON` is 1,299 of 1,629 statements (~89%)** — and those descriptions already live in full on the KG nodes (logical `table`/`column` + physical `physical_table`/`physical_column` `description` property; the DB COMMENT is a redundant bounded 255-char projection). So added a **`comments` deploy option (`all` | `table` | `none`)** threaded through `converter.convert` → `dialects/teradata._emit_table` → `declarative_model` → REST body, **defaulting to `none`** (DB comments off — the graph is the system of record). `all` = table + column comments (prior behavior), `table` = table comments only. **Measured live:** default `comments=none` cut the DDL phase from **~164s → ~69s (2.4×)** for restaurants/mvm corporate (1,629 → 330 statements; remaining time now dominated by the 131 soft-RI FK `ALTER`s, which are optimizer-valuable and kept); verified 34 tables + 131 FKs + **0 column comments**, full descriptions intact on the KG. **+5 CI assertions** (`test_pdm_converter` `test_comment_levels`) → **328 PDM total, 0 failures**. **Constructor modal UX:** the three deploy controls added across this work — **DB comments** (`none`/`table`/`all`), **Replace existing** (idempotent re-deploy, default on), **Metric views** — are now surfaced as a single compact wrapping row in the deploy sub-section of `kgIndustryModelModal.js` (with `title` tooltips, no extra vertical sprawl); stale "per-domain databases" labels/summaries replaced with flat-model-accurate text (one database; tables/FKs/comments/views/stats counts; `replaced` count on re-deploy). **Server restart** for the REST `comments` wiring; modal JS is browser-reload only. Doc: `docs/Architecture/INDUSTRY_MODEL_PDM_DEPLOYMENT_PLAN.md` banner update #6.
- **Jun 2026**: **PDM deploy — re-deploy idempotency (closes the prior open gap)**. `execute_ddl` issued bare `CREATE TABLE` (no `DROP`-first), so re-deploying over existing objects failed with **Error 3803 "table already exists"** — every re-run in the deploy work above needed a manual drop first. Fixed with `execute_ddl(replace_existing=True)` (default ON for the deploy via `declarative_model`, exposed as `replace_existing` in the REST body): a new `TeradataDeploymentBackend._drop_plan_objects(plan)` drops the plan's **own** views + tables before creating. **Scoped strictly to the plan's identifiers** (never arbitrary objects), **views-first** (they depend on tables), then a **multi-pass table drop** — a soft-RI parent can't drop while a child references it (Error 5313), so each pass drops the now-unreferenced tables until none remain (proven FK-safe; acyclic industry-model FK graphs converge; a true cycle stops and lets CREATE surface the real error). First/clean deploys: every drop is a no-op (Error 3807 "does not exist" ignored via `_is_missing_object`). `DeployResult.replaced` surfaces the dropped objects in the deploy summary. **Live-verified:** re-deploying over a fully-populated `restaurants_mvm_test` (34 tables + 27 views) succeeds with **0 Error 3803** (previously impossible without a manual drop). **+12 CI assertions** (`test_pdm_deploy`: `test_redeploy_idempotent_drops_then_creates` with a stateful RI-simulating fake, `test_first_deploy_drops_are_noops`, `test_replace_existing_off_does_not_drop`) → **323 PDM total, 0 failures**. **Server restart** for the REST `replace_existing` wiring.
