- **Jun 2026**: **PDM metric track — first live test surfaces + fixes 4 Spark→Teradata transpilation bugs + a REST wiring gap**. Every prior deploy used `include_metrics:false`, so the M7 metric track (KG metric enrichment + Teradata metric views + `compile_metric` tool) was untested live — and untested under the new flat namespace. Live testing (restaurants/mvm corporate, 27 metric views) found the metric **views create-or-query-fail on Teradata** because SQLGlot's Teradata dialect mis-renders four Spark constructs; all fixed in `dbdeploy/metric_compiler.py:translate_expr` via an AST `transform` (`_td_datefix`): **(1)** `TIMESTAMP_TRUNC`/`DATE_TRUNC(col, UNIT)` → `TRUNC(CAST(col AS DATE), '<fmt>')` (SQLGlot emitted a bare `TIMESTAMP_TRUNC` — no such Teradata function, Error 3706); **(2)** string casts rendered as `… AS TEXT` → `VARCHAR(4000)` (Teradata has no TEXT type, Error 3706); **(3)** boolean literals `TRUE`/`FALSE` → `1`/`0` (Teradata reads them as column names, Error 5628); **(4)** Spark `CAST` mis-mapped to Teradata `TRYCAST`, which only accepts CHAR/VARCHAR *input* → plain `CAST` (Error 9134 at query time on numeric/date casts). Plus a **transform-ordering fix**: the cast handler rendered its inner expression before nested functions (e.g. `DATEDIFF` inside a `CAST`) were transformed, freezing them — fixed by recursively `transform`-ing each child before rendering (`_render`). Also **`DATEDIFF`** (no Teradata equivalent) → `EXTRACT` month/year math or DATE subtraction, and **`DATE_ADD`/`TS_OR_DS_ADD`** → date arithmetic. **REST wiring gap:** `deploy_metric_views` was never passed into the constructor options dict in `rest_routes.py` (so metric views couldn't be triggered via REST) — added. **Validated end-to-end (direct, new code):** 27/27 views CREATE **and** QUERY against loaded data; KG metric nodes enriched (dimensions/measures counts); 27 `ddl_artifact` nodes (`implements` metric, `derives_from` table); the **`compile_metric` runtime tool** resolves a metric from its KG node, compiles ratio-safe slice SQL, and **executes against live Teradata** (5 grouped rows). **+4 CI assertions** (`test_pdm_metrics` `test_translate_expr`: TRUNC/VARCHAR/boolean/DATEDIFF) → metrics 63, **311 PDM total, 0 failures**. **Server restart** required for the REST `deploy_metric_views` wiring. Files: `dbdeploy/metric_compiler.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `test/test_pdm_metrics.py`.
- **Jun 2026**: **PDM deploy — canonical FLAT namespace + live-verified load/stats/generator fixes**. Live verification of the Teradata deploy against a real target drove a topology decision and three correctness/perf fixes. **(1) Flat single-database namespace (canonical).** Division and domain are now **logical-only KG entities** — never physical containers. Every table deploys flat into ONE root database under its bare name; a name is `<domain>_`-prefixed **only** on the rare ECM collision (validated globally-unique across all 30 MVM models / 5,556 tables; 20/30 ECM models reuse 1–6 generic names). This removes the logical↔physical asymmetry (division was in the *logical* containment chain but absent from the *physical* one), eliminates per-domain database sprawl + the PERM-subdivision scheme, and keeps the three-division scaffolding navigable in the graph. The single `schema` node `implements` nothing; each `physical_table` still `implements` its logical `<domain>.<table>` (logical name preserved via `PhysTable.logical_name`). "One LDM → many PDMs" holds — the deployed Teradata PDM is flat; the Databricks reference PDM (from the walker, `include_physical`) stays per-domain, distinguished by `infrastructure`. Impl: `dbdeploy/physical_model.py:flatten_to_single_database` + `flat_namespace=True` default in `converter.convert`; `declarative_model` provisions only the root DB. **(2) Native `executemany` bulk load** (replaces `copy_to_sql`): Teradata array binding (one parameterised `INSERT` per table) — faster (no per-table pandas+reflection) and surfaces the real row error via `{fn teradata_get_errors}` instead of a generic batch failure (`teradata_backend.py:_executemany_payloads`). **(3) COLLECT STATISTICS genuinely post-load:** `execute_ddl(include_statistics=False)` defers stats; a new `collect_statistics(plan, only_identifiers=…)` runs after the load on loaded tables only (was collecting on empty tables during DDL). **(4) Precision-aware synthetic generator:** `SyntheticDataSource` bounds `DECIMAL(p,s) < 10**(p-s)` and integers to their Teradata range (`BYTEINT` 127, `SMALLINT` 32767), fixing the numeric-overflow (Error 2616) that silently failed ~half the tables. **Known open gap:** re-deploy is **not idempotent** — `execute_ddl` issues bare `CREATE TABLE` (no `DROP`-first), so re-running over existing objects fails with Error 3803; cleanup-on-failure doesn't cover orphans from a prior aborted run (tracked for follow-up). **420 CI assertions** (added `test_pdm_converter` `test_flat_namespace`/`test_flat_collision_prefix`; mechanics tests pinned to `flat_namespace=False`). Live-verified: restaurants/mvm corporate → single flat `restaurants_mvm_test` (34 tables, 170 rows, stats post-load), KG physical layer flat with correct `implements`. Server restart for the backend changes. Docs: [ONTOLOGY_ARCHITECTURE.md §2.4a](Architecture/ONTOLOGY_ARCHITECTURE.md) (normative namespace rule), `docs/Architecture/INDUSTRY_MODEL_PDM_DEPLOYMENT_PLAN.md` (post-implementation banner). Files: `dbdeploy/{physical_model,converter,backend,teradata_backend,datasource,dialects/teradata}.py`, `agent/kg_constructors/declarative_model.py`, `test/test_pdm_{converter,dataload,constructor_deploy}.py`.
- **Jun 2026**: **PDM deploy — Teradata COMMENT length fix + no-content-loss guarantee** (live-verification fix surfaced by the transparent-error path: `[Error 5550] Comment string is longer than permitted` on `finance.general_ledger`). Teradata hard-caps `COMMENT ON` strings at **255 chars**; the industry-model `description` fields run far longer. **Best-practice resolution (graph = system of record, COMMENT = bounded DB-object label):** (1) the `COMMENT ON TABLE/COLUMN` value is clipped to the DBMS limit via a tunable `TeradataStandard.comment_max_chars` (default 255) + a charset-safe `_clip()` applied **before** SQL-literal escaping (apostrophe-doubling can't push a borderline comment over); (2) **no content loss** — the **full, untruncated** business description is now stamped onto the **physical KG node** (`physical_table`/`physical_column` `description` property in `_emit_kg_delta`), so the complete text is preserved on the physical layer of the graph (it was already on the logical node via the walker). The COMMENT is therefore an honest 255-char projection of content the graph holds in full. **+5 CI assertions** (`test/test_pdm_converter.py` `test_comment_truncation`: COMMENT ≤255 **and** physical nodes carry the full 600-char description) → converter 72 / dbdeploy 256 total, 0 failures. Server restart for the live deploy to pick up the converter change. Files: `dbdeploy/design_standard.py`, `dbdeploy/dialects/teradata.py`, `test/test_pdm_converter.py`.
- **Jun 2026**: **Industry-model metrics (M7) — KG metric enrichment + Teradata metric views + deterministic metric-compiler**. Metrics become first-class context, end to end. **(M7a)** the walker now parses each Databricks metric view's `WITH METRICS LANGUAGE YAML` body (from `metric_views[].sql`) and stamps the **full definition** on the logical `metric` KG node — `metric_source`, `dimensions[{name,expr}]`, `measures[{name,expr,additive}]` (additive heuristic: SUM/COUNT additive; AVG/DISTINCT/ratios non-additive) — not just counts (`industry_model_walker.parse_metric_definition`). **(M7b)** a pure, deterministic **metric-compiler** (`dbdeploy/metric_compiler.py`): given a metric def + a requested slice (dimensions/measures), emits Teradata SQL by aggregating the **base table at the requested grain** (`SELECT dims, measure-exprs FROM source GROUP BY dims`) — **ratio-safe by construction** (no re-aggregation of a pre-agg, so AVG/ratios stay correct at any grain; the `additive` flag is metadata). Spark→Teradata expression translation via **SQLGlot** (`CAST(x AS DOUBLE)`→`TRYCAST(x AS DOUBLE PRECISION)`, etc.; failures pass through + warn). **(M7c)** opt-in **metric→Teradata view generation** in the converter (`include_metric_views`): one `CREATE VIEW` per metric whose source table is deployed (others skipped + warned), plus a **physical `ddl_artifact` KG node** that `implements` the logical metric and `derives_from` the source `physical_table`. **(M7d)** a **`compile_metric` KG component tool** (`TDA_KnowledgeGraph` action) — the LLM only picks the slice (metric_name + optional dimensions/measures lists), the handler resolves the metric node + compiles deterministically (`resolve_metric_from_entity`); `[]` vs absent distinguishes "no dimensions" from "all". New deps **sqlglot>=25 + PyYAML>=6** (pinned). **59 CI-pure assertions** (`test/test_pdm_metrics.py`); 431 total across the PDM/KG suites. Advances [ONTOLOGY_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/ONTOLOGY_ARCHITECTURE.md) roadmap #1. Server restart for backend (walker/dbdeploy/handler + new deps); JS browser-reload. Files: `agent/kg_constructors/industry_model_walker.py`, `dbdeploy/{metric_compiler,physical_model,types,converter,dialects/{base,teradata}}.py`, `agent/kg_constructors/declarative_model.py`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/{handler.py,instructions.json}`, `requirements.txt`, `test/test_pdm_metrics.py`. - **Jun 2026**: **KG inspector — division/domain selector facets**. The KG viewer (`components/builtin/knowledge_graph/renderer.js`) gains **Division** and **Domain** filter tile-groups alongside the existing type pills, so a KG built from an industry model can be filtered to e.g. the `operations` division or the `finance` domain. **Conditional-on-presence:** a facet group renders only when the KG actually carries those values (the sampler returns a facet *catalog* of distinct division/domain values present). **Multi-select, server-side:** toggling re-queries a stratified subgraph (not a client-side hide), composing with the type filter + node budget + focus. Backend: `get_typed_subgraph(divisions=, domains=)` filters on the `division`/`domain` node properties (with name fallback for the domain grouping nodes) and returns `facets` — implemented in `kgstore/sqlite_backend.py` (`_node_facet_values` + facet catalog over the full graph), `kgstore/neo4j_backend.py` (Python post-filter since properties are a JSON string; catalog via a full-entity pass), `kgstore/base.py` (ABC fallback), and the `GraphStore` delegate; surfaced through `GET /v1/knowledge-graph/graph-spec` (`divisions`/`domains` params + `spec.facets`). Validated against the real models: table names are globally unique in **MVM** but have within-division collisions in **ECM** (e.g. `oil_gas` ECM: `field`, `wellbore`) — confirming **domain-level databases are the only universally collision-safe PDM layout** (divisions are a grouping tag with no `database_name`). **60 CI-pure KG assertions** (`test_kg_typed_subgraph` 45 + `test_kg_facets` 15). Server restart for backend (endpoint + kgstore); renderer is browser-reload. Files: `src/trusted_data_agent/kgstore/{sqlite_backend,neo4j_backend,base}.py`, `components/builtin/knowledge_graph/{graph_store,renderer.js}`, `src/trusted_data_agent/api/rest_routes.py`, `test/test_kg_facets.py`.
- **Jun 2026**: **Industry Data Model → PDM conversion + deployment (Teradata) + Database Connection connector**. Extends the `docs/Architecture/INDUSTRY_MODEL_KG_CONSTRUCTOR_PLAN.md` to **realize the physical model in a real relational backend**: convert the Databricks PDM → Teradata DDL, deploy it (databases/tables/soft-RI FKs), load demo data, and register the deployed objects back into the KG as the physical layer (`implements`-linked to logical). **(1) New `dbdeploy/` abstraction** (sibling of `vectorstore`/`kgstore`): a **pure converter** (`physical_model` → dialect emitter → DDL plan + CSV load-plan + KG physical delta; Teradata design standard — UPI/NoPI from PK, `MULTISET, NO FALLBACK`, BYTEINT booleans, `TIMESTAMP(6) WITH TIME ZONE`, LATIN VARCHAR, soft RI `WITH NO CHECK OPTION`, `COMMENT ON`, `COLLECT STATISTICS`) + a capability-negotiated **`DeploymentBackend` ABC + factory + `TeradataDeploymentBackend`** (`teradataml`, dry-run short-circuits before any I/O, cleanup-on-failure since Teradata DDL is auto-committed). **(2) Demo data is synthetic** — the Databricks repo ships **no** row data (its `samples/*.csv` are generated by Databricks' own deploy, not committed), so the default is a **deterministic, seeded, FK-aware synthetic generator** (`datasource.py`), with `ShippedCsvDataSource` retained. **(3) Constructor orchestration** (`declarative_model._deploy_pdm`): build KG → convert → dry-run/deploy DDL → load → `import_bulk` the Teradata physical layer; fully isolated (a deploy failure never corrupts the built KG). **(4) Centralized, user-centric Database Connection store** (`core/database_connections.py`, mirrors the VS-config pattern: metadata in `user_preferences`, secrets encrypted under `dbconn_{id}`, masking, `resolve()`, legacy `canvas_conn_*` unification + migration) — **one store every participant draws from** (Canvas execute + list and PDM deploy all route through it). **(5) Surfaced as a first-class connector, not a bespoke modal:** a **Database Connection** is a built-in **User-type connector** (`mcp_servers/builtin/uderia-database`, `connector_type=database`, `auth_schema.type=db_connections`) — browsable in Browse Registry, admin-governed in Administration → Components → Connectors, with per-user **multi-connection** management rendered inline in the Components → Connectors card (`platformConnectorHandler.js`). Master gate `is_database_connector_enabled()` gates the store's **mutating** endpoints (reads/`resolve` stay ungated so existing + legacy Canvas connections never break). **(6) Deploy UX:** the KG constructor modal reveals a deploy sub-section (connection dropdown + Load demo data + Dry run) only when "Include physical layer (PDM)" is checked; template inputs added. **(7) Database provisioning as a backend-abstraction capability with user choice + transparent errors:** the converter only *names* the root + per-domain databases (no raw `CREATE DATABASE`); `DeploymentBackend.ensure_database()`/`database_exists()` (capability `CREATE_DATABASE`, idempotent) own provisioning. The deploy offers **use-existing-root vs create-new-root** (the root owns the per-domain databases); on failure the exact backend error (e.g. Teradata `[5612] no PERM`) is wrapped in `DeploymentError` and surfaced to the frontend (`status=error, phase=provision_database`). **(8) Admin connector card is auth-type-aware** — the credential connector shows "Per-user connections" (not "OAuth per user"), hides the OAuth-credentials button + Permitted-Tools section + tool-selection toggle. **226 CI-pure assertions** across 6 suites (`test_pdm_converter` 67, `test_pdm_deploy` 26, `test_pdm_dataload` 42, `test_pdm_constructor_deploy` 40, `test_database_connections` 32, `test_database_connector` 19). **Server restart** for backend (new modules, connector manifest, endpoints, gating); JS browser-reload only; live Teradata deploy + the connector/deploy UI pending browser verification. - **Jun 2026**: **KG inspector — consistent in-place interaction model + complete-neighbourhood reveal + relationship projection; KG update-lifecycle hardening**. Builds on the reduce-then-render inspector below; the north star this round was **consistency** — one mechanism per concept, every gesture behaving predictably, **never a "refocus"** (a re-query/re-render that swaps the node set + resets the viewport). **(1) In-place interaction model** (`renderer.js`): **zoom = pure pan/scale** (removed the semantic-zoom node-set re-distribute + the zoom-threshold overlay toggle — both re-rendered and read as a refocus); **hover = neighbour highlight** (node + its DIRECT in-view neighbours brighten, the rest dims — generic across all types, not just tables) **+ a transient per-node derived-dependency peek**; **single-click = focus**, **double-click = pin** (sticky focus), disambiguated by a 240 ms timer. **(2) Relationship projection (link aggregation)** — when a type filter hides the level a relationship runs through (e.g. only `table` shown), lift each hidden endpoint to its nearest VISIBLE ancestor via the `contains` chain and render a **derived dashed edge** (`foreign_key ×N`); general across all types (`_derive_lifted_edges` SQLite recursive lift / Neo4j `*0..6 contains` projection). **Gated OFF by default** (compute-+render-heavy): surfaced **in place, edges-only** (no re-layout) via hover (lazy-fetched + cached `_ensureDerived`) and a toolbar toggle. **(3) Complete-neighbourhood reveal (the consistency guarantee)** — a focus gesture must never show a budget-truncated subset of a node's relationships. New `GraphStore.get_node_neighborhood(entity_id)` (SQLite + Neo4j; uncapped, highest-degree cap 500 + honest `truncated`/`total_degree`) + `GET /v1/knowledge-graph/node-neighborhood`; on click/double-click the frontend **merges the missing neighbours into the LIVE graph in place** — append-only (new nodes/links at the array tail → d3 `enter()` = exactly them), existing nodes **pinned** (frozen `fx/fy`) so only the new ones grow out from the focus, viewport never jumps, pins released after settle. Only grows when neighbours are genuinely hidden (already-complete node → no-op). Render core refactored so the merge reuses the SAME builders as the initial render (`_decorateNodeEnter`/`_decorateLinkEnter`/`_wireNodeHandlers`, per-link `_ensureGradient` stable ids; `nodeGroups`/`linkGroup`/`linkLines` are `let` so the merge re-selects and tick/handlers/animation pick up new elements). Hover stays a transient peek (no permanent growth on mouse-move). **(4) KG update-lifecycle hardening:** **extend/reduce scope** on the update modal (`kgUpdateVersions.js`) — installed options shown as toggles (Columns/Metrics/Glossary/Physical-PDM + Divisions); toggling re-runs `check-update` live with an `options_override` (merged onto the stored descriptor in `_rebuild_candidate_for_kg`), apply persists the merged descriptor (so a `NoPDM` KG gains the physical layer in-place); **diff robustness** — `graph_diff._norm()` treats `None`/`""`/`[]`/`{}`/absent as the same "no value" (keeps `0`/`False`) so a clean re-sync reads `~0` (was flagging every node whose empty fields an earlier walker stored but the current one drops); **"what's changing" breakdown** — `changed_prop_summary` (property → #entities) rendered as chips so a large `~changed` is legible as enrichment (root-caused a real case: a KG built by an earlier walker shows all nodes changed because the current walker now captures `references`/`definition`/`value_regex` — applying enriches in place → clean afterward); serialized diff lists capped (counts exact); **Cancel button fix** (`_setContent` wires ALL `.kg-uv-close`, was only the header X); **Neo4j fix** (`size((pattern))` → `COUNT { }` for newer Cypher). **227 CI-pure KG assertions** across 8 suites (`test_kg_typed_subgraph` 43 incl. projection + complete-neighbourhood; `test_kg_update_lifecycle` 27 incl. empty-normalisation + summary). **Server restart** for backend (endpoints, graph_diff, Neo4j); JS/renderer browser-reload only. - **Jun 2026**: **World-class KG inspector — reduce-then-render + trace-driven execution animation**. The KG viewer (`components/builtin/knowledge_graph/renderer.js`, shared by the inspect view, the component split panel, and inline cards) was rebuilt around the **data funnel** (Cambridge Intelligence / Neo4j Bloom / Linkurious) after research confirmed force layout is only legible at ~100–150 nodes — so a 25k-node dump is the failure mode, and the answer is reduce-then-render, not "render more". **(1) One sampler — `GraphStore.get_typed_subgraph(types, max_nodes, focus)` (SQLite NetworkX + Neo4j Cypher + ABC fallback): seed → connectivity-expand → fill.** Seed = `focus` ids (search/click/zoom/execution) else type-stratified high-degree per type (every type represented — fixes "missing types"); expand = BFS outward adding nodes most-connected to the visible set (a CONNECTED, dependency-coherent subgraph, not scattered hubs); fill = top up unused budget with high-degree leftovers (a small type no longer wastes its share — fixes "700 budget but 489 shown"). **(2) Three lenses:** *Detail* (full-catalog type pills with shown/total counts that **re-query** server-side, node-budget slider 50–2000, honest "showing N of M"); *Overview* (`get_schema_overview()` → type-level meta-graph, always tiny+complete — "Schema" toolbar button, click a type to drill in); *Focus* (search Enter finds across the whole KG, double-click expands a node's neighbourhood, **semantic zoom** re-distributes the budget to the zoomed region). All feed the same `focus` param. **(3) Trace-driven execution animation (component prerequisite):** `dispatchKGAnimation` no longer silently drops entities outside the sample — in-view nodes glow instantly, off-view touched entities accumulate as the running focus, get pulled in via a focus re-query, and **replay in order** (staggered = reads as a traversal path); focus accumulates across the run. **Zero added latency** — fire-and-forget overlay (execution is server-side, never waits), focus re-query is throttled (≥700 ms) + in-flight-guarded + debounced so rapid events can't churn the force layout. Works in the split-panel component (shared `renderKGFull`/`_graphState`; `_activeRequery` published module-side). **(4) graph-spec** gains `types`/`max_nodes`/`focus`/`focus_names` (names resolved server-side via `get_entity_by_name`) + returns the full type catalog + shown/total counts + `truncated`; new `GET /v1/knowledge-graph/schema-overview`. Inspect/graph-spec are **kg_id-scoped** (inspect the exact KG clicked, not the profile's active one). **27 CI-pure assertions** (`test/test_kg_typed_subgraph.py`: stratification-covers-all-types vs biased first-N, type filter, deterministic+importance, budget-fully-used, connected-expansion ≥70% one component, focus-seeding, schema-overview). Neo4j paths code-reviewed (CI covers SQLite). **Deferred:** visual combos (value already delivered by backbone sampler + `column` toggle + double-click expand). **Server restart** (backend); JS/renderer browser-reload only. - **Jun 2026**: **Industry Data Model → Knowledge Graph constructor + LDM/PDM layering + KG update/version lifecycle**. A new **deterministic, zero-LLM** KG constructor that ingests [Databricks Industry Data Models](https://github.com/databricks-industry-solutions/lakehouse-industry-data-models) (`model.json`, fetched from GitHub raw) and walks them directly into KG entities/relationships — distinct from the existing agent-discovery constructor (live DB + MCP + LLM). **(1) Constructor (template-based):** new `kg-industry-model` RAG template (`discovery_mode=industry_model`, registered in `rag_templates/template_registry.json`) routed through a new **`KGConstructorStrategy` ABC + registry** (`agent/kg_constructors/`, mirrors `EngineRegistry`); the existing tool/prompt agent path is left inline (additive dispatch — `AgentDiscoveryStrategy` is a capability descriptor, `supports_resync=False`). The **pure walker** (`industry_model_walker.py`) is the moat: zero I/O, fully unit-tested, **qualified node names** (`domain.table`, `domain.table.column`) so cross-domain name overlaps never merge tables and FKs resolve unambiguously; division filter; opt-in columns/metrics/glossary; honest drop diagnostics (dangling vs filtered). Endpoint dispatch in `kg_generate` (early return for `industry_model`, no MCP/agent/session); new `GET /v1/knowledge-graph/industry-models` (cached `models-info.csv`) drives the dropdown + live node-count estimate. Frontend `kgIndustryModelModal.js` (+ shared `kgConstructorShared.js`); any profile may own the KG. **(2) LDM/PDM layering (general KG concept):** every entity carries a `layer` (`logical`|`physical`); physical entities carry `infrastructure`. Enums extended additively (single def+validation site in `graph_store.py`): +`catalog`/`schema`/`physical_table`/`physical_column`/`ddl_artifact`, +`implements`. The walker's physical (Databricks PDM) layer is derived from `model.json` + `model_conventions` (catalog→schema→physical_table[→physical_column]); each physical node `implements` its logical counterpart (**one LDM → many PDMs**). Physical types get a distinct slate/teal palette (`handler.py` + `renderer.js`) so they render in the existing per-type filter pills. **(3) Update/version lifecycle (instance-owned, not constructor):** the constructor stamps a re-syncable **`source_descriptor_json`** onto `kg_metadata` (ALTER-on-first-use; on metadata not a graph entity, so `clear_graph()` can't wipe it); strategies expose `rebuild(descriptor)`. New pure `kgstore/graph_diff.py` (layer-aware) + `POST /v1/knowledge-graph/check-update` (rebuild source → diff, no mutation) and `/apply-update` (pre-sync snapshot → clear+import → post-sync snapshot; content-hash deduped = clean no-op on unchanged source). **Version switching reuses the existing `kg_version_db`** (versions list/restore gained an optional `kg_id` scope). KG Intelligence card gains **Update** (re-syncable only) + **Versions** buttons + a layer-grouped diff modal (`kgUpdateVersions.js`); `list_all_graphs` surfaces `is_resyncable`/`source_label`. **168 CI-pure assertions** across 6 test suites (`test_industry_model_walker`, `test_kg_constructor_strategy`, `test_kg_industry_constructor` [real SQLite backend + real schema/migration], `test_kg_update_lifecycle`, `test_kg_list_resyncable`, `test_industry_model_pdm`); validated live against the real Restaurants `model.json` (FK count recovers the model's declared `fk_count` exactly; LDM+PDM = 337 nodes / 167 implements). **Server restart** for backend (new modules, endpoints, enum/metadata changes, template registry); JS/renderer browser-reload only; `model.json`/`models-info.csv` fetched live (no vendoring). - **Jun 2026**: WS3 — **Task Transparency Classification Framework** (`eval/tasks.py`), a world-class, agent-type-consistent view of *what work an agent did*, driving the Agent Ops & Evaluation quality story. `classify_tasks(run)` is **polymorphic over `RunRecord` and `FlowRunRecord`**, turning a turn (signed provenance chain) or flow run (node runs) into discrete typed **Tasks** — deterministic, CI-pure, 0 tokens — so the same KPIs render on **every** agent's Quality card (all 5 profile classes + flow-agents). **Task classes:** `planning` (the whole Optimize planning phase collapses to **1 task**), `retrieval`, `tool`, `reasoning`, `coordination`, `correction` (rework — the quality class the Live Status filter omits). **What is deliberately NOT a task** (so the count is real work, not bookkeeping): `tactical_decision` (per-phase routing, usually FASTPATH → no LLM call); framework scaffolding tools `TDA_SystemLog`/`TDA_CurrentDate`/`TDA_ContextReport`/`TDA_SystemOrchestration` (orchestrator's wrapped calls are added separately as a parallel wave). `TDA_FinalReport` is the exception — it IS the answer synthesis, classified as `reasoning`, not `tool`. **Two-layer model (key distinction):** `steps` = the **planner's** planned-phase count (**`tool_enabled` only**); `tasks` = the **execution** units those steps decompose into. Example: a 2-phase Optimize plan (data query + final report) reads **`steps`=2, `tasks`=3 (1 planning · 1 tool · 1 reasoning)** — planner call, data tool, synthesis; the two FASTPATH tactical decisions are not tasks. **Three banded task KPIs:** `tasks` (work volume → bloat, all 5 + flow, `max_tasks`), `efficiency` (convergence `optimal_tasks/actual`), `parallel_efficiency` (latency speedup `tasks/waves`, parallel-capable classes `tool_enabled`/`genie`/`flow`, `min_parallel_efficiency`). **Parallelism is honest by construction** — a wave is established by an orchestrator group (`TDA_SystemOrchestration` gather) or provable timestamp overlap; profile-agent provenance steps are appended serially so `parallel_efficiency` **abstains** (never fabricates `1.0`) for most profile turns, while **flow-agents** — with real per-node timings — are the strongest case (2 overlapping SQL nodes + 1 LLM node → `1.50×`). **Composition transparency exposed end-to-end** — the `tasks` verdict carries the class split as structured `evidence` (`TaskSet.breakdown()`): the Quality card chip renders it inline (*`tasks ·metric 5 · 1 planning · 2 tool · 2 reasoning`*, `ui.js:_renderVerdictChips`), and the Agent Performance UX aggregates per-class counts (`build_quality_span` → `eval.task.<class>` → `online_quality_by_agent`/`by_flow` `task_composition`) into a **Work Mix** stacked composition bar in the agent detail (`agentPerformanceHandler.js:taskMix`). New **Tasks** tier on the Quality card (`ui.js:_KPI_TIER`), speedup formats `1.50×`; admin sliders gain `max_tasks` + `min_parallel_efficiency` (Tasks group) and `max_steps` moves to Planning. **319 eval assertions** across 9 suites (+`test_eval_tasks.py`, 34). Server restart for backend + `index.html`; JS browser-reload only. - **Jun 2026**: WS3 — `latency` KPI populated for **all five profile classes** (root-cause fix). The Quality-card `latency` chip abstained for Focus/Coordinate/Ideate turns because `RunRecord.duration_ms` read only the top-level `turn["duration_ms"]` key, which only Optimize and Conversation-success stamped; Focus/Coordinate recorded the wall-clock as `total_duration_ms` **inside their completion event** (the "execution complete" line in Live Status), and **Ideate never recorded duration at all**. Fix: **(1)** `executor.run()` sets one canonical `self.turn_start_time`; new `_turn_duration_ms()` helper is the single source of truth. **(2)** every engine that lacked it now stamps top-level `duration_ms` — Ideate (+ its `execution_complete` event for Live Status parity), Focus (both build sites), Coordinate, and the Conversation error path. **(3)** `RunRecord.duration_ms` (eval reader) falls back to the per-class completion event when the top-level key is absent, taking the **max whole-turn candidate** (`total_duration_ms`, or `duration_ms` on a completion-typed event) so a sub-step's own timing (e.g. a 78 ms retrieval step, or an inner agent's 2931 ms) is never mistaken for the turn latency — this lights up `latency` for **already-persisted historical turns** on Re-score without a re-run. Verified: the Focus turn now scores `latency=3198 ms`; latency resolves for rag_focused/genie/conversation/optimize across all saved turns (only *pre-fix* Ideate turns stay blank — unrecoverable; flows score via `FlowRunRecord`, not this path). All 8 eval suites pass (281 assertions). **Server restart** for the engine/executor changes (new turns); the `eval/types.py` reader fix already grades historical turns. - **Jun 2026**: WS3 — per-profile-class KPI harmonization. A deep assessment of what each profile class's execution signals can support drove a harmonization layer so the Quality card reads the same for all five classes and the Ideate/**LangChain ReAct** flow gets every KPI it can. **New/fixed scorers:** `steps` (`StepCountScorer`, METRIC, `tool_enabled`+`conversation_with_tools`, banded by `max_steps`) is now a first-class step-count KPI — works for the ReAct flow (steps = tool iterations from `conversation_agent_events`) as well as the Planner flow; it was previously **buried inside `efficiency`** (which now is purely the `optimal_steps/actual` convergence ratio and abstains without a target). `tokens` (`TokenUsageScorer`, METRIC, **all** classes, banded by new `max_tokens`) is a universal core KPI alongside cost/latency. `clean_termination` now derives "terminal answer produced" from answer+status when there's no signed provenance chain (ReAct/Ideate/Focus), so it applies to every class — not just Optimize. **Exposure (the harmonization layer):** the Quality-card chips **group by KPI tier** (`Core · Resource · Tools · Knowledge · Planning · Coordination · Quality`, `ui.js:_KPI_TIER`), each tier rendering only if the class produced it; per-metric formatting renders counts as `1` (not `1.00`), rates `0%`, cost `$…`, latency `4.1s`, tokens with commas. Admin thresholds gain a `max_tokens` input (the "Cost & Efficiency" group renamed "Resource": cost/tokens/steps/latency). Also from the same investigation (session b9691eb7): the Quality headline now goes **amber (Review)** with a caveat ("passed · recovered from a tool error · N self-correction(s)") instead of green "all gating checks passed" when non-gating health signals exist — a recovered tool error is honestly Review, not perfect. The Quality card is **collapsed by default** (headline + chevron; chips reveal on click). **Admin threshold UI overhaul:** the 18-number-input grid is replaced by **banded dual-handle sliders** (`static/js/handlers/thresholdSliders.js`) — one track per metric with two draggable handles + green/amber/red bands (direction-aware), a Strict/Balanced/Lenient/Clear preset bar, and per-metric Off; `adminManager` loads/saves via the module's `setThresholds`/`getThresholds` (stored `{healthy, danger}` shape + backend unchanged). The card lives in **Config → Operations**, is **collapsed by default**, and carries its **own "Save Evaluation Settings" button** (it was orphaned from the Features "Save Feature Settings" button when moved, so slider edits never reached `APP_CONFIG`). **Persistence:** a save updates `APP_CONFIG` **in memory** — immediate (no restart) for new turns + Re-score, but it does NOT rewrite already-persisted turn scores (frozen snapshots — Re-score to re-grade) and the whole `agent_eval` block **resets to `config.py` defaults on restart** (`APP_CONFIG` isn't persisted to disk/DB; set a permanent default in `core/config.py`). Per-class scorer counts: llm_only=14, conversation_with_tools=22, rag_focused=19, tool_enabled=24, genie=17. **281 eval assertions** (reliability 19→31). - **Jun 2026**: WS3 — deterministic coverage expansion + 3-band thresholds + cross-agent dashboards. **(1) 11 new reliability/quality scorers** (`eval/scorers/reliability.py`) derived entirely from the already-persisted trace (no new instrumentation): cross-cutting `latency`, `clean_termination`, `context_health`, `error_recovery`, `output_sanity`; per-class `tool_success_rate`, `no_tool_loops`, `numeric_fidelity`, `plan_execution` (tool classes), `retrieval_relevance` (Focus), `expert_success` (Coordinate). **(2) Admin-configurable global default thresholds** (`ONLINE_EVAL_DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS`, runtime-mutable via `agent_eval.default_thresholds` in `/v1/admin/app-config`) — make the nine threshold-bearing scorers band/gate live traffic instead of abstaining; `online.default_assertions()` seeds every live/manual case; a curated `EvalCase` always overrides. **(3) Per-metric 3-band model** — `Verdict.band` ∈ {healthy, review, danger, None} + `scorer.banded_metric()` (shared by all 9 threshold scorers): each metric takes **two cut points** (`<key>`=Danger/gate, `<key>__healthy`=Healthy split), `higher_is_better`-aware, `passed = band != "danger"` → **Review (amber) passes but is flagged; only Danger (red) fails the gate** ("warn, don't gate"). Legacy scalar = single line, no amber. **(4) Platform-wide 4-class health taxonomy** (Healthy ≥0.80 green · Review 0.50–0.79 amber · Danger <0.50 red · Inactive grey) — `HEALTH`/`healthClassFor()` in `agentPerformanceHandler.js` are the canonical constants (`HEALTHY=0.8`, `REVIEW=0.5`), mirrored by `agentKpiCharts.healthColor` and the Quality-card chips (`ui.js:_renderVerdictChips`); atomic binary surfaces (single verdict chips, per-turn spark bars, diff pills) stay 2/3-state by design. **(5) Cross-agent KPI dashboard + per-agent timeline** — `analysis.agent_kpi_dashboard(spans)` (trend/failing-checks/scoreboard/cost-latency) and `agent_timeline(spans, tag, bucket_seconds)` (day-bucketed pass-rate/cost/latency) drive a dependency-free inline-SVG 2×2 chart grid (`static/js/handlers/agentKpiCharts.js`) above the roster + a timeline card in agent detail; endpoints `GET /v1/evals/agents/kpi-dashboard` and `/v1/evals/agents/<tag>/timeline`. **(6) Admin card moved** to **Config → Operations → Agent Evaluation** (its own top-level card, was buried in the System Feature Availability accordion); thresholds UI is Healthy+Danger inputs per metric with band legend. Verified live (3-band scoring, admin round-trip incl. string coercion/blank-drop). **269 eval assertions across 8 suites.** Server restart for backend + `index.html`; JS browser-reload only. - **Jun 2026**: WS3 — automatic scoring of **every** turn + admin-controlled judges. The agent quality check is no longer manual-only or off-by-default. **Deterministic scoring is free + non-blocking, so it's ON by default and scores every executed turn and flow run** (`ONLINE_EVAL_ENABLED=True`, no sampling) at the `run_agent_execution` / `flow_executor._run_and_record` seams, feeding the Agent Performance roster. **Only the token-costing LLM-judge layer is stochastic** (`should_judge`: anomalous turns + a `ONLINE_EVAL_JUDGE_SAMPLE_RATE` fraction). The judge layer is an **admin-controlled parameter, not a static flag** — exposed via `GET/POST /v1/admin/app-config` (`agent_eval` block: `online_enabled`, `include_judges`, `judge_sample_rate`) + an "Agent Evaluation" card in the App Config admin tab; the online hook reads `APP_CONFIG` at runtime so changes take effect with no restart. Judges are now optional on **all three** scoring paths (automatic via `agent_eval`, manual overlay toggle, offline `--judges`); flows have only deterministic scorers. Also: manual "Score this turn" **persists** so it feeds the roster, the trajectory overlay **auto-displays a turn's existing score on open** (read-only `GET /v1/evals/turn-score`) instead of just a button, re-scores **dedup** by (session,turn)/run, the judge panel skips credential-less configs (no warning spam) + floats the default-profile model first, and duplicate judge verdicts were fixed (sync loop runs deterministic+metric only; judges solely via `judge_fn`). Verified live (admin `agent_eval` round-trips at runtime). **209 eval assertions.** `agent_eval` is runtime-mutable; `config.py`/`index.html` changes need a restart. Files: `core/config.py`, `eval/{online,judge,runner}.py`, `api/{admin_routes,rest_routes}.py`, `static/js/{adminManager,ui}.js`, `templates/index.html`, `test/test_eval_*.py`. **The Quality card renders after execution too** (not just on reload): the hook emits a `turn_score_complete` Live-Status event; `processStream` renders the same `injectTrajectoryEvalOverlay` card with a cost note; judge token cost flows through `_record_score_usage` (session/turn totals + idempotent `token_update` `call_id="turn_score"` → title-bar KPIs + consumption), survives reload via `turn_cost` + the read-only `GET /v1/evals/turn-score`. **`RunRecord` accessors are now defensive against engine shape variance** — the Optimize engine stores the plan as a *list* (not `{phases}`), which previously crashed `planned_tools()` and aborted the whole online hook (Optimize turns never scored); `planned_tools`/`knowledge_event`/`genie_metadata`/`provenance_meta`/`step_types` all guard with `isinstance` (regression `t_real_shapes`).
- **Jun 2026**: Agent Ops & Evaluation (WS3) — a world-class agent observability + evaluation system built on Uderia's existing signed-trace substrate (Ed25519 **Execution Provenance Chain** + per-turn `workflow_history`) rather than re-capturing traces, and best-in-class for **all five profile classes**, not just Optimize. **Three differentiators vs LangSmith/Galileo/Braintrust:** (1) a **profile-class-aware deterministic scorer suite** (16 CI-pure, 0-token scorers grading trajectory/cost/safety — grade-what-matters subset/must-not-call semantics, never exact-sequence) is the moat; LLM judges are reserved for the open-ended residue; (2) eval verdicts are cryptographically bound to the trajectory via signed attestations; (3) **agent-as-entity** UX (an IFOC-classed agent health roster) instead of a run firehose. **Scoring:** `eval/scorer.py` ABC + registry dispatch; `scorers/deterministic.py` (16 scorers, cross-cutting + per-class); `scorers/judges.py` (5 decomposed judges — one isolated dimension each, evidence-cited, "unknown" escape) via a **Panel-of-LLMs** (`judge.py`, diverse-family consensus — free given 10 providers) with **Cohen's-κ calibration** (`calibration.py`, judges non-gating until κ≥0.6). **Methods:** `runner.py` (pluggable executor, **pass^k** reliability + bootstrap CI + per-cohort/class aggregation), `gate.py` (regression gate → CI exit code), `mining.py` (golden cases from anomalous production traces via WS1 session API), `online.py` (**tail-sampled** live scoring at the `run_agent_execution` seam — recommender's defensive contract, deterministic-only, never blocks/mutates a turn; OTLP-shaped quality spans via a pluggable exporter; Ed25519-signed attestations bound to the turn's `chain_tip_hash`; **off by default** `APP_CONFIG.ONLINE_EVAL_ENABLED`). **Analysis** (`analysis.py`): failure-mode clustering, experiment diffing, per-agent/per-dimension aggregation. **Persistence:** `EvalStore` (SQLite: datasets/cases/runs/scores/annotations) + NDJSON online sink (`ONLINE_EVAL_SINK`; `tda_eval*` gitignored). **13 REST endpoints** (`/v1/evals/*`) + CLI (`python -m trusted_data_agent.eval.cli run|gate|mine|report|list`). **IA move:** agent eval is operational, not config — so it left Administration and became its own rail topic. The two performance lenses are now **siblings on the unit of analysis**: **Sessions** (renamed from "Executions" → "Session Performance", instance lens, existing `executionDashboard.js`) and **Agents** (NEW 8th rail topic → "Agent Performance", entity lens, `agentPerformanceHandler.js`); **Administration = configuration/governance only**. The **Agent Performance** view is agent-centric: portfolio KPIs + an **IFOC-colored agent health roster** (filter pills `All·Ideate·Focus·Optimize·Coordinate` + search + 52vh scroll; honest "unevaluated" empty states, never fake numbers) → per-agent detail → Experiments/diff → judge calibration/annotation queue, with a **My vs System** scope toggle (admin-gated by `VIEW_ALL_SESSIONS`, enforced server-side; spans carry `agent.profile_tag`/`user.uuid`). The **trajectory verdict overlay** (`ui.js:injectTrajectoryEvalOverlay`, wired in `eventHandlers.js:handleReloadPlanClick`'s `finally` so it covers every profile branch) is the concrete **Sessions↔Agents bridge** — a "Quality" strip on the historical trace that scores the viewed turn via `POST /v1/evals/score-turn` (deterministic default, opt-in live judges) and overlays pass/fail chips. Verified: **151 CI-pure assertions** across 6 suites (`test/test_eval_*.py`). **Server restart required** (backend + `index.html`); JS/CSS browser-reload only. **Architecture doc:** [docs/Architecture/AGENT_OPS_EVAL_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/AGENT_OPS_EVAL_ARCHITECTURE.md). - **Jun 2026**: WS3 phase-2 — **flows as a first-class evaluable agent type**. The Agents lens has **two agent types**: profile-agents (IFOC) and **flow-agents** (a flow IS the agent). A flow binds to a session only at execution and composes **0..N profiles** (flow-level `defaultProfileId` + per-node `profile_id`), so it's graded **as a whole, profile-agnostically** — never folded into one profile. `FlowRunRecord` (`eval/flow_types.py`) normalizes a flow run + `node_runs`; 6 CI-pure deterministic flow scorers (`eval/scorers/flow.py`, `applies_to={"flow"}`): `flow_completed`, `flow_nodes_succeeded`, `flow_nodes_reached` (subset), `flow_forbidden_nodes` (wrong-branch detection), `flow_cost`, `flow_efficiency`. `scorers_for("flow")` returns ONLY flow scorers (turn-shaped scorers never run on a flow; flows have no judges); `EvalCase` gains `flow_id`. Offline: `FlowEvalExecutor` runs a flow via `POST /flows/<id>/execute` (binds session) → poll → score; `CompositeEvalExecutor` routes mixed datasets by agent type (CLI `run` uses it). Online: gated, defensive hook in `flow_executor._run_and_record` → `evaluate_flow_run_online` → `agent.flow.eval` OTLP span keyed by flow identity (`agent.kind='flow'`) + signed attestation bound to the run id; `online_quality_by_flow` aggregates flows and **keeps flow spans out of the profile `by_agent`** (no double-count). Roster: flow-agents get their own cards (amber **Flow** badge, **Flows** filter pill, "flow run" units, **"uses @X · @Y"** composed-profiles line). Dashboard returns `by_flow`. Verified: **191 eval assertions** (7 suites; +40 in `test/test_eval_flow.py`) + live smoke scoring a real production flow run. **Server restart required** (`flow_executor.py` + `rest_routes.py` + `index.html`). Architecture doc §12a "Flow-agents". - **Jun 2026**: Next-Step Recommender **profile rebind** — the dock now re-filters to the composer's *effective* profile when you add/remove an `@TAG` override (or pick from the `@` selector) **without running a new turn**, **0 tokens**. Rationale: Tier A chips are profile-class-specific (`= result-shape × the profile's enabled components`); a profile switch changes only the component filter and the last result is fixed, so the chips can be rebuilt from a tiny stashed descriptor. Emit time stamps `{query, flags}` (`recommender.derive_render_flags` → `session_manager.set_turn_rebind_context`) onto **every** rebindable turn (independent of whether the emitting profile produced chips); the `next_step_suggestions` SSE payload now carries `profile_id` + `rebindable` and is emitted **even when empty-but-rebindable**. New `POST /v1/sessions/<id>/next-step-rebind {profile_id, turn_id?}` rebuilds the free **A+B** set via `recommender.build_rebind_suggestions` (**Tier C never runs on a toggle**; always degrades to `{items:[]}`). Frontend: debounced `scheduleProfileRebind()` (composer input / badge-remove / profile-select) → `applyEffectiveProfile` resolves the effective profile (`getEffectiveProfileId`, override-first mirror of the backend) and renders **cache-first** via a per-profile cache keyed `session→profileId` (`state.nextStepCache`, reappears instantly on toggle), with `state.nextStepRebind` marking the rebindable turn (both wiped by `clearDock` on new-submit/dismiss, preserved across session switch-away). Verified: **84 CI-pure assertions** (`test/test_recommender.py`). **Server restart required** (backend); JS browser-reload only. - **Jun 2026**: Next-Step Recommender ("Smart Next Steps") — ephemeral, token-light follow-up suggestions after every turn, designed to beat the market's "suggested questions" widgets on the three axes competitors handle poorly: **action-aware & tool-grounded**, **token-light by default**, and **anti-fatigue/optional**. **Cost ladder (cheapest first):** Tier A `action` — deterministic chips ("Chart this", "Pin to dashboard", "Build a flow", "Expand in graph", "Open in canvas", "Schedule this") gated by the *exact same enablement truth as the profile editor* (`_component_enabled_for_profile` mirrors `GET /v1/profiles/<id>/components`: global/user governance via `is_component_available` wins → else explicit `componentConfig.enabled` → else manifest `enabled_for` for the profile type) intersected with the turn's result shape, so every chip maps to a genuinely-enabled, real capability (0 tokens). **Do NOT gate Tier A on `ComponentManager.get_active_components` — it defaults an absent entry to `enabled=True` and ignores global/user governance, which leaks disabled components into suggestions.** *(Superseded Aug 2026: `get_active_components` now delegates to the one resolver `components/enablement.py` and honours global/user governance, so the two agree by construction. `_component_enabled_for_profile` remains the right call for chips — it additionally filters to action components.)* Tier B `followup` — follow-up questions retrieved from the existing RAG champion-case store seeded with the just-completed query (0 generation tokens); Tier C `llm` — opt-in, history-disabled, capped LLM call (uses tokens, default OFF). Default = A+B → **zero added tokens per turn**. **Tier C is a fully-instrumented LLM call (mirrors Session Name Generation):** emits a **single** `next_step_generation_complete` Live-Status step — rendered as a clean Suggestions/Tokens/Cost key-value card by `ui.js:_renderNextStepCompleteDetails` (wired into all three render dispatchers: `_renderStandardStep`/`_renderGenieStep`/`_renderConversationAgentStep`, so it renders for every profile type, live + reload) — computes cost via `CostManager`, rolls tokens/cost into live counters through a single `token_update` (`call_id="next_step_recommender"`, idempotent per-call ledger → no double-count), and logs to session history via `update_token_count` + `update_turn_token_counts` (recomputes `turn_cost`/`session_cost_usd`) + `ConsumptionManager.update_turn_tokens` + `session_manager.append_system_events_to_turn` (step re-renders on reload; `_getTurnCost` includes `next_step_generation_complete`). `_getLastStatementTokens` returns the chronologically-last of `session_name`/`next_step` so the reloaded "Last Statement" KPI reflects the Tier C call. Implemented in `recommender._run_tier_c_with_accounting`/`_record_tier_c_usage`; validated empirically (turn1 + turn2 token sums == session total, both incl. Tier C) across all 5 engine branches (each emits `turn_id` on `final_answer`). The data-only `build_suggestions` path (tests) runs Tier C without accounting. **Note:** session-name is billed *implicitly* (runs before the turn save → folded into the turn total); Tier C + extensions run *after* the save → bill *explicitly* via `ConsumptionManager`. **Single backend seam:** `execution_service.run_agent_execution` (covers all 5 engines + genie coordinator; skipped for nested genie *slave* sub-turns via `_is_genie_slave`); emits a `notification` event of type `next_step_suggestions`; fully wrapped so it can never break a turn. **Frontend is ephemeral by design** — rendered in `#next-step-dock` (a dock ABOVE the composer, OUTSIDE `#chat-log`), so suggestions are never captured by `sessionUiCache.chatHTML`, never persisted to chat history, never re-parsed as markdown, and never seen by the chat-log MutationObserver. Stored in `state.nextStepSuggestions` keyed by session id and re-rendered on session switch (session-guarded → no cross-session leakage); cleared on new submit and on switch-away. Chip click fills the composer and submits via the existing chat-form path (`click` for mouse+keyboard accessibility). **Governance (three levels):** global admin gate `APP_CONFIG.RECOMMENDER_ENABLED`; per-profile `recommenderConfig` block (`{enabled, tiers, maxSuggestions, relevanceThreshold, llmEnrichment}`, edited in Profile editor → "Smart Next Steps" card; absent block = sensible default A+B capped at 4); per-user mute via `localStorage` (`nextStepHandler.isRecommenderEnabledForUser`/`setRecommenderEnabledForUser`) + a one-click dismiss "×" on the dock. Near-duplicate follow-ups suppressed (tag-stripped, punctuation/case-insensitive dedupe vs the asked query). Theme-aware (CSS variables) + monochrome inline SVG icons (no emoji); accessible (real `<button>` chips, `role="group"`/`aria-label`, `:focus-visible` rings, `prefers-reduced-motion`). Verified: `test/test_recommender.py` (53 assertions incl. enablement-governance regression) + live REST end-to-end (per-profile chip set proven via same-payload-different-profile). **Server restart required** (backend + `index.html`); JS/CSS are browser-reload only. **Architecture doc:** [docs/Architecture/NEXT_STEP_RECOMMENDER_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/NEXT_STEP_RECOMMENDER_ARCHITECTURE.md). Files: `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/recommender.py` (new), `src/trusted_data_agent/agent/execution_service.py` (seam), `src/trusted_data_agent/core/config.py` (`RECOMMENDER_ENABLED`), `static/js/handlers/nextStepHandler.js` (new), `static/js/state.js`, `static/js/domElements.js`, `static/js/eventHandlers.js` (SSE handler + clear-on-submit), `static/js/handlers/sessionManagement.js` (session-switch render), `static/js/handlers/configurationHandler.js` (profile-editor load/save), `static/css/main.css` (dock styles), `templates/index.html` (dock element + profile-editor card), `test/test_recommender.py` (module tests).
- **Jun 2026**: Flow run-session model finalized + duplicate-session/freeze fixes (**supersedes the session-binding part of the entry directly below**). **(1) Fresh session per run, not persistent.** The earlier "one persistent `<flow> — runs` session reused across all headless runs" was reverted: a headless / "New Session" run now provisions a **fresh session per click**, named after the flow and created under the flow's effective profile. Runs are never folded into a prior session (pass your own `session_id` to share one). In the canvas the run target is a **selector + single button** — a toggle **In Chat** (current session, inline result) / **New Session** (fresh per run) next to one **Run Flow** button that honours the selection (so per-node "Run only this node" / "Run from here" use the same target). `flows.runs_session_id` + `get/set_flow_runs_session_id()` are now **vestigial** (kept, unread — no destructive drop). **(2) Duplicate sidebar-card fix (root).** `_provision_run_session` was emitting `new_session_created` *after* `POST /v1/sessions` had already emitted it (the endpoint's emit was added later, invalidating the old "endpoint doesn't emit" comment) → two sidebar cards for one session. Fixed by making `POST /v1/sessions` accept an optional `name` (applied *before* its single broadcast) and having `_provision_run_session` pass it + drop its own rename-and-re-emit. Defense-in-depth: the frontend `new_session_created` handler is now idempotent by session id (replaces, never prepends a duplicate). **(3) Flow-run card label is open-state aware** (parity with the inline flow card + all component cards): **"View in Canvas →"** when closed, **"Expanded in side panel →"** when this flow's canvas is open. `openFlowSplitPanel`/`closeFlowSplitPanel` stamp `#flow-split-panel` `dataset.flowId` + broadcast a `flow:panel-state` event; `ui.js _syncFlowRunCardButtons()` reflects it. **(4) Freeze fix:** that sync runs from the chat-log MutationObserver and writes `innerHTML` (an observed childList mutation) — without a guard it re-triggered the observer into an infinite loop that froze the tab. Now guarded by an idempotent `dataset.openState` check (write only when the state flips). **(5)** LLM-node prompts resolve refs via `str.format(**state_ctx)` against **immediate-predecessor** output only (no `{Node.col}` resolver, no cross-gap reach) — to feed a value to an LLM node, have its immediate predecessor carry it. Files: `api/rest_routes.py`, `core/flow_executor.py`, `core/session_manager.py` (`ensure_primary_profile_tag`), `static/js/notifications.js`, `static/js/ui.js`, `components/builtin/flow/renderer.js`. Backend changes need a **server restart**; the JS is browser-reload only.
- **Jun 2026**: Flows as first-class REST execution & monitoring citizens (+ session/UX model). The flow-run model is now a durable, session-bound, REST-monitorable unit on par with the query Task contract — without merging the two execution backends (the flow-run model is the stronger one: persistent + replayable SSE + per-node detail). **(1) REST surface documented** — new [restAPI.md §3.32 "Flow Execution & Monitoring"](RestAPI/restAPI.md) (execute/runs/run/node-data/cancel/stream, Task-Object aliases `status_url`/`last_updated`/`result`, SSE event catalog, end-to-end walkthrough). **(2) Session binding** — every run binds to a session: the caller's when provided, else the flow's **one persistent `"<flow> — runs"` session** (column `flows.runs_session_id`, self-applying migration) reused across all headless runs → one sidebar entry per flow, not per run. The bound `session_id` is stamped on `flow_runs.session_id` and broadcast live via `new_session_created` (the REST `POST /v1/sessions` path doesn't emit it; `_provision_run_session` does) so the sidebar updates without a refresh; the session name is re-asserted to `"<flow> — runs"` after each run (beats the LLM-driven auto-naming). **(3) Cohesive flow-run turn** (headless/REST only; suppressed for chat-triggered via `record_run_turn=False`) — a **display-only** turn written into the bound session: rich "Flow Run" UI card with a **"View in Canvas →"** button (opens the split panel to inspect run state/nodes, same affordance as the regular flow card; delegated `.flow-run-open-btn` handler in `ui.js`) + a compact `get_run` pointer in the LLM `chat_object` (pull-not-push, no context bloat) + a `workflow_history` entry carrying `profile_type='flow'`, `flow_id`, `flow_run_id`, and `source='rest'`+`origin='flow'` (the **"Rest Call" + "Flow"** chat badges). Accounting zeroed (`turn_cost=0`) so the run never double-counts; the true aggregate rides in `flow_total_cost`/`flow_tokens_*` from the run ledger (correct even in individual mode). On reload, `UI.renderFlowRunTrace` shows the node-by-node trace in Live Status (flow branch of `handleReloadPlanClick`). **(4) `node_session_mode` is governed by `settings.parallelExecution`** (serialize→compact, parallelize→individual), NOT the request param (vestigial) — guarantees the unsafe shared-session+concurrent-writers combo can't be selected. **(5) Bug fix:** `_execute_llm_node_once`'s create-new-session branch logged an undefined `profile_id` (NameError) — broke individual/parallel/`session_context:"new"` LLM-node sessions; fixed. Verified by `test/test_flow_rest_contract.py` (89-assertion REST contract gate) + browser checks. Files: `core/flow_executor.py`, `core/flow_db.py`, `api/flow_routes.py`, `components/builtin/flow/handler.py`, `static/js/{eventHandlers,ui}.js`. Docs: [FLOW_COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/FLOW_COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md) §6/§8/§9, [restAPI.md §3.32](RestAPI/restAPI.md). **Server restart required.**
- **Jun 2026**: Optimize fast-lanes + related profile/provider fixes. **(1) Optimize fast-lanes** — two *independent, opt-in, default-off* toggles on `tool_enabled` profiles (Profile editor → Advanced Configuration), making Optimize behave more like Ideate+tools on simple requests while keeping full power for complex ones. **Report fast-track** (`fastTrackSimpleReports` + `fastTrackMaxRows`): when the collected result is provably small (rows ≤ max **and** distilled data < 6 KB), `TDA_FinalReport` swaps its verbose CanonicalResponse prompt for a one-/two-sentence synthesis — the LLM call, parse, and result schema are byte-for-byte unchanged, only the prompt text differs. The decision is made in `phase_executor.py` (single source of truth, where the SSE events are emitted) and stamped onto the action; `adapter.py:_invoke_final_report_task` HONOURS the stamp (data-size guard kept as a net) rather than re-deciding. Live Status renders a distinct **"Fast-Track Final Report"** step. **Plan gate** (`planningGate`): a tiny SIMPLE/COMPLEX classification call runs before strategic planning; on SIMPLE it builds a minimal one-phase plan, ensures the report phase via `Planner._ensure_final_report_phase()`, and hands off to execution by mirroring the proven *replay* path (`meta_plan` + `state=EXECUTING`) — so the 12-pass planner core is untouched and there's NO new execution code; on COMPLEX / unparseable plan / ANY error it leaves state untouched so the full planner runs (escalation). Live Status shows **"Plan Gate: Evaluating Planning Necessity"** then **"Fast Lane — Strategic Planning Skipped"** or **"Full Planning Required"**. Both fail-safe: for non-opted-in profiles the report decision stays `False` and the gate block never runs → identical behavior. Trade (opt-in, by design): the gate plan bypasses RAG champion cases + rewrite passes, trusting the model more for simple requests; tool errors still go through normal self-correction. Files: `static/js/handlers/configurationHandler.js`, `templates/index.html`, `agent/phase_executor.py`, `agent/engines/optimize_engine.py`, `mcp_adapter/adapter.py`. Doc: [FUSION_OPTIMIZER_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/FUSION_OPTIMIZER_ARCHITECTURE.md). **Server restart required.** **(2) Tool/prompt selection — "allow zero" model:** `config_manager.get_profile_enabled_tools` / `get_profile_enabled_prompts` now ALWAYS return the profile's own selection, including an *empty* selection (= run with zero MCP tools/prompts). `inherit_classification` no longer overrides the *selection* — only the classification *metadata* (categories/scopes) is inherited, via the separate `load_profile_classification_into_state()` path. So an inheriting Optimize profile picks which classified tools to enable (down to none); editing tools on an inherited profile in the config takes effect verbatim. **(3) MLX tool calling enabled by default:** `_create_mlx_llm` no longer hardcodes `_no_function_calling = True` — `mlx_lm.server` accepts the `tools` param and capable models (e.g. Gemma) emit real tool calls (verified). Opt out per-config with `mlx_disable_tools: true`. **(4) Skill content injected for `conversation_with_tools`:** `ConversationEngine` previously surfaced only the *skills-applied metadata* — the skill markdown (e.g. `teradata-sql-expert`) never reached the model. It now combines the skill system-prompt + user-context blocks into a `skill_context` passed to `ConversationAgentExecutor`, appended to the system prompt (mirrors IdeateEngine/FocusEngine). **(5) Profile test probes tool-calling:** for `llm_only + useMcpTools` profiles, the profile test binds a probe tool and checks the model emits a tool call — `success`/`warning`/`info` surfaced in the results panel. Files (2–5): `core/config_manager.py`, `llm/langchain_adapter.py`, `agent/engines/conversation_engine.py`, `agent/conversation_agent.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`.

Add `'flow'` to `PIN_SUPPORTED` (`dashboardHandler.js`) so the conversation hover **Pin to Dashboard** button appears on `[data-component-id="flow"]` cards. `_renderTileContent` gains a `flow` branch that dynamic-imports the flow renderer and calls the new export **`renderFlowPreview`** (`components/builtin/flow/renderer.js`) in `_dashboardFill` mode: a static SVG schematic drawn from `definition.nodes[].position` + edges (no React Flow) that fills the tile, plus a live-state **"View in Canvas → / Expanded in side panel →"** button (`openFlowSplitPanel`); reconciles to live flow state by `flow_id` so a stale pinned snapshot self-heals. Flow tile **refresh = re-render only, no LLM** (special-cased in `_refreshTile` — re-running the originating prompt would re-create/modify the flow); tooltip "Sync with live flow". `component_id` has no DB CHECK so no migration — schema doc-comment only. **Bundled dashboard layout fixes:** inline viz-card footer buttons no longer wrap (`white-space:nowrap`+`flex-shrink:0` on `.dash-inline-btn`); table tiles cap to their grid-row span via inline `max-height` (`_spanHeightPx`) so tall tables scroll internally instead of overlapping the tile below, with a JS-toggled bottom scroll-fade; KG tile preview fills its tile (`_dashboardFill` in `renderKGInlineCompact`/`_renderMiniGraph`) instead of a fixed 200px block. - **Jun 2026**: Flow node-reference resolution — tolerant runtime + authoring canonicalisation (root-cause for weak models). A small model authoring a `decision`/`task_function` off a SQL/`task_tool` node invents endless reference syntaxes for the previous value (`{Count Customers}.result[0]…`, `$customer_count`, `{Get Customer Count.customer_count}`, `node-2d243c2d.customer_count`, `Label.customer_count`) — all broken, so the condition fails to eval and routes False silently. Teaching the model the "right" form proved unreliable; the platform absorbs it instead (intelligent-component principle). Three pieces: **(1) Column shortcuts** — `FlowState.resolve_for_node` exposes a predecessor `output`'s first-row columns as top-level, numeric-coerced names, so `customer_count <= 100` works directly (the raw list stays at `output[0]['col']`). **(2) Shared core `core/flow_refs.py`** (`rewrite_refs`, whole-then-last-segment) — ONE impl of `{ref}`/`{Node.col}`/`$name` parsing, reused by both the runtime resolver (→ values, `flow_executor._substitute_brace_refs`) and authoring (→ canonical names) — no drift. **(3) Authoring canonicalisation + validation `core/flow_validation.py`** (`validate_and_repair`), run at the persistence boundary (`flow_db.create_flow`/`update_flow`, which `apply_patch` routes through) so the STORED flow / canvas NEVER shows broken syntax — every invented form collapses to `customer_count <= 100`; `_strip_node_qualifiers` removes real node-id/label prefixes from bare dotted refs; SQL columns derived from `AS <alias>`; a reference to a value the upstream step can't produce is REJECTED on the LLM create path with a precise message so the model self-corrects in-turn. Server restart to load. Files: `core/flow_refs.py`, `core/flow_validation.py`, `core/flow_executor.py`, `core/flow_db.py`, `components/builtin/flow/handler.py`, `components/builtin/flow/instructions.json`, `skills/builtin/flow-designer/flow-designer.md`. - **Jun 2026**: Component-instance portability + marketplace. A uniform, manifest-driven contract for exporting/importing/publishing **component instances** (a specific flow, a specific dashboard — not the component code). **Contract** (`BaseComponentHandler`): `export_instance` / `import_instance(mode=create|update, target_id, mapping, dry_run)` / `list_instances`, opt-in via manifest `supports_instance_io` (surfaced through `to_api_dict`). Cross-references (profiles) travel as **tags** and remap on import; a deterministic `content_hash` (excludes `exported_at`) drives marketplace sync. Shared core in `src/trusted_data_agent/components/instance_portability.py` (inventory / preflight / remap / hash / dedupe) — flow + dashboard both on it, no drift; canvas plugs in for free. **File export/import**: generic endpoints `GET/POST /v1/components/<cid>/instances/<id>/export|import` (two-phase: dry_run preflight → commit), surfaced as Export/Import buttons in the **Workspace panel** AND the **Components → Flows tab**, driven by one shared **remap dialog** (`static/js/handlers/instancePortabilityUI.js` → `openRemapDialog`, endpoint-agnostic). **Marketplace** (new **Components** tab next to Skills): publish / fork / **subscribe + manual sync** / rate / targeted-visibility, gated so you can only publish/fork instances of a component **activated for you**. Subscribe materializes a local copy + captures the remap; Sync re-materializes **in place** (`mode=update`, preserves the local id) when the publisher's `content_hash` moves (never auto-pulls). Modelled on the KG marketplace; instances are DATA so there's no code-execution trust concern. - **Jun 2026**: Flow live execution animation — conversation-triggered runs animate the open canvas. Root cause: flow run events were emitted to one of two divergent buses by initiator (REST `/execute` → per-run stream; chat `TDA_Flow(execute)` → notification channel) and the canvas only watched the per-run stream + runs it started itself. Fix: one **canonical emitter** in `execute_flow` fans every event to BOTH the per-run stream AND the per-user notification channel for every initiator; callers stopped choosing a bus; per-run pub/sub moved into `flow_executor.py`. Canvas listens on the notification channel (guarded by `flow_id`) for run discovery + reconciles on mount (`GET /runs?limit=1`) so it self-heals across all timings (snapshot + stream). Files: `core/flow_executor.py`, `api/flow_routes.py`, `components/builtin/flow/handler.py`, `static/js/notifications.js`, `components/builtin/flow/renderer.js`.
