- **Jun 2026**: Flow edges missing on cold load — handle-bounds re-registration fix. On platform start / hard refresh, entering a session with a flow rendered the nodes (correctly positioned) but **no edges**; switching session away+back fixed it. All prior *timing* fixes failed because it's not a measurement delay. A store-vs-DOM probe proved: single clean mount, edges in the store, all nodes measured, but `node.internals.handleBounds` was `null` for every node (`0/N`). ReactFlow computes handle bounds during the node-measurement pass; on a **cold** mount (the `@xyflow/react` v12 CDN just finished loading) a custom node's `<Handle>` children mount one frame **after** the node is first measured, so the bounds pass misses them. Node *dimensions* still measure (nodes stay centred via `nodeOrigin:[0.5,0]`) but every edge loses its endpoints → zero paths; nothing re-measures handles afterward (the node `ResizeObserver` only fires on a size *change*). Warm remount works because handles are present in the first pass. Fix: **`HandleBoundsFixer`** — a component rendered as a child of `<ReactFlow>` (inside the store context, like `Controls`/`MiniMap`) that waits for `useNodesInitialized()` then calls `useUpdateNodeInternals()` for every node, with retries at 60/260 ms to land after the handles paint (gated on `_hasRFHooks`). A defensive `_mountSeq` token also coalesces duplicate concurrent `openFlowSplitPanel()` calls into one mount (hardening, not the edges fix). Browser-reload only (renderer.js); no restart. File: `components/builtin/flow/renderer.js`. Doc: [FLOW_COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/FLOW_COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md) §16.7.
- **Jun 2026**: Flow LLM-node extension picker — manifest-driven, root-cause fix (two bugs, one root each). The picker that attaches post-processing extensions to a flow `task_llm` node was driven by a hardcoded `BUILTIN_EXTENSIONS` array in `flow/renderer.js` that independently decided **eligibility** and **params**, drifting from the extension manifests. Symptoms: a newly-activated extension stayed invisible until a page reload; `pdf` was excluded only by omission; `summary`'s manifest param (`brief`/`detailed`) never showed. **(1) Single source of truth:** new manifest field `flow_node_eligible` (default `true`; only terminal/export extensions like `pdf` set `false`) surfaced through `manager.list_extensions()`. `renderer.js` `_fetchFlowExtensions()` now builds the picker from `GET /v1/extensions/activated` (already admin- + activation-filtered), keeping `flow_node_eligible !== false`; label/description/`hasParam` all read from the manifest. The frontend `BUILTIN_EXTENSIONS` array is reduced to `EXT_VISUALS` (abbr/colour hints only, with a derived fallback for unknown ids) — no longer an eligibility gate, so new built-ins/user extensions appear automatically. **(2) No stale cache:** the never-invalidated module cache (`_activatedExtsCache`) was removed — the picker re-fetches on every open (light endpoint, user-initiated), so mid-session activations appear without reload. The `!`-autocomplete in chat is intentionally NOT filtered by `flow_node_eligible` (`!pdf` stays valid). The executor (`_execute_extension_node`) resolves extensions by id with no activation gate — eligibility is purely picker-UX. **(3) Picker search + category grouping** (frontend-only, builds on the manifest data): the picker popover gained an auto-focused search box (matches id + name + description + keywords — same semantics as the Extensions config screen, mirrored as `_extMatchesSearch` since `renderer.js` is an isolated Preact module) and category-grouped results (`_groupExtsByCategory`, order Transform → Automation → Analysis → others) so it scales as the eligible list grows. Status/Level/Sort were deliberately NOT ported (Status is a no-op — only activated shown; Level is an authoring concern; Sort is replaced by grouping). Popover widened to 260px with a height-capped scroll list. **Server restart required for (1)** (`manager.py` loads at startup; `renderer.js`/manifests are reload-only). Files: `src/trusted_data_agent/extensions/manager.py`, `extensions/builtin/pdf/manifest.json`, `components/builtin/flow/renderer.js`. Docs: [FLOW_COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/FLOW_COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md) (§7 LLM-Node Extension Slots), [EXTENSION_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/EXTENSION_ARCHITECTURE.md) (Manifest Schema → `flow_node_eligible`).
- **Jun 2026**: Component tool calling hardened for weak/strict providers (root-cause, two independent fixes). **(1) Provider-agnostic tool schemas.** Component tools with dynamic-key object args (`TDA_Charting`'s `mapping` / `data`, declared `dict` / `list[dict]`) emitted an open `object` + `additionalProperties: true` schema. Strict provider validators (Groq, Cerebras, OpenAI strict mode) ignore `additionalProperties` and reject every key the model produces — surfacing via OpenRouter (a broker that forwards open-weights models like Llama to whichever upstream is cheapest/fastest, often Groq) as `Upstream error from Groq: ... additionalProperties not allowed` even though the user only selected "OpenRouter". Root cause = open-object nodes in the schema. Fix in `components/manager.py`: `_build_args_schema()` advertises these args as JSON-encoded **strings** (`Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(_coerce_open_object_to_json_str)]` → reliable `type: string` that survives strict-mode transformers, while a native dict/list input is coerced so Pydantic never fails); the field set is recorded as `__json_string_fields__`; `_decode_json_string_args()` decodes them back to native objects in `get_component_langchain_tools._run_component` before the handler runs (handlers unchanged). Scalar aliases `integer`/`number`/`boolean` added so `row_limit` etc. emit a real type, not an empty `{}`. Verified on Groq *directly* (forced `provider:{order:["Groq"],allow_fallbacks:false}` → HTTP 200). Connector tools already coerce non-scalars to `str`. **(2) Leaked tool-call recovery.** Weak models (e.g. Llama-4-Scout) sometimes emit a component call as plain-text JSON (`{"tool_name":"TDA_Charting","arguments":{...}}`) instead of invoking it, leaving a blank turn (the existing `_strip_leaked_tool_calls` removed it as noise). New `conversation_agent._recover_leaked_component_calls()` scans the answer for balanced `{...}` blocks naming a bound `TDA_*` tool that did NOT run this turn, invokes it for real (`tool.ainvoke`), extracts the payload, appends it, and strips the JSON — mirroring the existing `_auto_canvas_code_blocks` recovery. Verified: bar chart → "pie chart instead" now renders the pie chart on turn 2 even when the model leaks the call. Files: `components/manager.py`, `agent/conversation_agent.py`. Doc: [COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md) (Integration Points → Tool Call Routing).
- **Jun 2026**: Turn provenance tags (Flow / Genie Parent / Genie Child) — root-cause refactor of the chat turn badges. `source` had conflated transport with orchestration, so a flow turn could only show "Rest Call" and never "Flow". Split into two independent, server-authoritative facts persisted on the user turn: **`source`** = transport (`rest`/`scheduler`/`text` → Rest Call / Scheduled) and a new **`origin`** = orchestration driver (`flow` / `genie_parent` / `genie_child`). `origin` is stamped once in `execution_service.run_agent_execution` and persisted via `add_message_to_histories`, so every render path — historical reload, live REST (`rest_task_complete` payload), live UI (`user_message_profile_tag` event) — reads the same fact with no frontend re-derivation. Detection: the flow engine passes `origin='flow'` (the `/query` endpoint maps its `source:"flow"` body to `source='rest'` + `origin='flow'`); genie is auto-detected from the session — `profile_type=='genie'` → `genie_parent` (coordinator, top-level or nested; coordinator check wins), else `genie_metadata.is_genie_slave` → `genie_child` (expert sub-turn). Tags stack and are independent of transport: flow turn → **Rest Call + Flow**, coordinator over REST → **Rest Call + Genie Parent**, expert → **Rest Call + Genie Child**. Robust to profile rename/delete (recorded at execution). Files: `agent/execution_service.py`, `core/session_manager.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `static/js/{ui.js,notifications.js,eventHandlers.js,handlers/sessionManagement.js}`, `static/css/main.css`. Docs: [COORDINATOR_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/COORDINATOR_ARCHITECTURE.md) (§4 Turn Provenance Tags), [FLOW_COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/FLOW_COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md).
- **Jun 2026**: Flow extensions — cost/observability fixes + deterministic flow primitives. **Flow node cost/observability:** node cost now **sums** per-statement `cost_usd` across `token_update` events instead of keeping only the last (an LLM extension's `token_update` is emitted last, so the node was reporting only the extension's cost and dropping every main-LLM call's cost); tokens read turn-scoped `turn_*` (no cross-node bleed in serialized sessions); each LLM-backed extension is surfaced on `flow_node_complete` and rendered as a per-extension cost line (no longer an invisible folded cost); fixed the flow header live-cost counter (read `cost_usd`, not a non-existent `cost`, which kept it at $0). **New deterministic (no-LLM) extensions** for flow control: `!extract` gains scalar selectors (`first`/`last`/`max`/`min`/`sum` → one bare value) and `/regex/` capture — fixing the fragile positional `extract['numbers'][0]`; new `!condition` (bare-bool threshold / `contains=` / `/regex/`); new `!format` (template a message from extracted values). Shared `extensions/helpers/numbers.py`. **Incumbents:** `!classify` accepts custom categories (`:a,b,c`, was hardcoded to an ops vocabulary); `decision`/`boolean_check`/`classify` temperature 0.1→0.0; removed all n8n/Flowise/Airflow-specific wording (extensions serve any flow engine — the internal flow component or external automation alike). Catalog is now 9 builtins. Files: `extensions/builtin/{extract,condition,format,classify,decision,boolean-check,json}/`, `extensions/helpers/numbers.py`, `core/flow_executor.py`, `components/builtin/flow/renderer.js`, `test/test_flow_extensions.py`. Doc: [EXTENSION_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/EXTENSION_ARCHITECTURE.md).
- **Jun 2026**: Flow layout & render correctness — fixed the long-standing "flow opens as a vertical spine, must click Layout to fix" bug at the root. Cause: **two layout engines that disagreed**. The backend `compute_layout`/`apply_layout` (`flow_layout.py`) branches decision nodes (authoritative; used by create, every structural patch, and the Layout button via `POST /v1/flows/<id>/layout`), but a lighter client-side `_autoLayout` in `renderer.js` collapsed single-node ranks onto a vertical spine. `_realignToViewport` re-ran that client layout whenever auto-layout was on, and the `#flow-split-panel` ResizeObserver fires its **initial callback on mount** (display:none→flex is a size change) — so every open overwrote the correct DB positions with the spine ~150ms after mount. **Fix:** a topological DAG layout is width-independent — `_realignToViewport` now does **remeasure + `fitView` only**, never re-layouts; the backend is the single source of truth and the frontend renders the positions stored on each node. The client `_autoLayout` is confined to the `window.__flowDebug` helper — never reintroduce it into a render/resize path. Complementary fixes bundled: (1) `create_flow` + `generate_empty_flow` default `settings.autoLayout = True` so new flows arrange without a manual click; (2) `_normalize_decision_branches(definition)` (`flow_db.py`, called from `create_flow`/`update_flow`) assigns unused `'true'`/`'false'` conditions to condition-less decision edges + sets `type='conditional'` so True/False branch pills render and the executor actually follows them; (3) `_restoreFlowState` (`sessionManagement.js`) re-fetches the authoritative flow by `flow_id` before opening so a stale `localStorage` snapshot doesn't render old positions; (4) `GET /v1/flows/<id>/node-data` aggregates the latest result **per node across `list_runs(limit=25)`** (newest wins) so running a single node no longer wipes other nodes' earlier Data-panel results; (5) per-node execution-stats overlay (`showAnalytics`) is off by default and only rendered when on — prevents the overlay from displacing handles and making edges leak into node bodies. `renderer.js`/`static/` changes are browser-reload only; no restart. Files: `components/builtin/flow/renderer.js`, `src/trusted_data_agent/core/flow_db.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/core/flow_executor.py`, `src/trusted_data_agent/api/flow_routes.py`, `static/js/handlers/sessionManagement.js`. Doc: [docs/Architecture/FLOW_COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/FLOW_COMPONENT_ARCHITECTURE.md) (§7 Layout Engine — single-source-of-truth note).
- **Jun 2026**: Unified split-panel chrome — all five right-side component split panels (canvas, dashboard, flow, scheduler, knowledge graph) now share ONE theme-aware header system instead of each renderer injecting its own near-duplicate CSS. New `static/css/split-panels.css` defines the canonical classes `.sp-header` / `.sp-accent-icon` / `.sp-title` / `.sp-switcher` / `.sp-action-btn` (28px) / `.sp-divider` / `.sp-subtoolbar` / `.sp-switcher-menu`. Every panel `<aside>` carries `class="sp-panel"` + an inline `--sp-accent` sourced from its component manifest `icon_accent` (canvas `#3b82f6`, KG `#10b981`, scheduler `#a855f7`, dashboard `#0ea5e9`, flow `#f59e0b`), so a single CSS variable drives the identity icon colour, switcher hover, and active states per panel (accent tints via `color-mix`). New shared helper `static/js/handlers/splitPanelChrome.js` → `window.mountSplitPanelSwitcher({btnEl,listUrl,itemsKey,idField/idFn,labelField/labelFn,metaField,getCurrentId,onSelect,newLabel,onNew})` renders the instance-selector dropdown (body-portal menu, current-highlight, outside-click/Esc dismiss; copies `--sp-accent` onto the menu since it's portalled off the panel). **Instance switchers** added to canvas (`/v1/canvases`) and KG (`/v1/knowledge-graph/list` → graph-spec by profile); dashboard refactored onto the helper; flow's switcher moved INTO the shared header (the in-canvas React `.flow-selector` is hidden to avoid duplication); scheduler keeps a static `.sp-title` (it's a list of all tasks). **Canvas was the outlier** — it suppressed the standard header (`.canvas-split-header{display:none}`) and showed an editor-style bar instead; now it shows the standard `.sp-header` (accent code-icon + `#canvas-switcher-btn` + fullscreen + close) with its editor controls (tabs + Code/Changes/run/History/copy/download) as a secondary row below (`renderCanvasFull` skips the in-body icon/title + the toolbar fullscreen/close injection when `containerId` starts with `canvas-split-`). Fixes delivered: scheduler's dark-mode-invisible title (was hardcoded `#1e293b`), mismatched button sizes/borders/backgrounds/accents across panels, and flow's deep-navy canvas (`.flow-root .react-flow` was `--bg-primary`, now `--card-bg` to match the other panel bodies). Theme-aware throughout (CSS vars, monochrome icons). **Note:** `templates/index.html` edits require a server restart (Jinja caches the template at startup); `renderer.js` / `static/` changes are picked up on browser reload. Files: `static/css/split-panels.css`, `static/js/handlers/splitPanelChrome.js`, `templates/index.html`, `components/builtin/{canvas,dashboard,flow,knowledge_graph,scheduler}/renderer.js`. - **Jun 2026**: Workspace resource panel — a new icon-rail panel (briefcase icon, label "Work") in the right-side resource drawer that surfaces the persistent **instances** a user created with action components, grouped into collapsible sections (collapsed by default), one per component **enabled for the active profile**. Phase 1 covers dashboards, flows, canvases, and scheduled tasks. A section appears only if its component's `profile_enabled` is true (full governance merge from `GET /v1/profiles/<id>/components`); within a section ALL the user's instances are listed (instances are per-user — "profile-gate, show all"). Each row is a launcher: **Open** delegates to the component's own split panel (`import('/api/v1/components/<id>/renderer')` → `openDashboardPanel`/`openFlowSplitPanel`/`renderCanvas`/`openSchedulerSplitPanel`), **Delete** is an inline two-step confirm. Section identity (icon + accent) comes from each component's manifest `icon_accent`; behaviour (list endpoint, fields, open/delete) is a single `WORKSPACE_REGISTRY` entry per component, so a new instance-bearing component plugs in with one entry (Chart is excluded — ephemeral; Context Window is the existing Context panel). Loads on tab activation and on profile change (mirrors the KG/Context panels via `updateResourcePanelForProfile`); the rail item hides itself when no instance-bearing component is enabled for the profile. Theme-aware (CSS vars, monochrome icons). - **Jun 2026**: Flow component — Flowise-style parameters + world-class editor UX (entirely within the flow component; `instructions.json` / the LLM tool surface is unchanged). **Parameters & data flow:** three reference tiers — cross-flow **global variables** (`flow_variables` table, `GET/PUT /v1/flow-variables`, self-applying migration), per-flow **parameters** (`definition.global_params`, `update_global_params` patch op), and per-node **named outputs** (`output_as`, fixes the single-`output` fan-in collision) — all referenced as `{name}` or Flowise `$name` (sigil stripped before the sandboxed `eval`; value-substituted in prompts; `$digit` left intact). Context precedence: global vars → flow params → predecessor outputs. Helpers in `flow_executor.py`: `_normalize_param_refs`, `_substitute_dollar_values`, `_apply_output_alias`, `_load_global_variables` (fail-open). **Debugging:** partial execution — `execute_flow(start_node_id, run_mode)` with `single` / `downstream` modes, state-seeded from the latest run (`_compute_partial_targets`, `_partial_execution_order`); surfaced as context-menu "Run only this node" / "Run from here →" + an inspector **Data panel** (per-node Input/Output via `GET /v1/flows/<id>/node-data`). **Editor mechanics:** `SmartTextField` (`$`-autocomplete + inline unknown-ref validation + health-bar warnings), client-side undo/redo (`⌘Z`/`⇧⌘Z`, definition stack at the `patchFlow` chokepoint, restore via `PUT`), inline rename (double-click), color-coded True/False decision branch labels, duplicate (`⌘D`)/copy-paste (`⌘C`/`⌘V`)/marquee multi-select + bulk delete, hover-edge `+`/`×` (insert/disconnect). **Discoverability:** contextual selection toolbar, `?` help overlay, `⌘K` command palette; descriptive version-history labels (`_label_for_patch`). All surfaces theme-aware (CSS vars) + monochrome icons. Verified: 37 unit assertions (`test/test_flow_parameters.py`) + live REST smoke test of partial execution. - **Jun 2026**: Plan-based RAG-seeding gate (planner repositories) — successful turns are now only saved as champion cases if their plan contains at least one **data-acquisition phase**. Presentation/capability-only follow-ups ("show me a bar chart", "show me the knowledge graph", "put that on a dashboard", a bare final report) no longer pollute the planner repository — their value is content-independent and their arguments depend on prior-turn context, so they can never replay usefully and could surface as misleading champions. Classification is **closed against future components by construction**: a phase tool is *non-strategy* iff it is owned by **any** installed component (builtin/user/marketplace — resolved dynamically via `ComponentManager.get_component_by_tool()`, so new components are covered with zero edits) or is in a fixed framework-internal set (`TDA_FinalReport`, `TDA_SystemLog`, `TDA_ContextReport`, `TDA_CurrentDate`); `TDA_SystemOrchestration` (wraps MCP calls), MCP data-source tools, and connectors count as data. A future data-acquiring component opts back in via `"acquires_data": true` in its manifest. Implemented at the single seeding chokepoint `_extract_case_from_turn_summary` via new helpers `_tool_is_data_acquisition` / `_plan_has_data_acquisition` (fails open if the component layer is unavailable, so classification failure never silently kills learning). Maintenance: `maintenance/purge_presentation_seeds.py` retroactively removes faulty seeds from **all** planner repos across all users (dry-run default, `--apply` to delete, timestamped backup written first, cleans both ChromaDB + on-disk `case_*.json`, reuses the identical classifier). Files: `agent/rag_retriever.py`, `components/manager.py`, `maintenance/purge_presentation_seeds.py`, `docs/RAG/RAG.md`.
- **May 2026**: Dashboard tile refresh + provenance hardening — a tile is a `(data-source, visualization-spec)` pair; refresh re-acquires data and re-applies the fixed viz, never scraping a fresh conversational answer. **Three-tier refresh provenance:** (1) **MCP replay** (bolt ⚡) via `POST /v1/dashboards/<id>/tiles/<tile_id>/refresh-mcp` when `mcp_tool_name` is stamped; (2) **presentation-locked re-run** for chart tiles (`refresh_tile` scopes the prompt to "reproduce ONLY the chart"); (3) **embedded-spec extraction** fallback. **Non-destructive** (never blank a working chart) + **component-aware** (recover the chart from the embedded `data-component-id="chart"` spec) in both `_pollTileRefresh` (renderer.js) and `background_wrapper` (dashboard_routes.py). **Turn-bound MCP stamping via new `source_turn_id` column** (`ALTER` migration in `auth/database.py`): all three stamp sites — `add_tile` (`_mcp_stamp_for_turn`), `optimize_engine.py`, `conversation_engine.py` — bind to the originating turn instead of "the latest data tool in the session" (which cross-contaminated tiles across turns, e.g. an Ideate LLM-only tile inheriting an Optimize turn's `base_readQuery`). Turn number threaded `executor.current_turn_number` → `workflow_state` → both component-dispatch contexts (`adapter.py`, `manager.py get_component_langchain_tools`) → `_handle_add_tile`. **Profile badge** resolves by-tag-first (override-aware) with colour from the profile's own `color` field so the tile badge matches the chat chip; both pin paths (chart hover-pin in `dashboardHandler.js`, table interception in `ui.js`) read the tag from the originating user message's `.message-profile-badge` — never a document-wide `.profile-tag` scan (which leaked a stray `@FOCUS` chip onto unrelated tiles). Pin button CSS is self-contained in `dashboardHandler.js`. Also: `_strip_leaked_tool_calls` in `conversation_engine.py` removes echoed `TDA_Charting` tool-call JSON from llm_only answers. Architecture doc updated: [docs/Architecture/DASHBOARD_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/DASHBOARD_ARCHITECTURE.md) §§5,7,8,9. Files: `components/builtin/dashboard/{handler.py,renderer.js}`, `src/trusted_data_agent/api/dashboard_routes.py`, `agent/engines/{optimize_engine,conversation_engine}.py`, `agent/executor.py`, `mcp_adapter/adapter.py`, `components/manager.py`, `auth/database.py`, `static/js/ui.js`, `static/js/handlers/dashboardHandler.js`.

- **May 2026**: KG Store Abstraction Layer — `KGStoreBackend` ABC, `KGStoreCapability` enum, per-profile resolution chain (explicit `config_id` override → profile `kgStoreConfigId` → user default config → global SQLite fallback), SQLite+NetworkX backend (11 capabilities: full CRUD + BFS subgraph, cycle detection, importance ranking, shortest path), Neo4j Bolt backend (13 capabilities incl. `NATIVE_GRAPH_QUERIES`, `FULL_TEXT_SEARCH`; graceful `HAS_NEO4J=False` fallback when package absent), admin governance with `kg_backend_settings` table (per-tier enable flags + allowed-backend lists), 9 REST configuration/settings endpoints, `GraphStore` delegate wrapper with 10 `async def` CRUD methods, and **Graph Stores** admin UI tab (formerly "KG Stores"; Add/Edit/Delete/Test modal + governance section + profile KG Backend dropdown). `kg_store_config_id` persisted on `kg_metadata` and propagated through all lifecycle ops so each KG routes to its creation backend automatically. Backend selector dropdown added to KG Constructor modal and marketplace Fork modal. Backend badge (colour-coded) shown on all KG cards. Three raw-SQL abstraction bypasses fixed: agent-pack KG uninstall, `_delete_subscription_local_kg`, and `_rebuild_subscription_kg` — all now use `GraphStore.clear_graph()` / `GraphStore.import_bulk()`. UI renames: Configuration tabs "KG Stores" → "Graph Stores", "Context Windows" → "Memory"; section headings "KG Backends" → "Knowledge Graph Backends", "Context Window Types" → "Memory Types". Zero manual deployment steps — all schema migrations are self-applying on startup/first-use. Schema: `38_kg_backend_settings.sql`. - **May 2026**: KG marketplace **Subscribe** feature — live-tracking copies of marketplace KGs that auto-rebuild when the publisher republishes. New `kg_subscriptions` table (`schema/37_kg_subscriptions.sql`) + nullable stamps on `kg_metadata` (`is_subscribed`, `source_subscription_id`) and `marketplace_knowledge_graphs` (`subscriber_count`, `export_content_hash`). Endpoints: `POST/DELETE /v1/marketplace/knowledge-graphs/<id>/subscribe`, `POST .../sync`, `GET /v1/knowledge-graph/subscriptions`. **Materialization model is snapshot-with-sync** (different from collections' reference-based and agent-packs' frozen-snapshot): subscribe deep-copies entities/relationships into the subscriber's profile, marks the local KG `is_subscribed=1` (read-only via `KnowledgeGraphReadOnlyError` gates on `add_entity`/`update_entity`/`delete_entity`/`add_relationship`/`delete_relationship`/`import_bulk`/`clear_graph`); on republish, the publisher's KG export is rewritten in place and a thread-pool fanout (`_fanout_auto_sync`) raw-SQL DELETE+INSERTs each subscriber's local copy with the new content. **Republish-in-place** via the existing publish endpoint preserves `marketplace_id`, `install_count`, `subscriber_count`, etc — discovered via `(kg_id, publisher_user_id)` lookup, switches to UPDATE instead of INSERT. Unpublish cascades — every subscriber's local KG hard-deleted via `_delete_subscription_local_kg`. Subscribed KGs are **blocked from agent-pack export** with a warning ("convert to a Fork to include it"). Frontend KG marketplace cards show Subscribe / Sync / Unsubscribe buttons with `is_sync_available` driving the Sync button state. Feature gated by `is_kg_subscriptions_enabled()` (admin opts in via `kg_marketplace_settings.kg_subscriptions_enabled`; default off). Sessions don't bind to KG IDs (looked up per-profile dynamically via `kg_profile_assignments`) so no session-archive helper is needed; in-flight queries degrade gracefully on lookup miss. Verification gate: `scripts/verify_update_in_place.sh` (43 assertions including marketplace + subscriber simulation). Side fixes: (1) publish endpoint pre-existing 500 IndexError on `pack_row["is_owned"]` (column doesn't exist on `agent_pack_installations`) — now reads ownership via `agent_pack_resources`; (2) uderia_expert `doc_id` switched from abs_path to rel_path so builds are portable across hosts; (3) uderia_expert CDC source_uri wiring keyed by `document_id` instead of `filename` to avoid clobbering same-named docs. Agent Pack Marketplace browse gets a "Manage" button that resolves the local installation via `/api/v1/agent-packs` and reuses `openPublishPackModal()`. New REST endpoints: `GET/PUT /v1/marketplace/skills/<id>/targeted-users`, `GET/PUT /v1/marketplace/extensions/<id>/targeted-users`, `GET/PUT /v1/marketplace/knowledge-graphs/<id>/targeted-users`. Files: `api/skills_routes.py`, `api/rest_routes.py`, `api/kg_marketplace_routes.py`, `static/js/handlers/marketplaceHandler.js`, `templates/index.html`. Docs: `docs/RestAPI/restAPI.md` §§3.21.16a–b, 3.28.8–9.
- **May 2026 (v1.8)**: Microsoft 365 & Slack Platform Connectors — four new built-in user connectors: `uderia-outlook` (email + calendar via Graph API), `uderia-teams` (channel messaging + meetings), `uderia-sharepoint` (files + sites), `uderia-slack` (channel history + messaging). All Microsoft connectors share a single Azure AD app registration; Slack uses its own OAuth app. Registered in `connectors/registry.py`; builtin MCP servers in `mcp_servers/builtin/`. See [CONNECTOR_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/CONNECTOR_ARCHITECTURE.md).
- **May 2026 (v1.8)**: Per-user component settings — `user_component_settings` table (`schema/34_user_component_settings.sql`) lets admins grant or block individual components per user, independent of global `component_settings` and per-profile `componentConfig`. Governance chain: global disable_list → user override → profile componentConfig.
- **May 2026 (v1.8)**: Scheduler enhancements — three platform maintenance jobs seed `scheduled_tasks` (`schema/33_scheduler_enhancements.sql`) to auto-reset consumption counters (hourly, daily, monthly rollover) via APScheduler. Independent `profile_scheduler_enabled` / `platform_scheduler_enabled` gates in `component_settings` decouple profile and platform scheduler governance.
- **May 2026 (v1.8)**: Continuous Knowledge Sync (CDC) — `schema/32_knowledge_cdc.sql` adds `source_uri`, `ingest_epoch`, `sync_enabled`, `last_checked_at` to `knowledge_documents`; repositories auto-re-index changed files on a configurable schedule. Portable Source URIs allow repos to work across environments using a per-environment Source Root.
- **May 2026 (v1.8)**: SAML 2.0 + Generic OIDC SSO — `schema/30_sso.sql` and `schema/31_saml.sql` add admin-configurable IdP tables; JIT provisioning maps IdP group membership to Uderia tiers on every login. See [SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md).
- **May 2026**: Task Scheduler (Track B) — always-on autonomous agent execution via APScheduler `AsyncIOScheduler`; `TDA_Scheduler` builtin component lets users create/manage recurring tasks through natural language; tasks run through identical `execute_query()` pipeline (same LLM, profile, MCP tools); session context model: `NULL` = new ephemeral session per run, pinned `session_id` = run inside existing session with conversation history; overlap policies: `skip | queue | allow`; post-run token budget guard; result delivery via email, webhook (google_mail deferred); `source: 'scheduler'` badge in chat log; APScheduler optional dependency — graceful degradation if absent. Files: `components/builtin/scheduler/`, `core/task_scheduler.py`, `schema/28_scheduled_tasks.sql`. See [SCHEDULER_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/SCHEDULER_ARCHITECTURE.md).
- **May 2026**: Platform Connector subsystem rename + multi-type architecture — renamed all `platform_mcp_*` identifiers to `platform_connector_*` (DB tables, REST URLs, JS handlers, Python module, HTML element IDs); introduced `connector_type` discriminator (`mcp_stdio | mcp_http | rest | oauth_only`) with `ConnectorInvocationStrategy` ABC and `_INVOCATION_STRATEGIES` registry dict; `McpStdioStrategy` encapsulates subprocess logic; adding a new transport type requires one class + one dict entry. Encryption salt `b'platform_mcp_registry'` intentionally frozen to preserve existing encrypted credentials. Generic OAuth routes (`/api/v1/connectors/<platform>/auth|callback|status|connection`) replace hardcoded Google paths. `_inject_user_tokens()` now delegates to connector module's `inject_env_tokens()` via `connectors/registry.py`. Files: `core/platform_connector_registry.py`, `connectors/registry.py`, `connectors/google_connector.py`, `api/connector_routes.py`, `schema/29_rename_platform_connectors.sql`, `static/js/handlers/platformConnectorAdminHandler.js`, `static/js/handlers/platformConnectorHandler.js`. See [CONNECTOR_ARCHITECTURE.md](Architecture/CONNECTOR_ARCHITECTURE.md).
- **Apr 2026**: `llm_filter_deloop` rewrite pass — new deterministic pass (inserted before `multi_loop_synthesis`) that converts any TDA_LLMFilter loop phase to a standalone filter phase; prevents `redundant_argument_pruning` from stripping `data_to_filter` when the planner incorrectly places TDA_LLMFilter inside a loop. Planner now has 12 rewrite passes. File: `planner.py:_rewrite_llm_filter_deloop()`
- **Apr 2026**: Reflexion-pattern correction history — `correction_history: list` replaces single-overwrite `last_failed_action_info: str` on `PlanExecutor`; every failed tool call in a phase is appended (tool name, arguments, error, strategy); cleared at phase start; rendered into `{correction_history_section}` in `WORKFLOW_TACTICAL_PROMPT`; prevents oscillation where the tactical LLM repeats a previously failed call. Files: `executor.py`, `phase_executor.py:_build_correction_history_section()`, `WORKFLOW_TACTICAL_PROMPT.txt`
- **Apr 2026**: Universal JSON parsing hardening — new `agent/json_utils.py` with `robust_json_parse()` (three-tier: direct `json.loads` → `json_repair` → return None + one-shot retry); replaces all 9 brittle bare `json.loads` sites in `planner.py` and `phase_executor.py`; `json-repair>=0.30.0` added to `requirements.txt`; handles trailing commas, truncated output, markdown fences, single-quoted strings, and surrounding prose across all providers
- **Apr 2026**: Engine modularization — `PlanExecutor.run()` (formerly ~6,800 lines) split into 5 engine classes in `agent/engines/`: `IdeateEngine` (llm_only), `FocusEngine` (rag_focused), `CoordinateEngine` (genie), `OptimizeEngine` (tool_enabled), `ConversationEngine` (llm_only+tools). `EngineRegistry` provides a register decorator + resolve API. `executor.py` is now ~3,160 lines (shared infrastructure + dispatch only). See [Engine Modularization Architecture](Architecture/ENGINE_MODULARIZATION_ARCHITECTURE.md)
- **Apr 2026**: Independent phase parallelization — `OptimizeEngine._stream_parallel_phases()` uses `asyncio.gather()` to execute independent plan phases concurrently; events are collected per-phase (not interleaved) for clean Live Status rendering; `turn_action_history` post-sorted by `phase_num` for correct historical replay
- **Apr 2026**: Date range orchestrator parallelization — `execute_date_range_orchestrator()` now fires all per-day tool calls concurrently via `asyncio.gather()`; 30-day ranges drop from `30 × tool_latency` to `~1 × tool_latency`
- **Apr 2026**: SQL consolidation enabled by default — `ENABLE_SQL_CONSOLIDATION_REWRITE` flipped to `True`; consecutive SQL phases automatically merged into a single optimised query (CTE/JOIN) on every turn
- **Apr 2026**: LLM call timeout — every LLM call wrapped with `asyncio.wait_for(timeout=LLM_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)`; provider hangs raise `asyncio.TimeoutError` after the configured timeout (default 120 s) rather than blocking indefinitely
- **Apr 2026**: Cycle detection for recursive prompt chains — `visited_prompts` set threaded through the execution tree; circular prompt graphs (A→B→A) detected and short-circuited before hitting depth limit
- **Apr 2026**: RAG over-retrieval fix — `rag_retriever.py` fetch multiplier reduced from `k × 10` to `k × 3`; ~67% reduction in ChromaDB query + deserialization cost with no quality impact
- **Apr 2026**: Plan rewrite diff events — `planner.py` emits a `plan_rewrite_diff` event after each of the 12 rewrite passes, capturing before/after plan state and a diff summary; full pass-level auditability in the Live Status historical trace
- **Apr 2026**: Consumption enforcement hardening — quota check changed from fail-open (silent bypass on exception) to fail-closed; enforcement failures surface a `consumption_warning` SSE event and increment an audit bypass counter
- **Apr 2026**: Genie coordinator state fixes — 5 targeted fixes: lock creation atomicity via `dict.setdefault()`, memory leak cleanup in `finally` block, `clear_session_cache()` scope fix, `get_used_slave_sessions()` scope fix, sequential primer mode now iterates all statements
- **Apr 2026**: Live Status parallel phase event sequencing — FASTPATH events carry `phase_num` in details dict for correct post-sort positioning; tactical LLM slow path `phase_end` now calls `_log_system_event()` consistently with all other 5 sites; `renderHistoricalTrace()` defensive footer via `_addDefensivePhaseFooter()` when closing phase containers implicitly
- **Apr 2026**: RAG offload condensation for `conversation_history` — replaces destructive truncation with semantic retrieval via per-session ChromaDB (`SessionVectorStore`); `condense_rag()` keeps `floor_pct`% of recent turns via sliding window and fills the remainder from semantically retrieved earlier chunks; configurable per-module in Context Window Types; amber **RAG** badge + chunk count shown in Live Status panel when it fires
- **Apr 2026**: Tool Context Enrichment for @OPTIM profiles — every `tool_enabled` assistant turn in `chat_object` now carries a `tool_context` field with a compact `[Tool Execution Summary]` (tool name, key argument truncated at 120 chars, row count, column names, 1 sample row); makes `conversation_history` a richer RAG offload target with cross-turn tool awareness; TDA_ internal tools excluded; built in `executor.py:_build_tool_context_summary()` + `_format_tool_summary_line()`; rendered by `conversation_history/handler.py:_format_messages()` so the LLM sees it as part of the assistant's turn
